findings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor locations and clearance dimensions are required to demonstrate that buildings maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No such documentation is present on the site plan.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8, particularly Building 1 and Building 8 (closest to overhead electric lines on western and southern boundaries)
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms overhead electric utility lines (O.H.U.L.) with utility poles exist along Valley View Road (western boundary) and southern property boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1-8 with Building 1 dimensioned at 26.1' and Building 8 at 26.6' from the western property line. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) references existing OHE lines. However, NO building elevation sheets are provided in the 39-sheet set. NO dimension annotations show horizontal clearances from buildings to the outside conductor of overhead lines. NO surveyed conductor elevations are shown on any drawings.
findings.reasoning: While buildings are set back approximately 26+ feet from the property line, the requirement is to maintain a 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of overhead electric conductors. Without surveyed conductor elevation data, clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to building faces, and no building elevation drawings showing the vertical relationship, it is impossible to verify that the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained. The code requires clearance measured from the outside conductor (which may be offset several feet from the pole center on multi-conductor installations), not from the pole or property line. Applicant has acknowledged responsibility for maintaining clearances (Sheet 3, Block 8), but has not provided the necessary documentation to demonstrate compliance.

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets or dimension callouts showing 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor to Buildings 7 and 8. Provide registered surveyor elevation data and clearance dimension annotations.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 on southern boundary adjacent to OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) routing along and crossing the site. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows this OHE line running along the southern boundary of the property. Buildings 7 and 8 are positioned closest to this southern boundary. However, no clearance dimension lines or annotations are provided on either the site plan or any building elevation sheets showing the horizontal distance from the buildings' exterior walls or projections to the OHE conductor. No profile/section views are provided showing vertical clearances. The plans do not identify whether the OHE line is a primary, secondary, or neutral conductor, nor is there a surveyed elevation of the conductor provided. No dimension callouts originate from the conductor location itself—the critical measurement baseline required by code.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric conductors. This measurement must be from the outside conductor, not from the pole. The applicant has not provided evidence that this clearance is maintained. Without (1) building elevation sheets showing surveyed conductor elevations, (2) dimension annotations from the outside conductor to the building face, or (3) a registered surveyor's proximity survey per UCM § 1.10.3, the reviewer cannot determine whether the requirement is met. The conservative approach is to flag this as unclear pending submittal of required elevation documentation and proximity survey data.

findings.comment: Proposed buildings do not show measured clearance dimensions from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. All buildings with potential clearance concerns require clearance dimension annotations on site plan and building elevation sheets, measured from the outside (outermost) conductor, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Buildings and permanent structures throughout the site
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly shows overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) running along Valley View Road (western boundary) and the northern property boundary, with utility poles marked. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows eight multi-story residential buildings (ranging from 33'-5" to 36'-1" in height) positioned on the site. The overhead electric utility line is labeled '----OHE----' on the site plan running along the Valley View Road frontage (southern boundary). However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on Sheet 9 showing the horizontal distance from the outside conductor of the overhead line to any building face or structure. No building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions were found in the submitted plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, and secondary conductors. The regulation defines this as a vertical plane extending infinitely upward from a point 7.5 feet from the conductor. The site plan shows buildings within reasonable proximity to the overhead lines along Valley View Road, but the applicant has provided no dimensional evidence that the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal clearance is maintained. The absence of clearance annotations and dimensions constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance. Per the grouping documentation, clearance dimensions must be labeled on plans with dimension lines originating from the actual outside conductor location (not pole centerline).

findings.comment: Building elevation sheets prepared by the architect/engineer are required, showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations with clearance dimension annotations from the conductor to building faces, roofs, parapets, and all projections, for all buildings within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: All buildings proposed within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: The 39-sheet site plan set does not include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 9 shows building footprints and FFEs but is a plan view only. The README index lists sheets 1-39 with the following titles: Sheets 1-11 are general plans; Sheets 12-20 are utility and drainage plans; Sheets 21-39 are details and landscape plans. NO sheets titled 'Building Elevations,' 'Building Elevation Sheets,' or similar are listed. Consequently, surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are not present on any elevation sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors to be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The absence of building elevation sheets constitutes a failure to provide the required documentation. The code requirement is specific: 'Surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors not included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met' is identified as a deficiency.

findings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are missing. Provide building elevation drawings showing surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions to all building faces and projections.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 adjacent to southern OHE line; entire site with overhead facilities
findings.observation: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet site plan set. The README index lists sheets 1-39 as site/civil engineering and landscape drawings, with no architectural elevation sheets shown. Existing overhead electric lines are depicted on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) and Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan), but no surveyed conductor elevation data is provided on any sheet. No registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements are documented. The electrical survey required by Austin Energy Design per UCM § 1.10.3 does not appear to have been submitted.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires that surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The applicant has not submitted any building elevation sheets. This is a mandatory documentation requirement for any site with buildings within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities. The absence of this required documentation constitutes a deficiency regardless of actual clearances that might exist on the ground.

findings.comment: Building elevation sheets do not show surveyed elevations of existing overhead electric conductors. Sealed building elevation exhibits are required for all buildings with potential proximity to overhead lines, showing the surveyed elevation of the outside conductor and dimensioned clearances from the conductor to building faces and projections.
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents existing overhead utility lines running along the property boundary and service drop. The proposed buildings range from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1" in height. A complete set of building elevation sheets showing the surveyed elevation of the existing overhead conductors is not present in the submitted site plan set. While general notes on Sheet 3 reference benchmarks (B.M. #1 at 678.52' and B.M. #2 at 681.08' NAVD 88), these are general site control points, not surveyed overhead conductor elevations. No building elevation exhibits were found that show the actual conductor elevation overlaid with the building profile to verify vertical clearances.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Documentation Requirements section, 'Profile plans: Engineered, sealed profile drawings showing vertical relationships between overhead conductors and building features, including overhangs, balconies, and canopies, with dimensioned clearances' are required. The grouping cites UCM § 1.10.3 as requiring permanent clearances and explicitly states that clearance verification requires 'surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors included on building elevation sheets.' Without surveyed conductor elevation data on building elevation sheets, the applicant cannot demonstrate that the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance or other required clearances are met.

findings.comment: Provide section view exhibits (with title callouts such as Section A-A, B-B) on site plan or separate detail sheets showing dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of each building and all building projections, clearly labeling clearances in feet and inches.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 and retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings in plan view only with no section line callouts (A-A, B-B, etc.) that would reference section views showing clearances. Sheet 22 shows standard construction details for curbs, sidewalks, and driveways but contains no section views specifically showing clearances from outer electric conductor to building edges. Sheets 38-39 show wall construction details and sections but not clearance dimensions from overhead conductors to wall faces. Examined sheets do not include section or plan view exhibits with dimension lines originating at the outer electric conductor and extending to building edges or wall faces.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'Section and plan view exhibits [that] show dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of buildings and building projections for clearance verification.' This is a specific documentation requirement. The absence of any section views with dimension lines from the outer conductor to building edges or wall faces constitutes non-compliance. The requirement applies when buildings or structures are proposed within potential clearance distance, which is the case here.

findings.comment: No section/profile exhibits provided showing clearance dimensions from outer conductor to buildings and site features. Provide detailed section and plan views with dimension callouts from outside conductor to building edges and site improvements.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking areas; all structures within clearance distance of OHE line
findings.observation: No section or profile view exhibits are provided showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and site improvements. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows the OHE line and buildings in plan view only, without any profile views. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows contours and building FFEs but does not show overhead conductor elevation or clearance dimensions. No enlarged plan details with cross-section views have been submitted showing the relationship between conductors and building edges, parking surfaces, or driveways.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires dimension lines from the outer conductor to outermost building edges in plan and section views to verify clearance compliance. These dimension annotations are mandatory and must originate from the actual conductor location, not from the pole. The complete absence of section and profile exhibits with clearance dimensions is a deficiency. The applicant must provide these required exhibits.

findings.comment: Section and plan view exhibits do not show dimensions from the outside electric conductor to the outermost edges of proposed buildings, building projections, and other site features. Enlarged plan details and section views are required showing dimension lines originating from the outside conductor and extending to all building faces and structures within potential clearance distance, demonstrating compliance with the 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance requirement.
applicableAreas: Site plan sections and elevation views
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly identifies overhead utility lines with the notation 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road and the northern property boundary. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) both show overhead electric lines (labeled 'OHE' or '----OHE----') but NO dimension lines or clearance annotations extending from the outside conductor to the outer edges of any buildings, projections, site features, or structures. No section views or profile exhibits were found showing the cross-section relationship between the overhead conductor and site features. The landscape plan shows trees proposed near the OHE line but with no distance callouts or species specifications.
findings.reasoning: The grouping explicitly states: 'Common Violation Patterns: Clearances measured from pole instead of conductor... Dimension annotations read "10'-0" from pole" instead of "15'-0" from outside conductor"' and 'Missing profile plans: Site plan shows building and overhead lines in plan view only, no elevation/section view; no surveyed mid-span clearance data; cannot verify vertical clearances meet requirements.' UCM § 1.10.3 requires permanent clearances, which must be demonstrated through dimension callouts showing measurement from the outside (outermost) conductor to the building edge. The complete absence of these dimensions constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: Provide grading profile sections for proposed driveways showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations at the low point and dimension annotations verifying minimum 16-foot or 18-foot vertical clearance (depending on truck traffic designation) from the lowest point of all overhead conductors and attached equipment to the finished driveway surface.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveways crossing or passing under or adjacent to overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows driveways marked 'Construct Type II Driveway' and 'Construct Type III Driveway' on the western and internal portions of the site. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows existing and proposed contours with driveway grades and spot elevations, but contains NO profile sections showing the vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attached telecommunications lines) to the driveway surface. Sheet 22 shows standard driveway construction details (thickness, reinforcement, grades) but NO sections showing vertical clearance to overhead lines. The FFE elevations of buildings are provided (ranging from 683' to 687.5' NAVD 88), but overhead conductor elevations are not given.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires driveways to maintain minimum 16-foot vertical clearance (for parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot vertical clearance (for areas with truck traffic) from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments. This requires (1) surveyed conductor height data, (2) profile or section views showing clearance calculations, and (3) mid-span clearance verification if the clearance appears marginal. None of these are provided. Applicant has not verified mid-span clearances with registered surveyor data, and no vertical clearance dimensions are shown on grading or profile sheets.

findings.comment: No documented vertical clearance from finished driveway grades to overhead electric line. Provide grading plan section views with finished elevations at OHE line crossing and surveyed conductor height; specify truck traffic classification.
applicableAreas: Internal driveways and parking areas on southern portion of site where OHE line is routed
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows finished floor elevations and site contours but does not provide finished driveway grade elevations at specific locations relative to the OHE line shown on Sheet 9. No section views are provided showing the vertical relationship between the lowest point of the overhead electric line and the finished grade of parking/drive areas. Truck traffic classification (which determines 16-foot vs. 18-foot clearance requirement) is not specified on the plans. No mid-span clearance measurements from a registered surveyor are provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance for parking without truck traffic, or 18-foot with truck traffic, from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities (including service drops and telecommunications attachments). Without (1) documented finished grade elevations at driveway locations, (2) surveyed overhead line heights, and (3) specification of truck traffic usage, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant must provide site/utility profile views with documented vertical clearances.

findings.comment: The proposed driveway crosses the existing overhead electric line at Valley View Road. No section views, surveyed mid-span clearance measurements, or vertical clearance dimension annotations are provided to demonstrate the minimum 16-foot (or 18-foot for truck traffic areas) vertical clearance from the lowest point of the overhead line to the finished driveway grade. A registered surveyor's survey showing mid-span clearance is required, with results documented on section views and profile sheets.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveway intersection with overhead utility line at Valley View Road frontage
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows an overhead utility line labeled 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road (western boundary). The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows a proposed driveway at the bottom left (Valley View Road frontage) area. Per the vision analysis of Sheet 9, the proposed driveway 'crosses directly under the horizontal ----OHE---- line' along Valley View Road. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows the finished floor elevations and site grades but does not annotate the vertical clearance dimensions at the driveway location where the overhead line crosses. No registered surveyor data showing mid-span clearance measurements is provided. The roadway grade elevations are not dimensioned relative to the overhead line height.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 specifies: 'Driveway and parking without truck traffic: 16 feet minimum vertical clearance; Roads, streets, alleys, and areas with truck traffic: 18 feet minimum vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments.' The grouping documentation notes this is a 'Common Violation Pattern: Inadequate service-drop clearances: Driveway grade shown within 15-16 feet of overhead service drop without mid-span clearance verification; service drop sag at maximum load/temperature may contact vehicles.' Since the proposed driveway crosses under the overhead line, vertical clearance must be verified through surveyed mid-span clearance data showing the lowest point of the conductor at maximum sag. The absence of this documentation constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance.

findings.comment: All clearance annotations must be revised to show dimension lines originating at the surveyed outside conductor location (not pole center), with clear identification of which conductor is being measured from, and dimension values showing clearances in feet and inches from the conductor to site features.
applicableAreas: All proposed site features and infrastructure
findings.observation: Complete review of Sheets 9 (Site Plan), 11 (Grading Plan), and 21 (Electrical Plan) reveals NO dimension annotations showing clearances from buildings, structures, driveways, walls, or other site features to overhead electric lines. The only distances shown are from property lines and internal site features to each other. Sheet 4 shows the existing utility poles with symbols but no dimension annotations from the poles. No dimension lines on any sheet are shown extending from an identified 'outside conductor' location to site features. Applicant has not labeled the location of outside conductors or the measurement reference point for any clearance annotations.
findings.reasoning: All clearance dimensions (or lack thereof) must be measured from the outside conductor, not from pole center or pole structure. No clearance dimensions are provided on the plans at all, and no plans identify the location of the outside conductor for measurement purposes.

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on site plans, measured from outside conductor as required. All clearance dimensions must originate from the actual conductor location, with notation showing measurement source.
applicableAreas: All locations with clearance dimensions shown on overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows the OHE line on the southern boundary of the site but includes NO dimension callouts or clearance annotations of any kind. Wherever clearance dimensions should appear (from conductor to buildings, parking, driveways), none are provided. The few dimension lines visible on Sheet 9 relate to building setbacks and site distances, not to overhead line clearances. The critical requirement to show dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location (not pole centerline) is therefore not met—because no dimensions are shown at all.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires clearance dimensions to be measured from the outside conductor, never from the utility pole centerline. On multi-conductor installations, the conductor may be several feet offset from pole center, creating significant measurement errors if pole-based dimensions are used. The applicant has not provided any clearance dimensions from any overhead electric infrastructure. This is a foundational deficiency—without dimension callouts originating from the conductor, the plans cannot communicate or verify clearance compliance.

findings.comment: Clearance dimensions are not shown on any plan sheets. When clearance dimensions are eventually provided, they must originate from the outside (outermost) conductor, not from the utility pole centerline. Dimension lines should clearly identify the conductor location and show measurement to the building edge or feature being evaluated.
applicableAreas: All clearance dimension annotations on site plan
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows multiple utility poles and overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) on the property. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows the overhead electric line (OHE) running along the Valley View Road frontage. However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on the plans. The grouping documentation emphasizes that 'All clearances must be measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), never from the utility pole centerline or pole structure' and warns that 'Measuring from pole centerline instead of the conductor results in understated clearances and code violations.' Since no dimensions are shown on the plans at all, there is no evidence that the applicant is measuring from the outside conductor versus the pole.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Measurement Methodology section: 'Profile plans must show dimension lines originating at the conductor location, not at the pole. [This is critical.]' The complete absence of clearance dimensions means there is no opportunity to verify that dimensions originate from the conductor rather than the pole. This is a fundamental documentation failure that prevents verification of compliance. Without at least one dimension showing the measurement methodology and origin point (outside conductor), compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Landscape plan must identify all trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors and 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors, verify that species match ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list ('UC'-designated trees with mature height ≤20 feet), and include note requiring property owner responsibility for ongoing tree pruning/removal within 10 feet of centerline of overhead electric facilities per Austin Energy standard practice and Block 8 requirements.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings on landscape plan, particularly within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan, guide.md) explicitly states: 'Block 2: drawing — Main Landscape and Site Plan. A comprehensive site plan illustrating building footprints, parking layouts, sidewalks, utility lines (Water, Storm Drain, Overhead Electric), topographical contours, and the distribution of landscape elements.' This confirms overhead electric lines are shown on the landscape plan. The sheet index shows Sheets 30-35, 37 address trees and landscaping. However, NO dimension annotations or notes on the landscape plan specify which species are planted within 10 feet of distribution or 50 feet of transmission conductors, and no reference is made to ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list ('UC'-designated species). Without specific callouts showing tree locations relative to overhead conductors and without verification of species against the UC list, compliance cannot be confirmed. Trees exceeding the utility-compatible size/species may be planted in violation of clearance and future maintenance conflicts with the electric utility.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies a 50-lateral-foot clearance requirement for trees near transmission lines (more restrictive than the 30-40 feet mentioned in ECM § 2.4.1.D/2.4.2.C). Trees within these clearance zones must be from the Utility Compatible list (ECM Appendix F, marked 'UC', generally mature height ≤20 feet). The landscape plan shows tree plantings and site grading but provides NO verification that trees within 10 feet of distribution or 50 feet of transmission conductors are utility-compatible species. Additionally, Sheet 3, Block 8 requires that 'owner shall be responsible for any initial tree pruning and tree removal that is within ten feet of the center line of the proposed overhead electric facilities.' This suggests applicant acknowledges trees are a concern, but the landscape plan does not address compatibility.

findings.comment: Mitigation trees shown on landscape plan adjacent to overhead electric line lack species identification and utility-compatible designation. Identify all mitigation tree species and confirm UC (Utility Compatible) status per ECM Appendix F, or relocate trees to maintain 10-foot minimum lateral clearance from outside conductor.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary landscaping area with overhead electric line; mitigation tree plantings
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) running along the southern boundary. Multiple mitigation trees (labeled 'M' on the plan) are positioned directly along this southern boundary, within or immediately adjacent to (less than 10 feet lateral distance from) the overhead line. Sheet 32 (Tree List) identifies the surveyed existing trees with species and Appendix F designation (Y/N/I), but does NOT specify the species of the proposed MITIGATION trees shown as 'M' symbols on Sheet 31. No legend or note on Sheet 31 provides species names for the mitigation plantings. No reference to ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible trees (UC designation) appears in the landscape legend. No clearance distance annotations or notes document the required 10-foot lateral separation or specify that utility-compatible species are being used.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees proposed within 50 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors to be from the Utility Compatible tree list in ECM Appendix F (generally species with mature height ≤20 feet marked 'UC'). The applicant's landscape plan shows mitigation trees under the overhead line but does not identify the species. Without species identification, the reviewer cannot verify that utility-compatible trees are being used. The vegetation plan is deficient. The applicant must identify all mitigation tree species and confirm they meet the UC requirements, OR relocate trees to comply with the 10-foot minimum lateral separation for non-utility-compatible species.

findings.comment: The landscape plan shows trees proposed near overhead electric distribution lines but does not identify the botanical species for trees in proximity to the OHE line or provide distance annotations showing lateral clearances. Landscape plan must be revised to: (1) call out the specific tree species being planted in areas near the overhead line (refer to tree species list on Sheet 35), (2) show lateral distance dimensions from proposed trees to the outside conductor, (3) confirm that any trees within 10 feet of the overhead distribution conductor are from the Utility Compatible trees list per ECM Appendix F, or (4) demonstrate all proposed trees are planted beyond the 10-foot clearance zone.
applicableAreas: Landscape plantings near overhead distribution conductors at Valley View Road frontage and site perimeter
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) depicts the overhead electric (OHE) utility line running along the southern/Valley View Road boundary. The vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms that 'There are several proposed trees located along the bottom boundary line, in close proximity to the -OHE- line' and notes that trees are marked with functional type codes (M for mitigation tree, PL for parking lot tree, P for parking buffer point tree). However, 'Specific botanical species are not labeled on this sheet' and 'There are no specific dimensions or distance callouts explicitly stating the distance from these trees to the overhead electric line.' The landscape calculations sheet (Sheet 35) shows proposed plantings: Cedar Elm (10 trees), Live Oak (2 trees), Mexican Redbud (6 trees), Texas Mountain Laurel (2 trees), and various shrubs and groundcover. However, there is no cross-reference between the species list and the landscape plan to identify which species are being planted near the overhead lines, nor is there any notation confirming these species are Utility Compatible (UC) per ECM Appendix F.
findings.reasoning: The grouping states: 'Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors are from Utility Compatible Shade Trees list' and 'ECM Appendix F "UC" column (utility-compatible trees generally mature height ≤20 feet marked "UC").' The grouping further notes: 'Common Violation Pattern: Non-utility-compatible trees beneath lines: Landscape plan shows large trees beneath or within 10 feet of overhead lines; species not from Utility Compatible list in ECM Appendix F.' The landscape plan fails to: (1) identify which specific proposed tree species are located within 10 feet of the overhead distribution line, (2) provide distance callouts showing lateral distance from proposed trees to the conductor, and (3) confirm that any trees within 10 feet are marked as Utility Compatible in ECM Appendix F. Without this information, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Add note to cover sheet (Sheet 1) or general notes (Sheet 3) stating: 'Owner and contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work, excavation, or construction activities within or adjacent to areas containing overhead electric facilities and lines. Notification is required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, and UCM § 1.10.2. Contact information: [Austin Energy contact details]. Failure to notify may result in serious injury, fatality, or project delays.'
applicableAreas: Cover sheet and general notes for entire project
findings.observation: Comprehensive review of Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) reveals the following: Sheet 1 contains project title, location map, fire department requirements, environmental notes, various compliance statements, but NO note requiring 48-hour notification to Austin Energy before work begins near overhead lines. Sheet 3, Block 20 includes 'Electric Transmission Notes' (16 items) which specifically require (Item 3): 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction... OSHA requires a 20' clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' This note applies specifically to TRANSMISSION facilities and includes a 48-hour requirement for a SAFETY MEETING. However, Sheet 3, Blocks 8/14 ('Electric Notes') address general distribution lines but contain NO requirement for 48-hour notification before construction work begins near distribution overhead lines. Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, requires notification to utilities before work on high-voltage lines, and UCM § 1.10.2 incorporates this requirement. The plans do not include this general notification requirement for distribution lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 explicitly requires a plan note: 'Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' While Sheet 3, Block 20 requires a 48-hour pre-construction safety MEETING for transmission lines specifically, there is NO corresponding note for general construction notification before work begins near distribution overhead lines. This is a regulatory and safety requirement distinct from the transmission-specific safety meeting. The note is required to be on the cover sheet or in the general notes to inform owner, contractor, and City of the notification requirement.

findings.comment: Specific 48-hour notification note required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 is not clearly called out on cover sheet or plans. Add conspicuous note: 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work near overhead electric lines. Contact [Austin Energy contact information].'
findings.observation: Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) have been reviewed. Block 14 of Sheet 3 contains Austin Energy requirements addressing maintenance of clearances per NESC and OSHA but is phrased as developer responsibility language. The specific requirement per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 for owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines is not clearly called out as a discrete note on the cover sheet or title block. Blocks 14 and 20 of Sheet 3 reference general clearance responsibilities but the explicit 48-hour notification notice with contact information is not visibly highlighted or separated as a specific callout.
findings.reasoning: Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 Section 752.003 requires notification to Austin Energy 48 hours before work near overhead electric lines. This requirement must be conspicuously noted on site plans. While general Austin Energy notes are present on Sheet 3, the specific 48-hour notification requirement is not clearly set out as a distinct, stand-alone note with notification procedures. Best practice is to include this as a separate, highlighted note on the cover sheet with contact information for Austin Energy notification.

findings.comment: Plans do not include required note stating that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. Add this requirement to the cover sheet general notes or site plan release notes in a location where all contractors and the owner will see it during project execution.
applicableAreas: General notes on cover sheet or site plan sheets
findings.observation: The cover sheet (Sheet 1) and general notes sheet (Sheet 3) were reviewed in detail. Sheet 1 contains standard project information, Fire Department requirements, and administrative notes, but no mention of a 48-hour notification requirement to Austin Energy. Sheet 3 contains comprehensive notes about utilities, construction sequence, benchmarks, fire department requirements, and electric transmission clearances, but no explicit note requiring the owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy 48 hours before work near high-voltage overhead lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) similarly contains site plan release notes but no mention of the 48-hour notification requirement. While Sheet 9's release notes (Block 7) reference general utility relocation responsibility (Item 4: 'The owner is responsible for all costs of relocation of, or damage to, utilities' and Item 5: 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date'), there is no specific note stating that 'owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' as required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
findings.reasoning: The grouping's Documentation Requirements section explicitly states: '48-hour notification plan note: Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' The grouping further lists under Common Violation Patterns: 'Missing 48-hour notification note: Site has overhead lines and construction staging area adjacent, but no plan notes addressing notification requirement.' Since overhead electric facilities clearly exist on and adjacent to this site, and construction is planned adjacent to these lines, the required notification note must be prominently displayed on the plans.

findings.comment: Electrical conduit branch lines route directly to electrical meters mounted on the exterior walls of all 8 buildings. No dimensional callouts on the electrical plan verify that the required 5-foot horizontal clearance from building foundations to underground electric facilities is maintained at meter connection locations. Provide detailed electrical design or utility coordination drawings showing the routing of electrical branch lines and confirming minimum 5-foot clearance from building foundations, or provide documentation of an approved variance/coordination with Austin Energy if reduced clearances have been authorized.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters mounted on the exterior walls of all 8 buildings (Buildings 1-8). Branch conduit lines must route from the main underground electrical trunk lines to these wall-mounted meters. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that electrical routing approaches and connects directly to these meters on the building exteriors, with the branch lines definitely entering the area within 5 feet of building foundations at all meter connection locations. No dimensional callouts on the electrical plan verify that the 5-foot horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to building foundations is maintained at any of these meter connection points.
findings.reasoning: Building foundations must maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (duct banks, conduit, pull boxes) per UCM § 1.10.5.B. The electrical meters mounted directly on the exterior walls at each building require electrical service lines to run to those wall locations. The vision tool analysis explicitly noted that electrical routing enters the <5-foot zone at all eight meter connection locations. Without explicit dimensional documentation on the plans showing the 5-foot clearance is maintained, and given the physical requirement for conduit to reach wall-mounted meters, the minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified as met.

findings.comment: All eight building foundations have underground electric conduit routing within 5 feet (typically within 0 to 2 feet) of building walls to serve wall-mounted electrical meters. findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan, scale 1" = 20') reveals that electrical meters are mounted directly on the building foundation walls for all eight buildings. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires a minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (duct banks, conduit, pull boxes, manholes) to customer buildings and foundations. The site plan clearly shows electrical meters mounted directly on building walls with underground conduit routed immediately adjacent to building foundations. This is a direct violation of the minimum 5-foot clearance requirement. The presence of wall-mounted meters inherently requires conduit to enter the building within the 5-foot zone. This is not a design that coordinates with the clearance requirement—it fundamentally violates it.

No vertical clearance dimension, arc, or note documents the separation at this crossing. The applicant has failed to demonstrate compliance with the vertical clearance requirement. This is a clear deficiency: required information (vertical clearance dimensions at the water-electric crossing) is absent from the plans, and missing elements are deficiencies per the evaluation standards.

findings.comment: Transmission facility presence and location unclear. findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 contains 16 detailed notes referencing transmission structures, transmission easements, and requiring 25-foot no-dig/grade zones and Austin Energy coordination. findings.reasoning: Block 20 explicitly requires coordination with Austin Energy before grading within 25 feet of transmission structures and notes that grading near transmission must be coordinated with Andrew Perez (512-505-7153). The code citation UCM § 1.14.5.2 requires excavations deeper than 1 foot within 25 feet of transmission foundations to receive Austin Energy evaluation and approval. However, the plans do not clearly identify any transmission structures, their locations, or the boundaries of any transmission easement. The presence of detailed transmission notes combined with absence of transmission infrastructure depiction creates ambiguity about whether transmission facilities exist on or immediately adjacent to the property. Without confirmation of transmission structure presence and location, the applicability of this requirement cannot be determined, nor can compliance be verified. The plans must clearly establish: (1) whether transmission infrastructure exists on or within 25 feet of the property, (2) the specific locations of any transmission structures or guy anchors, and (3) the spatial relationship between grading areas and these structures.
