findings.comment: Electric easements not designated as aerial or non-aerial. Specify each easement as 'Aerial Electric Easement' (for overhead poles, conductors, guys) or 'Non-Aerial Electric Easement' (for underground conduit, pad-mounted equipment) to establish correct clearance and access requirements per UCM § 1.10.3 (aerial) and § 1.10.4 (non-aerial).
findings.observation: Sheets 2, 9, and 21 show five foot electric easements labeled generically as '5' Elec. Ease.' or '5' Electric Easement' without designation as aerial (for overhead facilities) or non-aerial (for underground facilities). Vision analysis found: two 5' electric easements on the plat; two 5' electric easements on Sheet 9; easement references on Sheet 21. No easement label specifies whether it accommodates overhead distribution lines/poles/guy wires (aerial) or underground conduit/pad-mounted equipment (non-aerial), despite the fact that Sheet 21 shows both overhead line on west boundary and underground infrastructure throughout site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that easements be clearly designated as to their function. Aerial easements must provide vertical clearance and lateral space for poles, conductors, and guy anchors; non-aerial easements must provide subsurface space for conduit and equipment pads with horizontal clearances. Without explicit designation, it is unclear whether shown easement dimensions are adequate for the type of infrastructure occupying them, and whether access, height, and clearance requirements are satisfied.

findings.comment: Plans do not distinguish between aerial and underground electric easements. Please designate each electric easement as either 'Aerial Electric Easement' (for overhead facilities: poles, conductors, guys, with required vertical clearances) or 'Underground Electric Easement' (for subsurface facilities: conduit, pad-mounted equipment) on all plan sheets showing easements.
findings.observation: Examined electric easement labels on Sheets 9, 11, 21. The 5' electric easements are labeled as '5' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76' or '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883' but have NO designation indicating whether they accommodate aerial (overhead) or non-aerial (underground) facilities. Sheet 21 shows existing overhead lines (OHE) and existing underground lines but the easements are not explicitly designated as 'Aerial' or 'Underground.' Per UCM § 1.10.0, aerial easements require vertical clearance maintenance (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radius); underground easements require subsurface clearance from other utilities. The failure to distinguish prevents verification of correct easement type.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires plans to 'distinguish between aerial electric easements and underground electric easements.' This is not a formatting preference but a regulatory requirement because aerial and underground easements have different clearance, maintenance, and access requirements per UCM §§ 1.10.3 and 1.10.4. Aerial easements accommodate poles, overhead conductors, guys, and require tree-free zones and vertical clearances. Underground easements accommodate conduit, pad-mounted equipment, and require different horizontal clearances. Without designation, it is unclear what uses are permitted within each easement, and AE staff cannot verify the design accommodates the correct infrastructure.

findings.comment: Electrical easements not distinguished as aerial vs. underground. Label all electrical easements to specify whether they accommodate aerial facilities (overhead poles, conductors, guy wires) or underground facilities (conduits, pad-mounted equipment, buried laterals), and ensure clearance requirements are applied appropriately to each type.
applicableAreas: Plans showing electrical easements - Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Plat (Sheet 2), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 2 (Plat) vision analysis: Easements are shown with width dimensions (5' P.U.E., 5' Elec. & Tel. Easement, 5' Elec. Easement) but the vision analysis explicitly states: 'No. The labels on the plat do not contain the words "aerial," "overhead," or "underground."' The lines running through or near some of these easements are labeled "OHE" (Overhead Electric), implying aerial use in those specific areas, but the easement labels themselves do not make this distinction.' Sheet 9 vision analysis notes: '5' Electric Easement is labeled along the right (eastern) property boundary' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement labeled near the bottom right' but no distinction of type. Both aerial (overhead conductors, poles, service drops, guy wires) and underground (conduit, pad-mounted transformers) electric infrastructure exist on this site. The regulatory overview explicitly distinguishes these: 'Aerial electric easements accommodate overhead facilities... with vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirements; non-aerial easements accommodate underground facilities... with horizontal and subsurface clearance requirements.' Without this distinction labeled on easements, plan reviewers cannot verify that clearances and access are adequate for the actual facility type using each easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires plans to show 'All public and private easements (electrical, gas, water, sewer, telecommunications, drainage) with locations and extents clearly delineated.' The grouping's Code References section (lines 72-90) identifies UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.4 as establishing different clearance requirements for aerial vs. non-aerial easements. The Regulatory Overview specifically states: 'Plans must distinguish between: Aerial vs. Non-Aerial Easements: Aerial electric easements accommodate overhead facilities (poles, overhead conductors, service drops, guy wires) with vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirements (7.5 ft horizontal, 15-ft radius); non-aerial easements accommodate underground facilities (conduit, pad-mounted transformers, underground laterals).' Without this distinction labeled on the plans themselves, it is impossible to verify that clearances meet requirements for the type of facility in each easement. Both overhead and underground facilities are shown on this site (OHE lines on Sheet 21, underground conduits on Sheet 21), confirming that both easement types exist.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 2 (Plat), 3 (General Notes), 9 (Site Plan), 19 (Utility Tap Plan), and 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan). Without examining landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, and elevation sheets, cannot confirm whether electric infrastructure is consistently shown across the full plan set and properly coordinated to prevent conflicts.

findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires plans to show electric infrastructure, and the grouping's common violation patterns specifically identify: 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical (especially down guy anchors conflicting with accessible paths, trees conflicting with clearance envelopes).' The principle is that all infrastructure must be consistently shown on all sheets where coordination is necessary. The Regulatory Overview states (line 54): 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical.' findings.comment: Projected electrical load not shown on plans. Calculate and show the total electrical load for the project (in kW or kVA) and identify the load for each building or service point, based on building size, occupancy classification, and code-required minimum loads.

The Regulatory Overview (lines 32-33) states that the plan documentation must show 'Approximate location and space for electric facilities, desired service point, projected load shown' as item #8 in the comprehensive baseline for applications. findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits are not provided, not engineered and sealed, or not included in the permitted plan set. No exhibits demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors (measured from outer conductor per AEDC § 1.10.3) are visible on the submitted site plan. Please provide engineered and sealed clearance verification exhibits showing both required clearance envelopes around all proposed structures and existing electric facilities.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan). Both sheets show existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along southern property boundary near street. Sheet 21 shows proposed transformer pad and underground electric lines. However, NO clearance verification exhibits were found. The sheets show facility locations but do NOT include engineered exhibits demonstrating compliance with AEDC § 1.10.3 clearance standards. Neither sheet shows calculated clearance zones, clearance dimensions measured from outer conductors, or exhibits demonstrating that the dual clearance envelope requirements (7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance) are satisfied. No profile or cross-section views with clearance dimensions are provided.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(2) and § 1.10.3 require clearance verification exhibits when proposed structures are located within required clearance zones of existing electric facilities. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes that BOTH clearance envelopes must be satisfied simultaneously and that clearances must be measured from the outer conductor, not pole centerline. Without engineered exhibits demonstrating these calculations, the applicant has not provided evidence of compliance. The burden of proof is on the applicant to demonstrate code compliance through specific exhibits; showing facility locations alone is insufficient.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits not provided. Plans must include engineered and sealed exhibits demonstrating both 7'-6" minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors (measured from outer conductor, not pole centerline). Exhibits must be drawn to scale and included in permitted plan set.
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 21, and 3 for clearance verification exhibits. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical infrastructure layout with transformers, pull boxes, and underground lines, but no clearance verification exhibits are present. No engineered drawings demonstrating both 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius clearance envelopes from conductors are provided. Master Comment Report Section 02 identifies Austin Energy Design Requirements including UCM § 1.10.3 (Permanent Clearances from AE Overhead Lines) as applicable, confirming clearance compliance must be demonstrated.
findings.reasoning: The grouping specifies clearance exhibits must demonstrate code compliance showing both 7'-6" horizontal AND 15-foot radius clearance envelopes. The vision analysis confirmed no such exhibits are present. The requirement applies because proposed structures are located in areas potentially affecting existing utility easements and overhead electric lines. Austin Energy's Master Comment Report lists clearance standards as preliminary design requirements, making exhibits mandatory for land development review approval.

findings.comment: No clearance verification exhibits provided demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance requirements from overhead distribution conductors as required by AEDC § 1.10.3. Engineered and sealed clearance exhibits must be included in the permitted plan set.
applicableAreas: Site-wide clearance zones around existing electric facilities
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to determine if clearance verification exhibits are provided. Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines, transformers, pull boxes, and meters with building footprints and FFEs labeled. Sheet 9 shows electric facility locations with property lines and easement boundaries. No dedicated clearance verification exhibits found on any sheet examined. No sheet displays both required clearance envelopes: the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from 7.5 feet horizontal distance from conductors, AND the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending infinitely downward from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No engineered and sealed clearance exhibit sheets appear in the 39-sheet plan set.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires clearance verification exhibits to be 'engineered and scaled' and 'included in the permitted plan set' when proposed structures are located within required clearance zones. AEDC § 1.16.0(2) mandates this documentation. While the electrical design plan shows proposed structures and electric facility locations, it does not provide a dedicated exhibit demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal AND 15-foot radius clearance requirements. The absence of clearance verification exhibits means the applicant cannot demonstrate code compliance with these dual clearance envelopes, which the grouping Regulatory Overview specifies must BOTH be satisfied simultaneously—satisfying one does not satisfy the other.

findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings are not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities/easements. Please provide engineered profile drawings showing all building elements with dimensions and clearances measured to the outer conductors of overhead electric lines.
applicableAreas: All areas where proposed structures may be within clearance zones of existing electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is a plan-view drawing only. No profile drawings, cross-section drawings, or elevation views showing vertical clearances have been found. While Sheet 21 shows basic building footprints with Finished Floor Elevations (FFE) for each building, no details show building element dimensions such as overhangs, balconies, awnings, or canopies with their heights and horizontal extents relative to existing or proposed electric facilities. The grouping regulatory overview explicitly states that 'Profile plans must be engineered, sealed, and drawn to scale showing all building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) with dimensioned clearances.' The applicant has not provided these critical documents, making it impossible to verify clearance compliance in the vertical plane.

findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities. Submit building elevations and profile drawings showing dimensioned clearances measured from outer conductors for all building elements that could encroach on clearance zones.
findings.observation: Searched document set for building elevations, profile drawings, and cross-section exhibits showing clearances. No building elevation sheets exist in the primary site plan (39 sheets total). Sheet 9 shows building footprints and heights in tables (ranging from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1"), but no elevations depicting building elements. Building elevations or profile drawings are required to show clearances but are completely absent. Without these drawings, clearances cannot be verified as required by AEDC § 1.10.3.

findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities. Engineered profiles drawn to scale and sealed must show vertical clearances and building element dimensions.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for profile/cross-section drawings showing clearances. Found only plan view with building footprints and FFEs; no profiles shown on this sheet. Examined Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) which contains detailed water utility profiles at 1"=20' horizontal and 1"=2' vertical scale. However, these profiles show ONLY water utility lines and do not include electric utility lines or building elements (walls, overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) needed to verify clearances from existing electric facilities. No building elevation sheets provided in the plan set that would show heights and element dimensions of proposed structures. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed: 'Building heights are NOT shown on this plan view. There are no explicitly delineated or labeled building overhangs, balconies, or canopies that might affect vertical clearances.'
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 and the grouping 'Documents to Review' section specifically require 'Profile Drawings / Cross-section Exhibits' showing 'clearances between proposed structures and existing electric facilities/easements' with 'all building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies)' and 'dimensioned clearances.' While utility profiles exist on Sheet 20, they do not include electric utilities or building elements. The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows only plan view without profiles or building element details. This deficiency prevents verification of compliance with the 7'-6" minimum clearance requirement measured from outer conductors as specified in the measurement methodology.

findings.comment: Clearance dimensions and heights are not specified for building elements, or clearances are measured from pole centerline instead of outer conductor. Please provide dimensioned clearance details on profile drawings showing measurement points from the outer conductor of the overhead electric line, with dimensions to all building elements (overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies).
applicableAreas: All areas with proposed structures within clearance zones of electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows building footprints with FFE (Finished Floor Elevations) but no detailed dimensions for building elements (overhangs, balconies, awnings). The sheet shows generic labels for 'Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', and 'Electrical Meters' but these labels lack any dimensional information. No callouts or dimension lines show clearances measured from outer conductors. The existing overhead electric line (OHE) location is noted but with no specific conductor height or clearance calculations. All dimensions and heights necessary for clearance verification from the outer conductor (not pole centerline) are absent.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 requires that clearance dimensions and heights be specified for all building elements where required for clearance verification. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Measure from outer conductor (the actual wire), NOT from pole centerline or pole structure. For three-phase overhead lines, measure from the outermost conductor farthest from the pole. Horizontal clearances are measured as horizontal distance only (not diagonal).' The submitted plans show generic facility locations without the specific dimensional callouts required to verify compliance with these measurement standards. This deficiency prevents verifiable clearance review.

findings.comment: Clearance dimensions and heights not specified for building elements. Provide detailed building elevations and profile plans with dimensioned clearances for all roof overhangs, balconies, awnings, and canopies, measured from outer conductor locations showing minimum distances of 7'-6" horizontal and 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution conductors.
applicableAreas: Building elevations and profile plans - all structures
findings.observation: Examined all site plan sheets for clearance dimensions and building element heights. Sheet 9 contains a Building Height Table showing overall structure heights, but no dimensions for building elements (roof overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) are provided. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed building FFE values are shown but no dimensional information about projecting elements. No building elevations exist. Clearance dimensions are completely absent from all drawings.
findings.reasoning: This deficiency applies because buildings on the site are in proximity to existing electric easements (Sheet 9 vision confirmed 5' and 15' Electric Easements). Without building elevations showing dimensions of overhangs, balconies, and canopies, and without clearance dimensions measured from outer conductor locations, compliance cannot be demonstrated. The absence of these dimensions represents a critical documentation gap.

findings.comment: Building element heights, clearance dimensions, and outer conductor measurement points not specified on electrical plans or profiles. All clearances must be dimensioned and measured from the outer conductor (actual wire) location, not from pole centerline.
applicableAreas: All building elements and electric facility locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows building footprints with Finished Floor Elevations (FFEs) labeled for all 8 buildings (e.g., Bldg. 1 FFE=687.50, Bldg. 5 FFE=683.0). However, no building heights are shown. No dimensions specify clearance distances from electric facilities to building elements. Vision analysis confirmed: 'The labels provide only generic identification. There is NO specific information provided on this sheet regarding voltage, size, equipment type (e.g., single-phase vs. three-phase), or ownership (e.g., Austin Energy vs. Private) for these facilities.' Transformer, pull box, and meter locations are shown but not dimensioned relative to property lines, building corners, or other reference points. No specification of clearances measured from outer conductor locations.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires 'Clearance dimensions and heights' to be 'specified for building elements' and 'clearances measured from outer conductor locations.' The Regulatory Overview emphasizes: 'Measure from outer conductor (the actual wire), NOT from pole centerline' and 'For three-phase overhead lines, measure from the outermost conductor farthest from the pole.' Sheet 21 contains no such dimensioning. The absence of building height dimensions, clearance measurements, and specification of measurement points from outer conductors means the plans do not demonstrate compliance with the clearance measurement methodology required by code.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits show only one clearance envelope (or neither envelope) instead of both envelopes required by code. Please provide clearance verification exhibits demonstrating BOTH the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND the 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors, clearly showing both envelopes on the same exhibit(s).
applicableAreas: Entire site where overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors are present
findings.observation: No clearance verification exhibits of any kind were found on Sheets 9 or 21. The site plan shows an existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along the southern property boundary. However, there are NO exhibits demonstrating either the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance envelope OR the 15-foot radius clearance envelope required by code. Neither envelope is depicted, labeled, or calculated on any submitted sheet.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 establishes two distinct, concurrent clearance requirements: (1) 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and (2) 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes: 'These are separate envelopes with different geometric properties. Both must be met; satisfying one does not satisfy the other. These requirements are in addition to NESC Section 234 baseline requirements, not substitutes for them.' The applicant has provided neither envelope on the submitted plans, failing to demonstrate compliance with this critical dual-requirement standard.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not show both required clearance envelopes. Provide engineered exhibits demonstrating BOTH: (1) 7'-6" minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from ground level at 7.5 feet horizontal distance from outer conductors, AND (2) 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending infinitely in all directions from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Both must be shown simultaneously.
findings.observation: Searched all sheets for clearance verification exhibits. No exhibits found showing either the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance or the 15-foot radius clearance envelopes. Sheet 9 vision confirmed overhead electric lines are shown along boundaries, and Sheet 31 vision confirmed overhead electric line shown on southern boundary. However, no clearance envelope diagrams exist on any sheet.
findings.reasoning: The presence of overhead distribution facilities confirmed by site vision analysis makes clearance verification mandatory. The grouping explicitly states Austin Energy requires BOTH clearance envelopes be satisfied simultaneously - these are separate envelopes with different geometric properties (7'-6" horizontal plane and 15-foot cylindrical radius). The complete absence of any clearance verification exhibits showing both envelopes means neither can be evaluated. This is distinct from EL-11.1 in that this specifically addresses the dual envelope requirement.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not depict both required clearance envelopes: the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from 7.5 feet horizontal distance from conductors, AND the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending downward from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Both envelopes must be shown simultaneously on all required sheets.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution electrical facilities shown on electrical and landscape plans
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21, 9, and 31 for clearance verification exhibits. No clearance verification exhibits found on any sheet. Sheets 9 and 21 show underground electric lines (-E- notation) and some overhead electric lines (-OHE- notation) but provide NO clearance envelope diagrams. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows one overhead electric line at bottom edge labeled '-OHE-' but includes no clearance zones, protection buffers, or clearance envelope drawings. The grouping Regulatory Overview states: 'These are separate envelopes with different geometric properties. Both must be met; satisfying one does not satisfy the other. These requirements are IN ADDITION TO NESC Section 234 baseline requirements, not substitutes for them.' No exhibits demonstrate BOTH envelope requirements simultaneously.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 requires dual clearance envelopes: (1) 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance, and (2) 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance. The grouping emphasizes these are separate geometric envelopes that must BOTH be satisfied. No exhibits on Sheets 9, 21, or 31 display both clearance envelopes. Sheets show overhead lines existing but provide no graphical demonstration of clearance compliance. The absence of exhibits showing both envelopes means the plans do not demonstrate code compliance with the dual clearance requirements.

findings.comment: Proposed point of service is not shown and labeled on all required plan sheets. Please clearly label and dimension the point of service on the electrical plan, site plan, and utility plan, specifying the exact location where service is received from Austin Energy.
applicableAreas: Electric service connection areas; transformer locations
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan). Sheet 21 shows a transformer pad location and underground electric lines with generic labels ('Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Electrical Meters') but no label explicitly identifying 'Point of Service' (POS). Sheet 9 shows 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' but does not label or dimension a specific point of service. The sheet reference to 'Sheet 19 for Profile' was checked; that sheet contains utility tap (water/wastewater) profiles, not electric service information. No explicit service connection point is labeled and dimensioned on the electrical plans or site plan.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(5) requires that the point of service be explicitly shown and labeled on all required plan sheets. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Must identify one point of service and one service voltage (unless exceptions apply). Plans must include one-line diagram of electrical riser.' The applicant has not provided an explicitly labeled point of service with dimensions showing where service enters the site from Austin Energy's infrastructure. This is a fundamental service documentation requirement that must be clearly marked on the plans.

findings.comment: Proposed point of service not shown and labeled on all required plan sheets. Clearly label and dimension the point of service on electrical plans, site plan, and utility plan with explicit call-out identifying it as the service connection location, including distance from property line and reference to the existing utility main.
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 19, and 21 for explicit Point of Service labeling. Sheet 21 vision analysis stated: "A line labeled 'Underground Electric Line' is shown entering the site from the west from the 'Valley View Road' right-of-way... However, there is no specific label explicitly stating 'Service Connection Point' or detailing the connection to the off-site utility main." Sheet 9 shows transformers and lines but no explicit service connection label. Sheet 19 shows utility routing but does not highlight a specific service entry point. The underground electric line entering from Valley View Road is depicted but not labeled as the service point.
findings.reasoning: The presence of the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan and new underground electric routing from Valley View Road indicates new service. AEDC § 1.16.0(5) requires the point of service to be shown and labeled on all required plans. Vision analysis explicitly found NO label stating "Service Connection Point" or identifying the connection location. While the service entry is visible, it is not explicitly labeled or dimensioned as required, creating ambiguity about the approved service point.

findings.comment: Proposed point of service not shown and labeled on all required plan sheets (electrical plans, site plan, utility plan). Point of service must be explicitly identified and dimensioned with reference to property lines and building entry points.
applicableAreas: Site plan, electrical plans, utility plan
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 revealed: 'There is no explicitly labeled "Point of Service" or "Point of Delivery" on this sheet. An "Underground Electric Line" is shown entering the property from the left (Valley View Road), but it lacks a formal service designation.' Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed: 'The exact point of electric service (such as individual meters on buildings or the primary tie-in point to the grid) is NOT clearly marked with a distinct "Point of Service" or "Meter" label, nor are there specific dimensions tying a service point to building corners or property lines.' Sheet 19 shows underground electric line routing in plan view but provides no explicit service point designation. No sheet examined shows a labeled point of service with explicit dimensioning from property lines, building entry points, or other reference points. Engineer's Summary Letter mentions water and wastewater service but does NOT mention electric service point.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(5) mandates that projects with new or relocated electric service must show the proposed point of service explicitly labeled and dimensioned. The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric lines entering the property but does not designate a specific, labeled point of service. No dimensioning ties the service entry point to property boundaries or other reference features. The absence of an explicitly labeled and dimensioned point of service means the plans do not meet the basic service documentation requirement.

findings.comment: Primary routing from AE transformer to building is not clearly shown on plans with adequate specificity and labeling. Please provide detailed routing on the electrical plan showing the specific primary distribution path from the transformer(s) to each building's service entrance with dimensions and specifications.
applicableAreas: Service routing from transformer to buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines routed to transformer pad and to the buildings, marked with generic labels ('Underground Electric Line') and letter 'E' designation on the routing lines. However, the routing is shown as generic blue lines without clear specification of: (1) which line represents primary routing from AE transformer, (2) specific path identification, (3) detailed routing sequence from point of service through transformer to buildings, or (4) conduit specifications. The routing appears generalized rather than specifically engineered to show the primary distribution path from AE's infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that primary routing from AE transformer to building be shown on plans. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Must demonstrate approximate location and appropriate space for electric facilities.' While some routing is shown, it lacks the specificity and clarity required for plan review. The generic routing with minimal labeling does not provide sufficient detail to verify that primary distribution from the transformer to each building is clearly documented with proper identification of the primary service path.

findings.comment: Primary routing from AE transformer to building not clearly shown or labeled. Provide clear routing diagram showing the complete path from transformer through pull boxes to service entrance of each building. Label routing with conduit size, conductor gauge, and service voltage specifications.
applicableAreas: Service routing - from utility to buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines and transformers. Vision analysis confirmed electrical infrastructure including transformers and pull boxes connected via routing. Sheet 19 legend shows "E | Proposed Underground Electric." However, the vision analysis does not explicitly confirm whether the routing FROM the AE transformer (or connection point) TO the buildings is clearly shown. The relationship between service entry, transformer, and building connections is visually present but not explicitly documented as complete primary routing.
findings.reasoning: Sheet 21 is titled "Preliminary Electrical Design Plan" indicating new service design. AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires primary routing from AE transformer to building to be shown. While electrical infrastructure and routing are shown per vision analysis, the available documentation does not definitively confirm whether routing FROM transformer TO individual buildings is completely and clearly shown with labels. The term "primary routing" may refer specifically to utility-to-customer routing, which may differ from what is depicted.

findings.comment: Primary routing from Austin Energy service point to buildings not explicitly shown on plans, and no one-line electrical riser diagram provided. Detailed routing path and specifications must be documented, along with a one-line diagram showing service flow.
applicableAreas: Electrical plans and utility plan routing
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 for documentation of primary routing from service entry to buildings. Vision analysis showed: 'An "Underground Electric Line" is shown entering the property from the left (Valley View Road)' and underground lines are shown routing through the site connecting transformers to buildings. However, the path is labeled generically as 'Underground Electric Line' with no specification of routing details (distance, path, conduit size, conductor gauge, voltage). Sheet 19 shows electric line routing in plan view but similarly provides only generic '-E-' labeling without detailed routing specifications. No one-line diagram is provided showing the primary routing from the AE transformer/service point through the distribution system to individual buildings.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that plans 'Must demonstrate approximate location and appropriate space for electric facilities' and specifically address primary routing. The grouping's Service Documentation Hierarchy states 'Must identify one point of service and one service voltage (unless exceptions apply)' and plans must include 'one-line diagram of electrical riser.' While the electrical plan shows general routing of underground lines, it does not provide: (1) a one-line diagram, (2) primary routing specifications (distances, path clarity, conduit/conductor details), or (3) clear service delivery path from external source through the distribution system. The generic labeling without detailed routing information prevents verification of adequate service design.

findings.comment: Electric facility labels are missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth for underground), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. Please revise all facility labels to include applicable technical specifications such as voltage, conduit/conductor size, burial depth, and ownership.
applicableAreas: All electric facilities on site and utility plans
findings.observation: Examined all labels on Sheets 21 and 9. Electric facility labels are limited to type descriptions only: 'Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Electrical Meters', 'Underground Electric Line', and 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)', 'OHE'. None of these labels include any of the following required information: (1) size/conduit diameter, (2) conductor gauge, (3) burial depth (for underground facilities), (4) voltage (primary voltage level), (5) ownership designation (AE vs. Customer). Sheet 3 General Notes and Electric Notes do not remedy this deficiency by providing detailed specifications for the electric facilities shown on the design sheets.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires facility labels to include applicable technical specifications. The grouping regulatory overview lists 'Labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth for underground), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information' as a common violation pattern. The applicant's generic labels fail this requirement completely. Without this information, reviewers cannot verify code compliance, safety standards, or service adequacy.

findings.comment: Electric facility labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. Add complete technical specifications to all electrical facility labels including transformer kVA/voltage, pull box conduit size/burial depth, meter voltage/amperage, and underground line conductor gauge/voltage/burial depth. Labels must appear on all plan sheets where facilities are depicted.
applicableAreas: All electrical facilities shown on plans
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 explicitly stated: "The labels only identify the general facility type (e.g., transformer, pull box, meters). They do not identify size (e.g., pad dimensions, conduit diameter), voltage, capacity (e.g., kVA), ownership, or other specific technical specifications." Specific findings: (1) Transformers labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad" only - no kVA capacity, voltage, or ownership noted. (2) Pull Boxes labeled as "Electrical Pull Box" only - no conduit diameter or depth specified. (3) Meters labeled as "Electrical Meters" only - no voltage or amperage rating specified. (4) Underground Lines labeled as "Underground Electric Line" only - no conductor gauge, voltage, or ownership specified.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires electric facilities to be labeled with complete technical information. The grouping specifies required information: size, depth, voltage, and ownership. Vision analysis confirmed that NONE of this information is present on the labels used on Sheets 21 or 9. Labels identify facility type only, which is insufficient. The deficiency is not about whether facilities are labeled, but whether labels contain complete information per code requirements.

findings.comment: Electric facility labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth), voltage (primary voltage level), and ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. All labels must include technical specifications relevant to each facility type for code compliance verification and construction clarity.
applicableAreas: All electric facility labels on electrical plans
findings.observation: Examined electric facility labels on Sheets 21, 9, and 19. Sheet 21 Vision analysis showed: 'The labels provide only generic identification. There is NO specific information provided on this sheet regarding voltage, size, equipment type (e.g., single-phase vs. three-phase), or ownership (e.g., Austin Energy vs. Private) for these facilities.' Labels observed: 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (no voltage, capacity, or phase information), 'Electrical Pull Box' (no conduit diameter or conductor specifications), 'Electrical Meters' (no voltage or capacity rating), 'Underground Electric Line' (no voltage, conductor gauge, or burial depth). Sheet 9 shows identical generic labeling without specifications. Sheet 19 shows only '-E-' notation without specifications. No labels include size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership information as required.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires that facility labels identify not just type but include relevant technical specifications. The grouping checklist item EL-11.11 specifically requires labels to include 'size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth for underground), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information where applicable.' The current labels omit all of these specifications. For example: transformers lack voltage class and capacity; conduits lack diameter specifications; underground lines lack burial depth; no labels distinguish Austin Energy facilities from customer-owned facilities. This deficiency prevents reviewers and constructors from understanding the technical specifications of the electrical infrastructure.

findings.comment: Projected load for electric service is not provided on electrical plans. Please provide the calculated electrical load for the proposed development (in kVA or kW) based on the 39 residential townhome units and any common area electrical requirements, and submit for Austin Energy capacity verification.
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 3 (General Notes), and facts.md project summary. No electrical load information is shown on any sheet. Sheet 21 shows facility locations and routing but no load calculations, service amperage, or projected demand information. Sheet 3 contains Austin Water capacity letters for water and wastewater service showing demands (60 gpm water, 20 gpm wastewater), but no corresponding electrical load letter or documentation from Austin Energy. Facts.md describes the project as 39 townhome units but provides no electrical load requirements. The preliminary electrical design plan contains no load analysis or specification.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that 'Projected load [be] required for electric service' for projects with new or upgraded electric service. This project is clearly a new development with 39 units requiring new electric service. The applicant must provide electrical load calculations showing the total demand (in kVA or kW) for the project based on the 39-unit residential load and any common area requirements. This information is required by Austin Energy for service adequacy verification and is fundamental to the preliminary electrical design.

findings.comment: Projected load required for electrical service not clearly provided. If new service is being provided, submit load calculations and electrical demand projections in kVA or kW with service voltage, transformer size (kVA), and amperage rating specifications. Confirm with Austin Energy whether load calculations are required in site plan or deferred to building permit design.
findings.observation: Searched Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and related sheets for projected electrical load information. Sheet 21 shows utility notes mentioning water and wastewater specifications but NO electrical load information. No kW or kVA load calculations are shown. No service amperage or voltage specifications are documented. No electrical one-line diagram or load calculation documentation exists. Master Comment Report lists UCM § 1.9.3 (Installation of Metering Equipment) as a preliminary design requirement, suggesting service design details should be provided.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires projected load for electric service. The grouping specifies this applies "Only for projects with new or upgraded electric service." The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan and routing of new underground electric service indicate new service is provided. If new service is proposed, load must be documented. However, applicability is UNCLEAR because whether this qualifies as "new service" requiring load documentation in site plan versus preliminary routing subject to later building permit design is ambiguous. Master Comment Report's inclusion of metering equipment requirements suggests loads should be specified.

findings.comment: Projected electrical load not provided on electrical plans. Estimated demand load in amperes (or kVA) must be calculated and shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan to demonstrate adequate service sizing.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for projected load information. The sheet contains: building unit counts (e.g., Bldg. 1: 3 units, Bldg. 2: 6 units), square footage per building, and FFE data. No projected electrical load (in kW, amperage, or kVA) is labeled on the sheet. No demand calculation is shown. No specification of service amperage or phases is documented. No load table is provided. The grouping's Service Documentation Hierarchy specifies 'New service >350A single-phase or >225A three-phase: AE Design review required' but no amperage or load documentation is shown to indicate whether this threshold applies or what the design service parameters are.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires 'Projected load' to be 'provided on electrical plans' for projects with 'new or upgraded electric service.' This 39-unit multi-family project requires new electric service, triggering the requirement. The electrical design plan shows physical layout of distribution infrastructure but does not quantify the electrical load that infrastructure must serve. Without projected load documentation, reviewers cannot verify that the service size, transformer capacity, and distribution infrastructure are adequate for the intended use. The grouping's threshold of 350A/225A for AE Design Review cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Provide dimensioned clearances from all four transformer pads to adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, and structures per UCM § 1.10.4 requirements (10 feet for hot-stick use area, 5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3-5 feet for other sides depending on building construction type). Confirm building construction types if any clearances are less than standard requirements.
applicableAreas: Four transformer pad locations on the site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies four locations labeled "Electrical Transformer Pad": (1) west of Building 1 near Unit 101, (2) west of Building 8 near Unit 801, (3) south of Building 5 near Unit 504, and (4) north of Building 7 near Unit 705. All four pads are shown as simple squares with no dimension lines showing clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, walkways, or structures. The site plan shows driveways and parking areas in close proximity to these pads, but no distances are dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements for pad-mounted equipment based on the type of adjacent structures and whether the equipment has operator/control access. Required clearances range from 3 feet (non-operator sides, non-brick/masonry buildings) to 10 feet (hot-stick use area). The absence of dimensioned clearances prevents verification that the design complies with these minimum setbacks and prevents determination of whether reduced clearances (3 feet instead of 5 feet) require AE Design written approval per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2. Building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) must be documented to determine which clearance column in Table 1.10.4 applies.

findings.comment: Clearances from the four transformer pads are not shown or dimensioned on any plan sheets. Design must provide UCM § 1.10.4 compliant clearances (10 ft hot-stick area, 5 ft operator areas, 3 ft other sides) dimensioned from each pad to buildings, parking, driveways, and other obstructions. Building construction type (brick/masonry 2-hour fire-rated vs. non-brick/masonry) must be documented to determine applicable clearance table.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8; near parking areas and driveways
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads with generic labels only ('Electrical Transformer Pad') and no specifications (kVA ratings, dimensions, or type). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) displays the same transformer locations in spatial context with buildings, driveways, parking spaces, and sidewalks. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that no clearance dimensions or lines are dimensioned from any transformer pad to nearby buildings, parking areas, driveways, or sidewalks. The drawing shows relationships graphically but provides zero quantitative clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements from pad-mounted equipment: minimum 10 feet on hot-stick use area (side with door), 5 feet on sides with operators/controls, and 3 feet on sides without operators/controls (from removable ventilated obstructions). Additionally, buildings affect these clearances—non-brick/masonry buildings trigger the standard clearances; brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating allows reduced clearances. No building construction types are documented, and no clearance dimensions are shown from the transformers to any adjacent structures. The plans cannot demonstrate compliance with Table 1.10.4 without these dimensions and without knowledge of building construction type.

findings.comment: Transformer pad clearances from buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, and other structures not shown or dimensioned on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned clearance details for both transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (minimum 3 feet to 10 feet depending on side and building type), including verification of building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) for clearance determination.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts two transformer pads on the site plan drawing. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that no dimensions or clearance radii are labeled for either transformer pad. The pads are drawn in proximity to parking areas, driveways, and building footprints, but no specific clearance distances are dimensioned or noted. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the overall layout with buildings and parking areas but provides no transformer pad clearance dimensions. The preliminary electrical plan shows the general locations of the two transformer pads but provides no evidence of compliance with the minimum clearance requirements specified in UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (10 ft hot-stick use area, 5 ft sides with operators/controls, 3 ft other sides based on building type and fire rating).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires specific clearances from pad-mounted equipment based on the side of the equipment and building construction type. The required clearances range from 3 feet to 10 feet depending on the side and building characteristics. The applicant's burden is to demonstrate compliance through dimensioned drawings. The absence of any clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan and site plan means the requirement cannot be verified. The deficiency is not that compliance might not exist in reality, but that the required documentation is absent. The preliminary design nature of the electrical plan (labeled as 'Preliminary Electrical Design') combined with the complete absence of clearance dimensions indicates this item must be addressed with detailed clearance callouts and notes before the design can be verified as compliant.

findings.comment: Add transmission notes to Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) referencing the detailed transmission clearance and access requirements shown on the general notes sheet, or verify that transmission facilities do not exist and remove transmission notes from Sheet 3 if inapplicable.
applicableAreas: Transmission easement area (if transmission facilities present on site)
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains an extensive "Electric Transmission Notes" section with 16 numbered items covering transmission clearances, digging restrictions, access requirements, and construction safety. However, examination of Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows no transmission-related notes—only standard utility easement references and general drainage/construction notes. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) likewise contains no transmission-related notes; the blocks shown reference only irrigation notes, general landscape notes, and legend definitions, with no text addressing transmission facilities, clearance zones, or construction restrictions related to transmission.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires that transmission notes be included on "coversheet, note page, grading plans, and landscape sheets when transmission facilities are present." The presence of comprehensive transmission notes on Sheet 3 suggests transmission facilities exist on or immediately adjacent to the site. Transmission facilities have substantially different access and construction restrictions than distribution facilities and require special contractor awareness and coordination with Austin Energy (per the 16 transmission notes on Sheet 3, including 48-hour pre-construction safety meeting, 25-foot clearance from structures, OSHA 20-foot clearance from energized lines, etc.). Contractors and workers reviewing the grading plan or landscape plan would have no awareness of these transmission-specific constraints, which creates a safety and compliance risk.

findings.comment: Resolve transmission facility status: Either transmission structures are present on or adjacent to the site (in which case they must be clearly documented on the existing conditions survey and transmission clearance compliance must be demonstrated), or transmission notes in Sheet 3 Block 20 should be removed per UCM § 1.16.0(8) requirements that notes match actual site conditions.
applicableAreas: Plat notes and general notes on cover sheet and grading/landscape plans
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes), Block 20 includes 16 detailed 'Electric Transmission Notes' referencing transmission structures, transmission easements, transmission wire, and access requirements (e.g., 25-foot clearance zones, 48-hour pre-construction meetings, 46,000 lb tandem axle road support, fire hydrants 20+ feet from transmission). Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not show any transmission structures or lattice towers—only standard distribution poles are visible. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) does not show any transmission infrastructure. Facts.md confirms the site is outside the 100-year floodplain and within a typical urban context.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires that transmission notes appear on cover sheets, plat notes, grading plans, and landscape plans ONLY when transmission facilities (60kV+, large structures) are present on the site. Conversely, these notes must be REMOVED if no transmission facilities exist. The applicant has included 16 transmission-specific notes (Block 20 on Sheet 3) but has not clearly documented whether transmission facilities exist. The existing conditions survey does not show transmission structures. If transmission does not exist, the notes should be removed. If transmission does exist, it must be clearly documented on the existing conditions survey and the plans must demonstrate compliance with transmission clearance requirements.

findings.comment: Transmission notes appear on coversheet (Sheet 3) but no transmission structures or transmission easements are evident on electrical plan or utility plan. Clarify whether transmission facilities (60kV+ voltage level) are present on or adjacent to the site. If no transmission facilities exist, remove transmission notes from coversheet, grading plan, and landscape plan per UCM § 1.16.0(8). If transmission facilities do exist, ensure all required transmission notes appear on all applicable sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes / Coversheet) contains detailed Electric Transmission Notes in Block 20, including 16 specific notes about transmission line clearances, safety meetings, barricading, access, and structural load requirements. These notes appear on the coversheet. The utility plan (Sheet 21) shows OHE (overhead electric) facilities marked as dashed lines along property boundaries. However, the vision analysis of the electrical plan and visual examination of other sheets indicate that the OHE shown on the property boundaries appear to be DISTRIBUTION facilities (poles and conductors along the boundary), NOT TRANSMISSION facilities (large steel transmission structures with 60kV+ voltage). The site plan does not depict any transmission line easement boundaries, transmission structures, or transmission-specific infrastructure. The checklist item requires determining: (1) whether transmission facilities exist, and if they do, transmission notes must be present on coversheet, grading plan, and landscape plan; or (2) if transmission does NOT exist, transmission notes should be removed. The extensive transmission notes currently on the coversheet suggest transmission facilities were expected but may not actually exist, or the engineer included them as a standard template.
findings.reasoning: The grouping distinguishes between 'transmission' (60kV+ voltage, large structures, transmission easements) and 'distribution' (less than 60kV, typical pole-mounted infrastructure). The presence of transmission notes on the coversheet suggests the design team anticipated transmission facilities on or near the site. However, visual review of the electrical plan and other documents shows only distribution facilities (OHE poles and conductors). The facts.md file did not identify any transmission easement or transmission structure on the property. This creates ambiguity: either (a) transmission facilities exist and are not properly depicted on plans, or (b) transmission notes were included as template language and should be removed. Without clear identification of whether transmission facilities are present, the status cannot be definitively 'pass' or 'fail'. The condition is UNCLEAR and requires clarification from the applicant regarding whether transmission infrastructure is present on or adjacent to the site.

findings.comment: Plans showing "Preliminary Electrical Design Plan" must include a note stating that electric facilities are conceptual design and final design will be coordinated with Austin Energy. Add disclaimer language to the general notes or electrical sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is titled "Preliminary Electrical Design Plan" in its title block. However, there are no notes on the site plan sheets (specifically the cover sheet, general notes, or electrical design sheets) that state the electric facilities shown are conceptual and represent preliminary design, not final design.
findings.reasoning: The grouping guidance explicitly states that "Plans showing conceptual electric facilities marked as 'final' or 'approved' must include disclaimers that facilities are conceptual and not for bidding purposes." Sheet 21 shows transformer pads, meters, and underground electric routing, but the preliminary status is only indicated in the sheet title, not in plan notes where it would be visible to contractors and reviewers. Without explicit textual disclaimers, there is ambiguity about the design status, which could lead to construction based on incomplete design specifications.

findings.comment: Add explicit note to Preliminary Electrical Design Plan stating that electric facilities shown are conceptual design and subject to final coordination with Austin Energy, and that this preliminary design is not approved for construction or bidding purposes.
applicableAreas: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and preliminary design coordination
findings.observation: Sheet 21 title block explicitly states 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan.' The sheet shows transformer locations, pull boxes, underground lines, and meters with minimal specifications. However, there is no explicit note on the electrical plan or general notes stating that the electric facilities are 'conceptual design,' 'not final design,' or similar language. The word 'Preliminary' appears only in the sheet title.
findings.reasoning: When Austin Energy has not completed final electrical design, plans must include explicit disclaimers that facilities are conceptual and not for bidding purposes, and that final design will be coordinated with Austin Energy. While the title 'Preliminary' conveys some design stage information, it is not a sufficient standalone note. The grouping's regulatory overview identifies this as a 'Common Violation Pattern': 'Plans show conceptual electric facilities marked as "final" or "approved". When AE Design has not completed final electric design, plans must include disclaimers that facilities are conceptual and not for bidding purposes, and that final design will be coordinated with Austin Energy.' An explicit text note stating the design is conceptual must be added to make this status clear to all reviewers and construction teams.

findings.comment: Plans do not clearly note that electric facilities shown are conceptual and not final design. Add explicit note to utility plan and/or coversheet stating: 'The electric facilities shown on this plan are preliminary and conceptual. Final electrical design will be coordinated with and approved by Austin Energy. These plans are not for bidding or construction purposes.'
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' which by definition suggests the electrical design is conceptual and not final. However, no explicit disclaimer note is visible on the sheet stating that 'electric facilities shown are conceptual and not for final design' or similar language. The coversheet (Sheet 3) and utility plan notes do not contain a visible note stating that the electric design is preliminary and not to be used for construction. The presence of the word 'Preliminary' in the sheet title provides some indication of design phase, but the checklist item requires an explicit note on the plans stating the facilities are conceptual and not final. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 did not identify such a disclaimer note in the visible text blocks.
findings.reasoning: The grouping specifies that when electric facilities are shown conceptually (i.e., when Austin Energy Design has not completed final design), plans must include disclaimers that facilities are conceptual and not for bidding purposes. The sheet title 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' suggests preliminary status, but this title alone may not be sufficient to serve as the required notice to contractors and builders. An explicit note stating something like 'The electric facilities shown on this plan are preliminary and conceptual. Do not use for bidding purposes. Final electrical design will be coordinated with Austin Energy' should be clearly visible as a text note on the electrical plan or coversheet. The absence of such an explicit disclaimer note, despite the preliminary design status, creates an unclear situation.

findings.comment: Plans must include note stating that electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes and will be subject to final Austin Energy design coordination.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design (transformer pads, underground routing, meters) but no note appears anywhere on the plans indicating that the electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes. The existing general notes and utility coordination notes do not include this disclaimer.
findings.reasoning: Preliminary designs are not construction-ready and contain assumptions subject to change. Construction contractors who bid based on preliminary electric design may face significant cost overruns or changes during final AE Design coordination. The absence of this note creates liability for the applicant and City. The grouping identifies this as a common violation pattern: "Plans showing conceptual electric facilities...must include disclaimers that facilities are conceptual and not for bidding purposes."

findings.comment: Add note to Preliminary Electrical Design Plan stating: 'Electric facility layout shown herein is preliminary design and should not be used for bidding purposes. Final electric design and coordination with Austin Energy is required before construction.'
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) contains utility notes and disclaimers about the application not constituting verification of all data and engineer responsibility for completeness and accuracy. However, there is no note explicitly stating that 'electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes.'
findings.reasoning: When electric facilities are shown in preliminary or conceptual design stage, UCM standards and reviewer convention require a note clearly stating the layout should not be used for bidding. This prevents contractors from using incomplete preliminary designs for cost estimation and prevents problems during construction when final designs differ. The absence of this note leaves ambiguity about whether preliminary facilities can be bid on.

findings.comment: Plans do not include note that electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes. Add explicit note to electrical plan and/or coversheet: 'This is a preliminary electrical design plan. These plans should not be used for bidding, material takeoff, or construction purposes. Final design will be provided by Austin Energy.'
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan,' indicating the electrical design is conceptual. However, the vision analysis of Sheet 21 and the utility notes block reviewed did not identify an explicit note stating 'The electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes' or equivalent language. The grouping states that when electric facilities are shown conceptually (not final AE Design), plans should include a note about not using the design for bidding. While the preliminary status is indicated in the sheet title, an explicit disclaimer note appears to be absent.
findings.reasoning: When electrical designs are preliminary and not finalized by Austin Energy, contractor and bidders must be explicitly warned not to use the preliminary design for estimating or construction. The sheet title 'Preliminary' provides some indication but may not be sufficient notice. A clear, prominent note stating the plans should not be used for bidding purposes is the more reliable method to communicate this requirement. The absence of such an explicit note constitutes a documentation deficiency, even if the preliminary status is indicated in the sheet title.

findings.comment: Direct line of sight from transformers to meters not verified. Provide line of sight analysis or building sections confirming unobstructed visual path from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter location(s), or provide documented AE Design approval for exceptions.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations and corresponding meter locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. Meters are shown on the exterior of all eight buildings. The four transformer pads are located in various positions around the site (near Buildings 1, 2, 4, and 7). While the 2D schematic plan shows the general proximity of transformers and meters, it is impossible from a top-down plan view to determine unobstructed visual line of sight. The site has buildings, landscaping, retaining walls, sidewalks, and other vertical obstructions that could block the line of sight between some transformers and their serving meters. For example, the transformer south of Building 4 to the meters on Building 4 might be blocked by the building itself depending on building geometry and roof configuration.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformers to be in direct line of sight to meters. This requires not only proximity but also unobstructed visual path from the transformer to the meter location. A 2D plan cannot adequately verify line of sight. Building sections, 3D visualization, or explicit note from AE Design confirming line of sight verification is needed. Without this verification, it is unclear whether all transformer-to-meter pairs meet the line of sight requirement.

findings.comment: Many meter locations on building faces do not have direct unobstructed line of sight to transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path. Meters on the east/west/south sides of buildings cannot see transformers on opposite sides. Provide: (1) Confirmation that all meters are relocated to faces that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer, OR (2) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units authorizing the non-line-of-sight meter locations per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
applicableAreas: Multiple buildings and meter locations throughout site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) to trace visual line-of-sight paths from transformer pads to meter locations. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Because the meters are distributed on multiple exterior sides of the buildings (e.g., east and west walls) and the transformers are located at specific single points near the drive aisle, many meters are on the opposite side of the building from their likely power source. Therefore, many meters do NOT have a direct line of sight to a transformer.' The four transformer pads are positioned at single points along the main drive loop (T1 west of Bldg. 2, T2 between Bldg. 4-5, T3 south of Bldg. 6, T4 west of Bldg. 8), while meters are distributed on multiple building faces (east side, west side, south side). Building structures physically obstruct the visual path from many meters to their source transformers.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 (Location of Meter Sockets) requires transformers to be 'within sight' of meter locations to enable Austin Energy personnel to 'verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations.' The Regulatory Overview for this grouping clarifies: 'Transformers must be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations.' Line of sight means an unobstructed visual path - if a building structure blocks the direct view from meter to transformer, the line of sight requirement is not met. The vision analysis explicitly identified that 'many meters are on the opposite side of the building from their likely power source,' which necessarily means building structures obstruct the line of sight. AE personnel cannot verify connections and perform coordinated operations if they cannot see both the meter and the transformer from a single vantage point.

findings.comment: Transformer pads not in direct line of sight to meter location. Buildings and trees block visual path from transformer pad to meters.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads to associated meters on Buildings 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows three transformer pads and eight building meters distributed around the site. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 determined that 'for most meters, there is no direct line-of-sight to a transformer pad. The buildings themselves obstruct line-of-sight, and the electrical routing often travels around the perimeters of the buildings to reach the meter banks.' Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not clearly label meter locations; vision analysis confirmed 'meters are not clearly marked on this site plan.' Additionally, vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted that 'if meters were placed on the nearest walls, the visual path from the transformer pad would cross directly through the adjacent parking stalls (potentially blocked by parked cars) and the future canopy of the tree designated by the "Tree Well."' This indicates obstructions (vehicles and trees) would block line of sight.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires transformers to be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations. The site plan electrical design routes conduit around building perimeters rather than direct paths, buildings obstruct sightlines, and trees (tree wells shown adjacent to transformer pad) would block visual paths from transformers to meters. The lack of clearly marked meter locations on the primary site and electrical plans prevents verification of compliance. Obstructions from buildings and trees indicate non-compliance.

findings.comment: Number of 90-degree turns in electrical routing from each transformer to meter not documented. Provide detailed electrical routing schedule or plan annotations showing the count of 90-degree bends in the conduit path from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter(s), confirming maximum two 90-degree bends.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing paths from transformers to meters on all eight buildings
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) which shows electrical routing from transformers to meters. Blue lines represent underground electric lines routed from transformers through pull boxes to meters on buildings. Visual inspection of the routing paths shows multiple turns. For example, routing from the transformer pad adjacent to Building 8 to the building's meters shows approximately 2 turn angles. However, the plan is schematic and does not explicitly count or label the number of 90-degree bends at each turn location. For many routing paths, multiple 90-degree turns are visually apparent as the lines navigate around building footprints and follow driveway layouts, but exact turn counts are not documented.
findings.reasoning: Code requires maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer and meter. While the electrical routing shows various path configurations, the plan does not explicitly document or count the number of 90-degree bends in each routing path. Without precise notation of turn counts, it is unclear whether any routing exceeds the maximum of two 90-degree turns. Some routing paths appear to have more than two distinct directional changes. The schematic nature of the plan makes definitive turn counting difficult without detailed field verification or explicit turn counts on the design.

findings.comment: Electrical routing shown on Sheet 21 contains at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary underground electrical loop, exceeding the maximum of 2 turns permitted by UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q. The rectangular loop configuration around the central buildings necessitates multiple directional changes. Revise the electrical routing design to limit turns between transformer pads and meters to a maximum of two 90-degree bends, or provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing the exceeding the standard 2-turn limitation for this site configuration.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing path from transformers to meters throughout site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 to trace electrical routing paths and count 90-degree bends. Vision analysis traced 'the primary electrical routing is denoted by a solid blue line. It enters the site from the mid-western boundary... splits to form a continuous underground loop that follows the inner perimeter of the internal drive aisle, circling the central buildings.' The analysis specifically identified: 'There are numerous 90-degree bends. Counting just the primary main loop (excluding small jogs to individual pads/meters), there are at least 6 distinct 90-degree corners to navigate the rectangular layout of the site.' The primary electrical loop makes a rectangular circuit around the central buildings, requiring approximately 6 90-degree directional changes (one at each corner of the rectangular loop). Branch connections from this main loop to individual transformers and meters add additional turns.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q (Current Transformers and Enclosures) specifies 'maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer pad and meter.' This limitation is imposed to maintain circuit performance and prevent voltage drop issues. The vision analysis conclusively identified at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary electrical routing loop, which is triple the maximum allowable. The rectangular main loop circuit requires a 90-degree bend at each corner (north, east, south, west), and the perimeter-following design necessitates these turns. This configuration cannot be reconfigured without a complete redesign of the electrical routing topology. The current design violates the maximum two-turn requirement.

findings.comment: More than two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer pad and meter. Most routing paths show multiple bends to navigate around building perimeters.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters throughout site
