findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan, scale 1" = 20') vision analysis identified the electrical routing pattern: 'There are numerous 90-degree bends throughout the site\'s electrical routing. Almost every path from a transformer to a distant meter (e.g., from the west pad to Bldg 3, or from the east pads to Bldg 5 and 7) involves multiple 90-degree turns to navigate around building corners and pull boxes.' The vision analysis did not identify a single routing path with two or fewer 90-degree bends; instead, it confirmed that most paths have 'multiple' (three or more) bends.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q limits electrical routing between transformer and meter to a maximum of two 90-degree bends. The site layout with buildings positioned around the central parking loop necessitates multiple turns to reach distant meter locations. Vision analysis explicitly confirmed 'numerous 90-degree bends' on most routing paths, with specific mention that paths to Buildings 3, 5, and 7 involve 'multiple 90-degree turns.' This pattern demonstrates systematic non-compliance across multiple meter routing paths.

findings.comment: Clearances between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure not documented. Provide dimension details or engineering notes confirming that electrical conduit routing maintains minimum 12-inch clearance from all drainage pipes, storm drains, and related infrastructure at all crossing and adjacent locations.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing paths crossing or running near storm drain infrastructure
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) and Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan). Sheet 21 shows blue electrical routing lines (marked 'E') crossing or running near dashed lines representing storm drain (SD) lines marked with square inlet symbols. Multiple crossing locations are visible on the plan. For example, electrical routing crosses storm drain lines between Building 2 and Building 8, and near Building 4. However, no dimension labels or callouts indicate the clearance distance between the electrical lines and storm drain lines at these crossing locations. No specifications confirm that minimum 12-inch clearance (or operational practice 5-foot clearance) is maintained.
findings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 12-inch clearance between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure. While the plans show electrical lines and drainage infrastructure, the clearance distances at crossing points are not dimensionally verified. Without specific clearance measurements at each crossing, compliance cannot be confirmed. The visual separation on a 1" = 20' scale plan may be deceptive and does not constitute adequate verification of actual clearances. Engineering coordination between electrical and drainage design should document these clearances explicitly.

findings.comment: Electrical routing shown on Sheet 21 is located adjacent to wastewater easements (T1, T4) and storm drain infrastructure (T2, T3), but no specific clearance dimensions are documented. Overlay Sheet 21 electrical routing with Sheet 12 drainage infrastructure details to verify minimum 12-inch clearance from drainage facilities. Provide cross-section details or a coordinate overlay demonstrating that electrical conduit maintains adequate clearance from all drainage infrastructure, or provide documentation from Austin Energy confirming acceptable separation distances for this site configuration.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing near Transformers 1, 2, 3, 4 and associated drainage infrastructure
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21, 9, and 12 to identify proximity of electrical routing to drainage infrastructure. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted: 'Drainage: There is an underground storm drain network (marked with dashed lines and SD) running parallel to the electrical lines in several places, particularly close to the routing near Bldg. 8 and Bldg. 4/5.' Vision analysis of Sheet 9 identified: 'T1 has Wastewater Easement nearby; T2 and T3 have Storm Drain lines adjacent; T4 has Wastewater Easement nearby.' The site plan shows utility lines for water (W), storm drain (SD), and wastewater (WW) running throughout the property. However, no specific clearance dimensions or separation distances are provided on any of the sheets. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows 24-inch and 18-inch HDPE storm drain pipes with specific elevations and profiles, but these details do not correlate with specific electrical routing clearance measurements on Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 (Clearances for AE Underground Cable, Conduit, and Underground Facilities) specifies 'minimum 12-inch clearance to other utilities.' The code citation language allows for interpretation - the minimum 12-inch clearance standard applies, but operational practice (referenced in the grouping as 'operational practice may require 5 feet for drainage infrastructure') may impose stricter separation for compatibility. Without specific clearance dimensions shown on the electrical plan or correlated details between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure profiles, it cannot be definitively determined whether the 12-inch minimum (or operationally appropriate 5-foot) clearance is maintained. The visual proximity noted by the vision analysis (routing 'very close' to drainage lines) suggests potential inadequate clearance, but cannot be confirmed without detailed profile views or cross-section details showing the vertical and horizontal separation distances between electrical conduits and drainage pipes.

findings.comment: Electrical routing from riser to transformer appears to cross drainage pipes and storm inlets. Clearance of drainage pipes and inlets with required minimum distance (12 inches per code, 5 feet per operational practice) cannot be verified from available evidence.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) vision analysis noted: 'The blue electrical lines frequently cross or run parallel to grey dashed lines labeled "SD" (Storm Drain) and "WW" (Wastewater) throughout the site layout.' Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows extensive storm sewer infrastructure with 18" and 24" HDPE pipes, grate inlets, and junction boxes distributed throughout the site. The electrical plan shows electrical routing as solid blue lines that cross the storm drain infrastructure (shown as grey dashed lines) at multiple locations. However, the electrical plan does not dimension the specific distances or clearances at crossing points, nor does it note minimum clearance requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires minimum 12-inch clearance from electrical conduit to drainage infrastructure; operational practice may require 5-foot clearance for drainage facility maintenance access. The site plan shows electrical routing crossing storm drain lines at multiple locations, but provides no documentation of achieved clearances at these crossings. Without specific distance callouts or sectional details showing clearance dimensions, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Point of service location is not explicitly marked or labeled on any of the required plan sheets. The plans show electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines) but do not identify the specific point where Austin Energy's infrastructure connects to the customer's electrical system. The POS must be clearly designated on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows an underground electric line entry point from Valley View Road on the western boundary, but does not include an explicit label or designation identifying this as the 'Point of Service' (POS) per UCM § 1.3.4. The plan shows transformer pads and meters but no specific POS location marker. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a single transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' without identifying which location serves as the point of service connection to Austin Energy infrastructure. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only overhead electric lines along the boundary, with no POS designation. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, the POS must be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that the point of electric service be shown on plan sheets. UCM § 1.3.4 defines POS as 'the location where Austin Energy's and the Customer's conductors are connected or terminated.' The presence of transformer pads and underground line routing does not constitute a clear POS designation. Without an explicit label identifying which location serves as the official POS, the requirement is not met. The applicant must clearly designate the POS location on all required sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.comment: Point of service (POS) location is not explicitly labeled on any required plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows electrical routing and infrastructure but lacks a clear 'Point of Service' designation. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 do not adequately identify the POS. Add explicit POS labeling to Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing where Austin Energy infrastructure connects to proposed customer infrastructure.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts electrical infrastructure including transformers, pull boxes, and meters, but does NOT contain an explicit label designating the Point of Service (POS). The plan shows where proposed underground electric lines enter from Valley View Road (western property line) and connect to electrical pull boxes, but the specific connection point to Austin Energy infrastructure is not labeled as 'Point of Service' or 'POS'. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only a single 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' without identifying the POS or primary source. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows overhead electric lines on boundaries but no identification of POS. The grouping's regulatory overview (UCM § 1.16.0) requires the POS to be clearly designated, and unless otherwise specified by Austin Energy, the POS must be shown on the required plan sheets (site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) and § 1.4.2.6 require that the point of service designation be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans). While Sheet 21 depicts the general electrical routing and infrastructure, the POS is not explicitly labeled or designated. Without clear labeling of the POS location, a reviewer cannot confirm compliance with the requirement to show the 'desired point of electric service' on the plans. This is distinct from merely showing infrastructure; the POS must be explicitly identified as the location where Austin Energy's and the Customer's conductors connect or terminate per UCM § 1.3.4.

findings.comment: Point of electric service (POS) location is not explicitly designated on required plan sheets. Add clear labeling of the point of service location (meter socket, pedestal, pull-box, or AE-designated enclosure) on all required sheets per UCM § 1.16.0(6) and UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing originating from west side of property but no specific label for "Point of Service" or "POS"; the connection point is shown but not explicitly designated as the POS per AE Design requirements. Sheet 9 shows a single transformer pad but no POS designation. Sheet 31 shows only overhead electric line on boundary, no POS marked. The point of service location and primary source location are not clearly labeled or designated on any of the required plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires the point of electric service to be shown on plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 requirements. While Sheet 21 shows electrical infrastructure and apparent connection points, these are not explicitly labeled as the "Point of Service" or identified as the location where Austin Energy's and the customer's conductors connect. Per UCM § 1.3.4, the POS is the specific location of connection or termination. The absence of explicit POS designation on required sheets (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) means the POS location cannot be verified as shown per code requirements. On Sheet 21, while the general routing is shown, the specific POS is not called out.

findings.comment: Underground electric cabling routing is shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but is missing or incomplete on other required plan sheets. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains legend symbols for underground electric but these symbols are not actually used in the drawing area. Underground electric routing must be consistently shown on the site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9), landscape plan (Sheet 31), and utility plans (Sheet 19) per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric line routing with '-E-' markings labeled 'Underground Electric Line,' routing from the western boundary through the site with pull boxes and connections to transformer pads. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) shows only a single transformer pad location without showing the underground routing from the source to the buildings or between transformers. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains legend symbols for 'Proposed Underground Electric' but these symbols are NOT actually drawn anywhere on the plan - the plan shows water, wastewater, and storm drain routing but zero electric line routing. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only the overhead electric line along the southern boundary with no underground electric cabling shown. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, underground electric cabling routing must be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and utility plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Customer Drawings Specifications' include the site plan showing all utilities, landscaping plan, and all electrical plans with appropriate detail. The requirement applies to showing underground electric cabling routing, conduit locations, and service lines from the source to the development and within the site. While Sheet 21 shows routing details, the required sheets per Table 1.4.3.B are incomplete: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) omits the routing details shown on Sheet 21; Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has legend symbols but NO actual electric routing depicted; Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only overhead electric, not underground routing. The inconsistency means the site plan showing all utilities does not adequately convey underground electric routing as required.

findings.comment: Underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations are not shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite these being required 'all utilities' plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Add underground electric line routing, conduit paths, and service connections to both sheets showing how power is distributed from the source (Valley View Road connection) to the transformer pads and to building meters.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows underground electric line routing with blue lines, conduit connections, and pull box locations. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does NOT show underground electric cabling routing despite being required as a sheet showing 'all utilities.' Sheet 9 displays other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain) with clear line designations but shows only a single transformer pad without any underground electrical lines routing from the source to that pad or to the buildings. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) similarly does NOT show underground electric line routing; it only shows overhead electric (OHE) lines on the western boundary and contains no depiction of the proposed underground electric service lines serving the development. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes a legend entry for 'Underground Electric' but the lines are not actually drawn on the plan view.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations to be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, the landscape plan, and all electrical plans. While the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) contains detailed electrical routing, the deficiency is that this information must be replicated on the site plan and landscape plan as required plan sheets. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) is identified as showing 'all utilities' but lacks the underground electrical routing information. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) is a required plan sheet per the grouping's regulatory overview but contains no underground electrical infrastructure. Absence of this information on sheets identified as showing utilities constitutes non-compliance, even if the information exists elsewhere in the plan set.

findings.comment: Underground electric conduit routing and service lines must be shown on all required plan sheets including site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31). Add underground electric line routing showing connections from property line source through site to service connection points per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows complete underground electric line routing from street entry point through site with conduit paths and connection to pull boxes and meters. Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) shows water (-W-), sanitary sewer (-WW-), and storm drain (-SD-) routing, but does NOT show underground electric line routing despite electric infrastructure being shown elsewhere on the site plan (one transformer pad noted). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only overhead electric (OHE) on the boundary, with no underground conduit or cable routing depicted. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes electrical symbols in the legend (-E- for Proposed Underground Electric) but contains NO actual underground electric lines drawn on the plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires underground electric cabling routing and service lines to be shown on required plan sheets including site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans. The inconsistency across sheets violates this requirement. While detailed electrical routing is shown on the dedicated Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), the required plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) do not show this infrastructure. The absence of underground electric routing on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) is particularly significant, as this sheet shows other underground utilities (water, sewer, storm) in detail but omits electrical routing. This note establishes clear responsibility for compliance with Austin Energy standards and for cost allocation of conductor installation. Its absence is a compliance gap.

findings.comment: Austin Energy Notes section must include a note establishing developer responsibility for conduit design and installation. Please add: 'Developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual, including installation of conductors if determined during design (prior to building permit issuance) that developer will fund conductor installation. Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve conflicts. All costs for these improvements are the applicant's responsibility.'
findings.observation: The Austin Energy notes on Sheet 3 include five notes addressing tree work, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and facility relocation. None of the notes present includes developer responsibility for designing and constructing conduit infrastructure or reference to the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. The grouping identifies that Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical routing and infrastructure, indicating that conduit infrastructure is a component of this project. No note is present establishing developer responsibility for conduit design and construction per current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.3.0 establishes basic requirements for electric distribution service, including developer-installed conduit when applicable. The required note must establish that: (1) the developer is responsible for designing and constructing conduit to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards, (2) the developer may be responsible for conductor installation if it is determined during design that developer funding is appropriate, (3) the developer must coordinate with other utilities to resolve conflicts, and (4) all costs are the applicant's responsibility. The current reference to 'Design Criteria Manual' (not outdated standards) is essential. Absence of this note creates ambiguity about developer responsibilities during construction.

findings.comment: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric service lines and associated infrastructure designed for the project, but no note on either Sheet 3 or Sheet 21 establishes developer responsibility for conduit and related infrastructure or requires compliance with current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. Add a note stating: 'Developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy (AE) Design Criteria Manual, including the installation of conductors if determined during the design process (prior to the issuance of the building permit) that the developer will fund the installation cost of the conductors. The Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve all conflicts. All costs associated with these improvements will be the responsibility of the applicant.'
applicableAreas: Sheet 3 Austin Energy Notes and Sheet 21 Electrical Design Plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly depicts underground electrical service with labeled 'Underground Electric Line' routing throughout the site, including transformer pads, pull boxes, electrical meters, and connections to eight buildings. This represents developer-designed and (presumably) developer-installed underground electrical infrastructure/conduit. Reviewed Sheet 3 Electric Notes (Blocks 8 and 14) and Sheet 21 Utility Notes (Block 6): Sheet 3 contains five notes but none address developer responsibility for conduit installation or infrastructure meeting Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. Sheet 21 Utility Notes specify only contractor verification requirements for existing utilities and private water/wastewater branch materials, with no mention of electrical conduit or developer responsibility for meeting electrical design standards.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.3.0 establishes developer responsibilities when underground electric service is being designed and installed. When a site plan shows developer-designed underground electrical infrastructure (as evidenced by the blue Underground Electric Line routing on Sheet 21), a note must be present establishing that the developer is responsible for designing and constructing conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards, including conductor installation costs if applicable. The absence of this note leaves unclear who is responsible for the infrastructure shown and fails to establish that the design must comply with current (not outdated) Austin Energy standards.

findings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that 'all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy.' The statute mandates approval, not merely preliminary review. The submission of a 'Preliminary' electrical design plan without an accompanying Austin Energy approval letter does not satisfy this requirement. The completeness check confirmation indicates that Austin Energy has reviewed the plans for completeness (procedural conformance), but approval (substantive compliance with design standards) is a separate and more rigorous determination. Without the formal approval letter and stamped site plan, this requirement is not satisfied.

findings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that sites requiring connection to Austin Energy must demonstrate compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1), which is adopted as part of the Utilities Criteria Manual. The grouping narrative states that 'all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy per LDC § 25-4-200' and this includes 'demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1)'. The electrical site plan is required to include UCM compliance notes, clearances dimensioned per UCM § 1.10.4, and equipment placement meeting UCM standards. The preliminary site plan shows electrical infrastructure but lacks documented references to specific Design Criteria Manual sections or evidence that the design has been evaluated against those standards. Without explicit UCM compliance documentation on the electrical site plan, the requirement to demonstrate compliance is not met.

Dimension clearances around transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4, specifying: (1) hot-stick use area (pad-locked sides) = 10 feet minimum clearance, (2) facing confined space (niche/vault) = 15 feet, (3) oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs = 20 feet, (4) adjacent brick/masonry building = 5 feet minimum, (5) adjacent non-brick/masonry building = 12 feet from oil-filled equipment. Add notes confirming equipment pad placement within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck access and specifying bollard requirements if within 4 feet. Transformer pads must be 2 feet from back of sidewalks.

However, the sheet contains no notes, callouts, or references demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM). findings.reasoning: The deficiency states 'Compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual not demonstrated.' The electrical design plan shows the proposed infrastructure layout but provides no evidence that this design was created with reference to UCM standards or that it meets those standards. Professional engineering practice and the code requirement for LDC § 25-4-200 compliance mandate that the design be explicitly documented as meeting the applicable design manual. Specificity is required: the sheet must show which UCM sections apply (e.g., § 1.10.4 for transformer clearances), what the requirements are (e.g., minimum 10-foot clearance from hot-stick use area), and how the proposed design meets them (dimensioned clearances and compliance notes). The absence of all this documentation is the deficiency.

findings.comment: Sheet 21 references an 'Electrical Vault Easement' but the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' Clarify whether the transformer is pad-mounted (compliant) or installed in a subsurface vault (non-compliant outside Network Area per UCM § 1.5.2.6). If a vault installation is proposed outside the Network Area, reconfigure to either: (a) pad-mounted transformer (clear to sky), or (b) specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, exterior access, proper ventilation, truck accessibility).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) visual analysis identified the presence of an 'Electrical Vault Easement' labeled near the southwest entrance of the site. The vision analysis noted this easement 'encompasses a transformer pad and pull box.' The site is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 in the MF-2 zoning district, which is not part of the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5). No Network Area service is indicated on the site plans. The term 'vault easement' is used in the labeling, but the transformer within it is described as a 'pad' (pad-mounted), which typically refers to aboveground equipment. However, the use of the term 'vault' in the easement designation creates ambiguity as to whether the transformer is truly a subsurface vault installation or simply an easement area serving a pad-mounted transformer.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.22 specifies 'Vaults or meter rooms proposed outside Network Area where vaults are not permitted' and applies only when 'vaults or subsurface/enclosed transformer rooms are proposed.' UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted (clear to sky) or installed in specialized niches meeting specific requirements (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3). The site is clearly outside the Network Area. The ambiguity arises from the sheet's reference to an 'Electrical Vault Easement' while the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' This terminology conflict must be clarified: if the transformer is truly installed in a subsurface vault, it violates UCM § 1.5.2.6. If it is a pad-mounted transformer within an easement area, it is compliant. The preliminary nature of the electrical plan and lack of detailed transformer installation specifications (normal pad-mounted vs. vault vs. niche configuration) prevent a definitive determination.

findings.comment: Transformer installation method and site location relative to Network Area require clarification. Confirm whether proposed installation near Building 8 is pad-mounted or vaulted. If vaulted, verify site location against Network Area Map (UCM § 1.11.5); vaults are permitted exclusively within Network Area. If outside Network Area and vault is proposed, verify specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, accessible from outside, proper ventilation, truck accessibility). Clarify 'Vault Easement' designation on electrical site plan.
applicableAreas: transformer installation near Building 8 (southwest portion of site)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (indicating pad-mount configuration per vision analysis). However, near Building 8 in the southwestern area, the plan also includes a label for 'Vault Easement,' which raises the question of whether a vault installation is being proposed in addition to or instead of a pad-mount transformer. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 notes this explicit 'Vault Easement' label in the bottom right area near the Bldg 8 transformer location. UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; vaults outside the Network Area are not permitted (vaults are only permitted exclusively within the Network Area boundaries per grouping narrative). The preliminary electrical site plan does not explicitly state whether a vault is proposed or whether the 'Vault Easement' is simply a property easement designation. The grouping narrative states that 'Network area determination requires cross-referencing the project address against the official Network Area Map at https://mcclibrary.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/codecontent/15312/483105/1-11-5.png, as this cannot be determined from site plans alone.' Thus, from the site plan alone, it cannot be confirmed: (1) whether a vault is actually being proposed, or (2) whether the site is within Network Area boundaries.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 states that transformer vaults are permitted exclusively within the Network Area boundaries. If the site is outside the Network Area and a vault is being proposed, this violates the requirement. The vision analysis found an explicit 'Vault Easement' labeled on Sheet 21, which suggests that some kind of vaulted or enclosed transformer installation may be planned. However, the same sheet labels transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (pad-mount). The ambiguity between the vault easement designation and the pad-mount labels, combined with the inability to verify Network Area status from site plans alone (per grouping instruction), creates an unclear status. If a vault is proposed outside the Network Area, this would be a clear violation; if only pad-mount installations are proposed, the vault easement may be a property easement that does not trigger this deficiency. The preliminary design stage may also explain the ambiguity.

findings.comment: Verify the site location relative to the Austin Energy Network Area Map (UCM § 1.11.5) at https://mcclibrary.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.com/codecontent/15312/483105/1-11-5.png. If the site is within the Network Area, confirm transformer installation is vault-type per UCM § 1.5.2.6. If outside the Network Area, confirm transformers are pad-mounted (as shown) or, if enclosed, demonstrate they meet specialized niche requirements: 35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, accessible from outside the building, proper ventilation, and truck accessibility per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four 'Electrical Transformer Pad' locations depicted as rectangular symbols. These appear to be pad-mounted transformers (clear-to-sky installation), not subsurface vaults or enclosed transformer rooms. The grouping states 'Only when vaults or subsurface/enclosed transformer rooms are proposed' and requires applicability assessment. UCM § 1.5.2.6 states 'Transformer Installation Requirements (vaults restricted to Network Area).' Pad-mounted transformers are permissible outside the Network Area. However, the Network Area status of the site at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 has not been verified from site plans or in the documentation. Without Network Area determination, and given that the transformers shown are pad-mounted (not vaults), this item appears to have limited applicability. However, if a vault installation were proposed, Network Area confirmation would be critical.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults exclusively to the Network Area. Outside the Network Area, only pad-mounted (clear-to-sky) transformers or specialized niches meeting specific requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, accessible from outside, proper ventilation, truck accessibility per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3) are permitted. The site plan shows pad-mounted transformers, which are compliant outside the Network Area. The Network Area determination cannot be verified from site plans. If the site is actually within the Network Area and the transformers should be vaults instead, or if specialized niches are being proposed, this would need verification. Without the Network Area map cross-reference, definitive assessment is unclear.

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations shown on Sheet 21 do not include dimensioned clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, or other features. Add dimensions to all transformer pads showing clearances to: adjacent buildings (minimum 10-15 feet per UCM § 1.10.4), parking/traffic areas (maximum 6 feet, with bollards if less than 4 feet), windows and doors (minimum 5-12 feet per orientation), and fire escapes/stairs (minimum 20 feet if oil-filled equipment). Verify all clearances meet Table 1.10.4 requirements.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts three electrical transformer pads: one west of Building 2/northwest of Building 8 near the western property line and street entrance; one between Buildings 8 and 6 in the central driveway/alley area; and one east of Building 5 near the eastern property boundary. The vision analysis confirmed: 'There are no specific dimensions (e.g., distance lines with measurements) provided on this sheet to indicate the exact clearances from the transformer pads to the buildings, doors, or windows.' No clearance dimensions are shown from any transformer pad to: adjacent buildings (Buildings 2, 5, 6, 8), building doors or windows, parking areas, sidewalks, or fire escapes. No dimensions verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requirements: 10 feet minimum for hot-stick use area to adjacent building, 15 feet if facing confined space, 20 feet from oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs, 5 feet lateral or 12 feet vertical from windows/doors, 6 feet maximum from parking/traffic areas for truck access, or bollard locations if within 4 feet of parking.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.27 specifies 'Proposed buildings, bike racks, or site features do not meet required safety clearances from Austin Energy facilities' and applies 'Only when site is adjacent to Austin Energy facilities requiring safety clearances.' The grouping instruction requires 'Check: Site plan dimensions, Austin Energy equipment locations (transformers, vaults), clearance compliance per Table 1.10.4 (10 ft to 20 ft depending on configuration).' UCM § 1.10.4 establishes specific minimum clearances from pad-mounted transformers and distribution equipment based on configuration and adjacent features. The site has three transformer pads shown on the electrical plan with buildings, parking, and sidewalks in close proximity. Without dimensioned clearances on the site plan, it cannot be verified that any of the proposed transformer locations comply with the safety clearance requirements of UCM § 1.10.4. The preliminary nature of the design and absence of clearance documentation means compliance is unverified.

Coordinate with Austin Energy Transmission C&M (per Sheet 3 Block 20 note: contact Andrew Perez 512-505-7153) to confirm building locations maintain required clearances from transmission poles/structures. Add clearance dimensions to site and electrical plans showing compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 and transmission facility requirements (25 feet from transmission structures, proper staging area clearances, etc.). Include Austin Energy clearance verification documentation on final plans.
applicableAreas: proposed buildings and site features adjacent to transmission facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 20 contains detailed 'Electric Transmission Notes' with 16 items specifying clearance requirements and restrictions for transmission facilities on the property. These notes reference no digging/grading within 25 feet of transmission structures, minimum clearances from aerial equipment and staging areas, road/driveway load requirements for easement areas, and prohibitions on structures in transmission easement. The transmission notes indicate transmission facilities are present and active on or immediately adjacent to the site. However, Sheet 21 (Electrical Site Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) do not show clearance dimensions between the proposed buildings (Bldgs 1-8) and transmission structures or indicate how the 25-foot no-dig/no-grade clearance has been maintained around any transmission poles or structures. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 found transformer pads and buildings depicted but no clearance annotations or dimensions between buildings and transmission facilities. The site plan does not show transmission pole or structure locations, making it impossible to verify from the documents whether buildings and site features meet the required clearances (e.g., 10 ft for hot-stick use area per UCM § 1.10.4 Table, 20 ft for oil-filled equipment to fire escapes per grouping narrative).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 establishes minimum clearances from Austin Energy equipment. Sheet 3 Block 20 demonstrates that transmission facilities are present on/adjacent to the site, requiring compliance with transmission facility clearances (25 feet no-dig, 20 feet for aerial equipment, etc.). Sheet 21 does not show transmission structure locations or clearance dimensions between buildings and transmission infrastructure. Without documented verification that buildings and site features maintain required clearances from transmission facilities, compliance cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Add clearance dimensions to the electrical site plan for each of the four transformer pad locations per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4. For each pad, dimension the clearances to: adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, pedestrian walkways, fencing, mail kiosks, and any other site features. Specify clearances in feet (minimum 5-20 feet depending on configuration). Indicate bollard locations if pads are within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. Specify sidewalk setback (minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalk) and truck access route (minimum 6 feet adjacent clearance). Add notes confirming compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads and clearances to buildings, parking, and site features
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations: (1) northwest corner near Building 1, (2) between Buildings 2 and 8, (3) between Buildings 4 and 5, and (4) between Buildings 6 and 7. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts these transformer pads in relation to buildings and parking areas. However, visual analysis of Sheet 21 found 'absolutely no dimensions, dashed clearance lines, or safety zones drawn or annotated around any of this equipment.' Similarly, analysis of Sheet 9 found 'no explicit clearance or setback dimensions shown between the Transformer Pad and the adjacent buildings, parking areas, or other site features.' UCM § 1.10.4 establishes specific minimum clearances for pad-mounted transformers and distribution vaults ranging from 5 feet to 20 feet depending on configuration and adjacent features.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 establishes mandatory minimum clearances from pad-mounted transformers: (1) Hot-stick use area (pad-locked sides) to adjacent building/structure: minimum 10 feet; (2) Hot-stick use area facing confined space (niche/vault): minimum 15 feet; (3) Oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs: minimum 20 feet horizontal/radial clearance; (4) Adjacent to brick/masonry building (2-hour fire rating): minimum 5 feet from side edges; (5) Adjacent to non-brick/masonry building: minimum 12 feet from oil-filled equipment; (6) Windows, doors, ventilating ducts: 5 feet lateral or 12 feet vertical if lateral less than 5 feet; (7) Equipment pads within 6 feet from parking/traffic areas must have truck access, and bollards required if within 4 feet; (8) Transformer pads must be 2 feet from back of sidewalks. The electrical site plan must show all four transformer locations with clearance dimensions to all adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, walkways, and fencing to demonstrate compliance. The absence of any clearance dimensions is the deficiency.

findings.comment: Electrical meters are scattered across multiple building locations throughout the site rather than grouped at a common location. Meters shown on Bldg. 1, Bldg. 2, Bldg. 5, Bldg. 8 areas, and spaces between buildings - separated by 60+ feet, exceeding the 20-foot maximum. No disconnects are shown on the plan. Applicant must group all meters and disconnects at a common location within 20 feet separation and line of sight.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters distributed across multiple locations throughout the site, with meters located adjacent to different buildings: north side of Bldg. 1/3, space between Bldg. 2 and Bldg. 4, east side of Bldg. 5, west side of Bldg. 8, and space between Bldg. 6 and Bldg. 7. This represents at least 5-6 separate meter locations spread across the entire site rather than grouped in one common location. The plan does not label or depict any disconnect switches or show grouping of meters and disconnects at a single location. No disconnects are explicitly shown anywhere on the sheet. The scale is 1" = 20', which means the distances between these scattered meter locations would be approximately 60-100+ feet apart based on the spatial distribution visible in the drawing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires that meters and disconnects be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and line of sight. The site plan shows meters scattered across multiple buildings throughout the 2.16-acre site - a configuration that cannot comply with the 20-foot maximum distance requirement. The applicant has failed to demonstrate that meters and disconnects are grouped at a common location or that the 20-foot maximum separation is met. The absence of any labeled disconnects on the electrical design sheet, combined with the scattered meter locations, constitutes non-compliance with the grouping and distance requirements.

findings.comment: Meters and disconnects not grouped together with documented separation distance. Identify and label all electrical disconnects on the site plan. Show distance measurements between meters and disconnects, documenting that separation does not exceed 20 feet and that meters and disconnects are within line of sight. Verify grouping in common location per UCM § 1.9.3.1(I).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows 'Electrical Meters' labeled on the exteriors of the eight buildings (noted near units 102/103, 201/202, 301/302, 401/402, 501/502, 603, 701/702, 801/802). However, 'Electrical Disconnects' are NOT explicitly labeled or identified anywhere on the sheet. No dimension lines or distance measurements are shown between the meter locations and any disconnect locations. No distance verification is possible to confirm meters and disconnects are grouped together or that separation does not exceed the 20-foot maximum. Pull boxes are shown but cannot be confirmed as disconnects.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires that meters and disconnects be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and within line of sight. Sheet 21 shows meters but does not identify disconnects as distinct labeled elements. Without both meters and disconnects identified and dimensioned, compliance with the grouping, separation distance, and line-of-sight requirements cannot be verified. The applicant has not provided sufficient detail to demonstrate compliance.

findings.comment: Meters and transformers are not grouped in a common location and are separated by more than 20 feet in multiple instances, exceeding the maximum separation allowed. Some meter/transformer pairs may lack adequate line of sight. Reconfigure electrical infrastructure to group meters and disconnects in common locations within 20 feet of each transformer, with clear line of sight maintained between all paired equipment.
applicableAreas: Transformers 1, 2, and 3 locations; building meter locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows three electrical transformer pads and six meter locations (on building exteriors). Vision analysis measured separation distances between transformer pads and associated meter banks: Transformer 1 to meters range 30-50 feet; Transformer 2 to meters range 10-150 feet; Transformer 3 to meters range 60-150 feet. The transformers are located in standalone pads in easements/common areas, while meters are mounted on building walls. These two types of equipment are not grouped together in common locations. Some meter/transformer pairs may have line-of-sight obstructions created by building corners.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires meters and disconnects to be grouped together in a common location, with maximum 20-foot separation, and within line of sight of each other. The separation distances measured on the electrical plan exceed the 20-foot maximum threshold for multiple transformer/meter combinations. Additionally, transformers and meters are not grouped in a common location but are dispersed across the site (transformers in separate pads; meters on individual building exteriors). The requirement for line of sight is potentially not met where building structures create obstructions between transformer pads and associated meters.

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations are shown on electrical design plan but distances to parking/traffic areas are not dimensioned. Bollard protection details are not shown. Verification required that all pads are either more than 4 feet from parking/traffic or that 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards are detailed per UCM § 1.10.4.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations near parking areas
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design) shows 4 transformer pads located at: west side near entrance drive (landscape island), southwest area near entrance (landscape island), east side central area (between Bldg. 4 and 5), and southeast area (between Bldg. 6 and 7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 10 surface parking spaces and 78 garage parking spaces, with surface parking primarily concentrated in the central entrance area and along the main drive aisles. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 indicated that 'None of the transformer pads appear to be within 4 feet of designated parking stalls' based on visual inspection, but the analysis noted the lack of explicit distance dimensions on the plan. Without precise distance measurements between the transformer pads and the nearest parking stalls/traffic areas, and without bollard details shown on the electrical plan, it cannot be definitively confirmed whether the 4-foot minimum clearance requirement is met at all locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that pad-mounted equipment within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas must have 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards per AE Design equipment pad details. The site plan shows transformer locations and parking areas but does not provide dimensioned distances from pads to parking/traffic edges. While vision analysis suggested pads are not immediately adjacent to parking stalls, the lack of explicit distance callouts and the absence of any bollard details on the electrical plan create ambiguity. The requirement applies if pads are within 4 feet, but precise verification requires either: (1) detailed measurements on the plan, or (2) explicit notation that clearance exceeds 4 feet. No bollard details are shown on Sheet 21.

findings.comment: Bollards not shown when equipment pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas. Add 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards around each transformer pad per Austin Energy Design equipment pad details. Show bollard locations and spacing on site plan with reference to AE Design standard details.
applicableAreas: Middle areas adjacent to drive aisles
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads (dashed rectangles) at locations middle-left (west of Bldg 1), bottom-left (west of Bldg 8), middle-right (between Bldgs 4-5), and bottom-right (between Bldgs 6-7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows these transformer pads immediately adjacent to internal drive aisles (parking and traffic areas). No bollards, protective barriers, or any protective posts are shown around any of the transformer pad locations. No callouts or notes reference bollard requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details when pad-mounted equipment is within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. The transformer pads shown on Sheet 9 are positioned directly adjacent to internal drive aisles and parking areas, placing them well within the 4-foot proximity threshold. The absence of bollards on all four transformer pads is a deficiency. Bollards are essential to protect pad-mounted transformers from vehicle damage.

findings.comment: Transformer 3 is located within 4 feet of surface parking and drive aisle but no bollards are shown. Provide 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollard posts per AE Design equipment pad details, positioned to protect the transformer pad from vehicular impact and maintain required clearances.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) depicts three transformer pads. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) confirms that Transformer 3 (located between Buildings 6 and 7 on the east side of the site) is positioned within a paved area with surface parking spaces to the northwest and the main concrete drive aisle immediately adjacent. The transformer is clearly within 4 feet of parking and traffic circulation areas. Sheet 21 shows the transformer pad symbol but contains no indication of bollards, protective posts, or any barrier/protection device at this location. No detail sheet (Sheets 22-39) provides bollard details for this transformer location.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details for pad-mounted equipment located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. Transformer 3 is clearly within 4 feet of surface parking spaces and a paved drive aisle. The absence of bollards shown on the electrical plan or detail sheets indicates this requirement has not been addressed. Bollards are required to protect the transformer pad from vehicular impact and to maintain safe clearance from traffic.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees are planted within 5 lateral feet of underground electric equipment due to lack of electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads and underground electric lines throughout site. Tree canopy symbols overlap with facilities at multiple locations. Sheet 31 does not show electrical infrastructure. Proposed trees listed on Sheet 35 cannot be located relative to underground equipment without electrical infrastructure on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot determine whether proposed trees are within 5 feet of underground equipment due to lack of electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan. This is a fundamental information coordination problem preventing compliance verification.

findings.comment: Proposed trees on the western property boundary are positioned directly on or within 5 lateral feet of the underground electric line. Remove trees from this zone or relocate the underground electric line to achieve minimum 5-foot clearance.
applicableAreas: Western property boundary street yard area
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) at 1"=20' scale shows proposed trees (marked with 'M' and 'ST' symbols indicating mitigation and street yard trees) positioned directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the underground electric line marked '-E-' running along the western property boundary. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) confirms underground electric lines route along this boundary. The vision analysis explicitly stated: 'Several tree symbols (tagged 'M' and 'ST') are drawn physically overlapping or immediately adjacent to the '-E-' line. Based on the 1"=20' scale, these proposed trees appear to be placed directly on top of, or within 5 feet of, this underground line.' This indicates violation of the 0-5 foot no-tree zone required for underground electric equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits any trees within 5 lateral feet of underground electric equipment (conduits, duct banks, cables, vaults, manholes, transformers). The landscape plan shows trees positioned directly over or immediately adjacent to the documented underground electric line. The visual positioning demonstrated in the plan drawings indicates non-compliance with the absolute 5-foot clearance requirement. This is not a case of approximate positioning that could be verified in the field—the plan itself shows the violation.

findings.comment: Trees planted within 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment require root barrier details showing minimum 4 feet depth and positioning 5 feet from equipment edge per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Root barrier details not provided and electrical infrastructure not shown on Landscape Plan.
applicableAreas: Trees within 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows tree canopy symbols positioned at various distances from transformer pads and underground electric lines. However, Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) does not depict any transformer pads, underground electric lines, or pull boxes. Sheet 37 provides standard tree details but contains NO root barrier detail. Cannot verify which proposed trees are within 5-20 foot zone requiring root barriers.
findings.reasoning: Trees within 5-20 feet of underground equipment require root barriers (minimum 4-foot depth, positioned 5 feet from equipment). Cannot verify compliance without: (1) electrical infrastructure shown on Landscape Plan, and (2) root barrier details provided. The lack of coordination between electrical and landscape plans prevents assessment of proposed tree clearances.

findings.comment: Provide root barrier construction details (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment edge) for all trees planted within 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. Include typical cross-sections on detail sheets and cross-reference on landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within 5-20 feet of underground electric equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 31 shows proposed trees and shrubs throughout the site near underground electric infrastructure. Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) provides standard tree planting details (Standard 610S-4 protection detail, tree planting pit specifications) but contains no root barrier construction details meeting UCM § 1.10.10.4 requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned exactly 5 feet from equipment edge). The plant list on Sheet 35 identifies 12 trees being planted throughout the property near electric facilities, but no detail sheets show root barrier specifications coordinated with underground electric locations. The only root-related details on Sheet 37 describe tree protection during construction and standard planting practices, not UCM-compliant root barriers for electrical equipment protection.
findings.reasoning: For trees planted between 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment, UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers minimum 4 feet deep, positioned exactly 5 feet from the equipment edge. The landscape documentation does not provide these specific root barrier details for any trees positioned in this clearance zone. Standard tree planting details do not satisfy the specialized root barrier requirement for proximity to electrical infrastructure. The lack of any reference to UCM root barrier specifications in the landscape notes or details indicates non-compliance.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees are planted within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted electric equipment due to lack of transformer pad coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 identifies four to five transformer pads with tree canopy symbols overlapping multiple pads (Northwest 0 ft, Central-West 0 ft, Southwest 0 ft, Central-East/South overlapping corners). Sheet 31 does not show transformer pads. Proposed trees from Sheet 35 cannot be located relative to transformer pads without electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot verify whether proposed trees are within 10 feet of transformer pads without showing transformer locations on Landscape Plan for correlation with proposed plantings.

findings.comment: Overlay transformer pad locations (from Sheet 21) on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and show 10-foot clearance zone around each pad. Verify all proposed trees and shrubs are outside these zones, or obtain Austin Energy written approval for any trees within this clearance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations throughout site (5 pads identified on Sheet 21)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 5 transformer pads positioned at specific locations: adjacent to Bldg. 1 (near entrance), adjacent to Bldg. 2, in courtyard between Bldgs. 4/5, in courtyard between Bldgs. 6/7, and adjacent to Bldg. 8. However, Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show these transformer pad locations or their 10-foot clearance zones. The landscape plan shows multiple proposed trees throughout the site without reference to transformer locations, making it impossible to verify that trees are kept outside the 10-foot minimum clearance zone required by UCM § 1.10.10.4.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted transformers or electric equipment. The applicant must demonstrate compliance by showing transformer locations and clearance zones on the landscape plan. The absence of transformer pads on the landscape plan means the applicant has not provided the minimum required documentation to verify compliance. This is a coordination failure between electrical design and landscape design.

findings.comment: License agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement required if landscaping is within electric easement areas. Electric easement boundaries are not shown on Landscape Plan, and license agreement documentation is not evident in current submittal.
findings.observation: Plat (Sheet 2) shows 5-foot electric easements along northern and southern boundaries. Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) does not show electric easement boundaries. No license agreement documentation evident in current submittal. Grouping guidance notes license agreements are administrative documents that may not be attached at early stages but must be verified before occupancy.
findings.reasoning: If landscaping within electric easements, UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Plans do not show easement boundaries coordinated with Landscape Plan, and agreement documentation not evident in current submittal. Unclear whether landscaping is within easements and whether agreement has been obtained.

findings.comment: Obtain a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing any landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings within electric easement areas. Provide executed copy with final site plan submittal or reference execution in a plan note.
findings.observation: Review of all available site plan documents and supplementary documents (including Master Comment Report) reveals no executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement for landscaping, trees, or irrigation within electric easement areas. The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section) references Austin Energy preliminary design requirements including UCM § 1.10.10.3, which requires a License Agreement before installing landscaping in electric easement areas. No such agreement is attached to the plans, referenced in any plan notes, or mentioned in any accompanying documentation. Sheet 31 shows trees proposed in areas where electric easements exist (per property records), but there is no evidence of the required license agreement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires that 'a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is required before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings that might obstruct access to Austin Energy facilities within electric easement areas. The agreement must be obtained and filed before the activity occurs.' The absence of this license agreement documentation on or with the site plan is a deficiency. While license agreements are administrative documents that may be obtained after plan approval, the applicant must provide evidence that the requirement has been addressed (or provide the executed agreement).

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether shrubs are within 10 lateral feet of access door side of pad-mounted equipment due to lack of transformer pad coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 35 lists shrubs to be planted. Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations. Sheet 31 does not show pads or their access door orientations. Cannot identify which side of each pad is access side without electrical infrastructure on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot verify whether shrubs are within 10 feet of access door side of pads without transformer pad locations and orientations shown on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Show transformer pad locations and access door orientations on the landscape plan. Mark 10-foot clearance zones on access door sides and verify no shrubs are positioned within these zones.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads with their locations but does not clearly indicate access door orientations. Sheet 31 shows shrubs and low vegetation symbols throughout the site (marked PM=Dwarf Palmetto, MB=Big Muhly, GC=Gulf Muhly, LS=Texas Sage, MC=Dwarf Wax Myrtle per Sheet 35) but does not show transformer pad locations or access door sides to verify 10-foot clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies that no shrubs be planted within 10 lateral feet of the access door side (hot-stick-use area/pad-locked side) of pad-mounted equipment. Without transformer locations and their access door orientations shown on the landscape plan, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether shrubs are within 5 lateral feet of non-access sides of pad-mounted equipment due to lack of transformer pad coordination and orientation on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 35 lists shrubs to be planted. Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations. Sheet 31 does not show transformer pads or their non-access side orientations. Cannot verify shrub clearances without electrical infrastructure shown on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot identify non-access sides of pads or measure shrub clearances without transformer pad locations and orientations shown on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Show transformer pad locations and identify access vs. non-access sides on the landscape plan. Verify shrubs are at least 5 feet from non-access sides.
findings.observation: Same as EL-16.15: transformer pad locations and orientations not shown on landscape plan, preventing verification of 5-foot shrub clearance on non-access sides.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires minimum 5-foot clearance from non-access sides of pad-mounted equipment. Landscape plan must show transformer locations and orientations to verify this clearance.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees are positioned between transformer access doors and drivable access routes due to lack of electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows driveways and access. Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations. Sheet 31 shows proposed trees but does not show transformer pads or access routes. Existing tree canopies on Sheet 21 appear near pads, but proposed new trees cannot be located relative to access corridors without electrical coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot determine if proposed trees block equipment access without transformer locations and access routes shown on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Show transformer locations and identify access doors on the landscape plan. Verify that no trees block the route from each transformer access door to the nearest drivable surface (street, alley, or parking area).
applicableAreas: Space between transformer access doors and drivable surfaces
findings.observation: Transformer pad locations not shown on landscape plan, preventing verification of tree-free access routes from transformer access doors to drivable surfaces (streets, alleys, parking areas).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees between the access door of pad-mounted equipment and drivable surfaces used for truck access. This zone must remain clear for bucket truck positioning during hot-stick work. Verification requires transformer locations and access routes to be shown on the landscape plan.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees block truck access to transformers or equipment set-up areas due to lack of electrical infrastructure and access route coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer locations throughout site. Sheet 31 shows proposed trees but does not coordinate with transformer locations or equipment access requirements. Cannot assess whether proposed plantings obstruct access without electrical infrastructure shown on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot verify access compliance without showing transformer locations and required turning radii/access clearances coordinated with proposed tree locations on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Show transformer locations and required truck access routes on the landscape plan. Verify no trees block access lanes or turning radii required for Austin Energy service vehicles (typical 40-50 ft turning radius for bucket trucks).
applicableAreas: Transformer locations and access routes throughout site
findings.observation: Transformer pad locations from Sheet 21 and access routes from Sheet 9 (Site Plan) are not overlaid on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Without this coordination, it cannot be verified that proposed trees do not obstruct access routes or turning radii for bucket trucks used to service transformers and Austin Energy equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping must not restrict Austin Energy personnel and equipment access. The landscape plan must show transformer locations and access requirements to demonstrate compliance. The absence of this coordination indicates non-compliance with the access requirement.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees block access to or overhang electric vaults due to lack of vault/manhole coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows pull boxes and transformers. Sheet 31 does not show pull boxes, vaults, or manhole locations. If subsurface electric equipment exists, its locations not depicted on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot verify tree canopy clearance from vault lids without vault locations shown on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Show vault locations on the landscape plan with tree locations and estimated mature canopy spreads. Verify no trees are positioned to create overhead obstruction of vault covers/lids.
findings.observation: Vault locations shown on Sheet 21 are not shown on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Vault covers/lids must remain clear of tree canopy for operational access, but without vault locations on the landscape plan, this cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires that vaults remain accessible for personnel and equipment. Trees positioned over vault covers prevent access operations. The landscape plan must show vault locations and tree canopy spreads to verify compliance.

findings.comment: Austin Energy overhead and underground facilities are not shown on landscape plans. Landscape Plan does not show transformer pads, pull boxes, or underground electric line routing shown on Electrical Design Plan, preventing verification of clearance compliance.
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) was analyzed for electrical infrastructure. Vision analysis explicitly determined: 'There are **no** underground electric lines (typically labeled -UGE-), public utility easements (PUE), or specific electric easements visually depicted or labeled anywhere on this landscape plan sheet.' Sheet 21 shows four to five transformer pads and underground lines marked '- E -' throughout site, but Landscape Plan does not include any of these facilities.
findings.reasoning: Electrical infrastructure must be shown on Landscape Plan to verify clearance compliance. The absence of transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground duct banks on the Landscape Plan is a coordination failure that prevents verification of clearances for EL-16.1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21 and other facility-specific items.

findings.comment: Overlay all electric facilities from Sheet 21 onto the landscape plan (Sheet 31), including transformer pads, underground electric lines (with 5-foot and broader clearance zones clearly marked), pull boxes, utility poles, vault locations, electric easement boundaries, and transmission easement boundaries. This overlay is essential for verifying compliance with all vegetation clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Entire site - all utility and landscape areas
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows all electric facilities: transformer pads, underground electric lines (marked '-E-'), pull boxes, meter banks, utility poles, vault easement, and various utility easements. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show any of these electric facilities. The landscape plan shows only landscape elements (trees, shrubs, paving, contours, irrigation notes) without any reference to electrical infrastructure locations. This prevents all clearance verifications required by checklist items EL-16.1 through EL-16.21.
findings.reasoning: Proper coordination between electrical and landscape design requires that electric facilities be shown on the landscape plan at the same scale. This allows visual verification of clearance zones, easement boundaries, and access routes. The absence of electrical infrastructure on the landscape plan is a fundamental coordination failure that prevents the reviewer from verifying compliance with any of the electric facility proximity requirements. This is not optional—it is a standard requirement for site plan review.

findings.comment: Plan documentation required: (1) identification of existing conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) on overhead lines; (2) dimension annotations showing minimum 15-foot radial clearance from buildings and other customer facilities to the outside conductor of distribution primary and neutral conductors; (3) clarification of whether existing lines are distribution or transmission voltage.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 in relation to distribution primary and neutral conductors on western and southern boundaries
findings.observation: Sheets 4, 9, and 21 confirm existing overhead electric (O.H.U.L.) facilities adjacent to the property. However, the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) are not labeled or identified on any plans. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies specifically to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No dimension annotations show radial clearances from any building or customer facility to these conductors. No plan notes identify whether the existing lines are distribution (voltage <60kV) or transmission (voltage ≥60kV), and no conductor types are labeled.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (including buildings) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of distribution primary and neutral conductors. Without identification of conductor types and without dimension annotations showing radial clearances from buildings to the conductors, compliance cannot be verified. The 15-foot clearance measurement requires identification of which conductors are primary/neutral vs. secondary, and this distinction is absent from the plans.

findings.comment: No registered surveyor proximity survey provided showing distances from proposed parking areas and site features to outside conductor of OHE line. Provide proximity survey documenting radial clearances from all customer facilities.
applicableAreas: Parking areas and site features on southern portion near OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 shows existing OHE line with associated utility poles. Sheet 9 shows the same OHE line routing along the southern boundary with parking areas, driveways, and site improvements in close proximity. The plans do not specify whether the overhead line serves distribution or transmission function, nor are the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) identified. No dimension annotations are provided showing distances from site facilities (parking, driveways, retaining walls) to the outside conductor. A registered surveyor proximity survey documenting existing and proposed facility locations relative to the OHE line is not provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (parking, driveways, site improvements) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors of overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The distinction between distribution and transmission affects the applicable clearance standard. Without a registered surveyor proximity survey showing the conductor type, voltage level, and radial distances from all proposed facilities, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant has not submitted this required documentation.

findings.comment: Building elevation or section exhibits are required showing all projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, canopies) with dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of projections, demonstrating both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances.
applicableAreas: Building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, roofs) for Buildings 1-8
findings.observation: Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows buildings 1-8 with footprints and general layout, but no section views or elevation drawings depicting building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) relative to overhead electric conductors. No surveyed conductor elevations are provided. Building architectural details or elevations showing projection dimensions are not included in the 39-sheet set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires building projections to maintain both (1) 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and (2) 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors. Without section views or elevation drawings showing the vertical and horizontal relationships between building projections and the overhead conductors, and without surveyed conductor elevation data, compliance with these requirements cannot be verified. Buildings can only be shown in plan view without cross-sections showing their height relative to conductor height.

findings.comment: No building elevation or profile sheets provided showing vertical clearances from Building 8 roof and overhangs to overhead electric line. Provide engineered building elevations with surveyed conductor elevation and clearance dimension annotations.
applicableAreas: Building 8 roof and overhang areas adjacent to southern OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows Building 8 positioned adjacent to the southern boundary where the OHE line is routed. However, no building elevation or section views are provided on the site plan set that show the roof elevation of Building 8, any rooftop projections (overhangs, canopies, HVAC penetrations, vents), or their vertical clearance from the overhead line. No profile sections are provided showing the relationship between building projections and the conductor location. Building height is specified as 36'-1" but the finished floor and roof elevations are not dimensioned relative to the OHE line.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance (horizontal) and implies vertical clearance verification for any building projections.
