Without profile or elevation sheets showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the building roof/overhang elevation dimensioned relative to that conductor, compliance cannot be determined. The applicant must provide elevation views with clearance dimensions for all building projections near the overhead line.

findings.comment: Provide registered surveyor field survey data documenting: (1) surveyed elevations of overhead electric conductors at mid-span locations above buildings, driveways, and parking areas; (2) calculated vertical clearances from the lowest point of conductors (including attachments) to the highest points of buildings, roof projections, driveways, and parking surfaces, demonstrating compliance with minimum clearance thresholds (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground for buildings, 16-18 feet for driveways/parking, others as applicable); (3) marked survey points and elevation measurements with registered surveyor certification.
applicableAreas: All proposed driveways, parking areas, buildings, and site features with potential vertical clearance concerns from overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Overhead electric lines (O.H.U.L.) are shown on existing survey (Sheet 4) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) but NO surveyed conductor elevation data is provided anywhere on the 39-sheet site plan set. Buildings have FFEs ranging from 683' to 687.5' (Sheet 9, 11), but overhead conductor heights are not documented. Driveways and parking pads have grading elevations shown (Sheet 11), but no profile sections with surveyed mid-span clearance data verify vertical clearances meet requirements. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted that buildings are approximately 26-30 feet horizontally from overhead lines on the western boundary—this distance is close enough that vertical clearance verification (mid-span clearance) should be provided per UCM § 1.10.3 guidance for situations where 'clearance appears marginal or insufficient.' No registered surveyor data confirming mid-span clearance is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'survey by registered surveyor showing pole locations and mid-span clearances not provided when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements.' The grouping guidance states that when vertical clearance 'appears marginal or insufficient based on site plan data,' registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is required. The site plan does not provide surveyed conductor elevations, making it impossible to calculate vertical clearances from building FFEs and driveway grades to conductor height. Furthermore, the presence of structures within approximately 26-30 feet horizontally of overhead lines, combined with the absence of conducted elevator data, suggests that clearance verification is required but not provided. This is a deficiency: applicant has failed to provide surveyor data for mid-span clearances.

findings.comment: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements provided despite buildings and parking areas being positioned adjacent to overhead electric line. Provide licensed surveyor measurements of overhead conductor heights and clearances to all proposed structures and site features.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking and driveway areas adjacent to southern OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 shows an existing OHE line with utility poles routed across the property. Sheet 9 shows Buildings 7 and 8 and parking/driveway areas positioned immediately adjacent to this overhead line (on southern boundary). Without seeing surveyed conductor elevations or documented clearance measurements, the vertical clearance appears potentially marginal—the minimum required clearances (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 16-18-foot for driveways, 7.5-foot for parking) cannot be visually confirmed from plan-view drawings alone. No mid-span clearance survey data from a registered surveyor is provided to document actual measured clearances.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements or when visual determination is insufficient. Given the close proximity of buildings and parking to the OHE line shown on the plans, and the complete absence of vertical clearance documentation, a registered surveyor's measurement is required to verify compliance. The applicant has not provided this required survey work.

findings.comment: Utility poles present along overhead electric line at property boundaries. Landscape plan shows trees positioned near poles but provides no clearance dimensions to verify 10-foot minimum distance from tree trunk to pole.
applicableAreas: western site boundary where utility poles are located along overhead electric line
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (electrical plan) shows existing overhead electric line (OHE) running north-south along the western boundary with utility poles represented by small circular symbols. Sheet 31 (landscape plan) depicts the OHE line with poles along the southern boundary and trees positioned along the boundaries where poles are located. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 states: 'several proposed trees positioned along the southern boundary that appear to be placed directly underneath or extremely close to the overhead electric line' and notes 'poles are positioned along this OHE line.' However, no clearance dimensions are provided on the landscape plan documenting the distance from tree trunk center to the nearest utility pole.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 establishes a 10-foot lateral distance minimum from tree trunk center to any overhead electric utility pole. Utility poles are documented on both the electrical plan and landscape plan along the overhead line. Trees are shown on the landscape plan positioned near these boundaries where poles are present. However, without clearance dimensions on the landscape plan, it cannot be confirmed whether the proposed and retained trees maintain the required 10-foot minimum distance from the pole. The vision tool noted trees appearing 'directly underneath or extremely close to' the OHE line, suggesting possible violations, but precise distances cannot be verified from available evidence.

findings.comment: Seven mitigation trees are shown with trunk centers plotted directly on the overhead electric line where utility poles are located, placing them within the prohibited 10-foot clearance zone from utility poles.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts seven (7) mitigation trees (marked 'M' designation) plotted with their trunk centers positioned directly at the overhead electric (OHE) line running along the southern property boundary. Vision analysis confirmed these tree symbols intersect the OHE utility line with zero (0) feet lateral distance measured. Two utility pole symbols (circles with crosses) are shown at the western and eastern ends of this OHE line. Trees are shown directly adjacent to or overlapping these pole locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of any electric utility pole (measured from trunk center to pole). The landscape plan shows trees with trunk centers plotted at approximately 0 feet from the utility line where poles are located, which is well within the 10-foot prohibited zone. This represents a direct violation of the pole clearance requirement. The vision tool's examination of the plan found no dimension callouts that would indicate these trees are actually set back to compliant distances.

findings.comment: Plant legend on landscape plan does not identify species of trees proposed near overhead electric facilities, and plant schedule does not reference ECM Appendix F utility-compatible (UC) designations. Field verification of proper species installation cannot be performed.
applicableAreas: landscape plan and plant schedule area
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (landscape plan) includes a plant legend identifying tree types by abbreviation (SY=Street Yard, PL=Parking Lot, P=Parking Buffer, M=Mitigation) but does not indicate species identification or mature height specifications. Sheet 35 (plant schedule) provides a plant list with species names and botanical names: Live Oak (Quercus Virginiana), Cedar Elm (Ulmus Crassifolia), Texas Mountain Laurel (Sophora Secundiflora), Mexican Redbud (Cercis Canadensis var. Mexicana), and various shrubs and groundcovers. However, the plant legend on the landscape plan does not cross-reference these species to allow field verification during plant inspection. The plant schedule specifies container size and caliper at planting but not mature height, and does not indicate utility-compatible (UC) designation from ECM Appendix F.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, when trees are proposed near electric facilities, the landscape plan and plant legend must identify the species of all trees near utilities to allow field verification during construction that the correct species have been planted and to verify compliance with utility-compatibility requirements per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Sheet 31 shows trees with symbols (SY, PL, P, M designations) but the plant legend does not identify which species corresponds to each symbol location. This prevents a field inspector from confirming that the correct species have been planted at each location. Additionally, neither the landscape plan nor plant schedule documents the utility-compatible (UC) status required by ECM Appendix F for species proposed within utility clearance zones.

findings.comment: The plant legend on the landscape plan identifies the seven OHE-line trees only by functional designation (M = mitigation tree) without specifying species. Specific species must be identified for electric utility clearance verification.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows seven trees positioned along the OHE line with only the 'M' (mitigation tree) functional designation in the legend. While Sheet 35 provides a plant schedule listing four tree species to be planted (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), the specific species of each of the seven trees shown on the OHE line cannot be determined from the landscape plan. The plant schedule symbols are defined in Sheet 35 but are not callout-labeled on the landscape drawing to identify which species corresponds to each tree location.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Reviewer Convention and common violation patterns (species misidentification), trees planted near electric facilities must be positively identified by species so their utility-compatibility status can be verified against ECM Appendix F. The landscape plan fails to provide species identification for the specific trees shown near the OHE line, making it impossible to verify whether they meet utility-compatible requirements or comply with size restrictions.

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows overhead electric line and trees positioned near utility infrastructure, but provides no clearance dimensions, distance annotations, or cross-reference methodology to verify tree positions meet required setbacks from overhead conductors.
applicableAreas: landscape plan in relation to overhead electric facilities along site boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (electrical plan) documents an existing overhead electric line (OHE) along the western boundary with poles and transition to underground service. Sheet 31 (landscape plan) depicts the same property with an OHE line notation along the southern boundary and utility poles shown. Trees are shown on the landscape plan with various symbols (SY, PL, P, M) positioned near the boundaries where OHE lines are present. However, the landscape plan provides no dimensional grid, no cross-reference with the electrical plan, and no clearance annotations (distances, dimensions, or notes) relating the tree positions to the overhead conductors or poles. Vision analysis confirms: 'There are no clearance dimensions or notes regarding tree placement near overhead electric lines or other utilities provided on this specific sheet.'
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, when overhead electric facilities are present or proposed, the landscape plan must display sufficient detail to allow verification of tree clearances from conductors. At a minimum, this requires: (1) overhead conductor locations and pole positions clearly shown in relation to tree locations; (2) clearance dimensions documenting distance from tree trunk center to outside conductor; (3) coordinate reference or clear spatial relationship allowing cross-reference with the utility/electrical plan. Currently, the landscape plan shows the OHE line notation and trees, but provides no dimensions, no notes confirming clearance distances, and no clear method for relating tree positions to conductor positions. An inspector cannot verify compliance with clearance zones without these dimensions.

findings.comment: Trees are shown on the landscape plan in proximity to the overhead electric line, but without clearance dimensions, distance callouts, or specification notes, clearance verification is prevented.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric line (OHE) along southern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does show the overhead electric (OHE) line and seven proposed trees in visual proximity. However, the plan lacks any clearance verification information: no dimension callouts, no written notes specifying distances or compliance status, no reference to conductor locations for measurement origin, and no identification of the specific tree species for those trees near the OHE line. While trees and utilities are graphically shown together, clearance verification is impossible due to the complete absence of dimensional or specification information required to confirm compliance.
findings.reasoning: The grouping specifies that trees must be 'shown on landscape plan in relation to overhead electric facilities, preventing clearance verification.' The intent of this requirement is to ensure viewers can verify that the spatial relationship satisfies clearance requirements. Although trees and OHE are displayed on the same drawing, the lack of any dimension, note, or specification information prevents any meaningful verification. Showing trees and utilities on the same sheet without clearance documentation is insufficient for code compliance verification.

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows trees positioned near overhead electric infrastructure. No Austin Energy written approval letters are provided authorizing placement of trees within prohibited clearance zones. Verification of whether proposed or retained trees are within restricted zones cannot be completed from available evidence.
applicableAreas: areas near proposed and retained trees within potential clearance zones of overhead electric infrastructure

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Electric Review section

findings.observation: The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section, line 19) lists 'UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 - Customer Activity in Utility Easements - Landscaping & Trees' and references 'Appendix F of the Environmental Criteria Manual' as preliminary design requirements from Austin Energy. However, no Austin Energy approval letters, written exceptions, or variance documentation are present in the supplementary documents provided. The landscape plan shows proposed trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) and depicts retained trees (including large Live Oak and Cedar Elm) positioned near or adjacent to the overhead electric line. The electrical plan indicates an existing overhead facility along the property boundary. No evidence of written approval from Austin Energy authorizing the placement of any tree within prohibited clearance zones is available in the submitted plans or comments.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits most non-utility-compatible trees and all large trees within defined clearance zones (15 feet for distribution non-UC trees, 25 feet for distribution large trees, 50 feet for transmission). The exception is for variations approved by 'explicit written approval from Austin Energy.' The landscape plan shows trees positioned adjacent to or very close to the documented overhead electric line, and the plant schedule lists species that may or may not be utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F. Without access to the full tree inventory with precise locations relative to conductors, and without documented mature heights, it cannot be definitively determined whether proposed or retained trees ARE in prohibited zones. However, the absence of any Austin Energy approval letters in the submitted documentation suggests that if trees are indeed in prohibited zones, required approval has not been obtained.

findings.comment: Trees are proposed at zero feet from the overhead electric line in direct violation of minimum clearance requirements. No documented written approval from Austin Energy is present on the plans to authorize this variance.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line where seven trees are plotted
findings.observation: Seven mitigation trees are shown on Sheet 31 with trunk centers positioned at approximately zero (0) feet lateral distance from the overhead electric (OHE) line. This placement is clearly within the restricted clearance zone (< 15 feet from distribution conductors, < 10 feet from utility poles). No documentation of Austin Energy written approval is present on the landscape plan, electrical plan, site notes, or in the supplementary documents (no letters or approval certificates are referenced or attached). The plans propose trees in prohibited zones with no evidence of required variance authorization.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states that 'Variations to planting distances and species identified as utility-compatible in ECM Appendix F require explicit written approval from Austin Energy.' Trees proposed within prohibited zones (< 15 feet distribution, < 10 feet poles) must include documented Austin Energy approval. The site plan shows no such approval. Without documented authorization, the proposed tree locations violate the clearance requirements.

findings.comment: Storm sewer plan shows multiple drain inlets throughout the site, and utility plan shows electric lines in the same areas with convergence in central site (Bldgs 4-7). No documentation verifies that drain inlets maintain required clearances from underground electric facilities or resolves any conflicts. Provide utility coordination documentation showing all drain inlet locations relative to electric lines and confirming required clearances, or revise inlet locations to avoid conflicts with electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Drainage inlets throughout site in proximity to electric lines
findings.observation: Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows multiple grate inlets distributed throughout the site (documented as 18-inch and 2'x2' grate inlets at various locations with rim and flowline elevations). Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows the proposed electric line routing throughout the site with blue solid lines. Vision analysis identified a complex area where utilities converge between Buildings 4 and 7, including the storm drain system. However, the utility plans do not provide explicit documentation showing the separation distance between any drain inlet and the underground electric lines at that location. The plans only include a contractor directive to 'field verify locations of utility crossings prior to beginning construction.'
findings.reasoning: Proposed drain inlets must not conflict with existing underground electric facilities without verification of required clearances per UCM § 1.10.5.B. While the plans show both drain inlets and electric lines, there is no documented verification of clearances or conflict resolution at any inlet location. Because drain inlets are excavated structures requiring surface access, their placement relative to underground electric facilities must be verified and documented on the plans, particularly in areas where electric lines and storm drain converge.

findings.comment: Multiple storm drain inlets are proposed within 5 feet of underground electric facilities. Specifically, courtyard inlets conflict with transformer pads, and the inlet west of Building 2 is positioned directly adjacent to the electrical utility line. Revise drain inlet locations to maintain 5-foot minimum clearance from all underground electric facilities, or coordinate with Austin Energy for encasement/protection measures if clearance cannot be achieved.
applicableAreas: Courtyard area between Buildings 4-7, near Building 2, near Buildings 7-8
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and cross-reference with Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) reveals multiple storm drain inlets positioned directly adjacent to or within close proximity of underground electrical infrastructure. Specific conflicts identified: (1) Central courtyard area contains four 18" grate inlets (Rim elevations 683.13, 683.15, 682.95, 683.10) positioned in the central landscaped/hardscape courtyard where transformer pads are located; (2) West of Building 2, an 18" grate inlet (Rim 683.82) is positioned directly adjacent to the "E" (electrical) utility line running along the western boundary; (3) South of Buildings 7 and 8, a series of 2'x2' grate inlets (Rims 679.30, 679.94, 680.99) are located in the drive aisle directly in proximity to electrical infrastructure serving those buildings. These drain inlets are located within the 5-foot horizontal clearance zone required between underground electric facilities and other site improvements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to site improvements and hardscape features. Storm drain inlets are site drainage improvements that require clearance from electrical infrastructure. The courtyard inlets appear to be directly adjacent to or within the transformer pad areas, and the Building 2 inlet is positioned directly on the electrical line corridor. Visual analysis at the 1" = 20' scale indicates these inlets fall within 5 feet (and likely within 0-3 feet) of the electrical conduit and transformer pads. This represents a coordination failure between drainage design and electrical routing.

findings.comment: Utility plans show Austin Water infrastructure (water and wastewater lines) in close proximity to electric utilities throughout the site (particularly a 150-200 foot parallel run behind Buildings 1-3 and convergence in central site area) but do not document the required minimum 5-foot horizontal separation for trench integrity. Provide utility coordination sheets documenting the separation between all Austin Water infrastructure and non-Austin Water utilities (electric, storm drain), or revise utility routing to achieve and document 5-foot separation per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2.
applicableAreas: Electric-water separation in central site corridor
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows water lines (cyan) provided by Austin Water and wastewater lines (magenta) both crossing and running in proximity to proposed electric lines (yellow). Vision analysis noted that 'Behind Bldgs 1, 2, and 3: yellow Electric line runs parallel and extremely close to magenta Wastewater line for roughly 150-200 feet. Given the scale, they appear to be within a very few feet of each other laterally.' Additionally, the vision analysis identified a central crossing area where multiple utilities including water and electric converge with no documented separations. However, the utility plan contains no explicit separation dimensions between Austin Water infrastructure and non-Austin Water (electric) infrastructure at any location. The plan only includes a general contractor note to field-verify utility locations.
findings.reasoning: Minimum horizontal separation of 5 feet must be maintained between Austin Water infrastructure and all other non-Austin Water infrastructure per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2. The utility plan shows Austin Water lines (water and wastewater) running in proximity to electric lines throughout the site, with the parallel run behind Buildings 1, 2, 3 appearing to be within only a few feet based on visual scale. No separation dimensions are documented on the utility plan. This failure to document the required separation violates the trench integrity requirement of the code.

findings.comment: Water and wastewater utilities from Austin Water are routed through the site in proximity to non-Austin Water infrastructure (electric and storm drain), but no separation distances are documented on the utility plans showing compliance with the minimum 5-foot horizontal separation requirement or the 3-foot residential service line exception. Provide dimension callouts or notes on the utility plans documenting that Austin Water infrastructure is separated from non-AW infrastructure by at least 5 feet (or 3 feet if residential service lines), as required.
applicableAreas: Utility corridors where Austin Water (water/wastewater) and non-AW infrastructure (electric, storm drain) run in proximity
findings.observation: The site plan documents show multiple utility types routed through similar areas of the property: Sheet 19 shows water (W) and wastewater (WW) lines (Austin Water infrastructure) routed through the central drive aisles; Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines (non-AW infrastructure) forming a perimeter loop; Sheet 20 indicates an electric crossing over water facilities. The plans do not provide any dimension callouts, notes, or specifications documenting the horizontal separation distances between Austin Water infrastructure and non-AW infrastructure (particularly electric) in the utility corridors. UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires 5 feet minimum horizontal separation between Austin Water mains and all other non-Austin Water infrastructure, with an exception allowing 3 feet for residential service lines only. No plan view or detail shows measured separations meeting either the 5-foot requirement or the 3-foot residential exception with supporting documentation of which requirement applies and at what locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum horizontal separation of 5 feet between Austin Water infrastructure and all other non-Austin Water infrastructure to maintain trench integrity, with an exception allowing 3 feet for residential service lines only. The site plan shows both Austin Water utilities (water and wastewater) and non-AW utilities (electric and storm drain) sharing utility corridors. However, no plan view provides documented separation distances between these utilities. The plans lack dimension callouts, notes, or specifications indicating that either the 5-foot standard separation or the 3-foot residential service line exception has been verified and applied. Without plan-based documentation of these required separations, compliance cannot be confirmed. This is an unclear determination because the available evidence is insufficient to verify that the requirement is met.

findings.comment: Electrical routing shown on the plans traverses the site to connect to building-mounted meters and runs through internal site corridors. Although the primary trunk lines may route around the building perimeter, no explicit documentation verifies that no underground electric facilities pass beneath the footprints of any of the 8 buildings, nor are any Austin Energy coordination agreements or exceptions noted on the plans. Provide a certified site plan overlay or coordination letter from Austin Energy confirming that no underground electric facilities pass under any building foundations, or revise electrical routing if conflicts exist.
applicableAreas: Building footprints relative to underground electric routing
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the footprints of all 8 buildings. Sheets 19 (Utility Tap Plan) and 21 (Electrical Design Plan) show proposed electric line routing throughout the site. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted that 'The routing is indicated by solid blue lines originating from a connection labeled Underground Electric Line on the western property boundary' and that 'The main trunk lines route primarily around the outer perimeter of the development rather than crossing under the building foundations.' However, the electrical plan also shows branch lines extending from the main trunk to connect to meters on each building, and internal routing that passes between buildings. While the vision analysis suggested main lines route around the perimeter, no explicit documentation was found verifying that no electric facilities pass under any building foundations, nor were any exceptions or coordination agreements noted on the plans.
findings.reasoning: Customer buildings and permanent structures shall not be installed over Austin Energy underground facilities per UCM § 1.10.5.B. The electrical routing shown on Sheets 19 and 21 demonstrates that electric lines do traverse the site. While the primary trunk lines may route around the building perimeter, branch lines must connect to meters and the overall routing passes through the site where buildings are located. Without explicit documentation verifying that no electric facilities pass beneath any building foundations, and without any noted exceptions or coordination agreements with Austin Energy, compliance with this prohibition cannot be confirmed. The vision analysis suggested routing avoids direct conflicts, but this is not the same as documented verification.

findings.comment: Underground electric conduit routing to serve wall-mounted electrical meters on all eight buildings would require conduit to pass beneath or through building foundations, which violates UCM § 1.10.5.B. Relocate electrical meters to pedestals or external equipment enclosures outside of building footprints, or coordinate with Austin Energy Design to document a license agreement and sealed engineering design if conduit must pass through building foundations, with metal sleeves allowing replacement.
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows that underground electric conduit is routed to and directly beneath building foundations to serve electrical meters mounted on building walls. Specifically: (1) All eight buildings have underground electric lines routing to wall-mounted meters; (2) These lines originate from transformers or pull boxes and run directly to the building serving as conduit entry points; (3) The conduit must pass beneath or immediately adjacent to building foundations to reach the meters; (4) In some cases (Buildings 2, 8), the meters are mounted in recessed notches in the building walls, requiring conduit to route into these recessed areas. This represents a direct routing of underground electric facilities beneath building foundations and service areas.
findings.reasoning: Wall-mounted electrical meters inherently require underground conduit to be routed to the building. When buildings are designed with slab-on-grade construction (as noted in the site data), conduit routing beneath the slab violates the prohibition. While some conduit may pass through retaining walls below grade (with an exception per UCM § 1.10.5.B requiring license agreement and engineering), the routing of conduit as the primary service to wall-mounted meters is not addressed by this exception.

findings.comment: Provide building elevations and a site plan diagram showing sight lines between all electrical meters and their serving transformers, confirming that: (1) meters are located on first floor or ground level, and (2) unobstructed sight line exists from transformer to meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows three transformer pads located on the property: (1) One west of Building 2; (2) One west of Building 8; (3) One centrally located in the courtyard between Buildings 4-7. Electrical meters are mounted on building walls for all eight buildings. However, the site plan does not provide line-of-sight verification or dimensional data showing the relationship between meter locations and transformer locations. Without building elevation drawings, it cannot be confirmed whether meters are on first floor/ground level relative to their respective serving transformers or whether sight lines between meters and transformers are maintained (unobstructed by buildings, walls, or other features).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires electrical meters to be located on first floor or ground level and within sight of the serving AE transformer. While the plan shows meters and transformers, it does not provide the elevation information (first floor vs. upper floors) or line-of-sight verification necessary to confirm compliance. Meters on a multi-story townhome building could potentially be on upper floors, and sight lines could be obstructed by other buildings or structures.

findings.comment: Electrical meters are shown on building exterior walls (Sheet 21), but no documentation is provided confirming that each meter is located on the first floor or ground level and within line-of-sight of its corresponding transformer. Provide notes or details on the electrical plan documenting the meter height and sight line relationship to each transformer.
applicableAreas: Building exterior walls where electrical meters are mounted in relation to transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies electrical meter locations on each building's exterior walls: Building 1 south side, Building 2 south side, Building 3 north side, Building 4 north side, Building 5 east side, Building 6 south side, Building 7 south side, and Building 8 south side. Blue branch lines connect from the main underground electric line network and transformer pads to these meter locations. However, the plan provides no dimension callouts, sight line indicators, arrows, or notes documenting that each meter location: (1) is on the first floor or ground level, or (2) is within sight of the corresponding transformer location as required. While transformer locations are shown separately from meter locations, no visualization or notation demonstrates the sight line relationship or confirms that meters are within line-of-sight of their respective transformers.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires that electric meters be located on first floor or ground level and within sight of the Austin Energy transformer. While Sheet 21 shows both meter and transformer locations on the site plan, it provides no documentation confirming that: (1) all meters are at first floor or ground level (the plan does not show building sections or elevations for meter height), or (2) sight lines from each meter to its transformer are unobstructed. Without specific notation, sight line diagrams, or elevation details confirming these requirements, compliance cannot be verified from the submitted plans. This is unclear because the available plan documentation is insufficient to confirm that the meter location requirements are being met.

findings.comment: Applicant must document that a pre-construction safety meeting has been scheduled with Austin Energy at least 48 hours before any construction commences. Contact Andrew Perez at 512-505-7153 to schedule. If tower cranes will be used, include Chuck Hendry (512-505-7151). Provide proof of scheduling or meeting completion before construction begins.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) explicitly requires 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction.' The sheet provides contact information for Andrew Perez (512-505-7153) and notes that Chuck Hendry (512-505-7151) should be included if cranes are used. However, the site plan provides no documentation that this pre-construction safety meeting has been scheduled or that Austin Energy coordination has occurred. No reference in construction notes or supplementary documents confirms this mandatory coordination has taken place.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3 are explicit contractual requirements that apply to this development. The presence of transmission poles, guy wires, and transmission easements on the site (confirmed on Sheet 4 existing conditions) makes this requirement applicable. The site plan shows construction will occur in proximity to transmission structures (buildings, grading, landscaping planned throughout site). While the requirement is stated, there is no affirmative evidence in the plans or supporting documents that the applicant has actually scheduled the required 48-hour-prior meeting or obtained Austin Energy's pre-construction approval. Per the permit standard, applicants must affirmatively demonstrate compliance, not merely reference the requirement.

findings.comment: Pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy not documented as scheduled or completed. Site plan references Andrew Perez contact information but provides no evidence of meeting confirmation 48 hours before construction.
applicableAreas: Construction near transmission poles and guy wires at NW and SW corners along Valley View Road
findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 (Electric Transmission Notes, Item 3) states: 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction. Call Andrew Perez at 512-505-7153 to schedule a tailgate safety meeting.' This requirement is documented on the plans. However, no evidence exists that this meeting has been scheduled, completed, or documented. Sheet 4 existing conditions survey confirms two power poles with guy wires exist at NW and SW corners on Valley View Road frontage. Construction is proposed within or immediately adjacent to these facilities (excavation visible on Sheet 11 near NW pole). No certificate or documentation of completed pre-construction safety meeting is provided in the site plan submittal.
findings.reasoning: While the site plan acknowledges the pre-construction coordination requirement by referencing the Austin Energy contact and the 48-hour notice requirement, there is no affirmative evidence that this meeting has been scheduled or completed. This is a procedural requirement that must be satisfied before construction begins. The presence of the requirement on the plans is not equivalent to compliance; completion documentation is necessary to confirm the deficiency is resolved.

findings.comment: Concrete retaining walls, Type III driveway, and concrete sidewalk are shown encroaching into the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 D.R.T.C.Tx.') and eastern boundary ('5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.'). The graphic evidence from Sheet 9 shows these structures encroaching into the dedicated easement areas. findings.comment: Trees and vegetation are shown within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas without documentation of a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. The site plan shows landscaping (trees) within easement boundaries but provides no documentation of an executed license agreement. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant. Missing executed license agreement documentation is grounds for deficiency, as this can result in certificate of occupancy holds and Austin Energy removal of non-compliant landscaping at the owner's cost.

findings.comment: The detention pond with required vegetation is located within the 5' Electric Easement but no executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is documented on the plans. Obtain and file license agreement with Austin Energy authorizing landscaping and vegetation within the easement, or relocate pond outside easement boundary.

findings.observation: Sheet 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles) maintenance requirements specify: 'No unvegetated area shall exceed ten (10) square feet. This performance requirement applies to the entire pond including the pond bottom, side slopes, and areas adjacent to the pond.' The absence of a filed license agreement is the deficiency.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires: 'A license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is required before installing any landscaping or irrigation that might obstruct access to facilities within electric easements.' The grouping description clarifies: 'Plans showing landscaping within easements must demonstrate the license agreement has been "obtained from and filed with" Austin Energy Public Involvement—not "to be obtained." Missing license agreements result in certificate of occupancy holds.' The detention pond's required vegetation (95% cover) constitutes landscaping within the electric easement. The submitted plans provide no evidence that an executed license agreement has been obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement.

findings.comment: Retaining walls, fences, landscaping, and other improvements within the electric easements obstruct required 24/7 vehicular maintenance access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. Ensure that easement areas remain completely clear of all obstructions and maintain a continuous, unobstructed access corridor at least 12 feet wide within the easement for Austin Energy maintenance activities.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts concrete retaining walls, a wood fence, driveways, and sidewalks located within or directly overlapping the southern and eastern 5' electric easement boundaries. These physical structures create barriers and obstructions to the easement area. Retaining walls run parallel to easement boundaries at the perimeter, creating access restrictions. The wood fence is drawn directly within the eastern 5' easement area. Driveways and sidewalks, while potentially providing some access routes, are designed for pedestrian and vehicle traffic to/from buildings rather than maintenance access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. No dimensions or callout indicate that a clear, continuous, drivable maintenance corridor is maintained within or adjacent to these easements. The plan shows landscaping (trees) also positioned within easement areas, further reducing open access.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping within easements is permitted only 'if landscaping does not restrict 24/7 access.' The phrase is also reinforced in the general prohibition language emphasizing that Austin Energy must maintain '24-hour unimpeded access to all electric facilities.' Retaining walls and fences are structures that inherently restrict access; trees and vegetation also impede equipment movement. The site plan shows these features within the easement boundaries, and there is no notation, callout, or specification stating that a 24/7 maintenance access corridor is maintained free of obstruction. The presence of these features within the easement area violates the requirement for unrestricted access.

findings.comment: The detention pond with required vegetation and concrete retaining walls within the 5' Electric Easement obstructs required 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate pond outside the easement or demonstrate 24-foot minimum clear drivable surface for maintenance vehicle access across the easement width.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirms the detention pond retaining wall is within the 5' Electric Easement. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that 'landscaping within easements must maintain 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment.' A concrete retaining wall enclosing a pond, combined with required dense vegetation (95% cover), creates a physical obstruction preventing free vehicular access across the easement. The maintenance requirements (routine vegetation trimming, inspections, replacement) also require Austin Energy to navigate around or within the landscaped pond area. This setup does not maintain unobstructed access.

findings.comment: A permanent wood privacy fence is shown within the eastern 5' electric easement. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 allows: 'Removable wooden fences may be allowed in easements under license agreement if removable to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access.' However, non-removable or permanent fencing prevents access. The deficiency is unclear because the fence material (wood) suggests it might be removable, but the details do not confirm this, and no license agreement documentation is provided.

findings.comment: Multiple trees and vegetation (site amenities) are shown within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the electric easement boundaries to comply with UCM § 1.10.10.2.

findings.reasoning: The regulatory overview explicitly states: 'Plans must explicitly designate easements as aerial when overhead facilities are present—generic electric easement labels are insufficient.' When overhead facilities are present, the easement must be labeled 'aerial electric easement' to distinguish it from underground electric easements and to communicate the vertical clearance requirements (16 feet minimum for access, 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance per UCM § 1.10.3) that apply to aerial facilities. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or utility-compatible plantings that might obstruct Austin Energy's access to facilities within electric easement areas. The visual evidence of trees plotted within the overhead electric easement boundaries triggers this requirement. The applicant cannot simply plant within easement areas; prior authorization is mandatory. The absence of (1) tree/landscape restrictions on the landscape plan, (2) a license agreement document, or (3) any acknowledgment of this requirement on either the landscape or general notes sheets indicates non-compliance. UCM § 1.10.10.3 further states that Austin Energy reserves the right to remove any obstruction without fault, and property owners are responsible for all costs.

findings.comment: Proposed conduit routing shown on Sheet 21, but conduit sizing (pipe diameter, duct bank dimensions, material specifications) not labeled or specified. Complete conduit sizing and material specifications must be added to all electrical routing documentation.

Utility Notes on Sheet 21 require contractors to verify existing utilities but do not specify proposed conduit sizes, material, or duct bank dimensions required for design compliance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iii) requires complete documentation of proposed electric facilities including distribution lines and all infrastructure. Incomplete facility specifications (missing conduit sizes, pipe diameters, duct bank details) constitute incomplete documentation of proposed infrastructure. The blue lines show routing paths but lack the engineering specifications necessary for Austin Energy approval and construction.

findings.comment: Proposed electrical facilities are incompletely shown. Please provide: (1) conduit sizing and material specifications for all underground routing on Sheets 9, 11, 19, and 21; (2) transformer pad kVA ratings and voltage configurations; (3) distribution line sizes; (4) pull box dimensions; (5) consistent depiction of all proposed equipment across all plan sheets (Site Plan, Grading, Utility Tap, and Electrical Plan sheets).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformers (4 pad-mounted), meters (attached to 7 buildings), pull boxes, and underground conduit routing in blue. However, vision analysis identified critical absences: No conduit sizing or material specifications are labeled, no transformer kVA ratings or voltage configurations are shown, no pull box dimensions, no distribution line sizes. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only one transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' and lacks all underground routing and meters. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows no electric distribution lines at all. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iii) and (5) require proposed electric facilities to be 'shown' with sufficient detail. While Sheet 21 provides some proposed facilities (transformers, meters, routing), the incompleteness includes: (1) no conduit/wire sizing, (2) no transformer ratings, (3) no voltage designations, (4) no equipment specifications. More critically, cross-sheet inconsistency means critical sheets (9, 11, 19) do not show the complete proposed design shown on Sheet 21, violating the requirement that proposed facilities be shown across applicable plan sheets. The lack of specifications on Sheet 21 and absence on other sheets together constitute incomplete documentation per UCM § 1.16.0(5).

findings.comment: Power source for proposed buildings not clearly identified. Please add: (1) equipment schedule or one-line diagram showing which transformer(s) serve which buildings; (2) service voltage and load data for each building; (3) connection routing from transformers to each building's service entrance; (4) clarification of whether multiple buildings share service or have individual service points.
findings.observation: Examined electrical design plan and site plan for power source indication. Sheet 21 shows 4 proposed transformer pads and meters on buildings but does not identify which transformer(s) serve which buildings. Sheet 9 shows one transformer pad but no meters and no indication of service routing. The electrical design does not include a one-line diagram, equipment schedule, or notes identifying the power source for the 39 residential units.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires plans to show 'Power source for proposed buildings.' The omission of this information means: (1) it is unclear which transformer(s) power which buildings, (2) there is no indication whether multiple buildings share service or each has individual service (violating potential unified development documentation), (3) load distribution among transformers cannot be verified. This is a fundamental requirement for demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.3.3 (one point of service, one service voltage per building).

findings.comment: Proposed power source and service specifications (voltage, amperage, service type) not identified for proposed buildings. Specify the service voltage (primary/secondary), amperage, and service type (single/three-phase) for each building or building group on the electrical design plan.
applicableAreas: Site plan, Electrical design plan - all proposed buildings
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which shows 8 proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8). Vision analysis confirms that meters are depicted on the buildings with generic 'Electrical Meters' labels, and transformers are shown as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' callouts. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires that plans show 'Power source for proposed buildings' as part of the application requirements for Austin Energy land development review. The grouping's Regulatory Overview states that 'Point of service identified with one service voltage' must be shown on plans (item #7 under Plan Documentation Requirements). The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms no text or labels indicating service voltage, amperage, or service type for the proposed buildings. While the physical locations of meters and transformers are graphically depicted, without identification of the power source (voltage level and capacity), the requirement to show 'power source for proposed buildings' is not met. This is distinct from EL-10.8 (proposed facilities shown) because the facilities themselves may be shown, but their functional designation as power source is missing.

findings.comment: Point of connection to existing Austin Energy facilities is not clearly identified on plans. Please add explicit callouts or a detailed connection diagram showing: (1) exact location where proposed electric service connects to existing AE infrastructure; (2) demarcation point between AE-owned and customer-owned facilities; (3) detailed connection at pole/underground main; (4) applicable voltage and amperage at point of service.
applicableAreas: Western site boundary, point of connection to existing AE facilities
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted: 'There is no explicit Point of Connection (POC) or Primary Service Point label clearly indicating exactly where the proposed blue line network taps into the existing utility provider's network. Blue routing lines originate near the existing OHE lines in the NW corner (near an Electrical Pull Box) and near the existing underground lines on the West edge, implying connection points in these general areas, but a definitive tie-in detail or label is absent.' The plan shows blue conduit lines approaching existing infrastructure but lacks callout, label, or detail showing the specific connection point.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires the 'Point of connection to existing AE facilities' to be shown. This is a fundamental requirement for demonstrating that the proposed design interfaces correctly with Austin Energy's infrastructure. Without an explicit callout showing exactly where the customer-owned facilities connect to the AE system (i.e., the 'point of service' boundary per UCM § 1.3.3), compliance cannot be verified and AE Design cannot approve the design.

findings.comment: Point of service connection to existing Austin Energy infrastructure not shown on plans. Identify and label the specific connection point to the existing AE electrical system, showing the demarcation between AE-owned and customer-owned facilities.
applicableAreas: Electrical design plan - service connection point
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows the proposed electrical infrastructure on the site, including transformers, pull boxes, meters, and underground electric lines connecting buildings. Vision analysis confirms that the sheet displays 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (multiple locations near buildings), 'Underground Electric Line' routing, and 'Electrical Meters' on building exteriors. However, the plan does not show the point where the proposed electrical system connects to existing Austin Energy (AE) facilities. The vision analysis notes that 'OHE' (overhead electric) lines are shown along property boundaries as existing facilities, but there is no labeled callout or note indicating where proposed conduit or service lines connect to the existing AE infrastructure. The sheet lacks any annotation, dimension, or diagram showing the actual connection point to the existing utility lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) explicitly requires plans to show 'Point of service identified with one service voltage.' The Regulatory Overview clarifies that 'Point of service identifies the demarcation between Austin Energy-owned infrastructure and customer-owned facilities.' Without a clear point of connection shown on the plans, there is no way to determine where the demarcation occurs, which infrastructure is AE-owned vs. customer-owned, or whether the proposed service configuration complies with AE policy requiring one point of service per lot. This is a critical documentation requirement for AE review and cannot be assessed from the available plans.

findings.comment: Electric site plan lacks required AE Design coordination details including measured clearances to existing overhead lines, disconnect location/distance, 20'×35' staging area dimensions with 35' vertical clearance, bollard details, and truck access path specifications (12-foot width, 16-foot height, 72,180 lb weight capacity). Add dimensioned clearance measurements, marked disconnect locations, delineated 20'×35' setup areas at each transformer pad, bollard/protective details, and truck access path dimensions.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad areas (3 locations); service entry point on west side; all building service connections
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows three transformer pad locations with labels, pull boxes, and building meter locations, but lacks the following AE Design coordination details: (1) Measured clearances from proposed facilities to existing overhead lines on west boundary - no clearance dimensions shown; (2) Disconnect location with distance specification from transformer pads - no disconnect marked; (3) 20' × 35' minimum setup area dimensions with 35-foot vertical clearance requirement - no setup area boundaries drawn; (4) Bollard/protective device details - none shown; (5) Truck access path specifications (width, height, weight capacity) - no truck routes detailed; (6) Staging area dimensions and restrictions - not documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that plans demonstrate coordination with Austin Energy Design standards, and UCM § 1.3.16 specifies minimum 20' × 35' horizontal clear zone with 35-foot vertical clearance in front of AE equipment. Complete coordination documentation requires measured clearances, equipment relationship specifications, access path dimensions, and staging area delineation. Absence of these details indicates incomplete AE Design coordination.

findings.comment: Electric site plan lacks required coordination and clearance details. Please provide: (1) 20' × 35' staging area dimensions and 35' vertical clearance in front of each transformer pad; (2) truck access path dimensions (minimum 12' horizontal width, 16' vertical clearance, capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight); (3) clearance measurements around all transformer pads (10' minimum on access door side, 5' minimum on operator sides); (4) disconnect location and distance from transformer; (5) bollard and protective barrier details; (6) mounting curb specifications for transformer access.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations, meter locations, access paths
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 found: 'Electric equipment dimensions or clearance information: None. There are no text callouts providing the physical dimensions of the transformer pads, pull boxes, or meter banks. There are no drafted clearance zones or textual notes defining required working clearances around the electrical equipment.' Examined Sheets 9, 21, 31 for coordination details: No staging area dimensions (20' × 35'), no truck access paths (12' horizontal × 16' vertical clearance), no setback measurements from transformers to buildings, no bollard details, no mountable curb information, no disconnect location callouts, no measurements for horizontal clearance (10 feet minimum on access door side).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) and § 1.3.16 require 'missing measurements for clearances, disconnect location, staging area, mountable curb, bollard, truck access details' to be shown. These details are essential for: (1) AE equipment installation and maintenance access, (2) ensuring landscaping/buildings don't impair access, (3) verifying compliance with PAD clearance requirements (10 ft on access door, 5 ft on sides), (4) providing 35-foot vertical clearance over 20' × 35' staging area. Their absence prevents verification of compliance and AE operability.

findings.comment: Recording information for existing electric easements is provided on plans but is inconsistent across sheets and partially illegible. Clarify and standardize recording information for all existing easements, ensuring volume/page numbers and instrument numbers are clearly legible and consistent across all sheets showing easements.
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) shows two 5' electric easements with recording information that is partially illegible due to image resolution. Vision analysis indicates: '5' Elec. Ease' on north boundary of Lot 2 has no visible recording reference; '5' Elec. Ease' on south boundary of Lot 1 has unreadable text in Volume/Page format.
