Sheet 21 references '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' Facts.md documents two 5' easements from Mecey Subdivision (Vol. 73, Page 76). Recording information is present but inconsistent across sheets and partially unclear.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that recording information (document number, volume/page, or plat reference) be provided for all existing electric easements. While recording citations appear on multiple sheets, the information is not consistently legible and references differ between sheets (Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 vs. Pg. 883), creating ambiguity about which easements are referenced and whether all easements are properly documented with complete recording information.

findings.comment: Recording information (volume/page, document number, or plat reference) not provided for existing electrical easements. Add recording information to all easement labels, cross-referencing the Travis County plat or deed document where the easement was recorded (e.g., 'Vol. 73, Pg. 76, Case C8S-75-160').
applicableAreas: All sheets showing electrical easements - Plat (Sheet 2), Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), and others
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'No. While there are volume and page references shown on the plat (in circles indicating adjacent property deed records, e.g., Vol. 3058 Pg. 2327), there are no specific Volume/Page references or document numbers attached directly to the easement labels themselves. The labels only indicate if they are "(Exist.)" or "(Existing)."' Sheet 21 vision analysis confirms easements are shown with labels like '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' (which does have recording info on this sheet), but upon closer examination, sheet 9 shows '5' Electric Easement' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement' with no volume/page references shown. The facts.md document (lines 135-143) identifies several existing electric easements: '5' Electric Easements (×2)' with 'Document Ref: Travis County Doc 73/76, Case C8S-75-160' and '7.5' Public Utility Easement' with the same reference. These recorded documents should be cited on the plans. On Sheet 2, the plat does not include volume/page references for the electric easement labels, representing an omission of required recording information.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires easements to be shown 'with locations and extents clearly delineated.' The term 'clearly delineated' encompasses not only spatial location and width but also legal identification. The Regulatory Overview explicitly states: 'Recording information: Electric infrastructure documentation requirements... UCM § 1.16.0 serves as the comprehensive baseline for land development review applications, specifying what must be shown on plans to obtain Austin Energy approval.' LDC § 25-4-132 (cited in Code References) requires 'Easement dimensions, locations, and designations to match exactly between plat and site plan.' Without recording information (volume/page or document number), easement locations cannot be verified against recorded documents, overlapping or conflicting easements cannot be identified, and the legal identity of each easement is unclear. This is particularly important where multiple easements may exist on the same site (this site has at least 7-9 documented easements per facts.md). Recording information must appear on all plan sheets showing easements.

findings.comment: Tree locations and electric infrastructure locations are not coordinated across plan sheets. Please provide: (1) notes on landscape plan specifying that trees within 15 feet of overhead electric conductors must be utility-compatible species (mature height not exceeding 15 feet); (2) exclusion of all landscaping (trees, shrubs, irrigation) from the 20' × 35' staging area in front of each transformer pad; (3) clearance notes showing trees will not encroach on 7.5-foot horizontal clearance from overhead primary and neutral conductors; (4) cross-reference between landscape plan tree locations and electrical plan transformer/line locations.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad staging areas, overhead line clearance zones, underground conduit areas
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees planted near the OHE line on the southern boundary but vision analysis found: 'There are no specific callouts, notes, or legend entries on this sheet indicating that these specific trees are utility-compatible, low-growing species chosen to coordinate with the overhead lines above them.' No trees are shown in the 20' × 35' staging areas in front of the transformer pads (in fact, the transformer pads themselves are not shown on Sheet 31). Sheet 30 (Existing Tree Plan) does not address coordination with electric infrastructure. There are no notes on any sheet requiring trees within utility clearance zones to be utility-compatible species.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires coordination across sheets, and § 1.10.3 specifies clearance requirements (15-foot radius from primary/neutral conductors, 7.5 feet horizontal minimum clearance). When trees are planted near electric facilities, the landscape plan must show: (1) tree species are chosen to not exceed mature height of 15 feet (typical for utility clearance), (2) trees are not planted within 10-foot radius of transformer access doors (part of 20' × 35' staging area), (3) trees do not interfere with overhead clearance envelopes. The current landscape plan shows trees near OHE without utility-compatibility restrictions, violating coordination requirements.

findings.comment: Tree locations not coordinated with overhead electric line clearances. Relocate all landscape plantings (particularly trees with mature canopies) to maintain minimum 15-foot radial clearance from the overhead electric (OHE) lines shown along the southern property boundary.
applicableAreas: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) - southern property boundary where overhead electric lines run
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows overhead electric lines labeled 'OHE' running horizontally along the bottom (southern) edge of the site. Vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'Yes, overhead electric lines are shown. A line clearly labeled "---OHE---" runs horizontally along the bottom edge of the site plan. Regarding vegetation clearance, there does NOT appear to be clear clearance. Several proposed tree symbols (circles representing canopies) are drawn directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the "OHE" line, particularly towards the bottom right section of the plan.' The Regulatory Overview (lines 61-64) establishes clearance requirements: 'Distribution facilities (<60kV, typically 12.47kV) with 15-foot radial clearances' and more specifically 'Permanent clearances from overhead distribution (UCM § 1.10.3): 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, secondary conductors; 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' Trees directly adjacent to overhead lines violate this 15-foot radial clearance requirement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires '15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' This is a safety clearance to prevent tree branches and fall hazards from contacting energized conductors. The grouping's Common Violation Patterns section (line 54) specifically identifies: 'trees conflicting with clearance envelopes' as a cross-sheet coordination problem. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms trees are 'directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the OHE line' rather than maintaining 15-foot separation. This represents a direct conflict between the landscape design (trees) and the electrical infrastructure (OHE lines with required 15-foot clearance). Sheet 21 shows the overhead electric lines exist on this site, and Sheet 31 landscape plan fails to maintain required clearance from those existing lines.

findings.comment: Plans do not document truck access paths, setup areas, or access preservation for Austin Energy maintenance. Delineate 12-foot horizontal width truck access path with 16-foot vertical clearance and 72,180 lbs weight capacity on all plans; show 20'×35' minimum setup area with 35-foot vertical clearance in front of all transformer pads and major electrical equipment; note any grade changes, barriers, or conflicts with AE access requirements.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad areas; service entry locations; existing overhead line areas on west boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, meters, conduit) but does not delineate truck access paths, setup areas, or clearance specifications needed for Austin Energy personnel to access and maintain facilities. UCM § 1.3.16 requires minimum 20-foot × 35-foot horizontal clear zone with 35-foot vertical clearance in front of AE equipment, and 12-foot horizontal width with 16-foot vertical clearance for truck access paths capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight. Sheet 21 lacks any dimensioned delineation of these access requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(4) explicitly requires that plans demonstrate preservation of Austin Energy personnel access to maintain current and proposed facilities. Absence of truck access path dimensions (width, height, weight capacity), setup area delineations (20' × 35' with 35' vertical clearance), and physical barriers or grade changes blocking access means the applicant has not documented their site design accommodates AE maintenance requirements. Without documented access preservation, site plan approval cannot demonstrate compliance.

findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate preserved Austin Energy personnel access to electric facilities. Please provide: (1) truck access paths (12-foot horizontal width minimum, 16-foot vertical clearance minimum) clearly marked on site plan, landscape plan, and grading plan from public right-of-way to each transformer pad and major disconnect location; (2) specification that access surfaces support minimum 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight; (3) grading and landscaping notes confirming no obstructions to access paths; (4) confirmation that grade changes and retaining walls do not block access to facilities.
applicableAreas: Truck access paths to all electric facilities, transformer staging areas
findings.observation: Examined all sheets for truck access path documentation. No sheet shows: (1) identified truck access lanes with 12-foot horizontal width and 16-foot vertical clearance, (2) pavement or surface capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight, (3) unobstructed paths from public right-of-way to transformer pads and other AE equipment, (4) grade changes or barriers that might block access. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) could show access paths but does not. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows grades but does not call out required access surface specifications. Vision analysis found these elements missing from all sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(4) requires plans to 'demonstrate that development preserves AE personnel access to maintain current and proposed facilities.' This requires showing truck access paths that meet AE specifications: (1) 12-foot minimum horizontal width, (2) 16-foot minimum vertical clearance, (3) surface capable of supporting 72,180 lbs. A bucket truck or crane must be able to reach all transformers and disconnect points for installation, maintenance, and emergency repairs. The failure to show and specify access paths prevents verification that AE operability is preserved.

findings.comment: Secondary riser configuration is not shown on plans, or one-line diagram of electrical riser is not provided. Please provide a one-line electrical riser diagram showing the distribution of service from the main service entrance through the secondary system to all buildings and units, drawn to standard electrical schematic conventions.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan') contains only a site plan view showing transformer locations, pull boxes, meters, and underground routing. The sheet reference to 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' directs to Sheet 19, which contains utility tap profiles for water and wastewater, not electrical service information. No one-line electrical riser diagram is present on Sheet 21 or referenced on that sheet. No secondary riser configuration showing how power is distributed from the main service entrance to individual building units is shown. The sheet is entirely plan-view without riser details.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that electrical plans include: '(1) secondary riser configuration; (2) one-line diagram of electrical riser; (3) plan-view of electrical layout.' The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Must include one-line diagram of electrical riser.' The applicant has provided only the plan-view portion. The critical one-line diagram and secondary riser configuration documentation are completely absent from the submitted plans. These are standard requirements for any new electric service application.

findings.comment: Secondary riser configuration not shown on plans and no one-line diagram of electrical riser provided. One-line riser diagram must be included on electrical plans showing secondary service distribution to all buildings and units.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 for secondary riser configuration and one-line diagram. Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and shows transformers, pull boxes, and meters serving the buildings. However, Vision analysis confirmed: 'There is NO one-line electrical riser diagram shown on this sheet, nor is there a reference note directing the reader to one on another sheet.' The sheet shows only plan view of underground distribution with no riser configuration details for secondary service to individual buildings or units. No one-line diagram appears on any sheet reviewed (Sheets 3, 9, 19, 20, 21, 31).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that electrical plans show 'one-line diagram of electrical riser' when secondary riser is part of the project design or new electric service is proposed. This 39-unit multi-family project with new electric service requires secondary service distribution to individual buildings/units. The absence of a one-line riser diagram on the electrical plans means the applicant has not provided the technical documentation required by code to show how secondary electric service is distributed from the transformers to the individual townhome units.

findings.comment: Electric facilities are not clearly labeled on plans or labels lack facility type identification and technical specifications. Please provide labels for all electric facilities that clearly identify the type (e.g., 'Transformer Pad - AE Owned', 'Service Entrance Conduit', 'Pull Box') along with applicable voltage, size, and ownership information.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electric facilities labeled with generic text callouts: 'Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Electrical Meters', and 'Underground Electric Line'. While these labels ARE legible and visible, they provide NO technical identification of the facilities. Labels do not indicate: (1) type with any specificity, (2) voltage level, (3) capacity/size, (4) ownership (AE vs. Customer), (5) whether underground or overhead, or (6) material specifications. Sheet 9 similarly shows only generic 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' and 'OHE' labels without detail. The labels fail to provide the level of identification necessary for clear plan review and code compliance verification.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires that electric facilities be 'clearly labeled' with identification. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Generic "existing utility" notation without specifying electric facility type, voltage, size, ownership' is identified as a common violation pattern. The applicant has used generic type-only labels without the required technical specifications. This deficiency prevents Austin Energy and City reviewers from clearly understanding what facilities are shown and their code compliance status.

findings.comment: Electric facility labels missing facility type identification (customer vs. Austin Energy owned, voltage class, capacity). All electric facilities must include clear type identification and relevant technical specifications.
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21, 9, and 19 for electric facility labels. Found labels on all three sheets: Sheet 21 uses generic text callouts such as 'Electrical Transformer Pad,' 'Electrical Pull Box,' 'Electrical Meters,' 'Underground Electric Line.' Sheet 9 uses abbreviated notation: '-OHE-' (Overhead Electric Line), '-E-' (Underground Electric Line), and 'Transformer Pad (Typ.).' Sheet 19 uses legend notation: '-E-' for 'Proposed Underground Electric.' However, Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed: 'The labels provide only generic identification. There is NO specific information provided on this sheet regarding voltage, size, equipment type (e.g., single-phase vs. three-phase), or ownership (e.g., Austin Energy vs. Private) for these facilities.' Facility type is identified (transformer, pull box, meter, line) but critical distinguishing information is absent.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires electric facilities to be 'clearly labeled.' While basic labels exist (e.g., 'Transformer Pad,' 'Pull Box,' 'Meter'), the grouping's Code References and Common Violations section specifies that labels should include 'facility type identification,' voltage, size, and ownership. The current labels lack this critical identifying information. Without knowing whether a transformer is customer-owned or Austin Energy-owned, or what voltage class it serves, the plans do not provide sufficient technical clarity for review and compliance verification.

findings.comment: Cannot fully verify from available evidence whether disconnects are shown and labeled on architectural electrical plans, as detailed electrical plans for individual buildings do not appear to be included in this preliminary site plan submission. If architectural electrical plans are required for this project, please provide them showing main service disconnects, transformer disconnects, and building-level disconnects clearly labeled and sized.
applicableAreas: Electrical plans and service entrance details
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed as the primary electrical design sheet. This sheet shows transformers, pull boxes, meters, and underground routing, but no electrical disconnects are labeled or detailed. The sheet does not show main service disconnects, transformer disconnects, or building-level disconnects. However, the sheet is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and may represent only a preliminary routing plan. Traditional architectural electrical plans (floor plans showing electrical layout, branch circuits, panel locations, and disconnect details) have not been examined, as they do not appear to be included in the 39-sheet site plan submission.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Disconnects [be] shown and labeled on electrical plans'. This is listed as an 'All sites' requirement. However, the existing site plan submission appears to include only a preliminary electrical site design plan showing routing and facility locations, not detailed architectural electrical plans that would typically show disconnect locations. Without access to complete architectural/electrical plans for the buildings, this requirement cannot be fully verified.

findings.comment: Disconnects not shown and labeled on electrical plans. Provide electrical plans showing the location of main service disconnect(s) for each building clearly labeled with amperage rating and voltage. Show the relationship between outdoor transformers/meters and indoor disconnect locations with routing information.

NO detailed electrical plans showing service panels, main disconnects, or riser diagrams are provided. No disconnects are shown anywhere in the document set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires disconnects to be shown on electrical plans. The grouping specifies this applies "All sites." The site plan contains only site-level utility routing, not building-level electrical details. If the scope includes customer electrical facilities per AEDC § 1.16.0, building-level service disconnects should be documented. Their complete absence represents a deficiency in the electrical documentation package.

findings.comment: Electric facility symbols are not identified in legend or symbols for proposed electric facilities are missing from the legend. Please provide legend entries for all proposed electric facilities shown on the plans (proposed transformers, proposed pull boxes, proposed meters, proposed underground lines, proposed service connections, and other relevant symbols).

Electric facility symbols shown in legend are: (1) Existing Power Pole & Down Guy; (2) Existing Electric Meter; (3) Existing Transformer Pad; (4) Existing Overhead Electric Line; (5) Existing Light Pole. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that electric facility symbols be 'identified in legend'. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes: 'Legend symbols that don't match symbols actually used on plans' as a common violation pattern. The applicant has provided a legend with EXISTING facility symbols only, but the plans show PROPOSED facilities without any legend symbols for them. This creates a documentation gap where proposed facilities cannot be clearly identified using the legend. UCM standards require consistent symbol usage across all sheets.

findings.comment: Electric facility symbols not identified in legend on electrical plan sheet. Legend defining all electric facility symbols must be present on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) or have an explicit cross-reference note directing users to the legend location.
applicableAreas: Cover sheet or general notes sheet with legend
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 6 legend. The plan relies on cross-reference to Sheet 3 legend, but no note on Sheet 21 directs readers to Sheet 3 for symbol definitions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Electric facility symbols' be 'identified in legend.' While a legend exists on Sheet 3, it is NOT on the electrical design plan itself (Sheet 21). Users of Sheet 21 must consult an external sheet (Sheet 3) to understand the symbols. This violates the principle that each plan sheet should be self-contained or have clear cross-references. The absence of legend identification on the electrical plan sheet means symbols used on Sheet 21 are not identified on that specific sheet as required by code.

findings.comment: Legend symbols do not match symbols actually used in plans. Please ensure that all symbols used on site plan, utility plan, electrical plan, grading plan, and landscape plan exactly match the symbols shown in the legend, or add legend entries for any symbols used that are not currently in the legend.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 legend shows symbols for EXISTING electric facilities only. Sheet 21 and Sheet 9 show PROPOSED electric facilities using generic text callout labels (e.g., 'Electrical Transformer Pad', rectangles with 'T' labels) that do not correspond to any symbol shown in the Sheet 3 legend. The symbols actually used on Sheet 21 (simple rectangular blocks, circles, and line designations) do not match any symbol table or legend legend. There is no consistency between the legend provided and the symbols/labels actually used to mark proposed facilities throughout the plan set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Legend symbols do not match symbols actually used in plans'. The grouping regulatory overview identifies this as a common violation: 'Legend symbols that don't match symbols actually used on plans'. The submitted plans fail this requirement. The legend provides symbols for existing facilities only, while the plans use unlabeled/generic representations for proposed facilities. This creates confusion and prevents consistent interpretation of the plans across sheets.

findings.comment: Legend symbols do not clearly match symbols actually used in plans. Clarify legend consistency: either standardize on use of legend symbols (e.g., 'T' symbol, '--- OHE ---' notation) on all plans, or provide alternative legend defining text callouts used (e.g., "Electrical Transformer Pad," "Electrical Pull Box"). Ensure consistent symbol and label use across all sheets.
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 3 Legend found: "Existing Transformer Pad (symbol), Existing Overhead Electric Line (--- OHE ---), Proposed Transformer Pad (Square symbol with 'T')." Vision of Sheet 21 found: "There are direct text labels (callouts) pointing to specific features... 'Electrical Pull Box,' 'Electrical Transformer Pad,' 'Electrical Meters,' 'Underground Electric Line.' There is no separate, dedicated legend or symbol key box present on this sheet." Vision of Sheet 19 confirmed legend showing "[T Symbol] | Transformer Pad" and "E | Proposed Underground Electric." DISCREPANCY: Legend on Sheet 3 defines Transformer Pad as a square symbol with "T", but Sheet 21 uses TEXT CALLOUTS ("Electrical Transformer Pad") instead of the defined symbol.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires legend symbols to match actual symbols used in plans. The issue is whether text callouts are acceptable alternatives to defined symbols. Sheet 3's Legend defines specific symbols, but actual plans use TEXT CALLOUTS instead. This creates ambiguity about whether callouts are alternative identification methods or whether symbols should be used per legend. The plans do not consistently use either the symbols defined in the legend or provide alternative legend definitions for the text callouts used.

findings.comment: Electric facilities may not be shown clearly and at legible scale on all required plan sheets. On Sheet 9 (Site Plan), electric facility routing and symbols lack the visual clarity and detail shown for other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain). Please enhance the electric facility representation on the site plan to provide equivalent clarity, with clearer routing, larger symbols, and more detailed labeling to match the standard used for other utility systems.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electric facilities at 1" = 20' scale with clear blue line colors and legible text callouts. Symbols are distinguishable, and overall presentation is clear for the plan-view routing shown. However, on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), electric infrastructure (transformer pad, existing overhead line) is shown with minimal detail and less visual emphasis compared to water, wastewater, and storm drain routing, which are shown with bold lines and extensive callouts. The inconsistency between sheets creates mixed clarity: Sheet 21 is clear, but Sheet 9 provides insufficient electric facility detail relative to other utilities shown.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1) requires that 'Electric facilities [be] shown clearly and at legible scale on required plans, [with] symbols [that are] not too small to distinguish facility types'. While Sheet 21 meets this standard for the preliminary design plan, Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not provide equivalent clarity and detail for electric infrastructure. Best practice requires consistent clarity across all sheets showing utilities. The site plan should show electric routing and facilities with comparable prominence to water, wastewater, and storm drain systems.

findings.comment: Electric facilities not shown clearly and at legible scale on landscape plan, or symbols too small to distinguish. Transformer locations, pull boxes, underground electric line routing, and electric easements must be shown on the landscape plan at adequate scale for visual coordination with landscaping.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) for electric facility display. Vision analysis revealed: 'Electric facilities are generally NOT prominently featured on this landscape plan. I do not see transformers, meters, or pull boxes depicted or labeled. There is one utility line shown: An overhead electric line indicated by a line with the text "-OHE-" running horizontally along the bottom edge of the site plan.' The overhead electric line shown is at minimal scale with only the '-OHE-' label; no transformer symbols, pad locations, meter locations, or underground line routing is depicted on the landscape plan. The vision analysis noted: 'Because there are no clearance zones marked, this visual overlap suggests a potential conflict between the overhead lines and the tree canopies,' indicating the electric line is difficult to distinguish from landscape features at the sheet scale.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1) requires that plans show 'electric facilities' at 'legible scale' on 'required plans,' and the grouping's Documents to Review specifies that electric facilities must be shown on 'Landscape Plan' with facilities 'clearly visible.' While the landscape plan (Sheet 31) contains one minimally-labeled overhead electric line, electric facilities are not shown 'clearly and at legible scale' as required. Transformers, pull boxes, underground lines, and easements are absent. The single overhead line shown without clearance zones or protection buffers makes it difficult to distinguish from landscape elements and does not provide the visual clarity required for landscape coordination.

findings.comment: Electric utility easements are not clearly delineated showing locations and extents on plans. Please add clear visual delineation (shading, hatch pattern, or bold boundary lines) to distinguish electric utility easements from the surrounding site area on site plan and utility plan, with labels showing easement width and recorded instrument numbers.

findings.observation: Sheets 9 and 21 show utility easements with text labels: '5' P.U.E.', '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14...', '3' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14...', and others. The grouping guidance states that this is an 'All sites' applicable requirement. Clear delineation means visual distinction that allows reviewers to readily identify and understand easement boundaries. Text labels alone without visual emphasis are insufficient. The applicant must use graphic techniques (color fill, hatch pattern, bold boundary lines, or other standard plan representation) to clearly distinguish easement areas from surrounding site area.

Their absence prevents verification that the proposed buildings and utilities do not conflict with these recorded restrictions.

findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate that development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities. Please show on the site plan marked access routes or note that access will be maintained to transformer pads, pull boxes, meters, and easement areas, ensuring that service vehicles can reach all electric facilities for maintenance and emergency response.
applicableAreas: Site layout and electric facility access routes
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 8) contains electric notes stating: 'The owner/developer of this subdivision/lot shall provide Austin Energy with any easement and/or access required, in addition to those indicated, for the installation and ongoing maintenance of overhead and underground electric facilities.' This indicates intent to maintain access but does not provide a specific demonstration on the site plan showing that development will NOT limit Austin Energy personnel access. Sheets 9 and 21 show building locations, driveways, and parking areas but do not include marked access routes or explicit documentation that Austin Energy will have clear access to transformer locations, pull boxes, meters, and existing overhead facilities along the property boundary.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(4) requires that 'Plans [demonstrate] that development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities'. While the electric notes express an intention to maintain access, the site plan does not explicitly demonstrate this through marked access routes, width clearances, or traffic pattern design that ensures Austin Energy vehicles can access facilities. This should be shown graphically on the site plan with clear access routes marked to transformers, pull boxes, meters, and easement areas.

findings.comment: Plans do not explicitly demonstrate that development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities. Access pathways, maintenance clearance zones, and vehicle turning radiuses must be shown and documented to ensure Austin Energy can access and maintain all electric infrastructure.
applicableAreas: All electric facility locations and easements
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21 for documentation demonstrating Austin Energy personnel access to electric facilities. Sheet 21 shows transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground line routing throughout the site. Easement areas are shown (5' Electric Easements on eastern and southern boundaries per vision analysis). However, no plans explicitly demonstrate or document that 'development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities.' No access pathways are labeled, no clearance zones for equipment trucks are designated, no maintenance access widths are specified. No notes on the plans state that a 20-foot equipment access corridor is maintained, or that easement roads support required vehicle loads. The grouping's Regulatory Overview mentions transmission easement road requirements (46,000 lb tandem axle) but no plans show access provisions for electric distribution facilities.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(4) requires that 'Plans must demonstrate that development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities.' The electrical design plan shows facility locations but does not explicitly document how access for maintenance, repair, or emergency response will be maintained. No access roads, clearance zones, or turning radiuses are shown or dimensioned. No notes certify that Austin Energy has adequate access to transformers, vaults, or other equipment for routine or emergency operations. The absence of access documentation means the plans do not affirmatively demonstrate code compliance with the access requirement.

From the printed sheet alone, only blue-colored display is observable, which contradicts the Magenta requirement but may not conclusively prove CAD file non-compliance without examining the source file.

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided. Site has existing overhead electric poles and lines adjacent to Valley View Road. Building elevations are required to show the relationship between proposed structures and existing electric poles/lines, and to verify compliance with clearance standards per UCM § 1.10.3 (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial clearance from overhead distribution lines).
applicableAreas: Locations of existing utility poles and streetlights adjacent to proposed buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) documents existing distribution poles with power lines along Valley View Road (western and southern property boundaries) and shows the overhead utility line (O.H.U.L.) symbols. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the site layout and building locations. However, the site plan set contains no building elevation sheets. The README.md lists 39 sheets in the site plan, primarily focused on site plan, grading, drainage, landscape, details, and utility plans—no architectural building elevation sheets are included. Without building elevations, the three-dimensional relationship between existing poles/lines and proposed buildings cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires that 'Building elevations shall be provided showing proposed structures with streets, streetlights, and electric poles.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement when electric poles or streetlights exist on or adjacent to the site. The applicant has not provided any building elevation sheets. This deficiency directly prevents verification of clearance compliance between proposed structures and existing overhead electric facilities.

findings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing proposed structures with adjacent streets (Valley View Road), streetlights, and electric poles. Provide front and side elevations for all buildings showing the relationship to Valley View Road, existing poles, and overhead/underground facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(2).
applicableAreas: Relationship to existing Valley View Road, poles, and streetlights
findings.observation: The site plan submittal (39 sheets total) contains detailed site plans, grading plans, utility plans, and landscape plans, but does NOT include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing site features and property context, but no building elevation views have been identified in the submittal. UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires building elevations showing the relationship between proposed structures and existing public infrastructure including streets, streetlights, and electric poles. The absence of building elevation sheets representing the buildings' relationship to Valley View Road and any adjacent utility poles/streetlights is a clear deficiency in the required documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires building elevations to show the relationship between proposed structures and existing streets, streetlights, and electric poles. These elevation views are essential for demonstrating clearance compliance and understanding site context. The site plan submittal includes plan views and details but lacks the elevation views specifically required by code. This is a documentation requirement that must be satisfied through the addition of building elevation sheets for all buildings, showing their relationship to Valley View Road and any adjacent utility infrastructure.

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided showing the relationship between proposed buildings and electric easements (north, south, and east boundaries). The 'preliminary' designation on this electrical plan suggests final details are pending, but the lack of any reference to AE Design specifications is a notable gap in the plan set.

findings.comment: Transformer pads NW of Building 1 and W of Building 2 are located within 4 feet of vehicle circulation driveways but lack bollard callouts and specifications. findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows all five transformer pads located immediately adjacent to vehicle circulation routes (driveways). Vision analysis confirmed that pads NW of Bldg 1, W of Bldg 2, W of Bldg 8, E of Bldg 4, and E of Bldg 7 are all within or very near the 4-foot threshold from vehicle circulation areas. The measure-distance tool confirmed the pad NW of Bldg 1 is 0 feet from the driveway edge (touching the driveway). Sheet 9 shows bollard callouts (labeled 'Bollard (Typ)') pointing to features at two locations: E of Bldg 4 and E of Bldg 7. These two pads have bollard protection documented. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies that equipment pads installed within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle routes must be protected by 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details, with spacing that allows equipment door opening. The site plan clearly shows two of five transformer pads (E of Bldg 4 and E of Bldg 7) with bollard protection documented via callouts. However, the other three pads (NW of Bldg 1, W of Bldg 2, and W of Bldg 8) are equally exposed to vehicle circulation (based on spatial layout) but lack any bollard documentation. This represents an inconsistency and likely non-compliance for the unprotected pads. At minimum, the pads at NW of Bldg 1 and W of Bldg 2 require bollard documentation.

The absence of any bollard callouts, specifications, or detail references on the electrical plan or construction details sheets suggests the requirement is not being addressed. Without explicit bollard documentation showing their location, spacing, and specifications per AE Design equipment pad details, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Transformer pads lack required clear zone: 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area in front of transformer equipment not maintained. Trees and tree wells immediately adjacent to transformer pads obstruct required vertical clearance and set-up depth.
