Sheet 9 site plan shows internal driveway widths ranging from 21.3' to 29.6' with parking stalls immediately adjacent to transformer pad. No plan sheets depict or dimension a 20' × 35' set-up area in front of any transformer pad, nor do they show 35-foot vertical clearances above the pads. Tree wells and tree canopies shown on both electrical plan and site plan would obstruct the required set-up area and vertical clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 20' × 35' set-up area in front of transformer equipment with 35-foot vertical clearance. The project plans show transformer pads with trees (canopy symbols and tree wells) immediately adjacent, obstructing the required set-up area dimensions and vertical clearance. No alternative notation of approved reduced clearances or AE Design variance is documented. The physical constraints of tree placement, building proximity, and parking layout make the required set-up area unachievable without relocating trees or redesigning the site layout.

findings.comment: Transformer pad 1 is directly adjacent to a tree well, which obstructs access and creates a site feature blocking the required clear zone around the transformer. Remove the tree well or relocate the transformer to a site location that is free of landscaping, trees, tree wells, and other obstructions within a minimum 20 ft × 35 ft clear set-up area. Alternatively, provide documented coordination with Austin Energy Design and the arborist confirming the tree well can be modified or removed to provide unobstructed transformer access.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 1 (western edge, adjacent to Bldg. 2)
Tree well and landscaping area near Transformer 1
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21 to identify site features near transformer pads. Transformer 1, located on the far western edge north of the main entrance driveway, is positioned directly adjacent to a labeled 'Tree Well' on Sheet 9. Vision analysis confirmed this transformer pad 'directly abuts a labeled Tree Well to its north.' Tree wells are protective structures around tree trunks that prevent direct vehicle access and movement. Additional overlapping tree canopy symbols were noted on Sheet 21 in the vicinity of T1. The transformer pad is surrounded by landscape elements that would restrict truck maneuvering and equipment placement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 and § 1.3.16 require that transformer pads 'be kept clear of all structures, landscaping, and improvements' to ensure Austin Energy personnel can install, operate, and maintain equipment with appropriate vehicle and personnel access. 'Trees, landscaping, street furniture, dumpster enclosures, water meters, grates, poles, fire hydrants' and other obstructions cannot block access to transformer pads or create safety hazards during equipment servicing. A tree well directly adjacent to the transformer pad represents a site feature that physically obstructs the clear zone and restricts the space available for truck approach, equipment landing, and personnel movement. Tree wells are designed to limit access to protect tree roots; this directly conflicts with the unrestricted access requirement for electrical equipment.

findings.comment: Site features (trees, landscaping in tree wells) blocking access to transformer pads. Transformer pads not kept clear of all structures and landscaping for Austin Energy 24/7 access.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) vision analysis identified large circular tree canopy symbols overlapping or immediately adjacent to all three transformer pad locations. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies a 'Tree Well' with tree symbol immediately adjacent (within 2-5 feet) to the westernmost transformer pad. Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) shows extensive tree planting with designations for street yard trees (SY), parking lot trees (PL), and mitigation trees (M), but does not exclude trees from transformer access zones. No notation on any sheet indicates trees are excluded from transformer pad clearance zones or set-up areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 and § 1.3.16 require transformer pads to be kept clear of all structures and landscaping to ensure Austin Energy 24/7 access. Trees are explicitly prohibited from transformer access zones and set-up areas due to interference with truck access, visual sight lines, root zone conflicts with subsurface infrastructure, and safety concerns. The presence of tree canopies and tree wells immediately adjacent to transformer pads (as shown on Sheets 21 and 9) creates obstructions that violate the requirement for unobstructed access and set-up area.

findings.comment: Vault Easement notation appears on electrical plan for property outside downtown Network Area. Clarify whether transformer vault rooms (subsurface rooms) are proposed; if so, provide evidence that site is within the downtown Network Area per UCM § 1.11.5. If site is outside Network Area (as facts indicate), transformer vaults are prohibited; transformers must be pad-mounted or in niches with AE Design consultation per UCM § 1.5.2.6.
applicableAreas: Transformer locations and proposed service configuration
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) showing four transformer pads labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". The property is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704, which is in South Austin. According to facts.md, there is no Network Area designation at this property and no regulating plan applies. The Network Area is defined in UCM § 1.11.5 as the downtown Austin area providing vault-only service. The site location is outside downtown and the project facts confirm no Network Area status. However, Sheet 21 shows one transformer location with an adjacent "Vault Easement" label, suggesting a possible vault configuration may be planned. If transformer vaults are being proposed at this location outside the Network Area, this would violate code requirements (UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.10.4 require vault-only service in Network Area; outside Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted or in niches per UCM § 1.5.2.6).
findings.reasoning: Code limits transformer vault rooms to the downtown Network Area only (UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5). Outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted or located in niches (with AE Design consultation). The site is clearly outside the Network Area (South Lamar area, no Network Area designation per facts.md). The presence of a "Vault Easement" label on Sheet 21 near Building 2 raises the question of whether a transformer vault room (subsurface room with multiple transformers) is being proposed outside the Network Area. If the vault easement indicates a planned vault room (rather than just vault infrastructure within a padmount config), this would be a code violation. Clarification is needed about the exact nature of the vault easement and whether transformer vault rooms are being proposed.

findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows a 'Vault Easement' notation adjacent to Transformer 4, indicating proposed vault infrastructure. The property is located outside the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5) where vault rooms are prohibited. Transformers outside the Network Area must be pad-mounted or in niches with AE Design consultation. Clarify: (1) Remove the Vault Easement notation if transformers will be pad-mounted, or (2) If a vault is intended, this site does not qualify per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5 and cannot proceed with vault design at this location.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 4 (southwestern side, west of Bldg. 8) and vicinity
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which shows Transformer 4 in the southwestern portion of the site (west of Bldg. 8). Vision analysis of this sheet identified that 'immediately adjacent to this pad is a dashed rectangle labeled "Vault Easement", suggesting below-grade infrastructure may be associated with this specific location.' The notation of a 'Vault Easement' indicates the applicant intends or is planning for vault infrastructure at this location. Per facts.md, the property address (3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704) is in South Austin, MF-2 zoning, and there is NO notation of the site being in the 'Network Area.' The facts.md specifically confirms: 'Regulating Plan: None' and the site address and zoning clearly place this property outside the downtown Network Area defined in UCM § 1.11.5.
findings.reasoning: The notation of 'Vault Easement' adjacent to Transformer 4 indicates an intent to construct or provide access to underground vault infrastructure. Per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5, transformer vault rooms are only permitted within the downtown Network Area. The property is clearly outside the Network Area (South Austin location, Valley View Road, MF-2 zoning). Therefore, vault room construction is prohibited at this location. The applicant must either: (1) remove the vault easement notation and confirm all transformers are pad-mounted only, or (2) if a vault is intended, relocate the infrastructure to a property within the downtown Network Area.

findings.comment: Multiple transformer pads appear to be located within 2 feet of concrete sidewalks per visual analysis of Sheet 9. Provide: (1) Updated site plan with dimension lines and callouts clearly documenting the distance from back of sidewalk to each transformer pad (T1, T2, T3, T4), confirming minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4, OR (2) Reposition transformers to achieve minimum 2-foot separation from all sidewalks, or (3) If clearance cannot be achieved, provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing reduced sidewalk clearance with specific approval conditions.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pads (T1, T2, T3, T4) relative to adjacent sidewalks and pedestrian paths
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to measure distance from transformer pads to sidewalks and pedestrian paths. Vision analysis identified clearances for each transformer: 'T1: A Concrete Sidewalk wraps tightly around the eastern and northern sides of this pad. It appears to be within 2 feet of the pad. T2: A concrete sidewalk running north-south along the side of Bldg. 4 passes very close to the western edge of this pad (appears to be within 2 feet). T3: A concrete walkway runs east-west just north of the pad, connecting the driveway to Unit 604. It appears to be within 2 to 5 feet. T4: A concrete sidewalk runs north-south just to the east of the pad, leading to Unit 801. It appears to be within 2 feet.' Three of the four transformers (T1, T2, T4) are documented as being within 2 feet of sidewalks, which meets or may slightly exceed the 2-foot minimum. T3 is within 2-5 feet. No specific dimension lines, callouts, or clearance annotations are provided on the site plan to document compliance with the 2-foot setback requirement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Transformer equipment pads not minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' The 'back of sidewalk' refers to the edge of the sidewalk surface farthest from the roadway or pedestrian area - essentially the inner edge of the sidewalk adjacent to property features. A 2-foot minimum separation is required to: (1) provide space for sidewalk maintenance and repair, (2) prevent sidewalk deterioration from transformer vibration or equipment settling, (3) ensure pedestrians are not placed in direct proximity to electrical equipment, and (4) allow for minor adjustments in sidewalk alignment during maintenance. Vision analysis indicates T1, T2, and T4 are at or potentially at less than the 2-foot minimum. While T3 may be within acceptable range (2-5 feet is unclear - 'within 2 to 5 feet' could mean 2 feet or could mean 5 feet). The absence of specific dimension documentation on the site plan creates ambiguity. To comply with the requirement, applicants must affirmatively demonstrate the 2-foot setback is maintained. Estimated visual distances are insufficient for compliance verification.

findings.comment: Transformer equipment pads not minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks. Sidewalk shown immediately adjacent to transformer pad without documented minimum clearance.
applicableAreas: Westernmost transformer pad location on western property line near Building 1
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a concrete sidewalk labeled 'Construct 6\' Concrete Sidewalk' immediately to the west of the transformer pad marked 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'. Vision analysis confirmed 'To the immediate west of the pad is a pathway labeled "Construct 6\' Concrete Sidewalk."' The exact distance between the transformer pad and the back of this sidewalk is not dimensioned on the plan. Visual estimation from the plan at scale 1" = 20' suggests the sidewalk is very close (potentially less than 2 feet) from the transformer pad.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires a minimum 2-foot clearance from transformer pads to the back of sidewalks. The site plan shows a sidewalk immediately adjacent to (west of) the transformer pad, but does not dimension the specific clearance. Visual inspection at plan scale suggests the clearance is minimal and potentially less than 2 feet.

findings.comment: Transformer locations must be shown on all required plan sheets. Currently shown only on electrical plan (Sheet 21) and site plan (Sheet 9). Missing from wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer locations with associated routing and infrastructure. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'. However, transformers are NOT depicted on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), Sheet 19 (Wet Utilities Plan), or Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile). Although Sheet 19 and 20 include a 'Transformer Pad' symbol in their legends, no transformers are actually drawn on these sheets.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer locations must be georeferenced on all required plan sheets to facilitate utility coordination and ensure proper design integration across all disciplines. The grouping guidance specifies that 'Transformer locations must be shown consistently across multiple plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and elevation sheets)' and that 'grading and storm plans must also show transformers when those disciplines are affected by transformer placement or routing.' Omitting transformers from the wet utilities, landscape, and grading plans means these critical disciplines have not integrated the electrical infrastructure and cannot verify conflicts, clearances, or impacts.

findings.comment: Transformer locations are not shown consistently across all required plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads, Sheet 9 shows 1 transformer, and Sheets 11, 12, 19, and 31 show no transformers. Add transformer locations to site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan. Ensure all transformer locations are consistent across all sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 4 transformer pads with locations in northwest, southwest, northeast, and southeast areas of the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1 transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" near Building 1. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains legend symbols for transformer pads but no actual transformer pads are drawn on the plan. Sheets 11 (Grading Plan), 12 (Storm Sewer Plan), and 31 (Landscape Plan) do not show any transformer locations. This creates significant inconsistency: 4 transformers are documented on the electrical plan but only 1 appears on the main site plan, and transformers are entirely absent from the wet utilities, grading, storm, and landscape plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that georeferenced AutoCAD drawings clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations across all required plan sheets. The standard sheet set for transformer documentation includes site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading/storm plans when applicable. The variance between sheets—with Sheet 21 showing 4 transformers and Sheet 9 showing only 1—indicates either incomplete documentation on the site plan or an incomplete electrical design on Sheet 21. The complete absence of transformers from Sheets 19, 31, 11, and 12 prevents verification of clearances, conflicts with other utilities, and tree preservation impacts. For a multi-building development with 4 transformers, omitting transformers from landscape and grading plans prevents the reviewer from verifying required clearances and access routes.

findings.comment: Each transformer must be labeled with its type: Pad-Mounted Transformer, Pole-Mounted Transformer, Vault, or Service Drop. Current labels 'Electrical Transformer Pad' lack explicit type specification.
findings.observation: Four transformers are shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) with locations and routing identified. However, each transformer is labeled only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no additional type designation. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding size (e.g., kVA), specific type, or whether they are CT metered or building metered.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that drawings 'clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations.' For Austin Energy personnel reviewing these plans, knowing whether transformers are pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault-mounted, or service drops is critical for design coordination and construction. The generic label 'Transformer Pad' may imply pad-mounted, but explicit specification of type (using standardized designations like 'Pad-Mounted Transformer' or 'Pole-Mounted Transformer') is necessary to meet code documentation requirements.

findings.comment: Transformer type not specified. Each transformer pad must be labeled with its specific type: pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault, or service drop. Add callout notes or legend entries identifying the type for each transformer on the electrical plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 electrical plan labels all transformer locations uniformly as "Electrical Transformer Pad" with no supplemental callouts, notes, or specifications indicating the type of transformer. The label alone provides no information to distinguish between pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault, or service drop configurations. No notes on the electrical plan specify transformer type for the site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly delineate electrical infrastructure with sufficient detail for Austin Energy to verify that the proposed service configuration meets code requirements. Transformer type is fundamental information: pad-mounted transformers require specific clearances per UCM § 1.10.4; vault installations must demonstrate conformance with niche design requirements and Network Area restrictions (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3); pole-mounted units have different access and safety requirements. Omitting type designation prevents verification of compliance with clearance and placement standards.

findings.comment: Transformer locations shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) must match the transformer locations shown on Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) in terms of quantity, position, and labeling. Currently, Sheet 9 shows one transformer marked '(Typ.)' while Sheet 21 shows four transformers with specific locations.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four distinct transformer pad locations distributed across the site (west of Building 1, west of Buildings 2/8, east of Building 4, and south-central between Buildings 6/7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only one transformer location labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)', positioned in the western area of the site. The single transformer shown on Sheet 9 appears to align roughly with the western area where transformers are shown on Sheet 21, but the representation is unclear. The notation '(Typ.)' on Sheet 9 suggests this is a typical or representative symbol rather than a precise location.
findings.reasoning: Transformer locations must be consistent across all plan sheets showing them so that all disciplines and reviewing agencies have a unified understanding of the infrastructure layout. When the same facilities appear on different sheets (site plan, electrical plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, grading plan), their locations should match precisely. The ambiguous representation on Sheet 9 (with a single '(Typ.)' notation) does not align clearly with the four transformers shown on Sheet 21, creating confusion about the actual number and locations of transformers on the site.

findings.comment: Transformer locations are not consistent across plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads while Sheet 9 shows only 1 transformer. Reconcile transformer locations and ensure all transformers appear on all required plan sheets with consistent positioning.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 depicts 4 transformer pads: one in the northwest area (west of Buildings 1 and 2), one in the southwest area (west of Building 8), one in the northeast central area (east of Building 4), and one in the southeast central area (east of Building 7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts only 1 transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" located near Building 1 (northwest area). The three transformers shown on Sheet 21 (southwest, northeast, southeast) are entirely absent from Sheet 9.
findings.reasoning: Transformer locations on Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) show 4 transformer pads, but Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1. This discrepancy violates the requirement for consistent documentation across plan sheets. Reconcile the transformer count and locations between sheets. Ensure all proposed transformers are shown on both the main site plan and the electrical design plan, with matching locations.

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations and 10-foot lateral clearance zones must be shown on the landscape plan to verify that tree locations comply with minimum required clearances from electrical equipment.
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows tree locations throughout the site with various tree types and sizes indicated. However, no transformer pads or electrical routing is depicted on this sheet. The plan includes a legend (Key Notes) defining landscape symbols and tree abbreviations but does not show electrical infrastructure. Vision analysis confirms: 'There are no transformers explicitly shown, labeled, or depicted on this sheet... The plan does not show transformer routing, nor does it depict or verify a 10-foot lateral clearance from any transformer pads.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.10.4, no tree may be planted within 10 lateral feet of any side of pad-mounted electric equipment. The grouping guidance requires 'Plans must show transformer routing on landscape sheets to verify compliance with tree clearance requirements.' Without showing the transformer locations and their 10-foot clearance zones on the landscape plan, it is impossible to verify that tree placement complies with the code-required separation distance. This is critical information for both design review and construction oversight.

findings.comment: Transformer routing not shown on landscape plan. Show all transformer pad locations and access routes on the landscape plan. Verify that no trees are planted within 10 feet lateral clearance from any transformer side or within access door swing areas. Indicate root barrier requirements for trees within 20 feet of underground electrical routing.
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show any transformer pad locations, electrical routing, or transformer access areas. The landscape plan contains only landscape elements (proposed paving, street yards, parking lot landscaping, trees, irrigation system) and overhead electric line notation on the property boundary. The proposed planting plan—which includes numerous trees and shrub locations throughout the site—cannot be verified against transformer clearance requirements because no transformer locations or routing are depicted on the landscape plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of any side of pad-mounted electric equipment and requires root barriers for trees within 20 lateral feet of underground equipment. The landscape plan is the primary document for tree locations and planting design. Without transformer routing shown on the landscape plan, the reviewer cannot verify compliance with tree clearance requirements, cannot confirm that proposed plantings don't conflict with transformer access door swings, and cannot assess root barrier requirements for trees near underground conduit. This omission prevents approval of the landscape plan.

findings.comment: Identify and show on plans a transformer-specific electrical easement with dimensions adequate to encompass the transformer pad location, all required clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side), and an access zone for Austin Energy operations and maintenance.
findings.observation: Sheet 9, 11, and 21 show various electrical easements (5' Electric & Tele. Easement, 5' P.U.E., etc.) labeled with recording information. However, these easements are shown as property-line-based boundaries and do not specifically delineate easement areas around the transformer pad locations. The grouping guidance states: 'Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover specific facility clearances and access requirements' and references UCM § 1.3.24 (Easements for Electric Distribution Facilities). No easement dimensions are verified against the specific clearance requirements for the transformer pads themselves (which require clearances ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side and use).
findings.reasoning: Austin Energy requires easements that are adequate in size to cover not only the physical location of electrical facilities but also the clearance zones and access areas required by code. The grouping notes state: 'There is no uniform "5-foot electrical easement" standard in Austin codes. Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover the physical location of facilities, required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side and configuration), and areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access per UCM § 1.3.24.' Without showing transformer-specific easement boundaries with dimensions verified against code clearance requirements, compliance cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Electrical easement around transformer facilities not shown or not adequate. Show dedicated easement boundaries around each transformer pad sufficient to cover: (1) the physical equipment location, (2) all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (10-15 feet depending on equipment side and access requirements), and (3) Austin Energy access and maintenance areas. Label easement with recording information or "to be dedicated" notation.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 4 transformer pad locations but does not show any dedicated electrical easement boundaries or polygons around the transformer facilities. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing electrical easements on property boundaries (labeled as "5' Electric Easement") but does not show proposed easements around transformer equipment. The grouping overview notes that electrical easements must be adequate to cover: (1) the physical location of facilities, (2) required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side), and (3) areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access. No such easement polygons are depicted in the site plan set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.24 defines easements as property rights necessary to ensure safe construction, operation, maintenance, and access to electric facilities. UCM § 1.10.4 specifies varying clearance requirements: hot-stick use areas require 10-15 feet clearance; sides with controls require 5 feet clearance from fencing; sides without operators may be 3 feet from removable fencing. Each transformer requires an easement adequate to encompass all clearance zones and access areas. UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly show easement boundaries. The complete absence of transformer easement delineation prevents verification that property within the site is reserved for electrical facilities and that access for Austin Energy maintenance is protected.

findings.comment: Each transformer must be labeled with its size in kVA (e.g., '150 kVA Pad-Mounted Transformer' or '300 kVA Pad-Mounted Transformer').
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) labels the four transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no size information. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding size (e.g., kVA).' No kVA ratings, load specifications, or capacity information is provided for any transformer.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must include sufficient detail for Austin Energy to coordinate service adequacy with the project's electrical load. Transformer size (kVA rating) is essential information for design review, equipment ordering, and installation planning. Without size specifications, Austin Energy cannot verify that the proposed transformers are adequate to serve the project and cannot identify any shortfalls or required upgrades.

findings.comment: Transformer size not specified. Label each transformer with its capacity in kVA (e.g., "50 kVA", "100 kVA") and include transformer specifications (phase, voltage, cooling method) on the electrical plan. Confirm with Austin Energy that the total proposed transformer capacity is adequate to serve all 39 units.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels all four transformer pads with the text "Electrical Transformer Pad" but provides no kVA size, capacity rating, phase configuration, or other specification. No notes on the sheet detail transformer sizes. The architectural and electrical load information that would determine required transformer capacity is not included in the site plan set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires sufficient plan detail for Austin Energy to verify that proposed service meets project requirements. Transformer size is essential information: it determines clearance requirements, cable sizing, cooling needs, and whether additional transformers are needed. Omitting size makes it impossible to verify that the four transformers are adequate to serve 39 residential units, or that sizing complies with Austin Energy design standards.

findings.comment: Label each transformer with its metering method (e.g., 'CT Metered' or 'Building Metered') to indicate how service measurement will be configured.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers but provides no labeling indicating metering method. Vision analysis confirms: 'The transformers are solely labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". There is no information provided regarding... whether they are CT metered or building metered.' No notation distinguishes between CT (current transformer) metered service, standard building metered service, or other metering configurations.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must specify the metering method because this affects service design. CT metering is used for larger transformer capacities (typically above 75 kVA), while building-level metering may be used for smaller loads. The metering method impacts the location of meter installation, the service distribution enclosure configuration, and the overall electrical service design. Without this specification, coordination with Austin Energy and proper electrical design cannot be completed.

findings.comment: Transformer metering method not labeled. Specify for each transformer whether it is CT metered (with secondary meter locations) or building metered (with individual unit metering). If meters are grouped (served from one service connection), label the service distribution enclosure, wireway, and meter bank location with grouping notation and reference to UCM § 1.9.3.4.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels transformers only as "Electrical Transformer Pad" with no indication of metering method. The eight meter locations are labeled as "Electrical Meters" but no callout specifies whether each meter is CT metered or building metered, or whether meters are grouped per UCM § 1.9.3.4 requirements. Service distribution enclosure or wireway locations are not identified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly detail service infrastructure. Metering method (CT metered at the transformer vs. building metered) affects meter placement, conductor sizing, and point-of-service configuration. For multi-unit developments, UCM § 1.9.3.4 requires that when two or more meters are served from one service connection, meters and disconnects must be grouped in a common location (meter bank/SDE) with specified clearances and line-of-sight requirements. Omitting metering method prevents verification of compliance with grouping and accessibility standards.

findings.comment: Meter locations must be shown and labeled on the site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) in addition to the electrical plan (Sheet 21).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows eight meter locations on building exterior walls, with each labeled 'Electrical Meters.' However, meters are NOT shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) - vision analysis confirmed 'There are no electrical meters shown or labeled on this sheet.' Meters are also NOT shown on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) - vision analysis confirmed 'There are no... meters shown or labeled on this sheet.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.A, meter locations must be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan). This allows all reviewing disciplines to verify meter accessibility, line of sight to transformers, separation from other utilities, and landscape or site features that might interfere with meter access or visibility. Omitting meters from the site and landscape plans means these disciplines have not verified meter integration with their designs.

findings.comment: Meter locations not shown on all required plan sheets. Show all electrical meter locations on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. Identify each meter location with a callout and label. Note whether meters are grouped (per UCM § 1.9.3.4) or individual. Verify that each meter location is: (1) at ground level, (2) readily accessible, (3) within sight of its serving transformer, and (4) positioned with disconnects within 20 feet for grouped configurations.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 8 meter locations labeled "Electrical Meters" on building exterior walls. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one gas meter but does not show electrical meter locations. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has a legend entry for utility symbols but no meters are drawn on the plan. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show electrical meter locations. The required site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan all lack electrical meter documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.A requires meter locations to be shown on plans. Meters must be on first floor or ground level, readily accessible, within sight of the transformer, and for grouped metering, positioned with disconnects in a common location per UCM § 1.9.3.4. The absence of meter locations on the site plan and landscape plan prevents verification of accessibility, sightlines to transformers, and clearances from other utilities. For a multi-unit development, meter locations are essential to demonstrating that the metering and disconnection configuration complies with grouped metering requirements.

findings.comment: Show and label all service disconnects on the electrical plan. Indicate their location relative to meters (grouped together per code requirements) and verify they are within 20 feet and line of sight of the meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows and labels eight meter locations on building exterior walls as 'Electrical Meters.' However, no disconnects are shown, labeled, or identified on the electrical plan. The grouping guidance specifies: 'Meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location... The disconnect must be grouped with the meter beside the AE transformer (adhering to transformer clearances per UCM § 1.10.4) or outside the building within line of sight of the transformer.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1 and 1.16.0, both meters AND disconnects must be shown and labeled on plans. The disconnect is where the customer's service is isolated from the utility service and is a critical safety component. Without showing disconnect locations, it cannot be verified that they are properly grouped with meters, within required distances, within line of sight of transformers, and accessible for emergency disconnection.

findings.comment: Meters and disconnects not labeled on all required sheets. Label all electrical meters and disconnects on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. For grouped metering, label the service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway location, and note the distance between meters and disconnects (maximum 20 feet, must be within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Specify meter specifications (single-phase, three-phase, main vs. sub-meter).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels meters as "Electrical Meters" with callout lines to building wall locations. Sheets 9, 19, and 31 do not show meters or meter labels. No callouts define meter specifications, disconnect locations, service distribution enclosure locations, or grouping configurations. For a multi-unit residential development, disconnect locations are not identified relative to meters.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 and § 1.16.0 require that plans clearly identify meter and disconnect locations. Meter labels and disconnect callouts enable Austin Energy to verify that the service configuration is accessible, properly grouped (if applicable), and compliant with spacing requirements (maximum 20 feet between meter and disconnect per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Without labels and callouts on the site, wet utilities, and landscape plans, the reviewer cannot confirm that the metering design meets code requirements across all plan disciplines.

findings.comment: Indicate on the electrical plan that all meter locations are within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. Include sight-line notation or written confirmation on the plan for each meter-to-transformer relationship.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exterior walls and four transformers at various site locations. Vision analysis confirms: 'Meter locations are marked by small grouped rectangles on the building exteriors and are explicitly labeled "Electrical Meters" with leader lines pointing to them. There is no text, notation, or graphic indicating a required line of sight to the transformers.' The grouping guidance notes: 'current code requires "within sight" visibility but does not specify a maximum distance—older references to "150 ft line of sight" are not codified in current UCM.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B, all meter locations must be 'within sight of an Austin Energy transformer.' From a 2D site plan view, it is difficult to definitively determine whether meters on building walls can see transformers located elsewhere on the site without 3D visualization or explicit line-of-sight notations. The site plan does not include sight-line annotations, distance measurements, or clear notation confirming that each meter location is within sight of at least one transformer. This creates ambiguity about compliance.

findings.comment: Meter sight line to transformer not verified. Show on the electrical plan or a separate diagram that each electrical meter is within clear sight line of its serving transformer. If any meter does not have direct line of sight to the nearest transformer, provide written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units for the exception. Provide sight line diagrams or cross-reference elevation views confirming visibility.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations on building exterior walls and 4 transformer pad locations distributed across the site. Meters appear to be positioned on various building sides (north, west, south, east). Transformers are located in northwest, southwest, northeast, and southeast areas. Without clear sight line diagrams, elevation views, or explicit distance callouts, it is not possible to verify that all 8 meters are within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. The term "within sight" in UCM § 1.9.3.1.B does not specify a distance limit (older references to "150 ft line of sight" are not codified), but direct visual contact must be apparent. Given the distributed meter and transformer locations, several meters may not have clear line-of-sight to a transformer.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. The grouping notes that "within sight" visibility is the current code requirement with no maximum distance specified, but direct visual contact is required. Without sight line diagrams showing clear, unobstructed lines between each meter and its serving transformer, the reviewer cannot confirm compliance. The scattered distribution of transformers and meters across 8 buildings suggests that some meters may be obstructed by building walls or other structures, requiring line-of-sight verification or AE Design approval for exceptions.

findings.comment: Clearly identify and label the Point of Service (where Austin Energy service conductors connect to customer service equipment) on the electrical plan. This may be shown as a meter socket, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or other AE-approved location.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows service entry point labeled 'Underground Electric Line' at the western property boundary, transformers, pull boxes, and meters. However, no specific location is labeled as the 'Point of Service' where Austin Energy's service conductors hand off to the customer's service conductors. The grouping guidance defines point of service as 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect.' While pull boxes are shown, it is unclear which component represents the actual point of service.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.3.4 and the grouping definition, the point of service must be clearly identified on plans because it defines the boundary between Austin Energy's responsibility and the customer's responsibility for electrical infrastructure. This location also determines where disconnects and service distribution enclosures must be placed per UCM § 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B. Without clear identification, design coordination and code compliance verification are incomplete.

findings.comment: Point-of-service location not shown. Identify and label the point-of-service (POS) location(s) where Austin Energy conductors connect to customer conductors. This may be at a meter socket, pedestal, SDE (service distribution enclosure), pull box, or other approved enclosure. Label with "Point of Service" notation and specify the type of enclosure. Verify that all customer conductors originate from the labeled POS.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electrical routing, transformer pads, and meter locations, but does not explicitly identify or label a point-of-service (POS) location. UCM § 1.3.4 defines point of service as the location where Austin Energy's conductors connect with the customer's conductors. The plan shows meters on building walls and transformers in common areas but does not label the specific location(s) where the connection point(s) between AE and customer infrastructure occur. No callout identifies the meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull box, or other location where the POS connection is made.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines point of service as a critical infrastructure element. The POS location must be clearly identified because it designates the boundary between Austin Energy responsibility (up to the POS) and customer responsibility (from the POS onward). Without explicit POS identification, the reviewer cannot verify that the service configuration is properly documented, that customer conductors are correctly routed, and that Austin Energy access to the service point is protected. For multi-unit developments, the POS is especially important for understanding service distribution, metering grouping, and disconnect coordination.

findings.comment: Clearly identify the Point of Service location (where AE and Customer conductors connect) on the electrical plan, then verify that service conductors from this point to AE facilities (transformers, service entry) are shown and properly routed.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows blue lines labeled 'Underground Electric Line' routing from the service entry point (western property boundary) through pull boxes to transformers and then to meters. The routing from the primary service entry to the transformers is shown. However, the 'point of service' where customer and Austin Energy conductors connect is not clearly identified, making it ambiguous whether the service conductors 'FROM the point of service' are properly shown.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, 'Service conductors from point of service to AE facilities' must be shown. If the point of service is not clearly labeled, it is unclear which portions of the routing shown represent service conductors 'from' the point of service vs. before it. The grouping guidance defines point of service as 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect,' but the electrical plan does not explicitly identify which element is the point of service.

findings.comment: Service conductors from point of service to AE facilities not clearly identified. Label the point where the underground service stub enters the site and the point of service connection (where AE and customer conductors meet). Show the routing clearly with callouts identifying: (1) service entry point from AE (duct bank, pole, or underground source), (2) point of service location, (3) service distribution enclosure (SDE) or main disconnect location, (4) direction of conductor flow to transformers and meter banks. Verify that service conductors are protected per code and sized per load calculations.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows "Underground Electric Line" routing from the west property edge, through pull boxes, to transformers and meter locations. The underground line enters the site from the left (west) boundary and is drawn as a continuous blue line. However, the plan does not explicitly label: (1) where the service stub originates or enters the site, (2) the specific point of service where AE and customer conductors connect, (3) the direction of conductor flow from the POS to transformers and meters. The routing is shown but the origin point and termination points are not clearly called out.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that service conductor routing be clearly shown from point of service to AE facilities (transformer). The current documentation shows the routing line but lacks explicit identification of the POS location and the service stub entry point. This creates ambiguity: it is unclear whether the line entering from the west represents a service drop from overhead AE lines, an underground service stub from an AE duct bank, or another configuration. Without explicit callouts identifying the POS and service origin, Austin Energy cannot confirm that customer conductors are properly sized, protected, and routed.

findings.comment: Poles or service drops are not clearly shown and labeled on the required plan sheets. While pull boxes are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), utility poles along existing overhead electric lines are not explicitly marked on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). All poles and service drop infrastructure must be clearly identified on the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' at multiple locations along the underground electric routing. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows possible utility poles (cross-mark symbols) along the overhead electric line on the southern boundary, but these are not explicitly labeled as poles. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show any poles or service drops marked or labeled. Per the project's 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' title and visual analysis, the internal site service is underground (no new poles or overhead drops within the site boundaries shown), but Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 do not adequately depict the utility poles that may serve the existing overhead electric line on the southern boundary or any service drop infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that poles or service drops be shown on required plan sheets. While Sheet 21 shows pull boxes (dry infrastructure), and Sheet 31 may show existing poles via symbols, the required sheets (Site Plan showing all utilities and Landscape Plan per Table 1.4.3.B) do not clearly label or identify poles and service drops. The pull boxes shown on Sheet 21 must also be depicted on the Site Plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) to meet the requirement of consistent infrastructure documentation across all required sheets.

findings.comment: Poles and service drops are not clearly shown on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Add pole locations and service drop routing to this sheet to demonstrate coordination with site grading, landscaping, and building placement. Show specific utility pole locations and how overhead or underground service is routed to serve the development.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows poles and service routing via overhead electric lines on the western boundary (OHE designation) and underground routing throughout the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing overhead electric lines along boundaries (OHE designation) but limited detail on service routing. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows OHE (Overhead Electric) lines along the southern boundary but does NOT show any specific poles or service drop locations. The vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirmed: 'While an Overhead Electric (OHE) line is shown along the bottom perimeter, specific utility poles are not distinctly labeled, nor are service drops routing power from the main line to the individual buildings.' The landscape plan is deficient in showing poles and service infrastructure details.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires poles or service drops to be shown on all required plan sheets including the landscape plan. The Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) is explicitly listed as a required plan sheet per the grouping's documents to review and regulatory overview. While Sheet 31 shows overhead electric line designation (OHE), it does not show specific pole locations or service drop routing to buildings. This omission prevents verification of clearances to structures, vegetation conflicts, and proper utility coordination. The grouping's 'Common Violation Patterns' specifically notes 'Incomplete infrastructure across sheets: Electric infrastructure shown on site plan but omitted from landscape plan or electrical plans, violating the requirement to show infrastructure consistently across all required sheets.'

findings.comment: Duct bank routing and locations cannot be verified from available site plan sheets. Whether duct banks are required must be confirmed through Austin Energy ESPA documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes. If duct banks are determined to be required, they must be shown on the electrical site plan and cross-referenced on the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric line routing with labeled callouts for 'Underground Electric Line' and pull boxes, but does not include specifications for cable sizes or conduit dimensions. The grouping definition states that duct bank requirements 'cannot be determined from plans alone' and require Austin Energy Design confirmation through ESPA documentation or Letter of Agreement. No cable size specifications, conduit sizing (such as '5-inch conduit' or '1000 MCM cables'), or main line distribution designations are visible on Sheet 21. The supplementary documents (Master Comment Report, Engineer's Summary Letter) do not reference duct bank requirements or main line distribution infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's own regulatory overview, duct bank determination 'cannot be definitively determined from site plan sheets alone' and requires AE Design confirmation based on service voltage, load, and distribution system design. The applicability of this checklist item depends on Austin Energy Design determining whether duct banks are required, which would be documented in ESPA documentation or a Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service. Without access to AE Design documentation confirming duct bank requirements, the status cannot be definitively determined to be fail. However, if duct banks ARE required per AE Design, they are not shown on the plans.

findings.comment: Cannot verify whether duct bank routing and locations are required for this project from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval letter, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes confirming whether main line duct banks are required or service-only routing is approved.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 electrical plan which shows underground electric service with standard service lateral conduit routing to each building. The electrical routing appears to show typical service-only conduit sizes (not the 1000 MCM cables in 5-inch conduit that would indicate main line distribution). No Austin Energy ESPA documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes are provided in the supplementary documents that would indicate whether duct banks are required for this project. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references Austin Energy design criteria but the actual AE comments are on an external Bluebeam link that cannot be accessed for this review.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item notes this determination "cannot be determined from plans alone" and requires checking Austin Energy ESPA documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes indicating duct bank infrastructure. Sheet 21 shows what appears to be service-only routing, but without formal AE Design documentation confirming that duct banks are NOT required, the requirement cannot be definitively verified. The absence of AE Design approval documentation in the project file means the applicant may have received AE determinations that are not available in this document set. This determination requires confirmation from Austin Energy as referenced in the grouping's regulatory overview.

findings.comment: Street lighting layout and light pole locations are not shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), though the site has public street frontage on Valley View Road. If street lighting is required per Austin Energy Design determination, the layout and pole locations must be shown on the site plan and landscape plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Confirm with AE Design whether street lighting is required for this project and provide documentation of the determination.
findings.observation: The site plan shows the development abuts Valley View Road to the west. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows street frontage along Valley View Road and references street improvement requirements in the general notes ('For construction within the right-of-way, a ROW excavation permit is required'). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows a street yard area along Valley View Road (labeled with H.2 'STREET YARD' symbol). Neither Sheet 9 nor Sheet 31 shows any street lighting layout, light pole locations, or street lighting infrastructure marked or labeled. The project appears to include public street frontage triggering street lighting applicability per UCM § 1.6.0, which directs customers to 'contact AE Design' for specific requirements. No indication of street lighting coordination or requirements is present in the visible plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 addresses Street Lighting requirements. The grouping's applicability guidance states street lighting applies when 'site includes or abuts public streets requiring street lighting.' This site has frontage on Valley View Road (a local street per facts.md), which would typically require street lighting evaluation. The grouping notes that 'specific street lighting requirements are determined by contacting AE Design' and the applicant should verify coordination with AE Design. The absence of any street lighting layout or infrastructure markings on Sheets 9 and 31 (the Site Plan and Landscape Plan where street lighting must be shown per UCM § 1.4.2.6) constitutes non-compliance unless AE Design has waived street lighting for this project. Documentation of AE Design waiver or determination is not visible in available documents.

findings.comment: Cannot verify whether street lighting is required for this site from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required for the Valley View Road frontage per UCM § 1.6.0. If required, show street light layout and pole locations on site plan and landscape plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) were examined for street lighting layout and light pole locations. Sheet 9 includes a Lighting Note addressing "exterior lighting" (building wall-mounted lights), not street lighting infrastructure. No street lighting, light poles, or photometric layouts are shown on either sheet. Facts.md indicates Valley View Road is classified as a local street (ASMP Level 1) with existing lane count not on file and a 2-undivided-lane cross-section planned. The site plan does not show street improvements along Valley View Road frontage that would typically trigger street lighting requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 requires street lighting to be shown when required, and the grouping notes state to "Check: Site plan for street frontage and street improvement requirements; contact AE Design business unit for street lighting determination." The absence of explicit street improvement requirements on Valley View Road frontage and the absence of street lighting from the plans suggest it may not be required. However, the determination cannot be made from site plan review alone per UCM § 1.6.0 - it requires direct contact with AE Design. The checklist item states this determination "cannot be determined from plans alone" and must be verified through AE Design coordination, which does not appear to have been completed or documented.

findings.comment: Street light conduit plan, conduit connections, and routing are not shown on any of the required plan sheets (Site Plan, Landscape Plan, Electrical Plans). If street lighting is required for this project, complete conduit plans must be provided per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. Confirm street lighting requirements with Austin Energy Design.
findings.observation: No street lighting conduit plan, conduit routing, or conduit connections are shown on any of the reviewed sheets (Sheet 9, 21, or 31). The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows only building service conduit routing and meter connections, with no separate street lighting conduit layer or specifications. Sheets 9 and 31 show no lighting conduit markings. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, if street lighting is required, the conduit plan must be shown on the site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 governs Street Lighting. If street lighting is applicable to this project (site has Valley View Road frontage per facts.md), then the street light conduit plan, connections, and routing must be shown per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B on the site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans. The complete absence of street lighting conduit documentation on all sheets constitutes a deficiency if street lighting is required. This must be confirmed with AE Design and, if required, the conduit plans must be added.

findings.comment: Cannot determine applicability from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required. If required, provide street light conduit plan showing conduit connections and routing on site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.6.0.
findings.observation: No street light conduit, conduit connections, or conduit routing are shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), or Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan). As noted in EL-17.7 findings, street lighting infrastructure is not visible anywhere in the plan set. The applicability of this item depends on whether street lighting is required, which per UCM § 1.6.0 must be determined by contacting Austin Energy Design.
findings.reasoning: Per the checklist item's applicability note, this item applies "Only when street lighting or parking garage lighting is required." The grouping's regulatory overview (Section 8 of grouping file) states: "Specific street lighting requirements are determined by contacting AE Design (UCM § 1.6.0)." Without documentation of AE Design's determination regarding street lighting applicability, this item's applicability cannot be confirmed. If street lighting is determined to be required by AE Design, then the absence of street light conduit plans would be a deficiency.

findings.comment: Electrical service pedestals are not shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), which instead shows pad-mounted transformers. Whether pedestals are required must be confirmed through Austin Energy Design documentation or Letter of Agreement. For a multi-family development of this scale, pad-mounted transformers appear more appropriate, but final service type determination requires AE Design confirmation.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows two pad-mounted transformer pads labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad' but does not indicate whether electrical service pedestals are required or planned for this development. UCM § 1.5.3.4 establishes that electrical pedestals may be used for 'residential lots up to 200 amp maximum underground services' per optional policy. However, this is a multi-family townhome development (39 units in 8 buildings), not traditional residential lots, and pedestals would typically not apply to multi-family service. The applicability of this item depends on whether Austin Energy Design has determined that pedestals are required for the service type selected for this development.
findings.reasoning: The grouping definition states this item applies 'Only when electrical pedestals are required for service' and requires checking 'Austin Energy Design documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes specifying pedestal service.' Without access to AE Design documentation confirming pedestal service is required for this multi-family development, the status cannot be definitively determined. Pedestals are typically used for single-family or small residential lots with limited service capacity (≤200 amps), not multi-family buildings with distributed service. If pedestals ARE required per AE Design, they should be shown on the plans.

findings.comment: Cannot verify whether electrical service pedestals are required from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the approved service type and equipment enclosure specification (pedestal, meter socket, service distribution enclosure, or other AE-approved enclosure) per UCM § 1.5.3.4.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 electrical meter locations labeled "Electrical Meters" but does not specify whether these are pedestal-mounted service equipment or other enclosure types. The site plan shows pad-mounted transformers with underground service to meter locations, but the specific meter enclosure type is not detailed. No Austin Energy Design documentation (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement, utility coordination notes) is provided confirming whether pedestals are the approved service type for this project. UCM § 1.5.3.4 notes pedestals are typically used for residential services up to 200 amps maximum.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item's applicability note states: "Check: Austin Energy Design documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes specifying pedestal service." The absence of this documentation means the service type (whether pedestals are required/approved) cannot be verified from site plan review alone. While the physical location of meters is shown, their enclosure type (pedestal vs. other) is not specified on the drawings.

findings.comment: Trenching assignments and responsibilities are not indicated on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21). While customer trenching responsibility is established in UCM § 1.5.3.4 for underground work, the plans should include notes specifying trenching depths, materials, and construction responsibilities to ensure proper coordination with the contractor.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) indicates underground electric service ('Underground Electric Line' label) and shows the internal routing. However, the plan does not include any callouts, notes, or designations showing trenching assignments (which party is responsible for trenching and at what depths). Per UCM § 1.5.3.4, the 'customer is responsible for trenching' for underground electric work, but the plan does not include notes or specifications assigning trenching responsibilities or depths to the contractor/customer.
findings.reasoning: The grouping definition states this item applies 'Only when underground electric work is required' and notes that 'Customer responsible for trenching per UCM § 1.5.3.4, but specific plan documentation requirement is operational practice.' Since underground electric service is clearly required (shown on Sheet 21), and trenching will be necessary, the lack of specific trenching assignment notes on the plan represents incomplete design documentation. However, this is noted as an 'operational practice' rather than a codified requirement, making determination difficult. If present, trenching assignments should include depth specifications, material specifications, and responsibility assignments.

findings.comment: Add trenching assignment notes to the electrical design plan. Clearly identify the customer's trenching responsibilities, including trench depth, locating and avoiding existing utilities, and any special constraints per UCM § 1.5.3.4 and standard construction practice for underground electric service.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric service is required (indicated by "Underground Electric Line" routing and underground conduit to all buildings). However, no trenching assignments are shown on the plans. No notes or callouts indicate which party (customer vs. contractor) is responsible for trenching work, no depth specifications are provided, no existing utility conflict avoidance strategy is shown, and no trenching sequence is documented. This is in contrast to water and wastewater utility notes on other sheets which specify material sizing and installation standards.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.3.4 states "Customer responsible for trenching per UCM § 1.5.3.4, but specific plan documentation requirement is operational practice." While the code makes the customer responsible, the plan documentation of this responsibility and associated requirements (depths, conflicts, sequencing) is standard practice for underground utility projects. The absence of trenching assignments on the electrical plan creates ambiguity regarding customer obligations for installing the conduit and cables.

findings.comment: Plans do not indicate whether natural gas service is required or identify which site components will use gas service. Add notation to the site plan and utility plans indicating gas service requirements and which buildings or building systems will use natural gas (e.g., unit heating, hot water systems).
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical infrastructure (transformers, underground lines, meters) but does not include any indication of whether natural gas service is required for the development or identify which site components (if any) will use gas service. The Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows water and wastewater utilities but does not address gas service. The Engineer's Summary Letter (supplementary document) discusses only water and wastewater utilities, with no mention of gas service requirements or coordination with gas providers. There is no notation on any sheet indicating whether this multi-family townhome development will include gas service for heating, cooking, hot water, or other building systems.
findings.reasoning: The grouping definition establishes that checklist item EL-17.15 applies to 'All sites' and requires the plans to 'indicate whether gas service is required or identify which site components will use gas service.' This is a general site requirement under Reviewer Convention. The complete absence of any reference to gas service documentation on any plan sheets constitutes non-compliance. Multi-family townhomes typically require gas service for heating and hot water, and this coordination must be documented.

findings.comment: Add a note to the site plan or utility plan clarifying whether natural gas service is required for the development. If gas service is required, show routing and service connection details. If gas service is not required, add a note stating "Gas service not required for this development" per Reviewer Convention.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and the Engineer's Summary Letter. No gas service infrastructure is shown on any electrical or site planning documents. No notes indicate whether gas service is required or planned for the development. The Engineer's Summary Letter (supplementary-docs/engineer-s-summary-letter) discusses water and wastewater utilities in detail but makes no mention of gas service requirements or determination. No notation indicates which buildings (if any) will use gas service, nor is there any statement that gas service is not required.
findings.reasoning: This is a Reviewer Convention item applicable to all sites. While natural gas is not always required, best practice dictates that plans should indicate whether gas service will be used or is not applicable to the development. The absence of any reference to gas service on plans or in project documentation creates ambiguity - it is unclear whether gas service was considered and determined unnecessary, or whether the requirement was overlooked. For a residential development with 39 units, gas service determination is a material utility planning item.

findings.comment: Whether electric line extension is required cannot be determined from the site plan alone. This determination must be made by Austin Energy Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval documentation, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes confirming whether line extension is required and any associated costs or conditions.
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric line routing entering the site from Valley View Road on the west side, but does not include any notation indicating whether a line extension from Austin Energy's existing infrastructure is required. The supplementary documents (Master Comment Report referencing Austin Energy Design Criteria, Bluebeam link to AE comments) suggest that Austin Energy has reviewed the project, but the specific comments regarding line extension determination are not accessible in the available documents. The grouping definition explicitly states that 'whether line extension is required (vs. Service-Only service) cannot be determined from site plan features alone - this determination is made by AE Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location.'
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping definition, 'Line extension' determination cannot be made from site plan analysis alone and requires 'Austin Energy ESPA approval letters, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes stating line extension requirement and costs.' The presence of underground line routing on Sheet 21 could indicate either a service-only installation (connecting to existing nearby AE infrastructure) or a line extension (new AE infrastructure required). The applicant must provide AE Design determination documentation.

findings.comment: Cannot verify whether electric line extension is required from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service confirming whether line extension is required and, if so, showing the extent of the line extension on the electrical design plan per UCM § 1.3.12 and UCM § 1.16.0(6).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric service routing from the existing right-of-way at Valley View Road to the site, with connection to transformer pads and building meter locations. However, no documentation indicates whether this represents a "Line Extension" (customer-paid infrastructure extension to reach the site) or a "Service-Only" connection to existing nearby infrastructure. No terms such as "line extension," "CIAC" (Contribution in Aid of Construction), or "service-only" appear on the plans. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references Austin Energy Design Criteria but the actual AE Design determination (via ESPA approval or Letter of Agreement) is not provided in the project file.
findings.reasoning: The grouping's regulatory overview states: "Whether line extension is required (vs. Service-Only service) cannot be determined from site plan features alone - this determination is made by AE Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location." The checklist item applicability note directs reviewers to: "Check: Austin Energy ESPA approval letters, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes stating line extension requirement and costs." The absence of this critical AE Design documentation means line extension applicability cannot be verified from available evidence.

findings.comment: A 'Preliminary' Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) is included in the site plan set, but it is unclear whether a complete, detailed Electric Site Plan has been submitted as a separate document or whether Austin Energy has accepted this preliminary sheet as adequate. Confirm with Austin Energy whether a more detailed separate Electric Site Plan submittal is required for this project. If required, provide the detailed electrical site plan as a separate document in the AB+C portal.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 of the primary site plan is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan,' which suggests this may be a preliminary or partial electrical design. However, this is the only electrical infrastructure sheet visible in the 39-sheet primary site plan set. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires profile plan and detail drawings of fence and existing utility facilities be provided for AE Design review and preliminary approval when fence installation may affect or be near existing AE utilities. The fence shown is in electric easement areas (Sheet 9: 'Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14'; Sheet 11: '15' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76'). Profile plans showing vertical clearances and utility coordination are necessary for AE Design to confirm the fence design will not interfere with easement access or damage underlying facilities.

findings.comment: No profile plan or detail drawings are provided for the wood fence near the AE electric easement on the eastern boundary. Submit profile plan view showing fence alignment and easement boundary relationship, and provide section details showing fence construction, post spacing, materials, and clearances to AE facilities for AE Design review and preliminary approval.
applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary; wood fence and AE easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) both show a wood fence on the eastern property boundary adjacent to the 5' Electric Easement. Review of construction detail sheets (Sheets 22-28) shows only standard details for curbs, sidewalks, water infrastructure, wastewater, and storm drain features; no fence profile plan or detail drawings are provided. Sheet 38-39 contain retaining wall details but not fence details. No profile plan view or section views of the fence and adjacent AE easement/facilities are present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires profile plans and detail drawings of fences and existing utility facilities when fence installation may affect or be near existing AE utilities. These drawings must be submitted for AE Design review and preliminary approval. The site plan is missing the required profile plan (showing fence alignment relative to the easement in plan view with elevation references) and detail sections (showing fence dimensions, materials, post placement, and relationship to the underlying easement).

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations shown on Electrical Design Plan but drainage direction around pads is not indicated on either electrical or grading plans. Grading Plan does not depict transformer pads, creating no cross-reference showing how stormwater drains relative to oil-filled equipment. Provide drainage direction indicators (arrows and spot elevations) on either the electrical or grading plan demonstrating that drainage flows away from buildings as required by UCM § 1.10.4.
applicableAreas: grading and drainage areas around electrical equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design) depicts 4 transformer pads but provides no specific drainage direction indicators, spot elevations, or grading notes showing how stormwater is directed around these pads. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show transformer pad locations at all - it only shows building footprints, storm drain routing in the drive aisles, retaining walls, and drainage easements.
