findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electrical easements labeled with recording information (Vol. numbers, Pg numbers, document references) such as '5' Electric & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' However, these labeled easements are plat-dedicated easements of record (existing easements), not proposed easements around the transformer facilities. The facts.md lists several existing electric easements (5' electric easements per plat documents) but no analysis is provided showing whether these existing easements are adequate to cover the 5 transformer pad locations, their required clearances (which can range from 3-15 feet per UCM § 1.10.4), and access requirements. No proposed electrical easement is shown around transformer facilities.
findings.reasoning: Electrical easements around transformer facilities must be shown or proposed with adequate dimensions to cover physical location, all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4, and access requirements per UCM § 1.3.24. Existing plat-dedicated easements shown on Sheet 21 are 5 feet wide, but transformer clearance requirements can extend 10-15 feet depending on equipment orientation and building features. Unless a detailed analysis demonstrates existing easements are sufficient, proposed easement dedications or modifications must be shown.

findings.comment: Individual transformer labels are missing on the plans. Assign unique identifiers to each of the five transformer pads (e.g., 'XFMR-1', 'XFMR-2', 'XFMR-3', 'XFMR-4', 'XFMR-5') and show these labels clearly on Sheet 21 and on all other plan sheets where transformers appear. This will enable clear cross-referencing in specifications and coordination documents.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads marked with blue square symbols and labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' at their locations (NW, W-central, SW, E-central, SE). While the transformers are labeled with the equipment type 'Electrical Transformer Pad,' they are not individually labeled with unique identifiers (e.g., 'XFMR-1', 'XFMR-2', etc.) that would allow specific reference in specifications, electrical calculations, or coordination with other disciplines. This generic labeling without individual identification creates ambiguity in referring to specific transformers.
findings.reasoning: Clear identification and labeling of each transformer is essential for permit review, coordination with other trades, and construction. Generic labels like 'Electrical Transformer Pad' do not distinguish between the five different transformers. Each transformer should be uniquely labeled so that specifications, clearance calculations, meter assignments, and building connections can be clearly correlated to specific equipment. This is standard engineering practice for electrical documentation.

findings.comment: Transformer size (kVA) must be specified for each of the five transformer pads on Sheet 21. Include a specification note, callout label, or table showing: (1) transformer kVA rating for each pad, (2) quantity (number of units at each location), (3) metering method, and (4) buildings served by each transformer.
findings.observation: The 5 transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 are labeled only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no size specification. No callouts, notes, or specifications indicate the kVA capacity of any transformer. No table or legend provides transformer specifications. The vision analysis confirmed: 'Size/Capacity: Not specified' for all five transformers. Without size information, it cannot be verified that transformer capacity is adequate to serve the development's electrical demand.
findings.reasoning: Transformer size (kVA rating) is essential information for: (1) verifying adequate capacity to serve all buildings, (2) determining construction, operation, and maintenance needs, (3) establishing clearance requirements, and (4) coordinating with Austin Energy. UCM § 1.16.0 requires complete and detailed electrical facility information. Omitting transformer sizes is a significant deficiency.

findings.comment: Transformer pad dimensions must be shown on all plan sheets depicting transformers. Provide specific dimensions for each pad (length × width) on Sheet 21 and verify the same dimensions are shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) where transformers are added. Typical pad-mounted transformer pads are often 24" × 36" or 30" × 48" - specify the exact size for this project.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pad locations marked with blue square symbols. No dimension callouts are provided on Sheet 21 for the pad dimensions themselves (length and width of the equipment pad). Vision analysis stated: 'Transformer pad dimensions not consistent across all plan sheets.' Since transformers are not shown on Sheets 9, 11, 31, or 12, pad dimensions cannot be verified on any sheet other than Sheet 21. On Sheet 21, no specific pad dimension measurements (e.g., 24" × 36", 30" × 48") are annotated.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad dimensions (length and width) must be shown on all plan sheets where transformers appear to ensure consistency and allow verification of clearances and access. Sheet 21 shows transformer locations but no pad dimensions are annotated. Since transformers don't appear on other sheets, consistency across sheets cannot be evaluated. Standard pad-mounted transformer dimensions should be specified in the electrical specifications or on the plans.

findings.comment: Confirm that transformer capacity is adequate to serve all 39 units and 8 buildings. Provide electrical load calculations showing: (1) total electrical demand for the development, (2) the kVA rating of each of the 5 transformers, (3) the total combined capacity, and (4) confirmation that capacity exceeds demand with appropriate safety margin. Show this information on Sheet 21 in a specifications table or notes section.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads serving 8 buildings with 39 units total. The buildings are described as 4-plexes, 5-plexes, and 6-plexes with gross floor areas ranging from 3,290 sf to 4,997 sf per building. The electrical plan shows 5 transformers but provides no specification indicating: (1) the total capacity of all transformers combined, (2) the electrical demand of all 39 units and 8 buildings, (3) the load distribution among the 5 transformers, or (4) whether the total transformer capacity is adequate to serve all buildings. No transformer sizing analysis or electrical load calculation is provided.
findings.reasoning: Transformer capacity must be adequate to serve all buildings in the development. This is a fundamental design requirement. Without showing transformer sizes and confirming that total capacity meets or exceeds the calculated electrical demand for 39 residential units, the adequacy of the electrical service cannot be verified. Austin Energy design review typically requires load calculations demonstrating adequate capacity.

findings.comment: Metering method must be labeled for each transformer on Sheet 21. Specify whether each transformer is: (1) CT metered (with meters located at individual buildings), or (2) building metered (with grouped meters at central location). This designation must correlate with meter locations shown on the plans and must confirm that meters remain within sight of transformers per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' and 8 meters labeled as 'Electrical Meters' but does not provide metering method designations for any transformer. No notes or callouts indicate whether the transformers are: (1) CT metered (current transformer metered at transformer, with meters located remotely at buildings), or (2) building metered (meters located at each customer/building adjacent to transformer). The vision analysis confirmed: 'Metering Method: Not labeled' for all five transformers.
findings.reasoning: The metering method (CT metered vs. building metered) is critical information that determines: (1) where meters are located, (2) where service disconnects must be positioned, (3) clearance and access requirements, and (4) coordination between transformer location and meter location. UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be within sight of the transformer. The metering method must be clearly specified on plans so that meter locations can be verified as compliant.

findings.comment: Add a legend to Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identifying all proposed electrical utilities with symbols and descriptions, including: Transformer Pad, Electrical Meter, Pull Box, Underground Electric Line, and any other electrical facilities shown. Also add or enhance the legend on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to clearly show proposed electrical infrastructure symbols. Ensure symbols are consistent with any legend shown on other utility plan sheets (Sheets 19, 20).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) does not include a title block legend or notation delineating transformers, meters, and pull boxes as proposed utilities. The plan has leader lines pointing to individual equipment with text labels ('Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Meters', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Underground Electric Line') but no formal legend or symbol key is shown on the sheet. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) mentions overhead electric lines but shows limited electrical symbols. No formal legend on either sheet identifies proposed electrical utilities with symbols and explains what each symbol represents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that proposed utilities be clearly delineated in plan legends. A proper legend helps readers understand the plan symbols and ensures consistency across all sheets. Without a legend on the electrical plans identifying transformers, meters, pull boxes, and underground lines as proposed utilities, the plans are incomplete. Other disciplines reviewing the electrical plans must have clear symbol definitions.

findings.comment: If niche service is required or proposed for any transformer, provide: (1) niche plan showing equipment location within building footprint, (2) profile showing niche dimensions and exterior access, (3) evidence of AE Design consultation and approval. If only pad-mounted transformers are used (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 pad-mounted transformer pads, all positioned outside buildings on the site surface. There is no indication of any niche service (specialized transformer installation within building footprint, accessible from exterior). The applicability note states this item applies 'only when transformer service via specialized niche' and requires 'transformer service via specialized niche (equipment within building footprint, accessible from exterior, site outside Network Area).' The site plan shows all transformers as surface pad-mounted equipment, not niches.
findings.reasoning: Niche service is a specialized configuration where transformer equipment is installed within a building's footprint but remains accessible from the exterior for Austin Energy access. This is fundamentally different from the pad-mounted transformers shown on the plans. Without indication of niche service in the design, this item does not apply.

findings.comment: If this is a multi-site development (multiple distinct sites, each potentially serving independent customer groups), verify that each site has its own transformer. If this is a single-site development (as currently described), this item is not applicable.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows a single development with 8 buildings and 39 units served by 5 transformers. The applicability note states: 'Only for multi-site developments. Check: project description or site plan for number of distinct sites.' The site plan (Sheet 9) describes the project as a single site: 'Valley View Townhomes' on 'Lot 1, Mecey Subdivision.' The facts.md confirms a single parcel (Parcel ID 0406100252, 2.16 acres). There is no indication this is a multi-site development.
findings.reasoning: This item is conditional on the project being a multi-site development where each site should have its own transformer. The Valley View Townhomes project is a single development on a single lot. Therefore, this item does not apply.

findings.comment: If Austin Energy Design requires switchgear for this multi-transformer configuration, show the switchgear location on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). Provide documentation of Austin Energy coordination confirming whether switchgear is required. If switchgear is not required, note this in the electrical specifications.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads serving 8 buildings. The applicability note states: 'Only when two or more transformers proposed or otherwise required per Austin Energy Design. Check: transformer count on plans or Austin Energy requirements letter.' Five transformers are proposed, which appears to meet the threshold of 'two or more.' However, the note also requires 'AE Design coordination to determine applicability' for switchgear location. No switchgear location is shown on the plans, and no documentation indicates whether Austin Energy Design has specified a switchgear requirement for this configuration.
findings.reasoning: Switchgear may or may not be required depending on Austin Energy's specific design for this project. The plans do not indicate whether switchgear is part of the approved electrical design. Without explicit Austin Energy Design coordination documentation, the applicability of this switchgear requirement cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Meter locations must be shown on all required plan sheets. Add 8 meter locations to: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan) - mark meter positions on each building; (2) Sheet 19 or 20 (Wet Utilities Plan) - show meter positions relative to water, wastewater, and storm drain utilities; (3) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) - show meter positions to verify clearances from plantings. Label all meters with unique identifiers matching the electrical plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations labeled as 'Electrical Meters' positioned on or near each of the 8 buildings (Bldg. 1-8). However: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show meter locations - no meters are labeled or visible; (2) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show meter locations - vision analysis confirmed 'No meter locations are shown or labeled'; (3) Sheet 19 (Wet Utilities Plan) contains a legend that includes symbols for meters but no actual meter locations are depicted on the plan drawing. Therefore, meter locations are NOT shown on all required plan sheets as specified in the checklist.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.A requires meter locations shown on site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. This allows review of meter accessibility, visibility to transformer, and clearance from other utilities and building features. Sheet 21 shows meters but they must also be shown on the Site Plan, Wet Utilities Plan, and Landscape Plan for complete coordination.

findings.comment: If the electrical design includes any grouped meter configuration (two or more meters at a single location served from one service point), show the meter bank/rack location on Sheet 21. If meters are distributed individually to each building (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters labeled as 'Electrical Meters' positioned individually on or near each building (Bldg. 1-8). The applicability note states: 'Only when two or more meters are installed at one location and served from one set of service conductors. Check: electrical plan for number of meters and service configuration.' The current design shows 8 separate meter locations, one per building, not multiple meters at a single location served from one service point. There is no meter bank or grouped meter installation shown.
findings.reasoning: This item applies to meter bank/rack configurations where multiple meters are physically located together at one point of service. The current design shows distributed metering with individual meters at each building. Therefore, this item does not apply.

findings.comment: If any existing electrical meters remain on the site from prior development, show their locations on the plans. If the site is vacant and cleared (as indicated), this item is not applicable.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 does not show any existing meter locations. The applicability note states: 'Only when existing meters present on site. Check: utility locate documentation or survey for existing meters.' The site plan indicates this is vacant land following demolition of a prior assisted living facility (demolished June 2022 per facts.md). The survey and plan submissions do not indicate existing electrical meters on the current site. Therefore, no existing meter locations require documentation.
findings.reasoning: This item applies only if existing meters are currently on the site. For a development on a vacant site (demolished and cleared), there would be no existing meters to show.

findings.comment: If the electrical design includes grouped metering for multiple buildings from a single service point, verify that meters and disconnects are grouped in a common location with service distribution enclosure and wireway per UCM § 1.9.3.4. If individual building service is provided (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters distributed individually to 8 buildings (one meter per building) and 5 transformers distributed across the site. The applicability note states: 'Only when multiple meters are served from one set of service conductors or when meters and disconnects must be grouped per code. Check: electrical service configuration showing single point of service serving multiple units.' The current design shows 8 separate service connections (one per building), not multiple meters served from a single service point.
findings.reasoning: This requirement applies to grouped metering configurations where multiple meter units share a common service point. The current electrical design shows individual building-level service, not grouped multi-unit metering. Therefore, this item does not apply.

findings.comment: Individual labels are required for all meters and disconnects. Assign unique identifiers to each of the 8 meters (e.g., 'M-1' through 'M-8' corresponding to Buildings 1-8) and to all pull boxes (e.g., 'PB-1', 'PB-2', etc.). Show these labels clearly on Sheet 21 and on all other plan sheets where meters appear. Create a meter schedule or specification table on the electrical plan showing meter identification, building served, location, and type.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters labeled generically as 'Electrical Meters' and 8 pull boxes labeled as 'Electrical Pull Box' without individual identifiers. No unique labels (e.g., 'METER-1', 'METER-2', 'PB-1', 'PB-2', etc.) are provided. While the meters and pull boxes are positioned on the plan, they cannot be specifically referenced or correlated with building designations without individual identification. No specification table or notes section provides meter and disconnect information.
findings.reasoning: Each meter and disconnect must be individually labeled and identified so that: (1) it can be specifically referenced in specifications and coordination documents, (2) building service connections can be clearly traced, (3) service upgrades can be implemented with precision, and (4) inspectors can verify the correct equipment is installed. Generic labels are inadequate.

findings.comment: Verify and document that all meter locations are within sight of serving transformers per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B. Add a note to Sheet 21 stating: 'All meters are located within sight of their serving transformer. No line-of-sight exceptions are claimed.' OR, if any meter locations do not have clear sight-line visibility, provide documentation of written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering for the exception. Alternatively, add sight-line symbols or dashed lines from each meter to its serving transformer to visually demonstrate visibility.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations and 5 transformer locations. The vision analysis indicated that meters are 'generally corresponding to the eight buildings on the site' and transformers are distributed across the site with underground electric routing connecting them. However, no explicit visual confirmation is shown on the plan that each meter has clear line-of-sight visibility to its serving transformer. No callouts, sight-line diagrams, or notes state that meters are within sight of transformers. The arrangement suggests meters should be visible to transformers (given underground routing), but this critical requirement is not explicitly documented on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be 'within sight of an Austin Energy transformer.' This is a specific requirement for safety and operations. Without explicit sight-line confirmation on the plans, or without a note stating that meters are positioned for visibility, there is no documented verification of compliance. Additionally, the plans do not state whether any exceptions requiring AE Design approval are being claimed.

findings.comment: Since the site is in FEMA Flood Zone X (outside 100-year floodplain), minimum flood elevation requirements for meters do not apply. This item is not applicable.
findings.observation: The facts.md confirms the site is in 'FEMA Flood Zone: Zone X (outside 100-year and 500-year floodplain)' and 'COA Flood Zone: Zone X' with 'Floodplain intersection: None.' Sheet 21 does not indicate meter elevations relative to flood levels because the site is not subject to the 100-Year Reference Flood Datum requirement. The applicability note states: 'Only when site is subject to 100-Year Reference Flood Datum ordinance.' Since the site is in Zone X (no floodplain), this requirement does not apply.
findings.reasoning: This item applies only to sites within a 100-year floodplain subject to elevation requirements. The Valley View Townhomes site is outside the floodplain in Zone X, so flood elevation requirements do not apply.

findings.comment: Clearly identify the point-of-service location on Sheet 21. Label the specific equipment (meter socket, service distribution enclosure, pull box, or other approved enclosure) that serves as the point where Austin Energy facilities connect to customer conductors. Add a note stating the point-of-service definition and location(s). This should be shown for each service/building connection.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters and pull boxes but does not explicitly identify which location is the point-of-service (point where AE conductors connect to customer conductors). The grouping definition states that Point-of-Service is the 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect.' Without a clear label or callout indicating the point-of-service location, it cannot be determined where Austin Energy's responsibility ends and customer responsibility begins.
findings.reasoning: The point-of-service is the critical junction where utility responsibility transfers from Austin Energy to the customer. It must be clearly marked on plans so that: (1) Austin Energy and customer can verify the boundary of responsibility, (2) disconnects are properly located, (3) permits can be accurately issued, and (4) inspections can verify correct installation. Without explicit identification, there is ambiguity about which equipment serves this critical function.

findings.comment: If pull boxes are required by Austin Energy electrical service design specifications, confirm their locations are shown on all utility plan sheets. If not required, this item is not applicable. Clarify in the electrical specifications whether pull boxes are required or optional for this installation.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 pull boxes labeled as 'Electrical Pull Box' positioned throughout the site on the underground electric routing. However, the vision analysis determined that these are likely pull boxes for the electrical service routing (standard for underground utility systems) but the plans do not explicitly state whether pull boxes are 'required by electrical service design' or whether they are only being provided as standard practice. The distinction matters for this checklist item: if pull boxes are required per Austin Energy design specifications, then showing them is required; if they're optional, then omitting them would not be a deficiency.
findings.reasoning: The applicability note for EL-15.37 states 'Only when pull boxes required by electrical service design.' This checklist item is conditional. Pull boxes are standard in underground electrical systems for drawing cable and navigation, but they must be explicitly required by Austin Energy or electrical specifications to trigger this checklist requirement. Without clear indication that pull boxes are required by design, the applicability cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: If any existing electrical pull boxes or utility infrastructure remain from prior development, show their locations on the plans. If the site is vacant and cleared, this item is not applicable.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 pull boxes for the electrical routing system but does not show any existing pull box locations. The applicability note states: 'Only when existing pull boxes present on site.' The site is vacant following demolition of the prior assisted living facility. No existing utility infrastructure from the prior use remains on the site (demolished June 2022). Therefore, no existing pull boxes require documentation.
findings.reasoning: This item applies only if existing pull boxes are present from prior development. For a vacant, cleared site, there would be no existing pull boxes to show.

findings.comment: If a load center is required by the project electrical design, show its location on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). If no load center is required, note in the electrical specifications that the design uses distributed building-level service without a central load center. Clarify this in the design submittal.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads and 8 pull boxes but does not show any load center location. The applicability note states this item is only required 'when load centers required by project electrical design.' No load center is indicated on the preliminary electrical plan shown. It is not clear from the submitted plans whether a load center is required for this project or whether the building service connections are made directly from meters.
findings.reasoning: Load centers are not always required; they depend on the electrical service design and building layout. The applicability of this item depends on whether the project's electrical design includes a centralized load center. Without an explicit requirement stated in the electrical design documents or specifications, this item's applicability cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Clarify whether this project includes any underground electrical vaults or transformer vaults requiring manhole access. If only pull boxes are used (as currently shown), this item is not applicable. If underground vaults are required, show manhole locations on all required plan sheets (site, wet utilities, landscape).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' but does not explicitly show any separate manhole locations distinct from pull boxes. Pull boxes and manholes are different - pull boxes are small access points for drawing cable, while manholes are larger access points for vault-like underground utility infrastructure (such as underground transformer vaults or junction points). The plans do not indicate whether any true underground vaults or transformer vaults are required. The applicability note states 'Only when manholes required for electrical service,' which is a conditional applicability requirement.
findings.reasoning: Manhole locations are only relevant if the electrical service design includes underground vaults, transformer vaults, or other vault-like installations. The current design shows pad-mounted surface transformers and pull boxes, not underground vaults. Without explicit indication that underground vaults requiring manhole access are part of the design, this item may not be applicable.

findings.comment: If any existing electrical vaults or manholes remain from prior development, show their locations on the plans. If the site is vacant and cleared (as indicated), this item is not applicable.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 does not show any existing manhole locations for electrical service. The applicability note states: 'Only when existing manholes present on site.' The site is vacant land following demolition (June 2022). No existing electrical infrastructure remains on the site. Therefore, no existing manhole locations require documentation.
findings.reasoning: This item applies only to existing manholes from prior development. A vacant, cleared site would have no existing electrical vaults or manholes to show.

findings.comment: Review the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4 or external survey document) to confirm whether existing poles or driveways conflict with proposed transformer, electrical routing, or access route locations. If relocations are required, show this on the Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and coordinate with Site Plan (Sheet 9) for driveway relocation scope. If no conflicts exist, this item is not applicable.
findings.observation: The applicability note states: 'Only when pole or driveway relocation required. Check: survey for existing poles/driveways in conflict with proposed development.' The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4 per README) and the site plan show the site is cleared following demolition of the prior assisted living facility. The site plan shows proposed driveways and parking in locations consistent with site topography and building locations. The survey references (CDS Survey noted in facts.md from 2018) would need to be examined to confirm whether existing poles or driveways remain in the proposed improvement area.
findings.reasoning: This item is conditional on whether relocation of poles or driveways is required. Without explicit indication in the plan notes that relocations are necessary, or survey evidence of conflicts, the applicability cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Verify with City GIS or Austin Energy records whether any historic moonlight towers are located within 100 feet of the Valley View Townhomes construction site. If a moonlight tower is present within 100 feet, show its location and guy wires/posts on the plans and provide documentation of Special Moonlight Tower Construction Permit compliance (Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201).
findings.observation: The grouping guidance states: 'Note: Cannot be determined from plans alone—requires external location data. Flag for human verification if proximity uncertain.' The site is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704 in Council District 5. Austin maintains 17 historic moonlight towers throughout the city. The closest known moonlight tower locations would require City GIS lookup or Austin Energy records. The survey and plans do not indicate any moonlight tower presence within 100 feet of the construction area.
findings.reasoning: Moonlight tower locations are not defined in code and cannot be determined from plan review alone. This requires external City GIS or Austin Energy records verification. The grouping instructions state this item 'cannot be determined from plans alone.'

findings.comment: Measure the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area on Sheet 21. If any transformer is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas, show bollard locations and spacing (sized to allow equipment door opening) on the Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Site Plan (Sheet 9), and Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). If all transformers are more than 4 feet from parking/traffic areas, note this on the plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads but does not display bollard symbols or callouts. The checklist item specifically applies 'only when pad-mounted transformer is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas.' Transformers are not shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or other discipline plans, making it impossible to accurately measure distances from transformer pads to the nearest parking or traffic areas using the plans. Sheet 21 shows the site layout and parking areas, but without clear transformer locations and precise measurements marked, the 4-foot threshold cannot be verified from available evidence.
findings.reasoning: This item is conditionally applicable only if any of the 5 transformers are located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. While Sheet 21 shows both transformers and parking areas, the distance relationship is not explicitly annotated with dimensions. To verify whether bollards are required, the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area must be measured or explicitly noted on the plans. Without such measurements, the applicability cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Specify whether transformers are oil-filled or dry-type on the Electrical Design Plan. If oil-filled: (1) Show transformer pad locations on Grading Plan (Sheet 11) with contour lines and spot elevations; (2) Add drainage arrows or notes confirming that ground grading slopes away from transformer pads and toward properties; (3) Verify that no oil spill pathway leads toward building foundations or sensitive areas.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 pad-mounted transformers but does not indicate whether they are oil-filled (which requires drainage considerations) or dry-type. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show transformer pad locations, so there are no grading details or drainage arrows visible around any transformer pads. No contour lines, spot elevations, or drainage flow arrows are shown in the vicinity of transformer locations. If the transformers are oil-filled, UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 1 requires grading to direct liquid flow away from buildings.
findings.reasoning: Oil-filled transformers pose an environmental and safety risk if oil leaks. Grading must be designed to prevent spilled oil from flowing toward buildings. This requirement only applies to oil-filled transformers. Without: (1) specification of whether transformers are oil-filled or dry-type, and (2) grading details around oil-filled transformers (if applicable), compliance cannot be verified. The omission of transformer locations from the Grading Plan means this critical drainage requirement cannot be addressed.

findings.comment: Confirm whether flammable liquid storage or handling occurs on this site. If no flammable liquids are stored or handled, this item is not applicable. If flammable liquid storage is planned, provide documentation of AE Design approval for transformer location relative to flammable liquid facilities.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads and the site plan shows no fuel storage, chemical storage, flammable liquids facilities, or hazardous material storage areas. The site is a residential townhome development with water service, wastewater service, and stormwater facilities. No indication is given that flammable liquids are stored or handled on-site.
findings.reasoning: This checklist item is conditional: 'Only when flammable liquid storage or handling occurs on site.' Without evidence that flammable liquids are present on-site, this item may not be applicable. The site appears to be residential only without commercial operations involving hazardous materials.

findings.comment: Verify that all electrical meter locations maintain minimum 3-foot separation from gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C. If gas appliances or other utility apparatus are present, show their locations on the Electrical Design Plan and annotate distances to electrical meters.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations labeled as 'Electrical Meters' but does not provide specific callouts showing distances from each meter to gas meters, regulators, relief valves, or other electrical apparatus. The site plan does not show gas meter locations or other utility equipment that might create conflicts. Without detailed site analysis showing the location of all meters and utility apparatus, the 3-foot separation requirement cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: This requirement depends on identifying all gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus on the site, then verifying at least 3-foot separation from electrical meters. Sheet 21 does not provide this level of detail for meter-to-utility spacing.

findings.comment: If meters and disconnects are paired, show their spatial relationship on Sheet 21 with: (1) clear identification of meter-disconnect pairs, (2) distance callouts showing the separation between each meter and its disconnect, (3) verification that distance does not exceed 20 feet, and (4) confirmation that meters and disconnects are within line of sight of each other. If meters and disconnects are not paired, clarify the electrical service configuration.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations and transformer locations, but does not specify which meters are paired with which disconnects, nor does it provide distance callouts showing meter-to-disconnect distances. The checklist item requires: (1) meter to disconnect distance not to exceed 20 feet, and (2) meter and disconnect within line of sight. Without explicit labeling of meter-disconnect pairs and distance callouts, these requirements cannot be verified from the plans.
findings.reasoning: This requirement is conditional on having grouped metering with associated disconnects. If meters and disconnects are paired, their locations and distances must be clearly shown and verified on the plans. Sheet 21 does not provide sufficient detail for this verification.

findings.comment: Root barrier details are missing from Landscape Details sheet. When required, root barrier details must show minimum 4-foot depth and positioning exactly 5 feet from underground electric equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
findings.observation: Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) provides tree planting, shrub planting, and tree protection details but contains NO root barrier detail drawing. The sheet shows standard details (Block 1: tree planting, Block 2: shrub planting, Block 3: tree protection fence) but no detail addressing root barrier construction for underground utilities. No specification for barrier material, depth, or placement relative to equipment is shown.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barrier details showing minimum 4-foot depth and positioning exactly 5 feet from equipment edge. These details are completely absent from Sheet 37. Without a detail drawing showing root barrier specifications and construction, the contractor has no standard to follow for compliant installation.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees are planted directly on top of underground electric duct banks due to lack of electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines marked '- E -' throughout site with tree canopy symbols overlapping lines in multiple locations. Sheet 31 does not depict underground duct banks or conduits. Proposed trees cannot be correlated with underground routing shown on Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: Cannot verify whether proposed trees are planted on top of duct banks without electrical infrastructure shown on Landscape Plan for coordination with proposed plantings.

findings.comment: Tree wells or pits may be placed on underground electric utilities. No tree well details are shown on Landscape Details, and electrical infrastructure is not coordinated on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 37 does not include tree well details. Sheet 31 does not show transformer pads or duct banks. Cannot determine whether tree wells would be placed on utilities.
findings.reasoning: Verification requires showing utility locations on Landscape Plan and providing tree well details that address utility avoidance. Neither is provided.

findings.comment: Proposed tree species appear to be Utility Compatible, but clearance verification is incomplete due to unclear distribution vs. transmission designation and lack of dimensioned clearances from proposed trees to overhead electric line.
findings.observation: Sheet 31 shows overhead electric line '- OHE -' along southern boundary. Proposed species are all Utility Compatible (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud). Landscape Plan does not indicate whether line is distribution or transmission or dimension clearance distances from proposed trees.
findings.reasoning: All proposed species are UC-designated, which satisfies this requirement if within clearance zones. However, line voltage classification and clearance distances not clearly indicated on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Proposed large trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm - mature height >= 40 feet) may be planted within 25 lateral feet of overhead electric distribution line. Clearance distances are not dimensioned on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Proposed 2 Live Oaks and 10 Cedar Elms appear to qualify as 'large trees' (mature height >= 40 feet). Sheet 31 shows overhead electric line but does not dimension distances from proposed large trees to this line. Landscape Plan does not explicitly identify which trees are large trees or their proximity to OHE line.
findings.reasoning: Large trees within 25 feet of distribution line prohibited, but clearance distances not dimensioned on Landscape Plan. Cannot verify compliance without distance specifications.

findings.comment: Show transmission easement boundaries on the landscape plan. Verify and document that no proposed trees or shrubs are located within transmission easement areas. If any trees currently exist within transmission easements, indicate their removal or obtain Austin Energy written approval.
findings.observation: The property plat (Sheet 2) and facts.md document record that electric easements exist on the property, including plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements. Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 20) explicitly states: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' However, the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show transmission easement boundaries, preventing verification that no trees are planted within transmission easements. Without visible easement boundaries overlaid on the landscape plan, compliance with the absolute prohibition on trees within transmission easements cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits all trees from being planted within electric transmission easements (facilities ≥60kV phase-to-phase). This is an absolute requirement with no exceptions based on tree size or species. The site plan notes on Sheet 3 reiterate this requirement. The applicant must show transmission easement boundaries on the landscape plan and demonstrate that no trees are positioned within them. The absence of easement boundaries on the landscape plan constitutes non-compliance with the documentation requirement.

findings.comment: Proposed tree species are Utility Compatible, which would satisfy transmission clearance requirements if overhead electric line is transmission (>= 60kV). However, overhead line voltage classification and clearance distances are not clearly indicated on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: All proposed species are Utility Compatible (UC). Overhead electric line shown on Sheet 31 but line voltage classification (distribution vs. transmission) not clearly indicated. Distance to proposed trees not dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: All UC species would satisfy requirement even if line were transmission. However, line voltage and clearance distances not clearly specified on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Proposed large trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm - mature height >= 40 feet) may be planted within 50 lateral feet of overhead electric line. Transmission facility classification and clearance distances are not clearly indicated on Landscape Plan.
findings.observation: Two Live Oaks and 10 Cedar Elms qualify as 'large trees' (mature height >= 40 feet). Landscape Plan shows overhead electric line but does not dimension clearances or identify which trees are large. Line voltage classification not specified.
findings.reasoning: Cannot verify whether large trees are within 50 feet of transmission line without: (1) confirming line is transmission, (2) identifying which plantings are large trees on Landscape Plan, and (3) dimensioning clearances.

findings.comment: Identify and show utility pole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 10-foot clearance zones around each pole and verify all proposed trees are outside these zones.
applicableAreas: Utility pole locations along street right-of-way
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows utility poles depicted as small circles with crosshairs located along the far left edge of the property along the street right-of-way. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show these utility pole locations. Without the pole locations shown on the landscape plan, there is no means to verify that proposed trees maintain the required 10-foot minimum clearance from poles.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that no trees be planted within 10 lateral feet of electric utility poles. The landscape plan must show pole locations to enable verification of compliance. The absence of pole locations on the landscape plan means the applicant has not provided sufficient documentation to verify this clearance requirement.

findings.comment: Show vault and manhole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 8-foot clearance zones around each vault/manhole requiring personnel access and verify shrubs and obstructions are outside these zones.
applicableAreas: Subsurface electric vaults and manhole locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows vault and manhole locations (including a labeled 'Vault Easement' at transformer pad near Bldg. 8). Sheet 31 does not show these vault/manhole locations. Without them overlaid on the landscape plan, the required 8-foot clearance zone around vaults/manholes cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires minimum 8-foot clearance around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, or manholes requiring personnel access. The landscape plan must show vault/manhole locations to enable verification.

findings.comment: Variations to clearance distances or species requirements require written Austin Energy approval. No such approval documentation is evident in current submittal. However, the lack of electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan prevents determination of whether variations are needed.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan deviations from clearance standards
findings.observation: All proposed species are Utility Compatible per Sheet 35 listing. No Austin Energy approval documentation evident in current submittal. However, cannot determine if variations are needed because electrical infrastructure not shown on Landscape Plan to evaluate clearance distances.
findings.reasoning: Cannot determine if variations approval is required without knowing whether proposed trees are within clearance zones. Lack of Austin Energy approval documentation visible, but unclear if needed without electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan (EL-16.22 deficiency).

findings.comment: Surveyed elevations of overhead conductors with clearance dimension annotations from the outside conductor to building faces are required, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from electric facilities in the adjacent Valley View Road right-of-way.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1, 2, 8 adjacent to Valley View Road right-of-way where overhead electric facilities are located
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows overhead utility lines and utility poles along Valley View Road (western boundary). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1, 2, and 8 positioned near the western property line adjacent to Valley View Road ROW. Building 1 is dimensioned at 26.1' from the western property line; Building 8 at 26.6'. However, NO surveyed conductor elevation data is shown, NO dimension annotations show clearances from buildings to the outside conductor, and NO section views demonstrate that permanent 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained from electric facilities in the adjacent ROW.
findings.reasoning: No surveyed elevation data or clearance dimensions provided showing that buildings adjacent to Valley View Road maintain required permanent clearances from outside conductor of overhead electric facilities in ROW. Proximity survey data by registered surveyor is needed.

findings.comment: Provide section views of retaining walls showing the surveyed overhead conductor elevation and clearance dimensions (measured horizontally) from the outside conductor location to the near face of the retaining wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls, particularly along southern property boundary where OHE line is located
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows retaining walls labeled 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall' along the southern boundary and other site perimeter locations. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) shows an overhead electric line (O.H.U.L.) running along the southern property boundary. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans) provide wall construction sections showing max 14-foot height, reinforcement details, and structural dimensions, but contain NO sections showing clearance dimensions from the overhead electric conductor to the wall face or top. Wall plan sheets show only structural reinforcement and soil pressure calculations, not clearances to adjacent overhead lines.
findings.reasoning: The requirement under UCM § 1.10.3 is to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. Retaining walls up to 14 feet tall are proposed along the southern boundary where overhead electric lines are present. Without section views showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the distance (measured horizontally at ground level) from the conductor to the wall face, compliance cannot be verified. The wall height is known (up to 14 feet from foundation), but the conductor height and horizontal distance from the conductor to the wall are not documented.

findings.comment: Provide section view exhibits of each retaining wall showing the surveyed outside conductor location with dimension lines to the outermost edge (top/face) of the wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from the conductor to the wall.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric facilities on southern and eastern boundaries
findings.observation: Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans and Wall Details) contain section views of retaining walls showing structural reinforcement, backfill requirements, footing details, and maximum heights (14 feet). However, these section views show only internal wall construction and soil pressure relationships. NO section views include dimension lines showing clearance from an outer electric conductor to the outermost edge (top or face) of the retaining wall. Sheet 9 shows OHE line along southern boundary, but Sheets 38-39 do not cross-reference or show the conductor on their wall sections.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 specifically requires 'Retaining walls lack section exhibits showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of wall for clearance verification' to be addressed. This is an explicit documentation requirement. The wall construction sections present on Sheets 38-39 do not show the overhead conductor location or clearance dimensions from the conductor to the wall. The requirement is for section exhibits that include both the wall profile AND the conductor location with a dimensioned clearance.

findings.comment: Provide section views of parking areas with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum vertical clearance (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, or 18 feet for areas with truck traffic) from lowest point of conductors to finished parking surface. Add note to site plan specifying clearance requirement and designation of parking areas (truck vs. non-truck traffic).
applicableAreas: Vehicle parking and display areas beneath overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 10 surface parking spaces and 78 garage parking spaces for a total of 88 spaces (per site plan data table). The parking layout is shown on the plan view, but NO section views show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead electric lines to the parking surface. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows parking pad elevations and site topography but does not provide surveyed conductor heights or clearance verification. No note on site plan indicates the vertical clearance requirement or that parking must maintain minimum clearance from overhead lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires parking areas to maintain minimum vertical clearance from overhead electric lines (12 feet for residential pedestrian areas, 16 feet for parking without trucks, 18 feet with truck traffic). Without surveyed conductor elevations and section views showing the vertical relationship between parking pads and conductors, compliance cannot be verified. Additionally, a site plan note is required indicating the clearance requirement. No such note is present on Sheets 9 or 11.

findings.comment: Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing clearance distance from proposed sidewalk alignment to existing power poles at each end of the property along Valley View Road right-of-way frontage. Confirm sidewalk clearance from pole locations, particularly at northwest and southwest property corners.
applicableAreas: Sidewalks along Valley View Road at property limits
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows utility poles along Valley View Road adjacent to the property. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a proposed '5' Concrete Sidewalk' labeled 'Construct 5' Concrete Sidewalk' in the sidewalk easement area along the western property boundary adjacent to Valley View Road. However, Sheet 9 provides NO dimension annotations showing the alignment of the proposed sidewalk relative to the existing utility poles. The sidewalk alignment appears to follow the property line, but the exact horizontal distance from poles is not dimensioned. Sheet 22 shows standard sidewalk construction details but contains no site-specific dimension relating the sidewalk to pole locations.
findings.reasoning: The requirement under Reviewer Convention is that sidewalks must be 'cleared from existing power poles at each end of property along right-of-way.' This implies that the sidewalk should not conflict with or be immediately adjacent to pole locations at property corners. Without dimension annotations showing the distance from the proposed sidewalk to existing pole locations at the northwest and southwest property corners where the property meets Valley View Road, compliance cannot be verified. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted an 'AT&T Pole' at the northwest corner, suggesting a utility pole exists at or near that location.

findings.comment: Provide comprehensive easement exhibit on site plan showing all recorded easements (Greenbelt Access, City Drainage, 5' Electric Easements ×2, 7.5' Public Utility Easement, and any others per county records) with accurate boundary dimensions. Provide registered surveyor proximity survey confirming: (1) no customer facilities are located under or over overhead distribution lines (absolute prohibition); (2) all facilities within electric easement boundaries maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor; (3) all facilities comply with easement use restrictions.
applicableAreas: All proposed customer facilities, building structures, and site features relative to existing electric easements and overhead distribution facilities
findings.observation: Facts.md identifies two perpetual easements with NO development permitted: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres) in NE interior—explicitly marked as 'strict no-build zone'; (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres) in NE corner with unlimited City access rights. Both are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan (facts.md: 'NOT depicted on the submitted site plan and NOT in the COA GIS easement layer'). Additionally, a 5' Electric Easement (×2) and 7.5' Public Utility Easement are plat-dedicated per facts.md but locations relative to proposed improvements are not verified on site plans. Sheet 2 (Plat) should show all easements, but facts.md notes these are not shown. Sheet 9 shows the general site layout and street easements, but does not clearly depict all recorded electric easement boundaries or verify that proposed features maintain adequate clearance from easement areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition: 'customer facilities proposed to be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities' is prohibited 'regardless of clearance distances.' Additionally, items within electric easements must maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from the outside conductor. The facts.md documentation reveals that critical easements (Greenbelt, Drainage, Electric, PUE) are either not depicted or not verified on the site plan. Without accurate easement boundaries shown on plans, applicant cannot demonstrate that (1) no facilities are placed under/over overhead distribution lines in violation of the absolute prohibition, or (2) items within easements maintain required 7.5-foot clearances. A proximity survey by registered surveyor is required to confirm easement boundaries and facility compliance.

findings.comment: Provide detailed photometric plan or lighting layout showing all proposed exterior and decorative light fixture locations with: (1) horizontal and vertical clearance dimensions from surveyed outside conductor locations; (2) confirmation that fixtures maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances, OR; (3) relocation notes if fixtures cannot meet clearance requirements. Include note on site plan indicating clearance requirement for lighting.
applicableAreas: Proposed exterior lighting fixtures throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan, Block 2) includes a 'Lighting Note' requiring all exterior lighting to be 'full cut-off and fully shielded in compliance with Subchapter E 2.5' and providing 'Figure 34: Examples of Fully-Shielded Light Fixtures.' This addresses design standards for light shielding but does NOT address clearances from overhead electric lines. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows the site layout with various landscape elements but does not include dimension annotations showing horizontal or vertical clearances from proposed light fixtures to overhead electric lines. No site plan contains a photometric plan or detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations with clearance dimensions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires decorative lighting proposed under existing overhead electric lines to meet clearance requirements (7.5-foot sky-to-ground horizontal, 15-foot radial) or be relocated. The site plan shows a general requirement for 'full cut-off' lighting compliance but does not identify where exterior lighting fixtures will be located or provide clearance verification from overhead conductors. Without a detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations and without clearance dimensions from conductors, compliance cannot be verified. If lighting is proposed beneath or within 15 feet of overhead conductors, relocation or clearance documentation is required.

findings.comment: Clearly depict on site plan the location of existing down guy wire anchor points shown on the existing survey (Sheet 4). Verify that proposed driveways, accessible paths, parking areas, and other site features do not conflict with guy anchors or guy wire cables. If conflicts exist, provide notes addressing resolution through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles per utility company standards.
applicableAreas: Proposed accessible paths, driveways, and site features relative to down guy wires from existing utility poles
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a 'GUY ANCHOR' symbol (per the legend) at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road, indicating down guy wires are present on the existing utility infrastructure. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site layout with driveways, sidewalks, and pedestrian paths, but does NOT depict existing guy wire locations or down guy anchor points. The survey shows the guy anchor exists, but its location relative to the proposed driveways and accessible paths is not dimensioned or verified on Sheet 9. Without down guy wire locations being shown on the site plan and without verification that proposed accessible routes, driveways, or site features do not conflict with guy anchors and cables, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.reasoning: Down guy wires are support cables from distribution utility poles to ground anchors. They represent a potential obstruction and conflict risk if proposed accessible paths, driveways, or site features are routed over or through the guy anchor zone. UCM § 1.17.0 (Glossary) defines 'Down Guy' as a distinct feature. The grouping guidance notes that electric utility infrastructure (poles, guy wires, guys) is 'frequently omitted from plans,' suggesting this is a common deficiency. Sheet 4 confirms a guy anchor exists, but Sheet 9 does not show where it is located in relation to proposed site features. If the guy anchor conflicts with proposed improvements, the code requires either (1) pole relocation, or (2) conversion to self-supporting steel poles. The applicant has not addressed this possibility.

findings.comment: Depict on site plan and plat all down guy anchor easement boundaries for existing utility poles, showing 10-foot easement width extending minimum 5 feet past the point where the guy wire enters the ground. Verify that proposed site features (buildings, driveways, sidewalks, landscaping) do not encroach on or obstruct the down guy anchor easement area.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from existing utility poles
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a guy anchor symbol at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road. Sheet 2 (Plat) should show easement boundaries, but facts.md indicates that critical easements are not depicted on the submitted site plan. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show or reference down guy anchor easement boundaries. The grouping guidance specifies that down guy anchor easement requirements are: '10 feet wide extending 5 feet past where down guy enters ground' (per Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards). Without easement boundaries shown on the plat or site plan, and without dimension annotations confirming the 10-foot width and 5-foot extension, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: According to Reviewer Convention and Austin Energy standards, down guy anchor points require dedicated easements to ensure access for maintenance, replacement, and inspection. The required easement is 10 feet wide with minimum 5-foot extension beyond the anchor ground entry point. The existing survey (Sheet 4) confirms a guy anchor exists, but the plat (Sheet 2) and site plan (Sheet 9) do not show or reference the dedicated easement for this anchor. Without easement boundaries shown and dimensioned, applicant has not demonstrated that required easement space is provided and protected from development impacts (buildings, paving, landscaping, etc.).

findings.comment: Provide section views of proposed transformer pads showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum 7.5-foot vertical clearance from the lowest point of overhead conductors to the highest point of transformer equipment. If transformers are located beneath existing overhead lines, provide specific clearance verification or relocation notes.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows multiple transformer pad locations throughout the site (labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' at several locations). However, the electrical plan is a plan view showing horizontal placement only. NO section views or elevation drawings accompany the electrical plan showing the vertical relationship between transformer pad height and the surveyed elevation of overhead electric conductors above the site. No vertical clearance dimension annotations are present. Overhead electric lines are shown on the plan as existing 'OHE' lines on the western and southern boundaries, but no section showing the clearance from these conductors to the tops of transformer pads is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires transformers (whether pole-mounted or pad-mounted) to maintain minimum 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric lines. This is a vertical clearance requirement, requiring knowledge of both the transformer height and the conductor height. The electrical plan shows transformer pad locations but does not provide the surveyed conductor elevation or section views demonstrating that the 7.5-foot clearance is maintained. This is particularly important if any transformers are located beneath existing overhead lines or where overhead conductors pass over transformer equipment.

findings.comment: Provide construction staging/logistics plan (or site phasing plan) showing: (1) all proposed equipment staging areas, material storage zones, and laydown areas; (2) 10-foot radial clearance boundaries from overhead distribution lines (marked as exclusion zones); (3) crane swing radius zones with 10-foot radial clearance from energized lines; (4) 20-foot clearance from transmission lines if transmission structures are present; (5) note requiring contractor to maintain clearances and reference to OSHA 1910.333 working clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, material storage zones, and equipment laydown areas throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) addresses temporary erosion control measures and construction sequencing but does not include a detailed construction staging plan or equipment layout plan showing staging areas, equipment zones, crane swing radius, or material storage locations in relation to overhead electric lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site development layout but does not designate specific construction staging areas or address 10-foot radial clearances during construction. NO plans address OSHA and UCM § 1.10.2 requirements for 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines during construction activities. The sheet list shows no separate 'Construction Phasing Plan' or 'Construction Staging Plan' sheet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 references OSHA 1910.333 and Texas law requirements for construction working clearances. The grouping guidance states: 'Minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines (OSHA 1910.333, UCM § 1.10.2) [for] construction working clearances.' This is a mandatory safety requirement during construction and is distinct from permanent clearances. Additionally, the grouping notes: 'OSHA requires a 20-foot clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' The plans do not demonstrate that construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, crane swing radius, or work platforms will maintain required clearances from overhead energized lines. This is a deficiency: applicant has failed to provide a construction staging/logistics plan addressing these safety clearances.

findings.comment: Plant schedule lists tree species proposed near overhead electric line, but does not document utility-compatible (UC) status per ECM Appendix F required by UCM § 1.10.10.4. Clearance distances from tree trunks to outside conductors are not dimensioned on landscape plan, preventing verification of compliance with 15-foot minimum distance for non-utility-compatible species near distribution conductors.
applicableAreas: western site boundary where overhead electric line is present
areas within 15 feet of overhead distribution conductor
findings.observation: Sheet 21 documents an existing overhead electric line (OHE) running along the western boundary with utility poles and a service transition to underground infrastructure. Sheet 31 (landscape plan) shows the OHE line and depicts trees positioned along the site boundary near this overhead line. Sheet 35 provides a plant schedule listing proposed tree species: 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus Crassifolia), 2 Live Oak (Quercus Virginiana), 6 Mexican Redbud (Cercis Canadensis var. Mexicana), and 2 Texas Mountain Laurel (Sophora Secundiflora). However, the plant schedule does not indicate the utility-compatible (UC) status of any species per ECM Appendix F, and no clearance dimensions are provided on the landscape plan to verify distances from these species to the outside conductor.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that only utility-compatible trees (marked UC in ECM Appendix F) be proposed within 15 feet of distribution conductors. The landscape plan shows trees near the overhead line, but: (1) the voltage classification of the OHE line (distribution vs. transmission) is not documented on the plans; (2) the plant schedule provides species names but does not reference ECM Appendix F or identify UC status for any proposed species; (3) no clearance dimensions are shown to verify compliance with the 15-foot minimum for distribution. Without documented UC status from ECM Appendix F and without clearance dimensions, it cannot be determined whether proposed non-utility-compatible species are located within 15 feet of the outside conductor.

findings.comment: Large trees (Live Oak and Cedar Elm) with typical mature heights of 40-50 feet are shown on landscape plan and tree survey adjacent to overhead distribution conductors. Plans do not document mature heights to identify large trees (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F), and no clearance dimensions are provided to verify compliance with 25-foot minimum setback from distribution conductor.
applicableAreas: western and southern site boundaries where overhead electric lines are present
areas within 25 feet of overhead distribution conductor
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (landscape plan) shows overhead electric lines (OHE) running along site boundaries with utility poles, and trees positioned along these boundaries. Sheet 32 (tree inventory) documents surveyed trees on site including large native species: Live Oak specimens with DBH of 32 inches (Tree 4018), 36 inches (Tree 4026), 27 inches (Tree 4027), and 24 inches (Tree 4038), all marked as Appendix F species; Cedar Elm 17 inches DBH (Tree 4010); Pecan 24 inches DBH (Tree 4015). These large DBH trees typically have mature heights exceeding 40 feet (Live Oak and Cedar Elm commonly 40-60 feet). Sheet 35 specifies proposed planting of 10 Cedar Elm and 2 Live Oak. The landscape plan shows multiple tree symbols positioned directly adjacent to or overlapping the OHE line along the southern boundary (per vision analysis: '3+ trees positioned directly underneath or extremely close to the OHE line'). However, the landscape plan provides NO clearance dimensions from tree trunks to the outside conductor, and the plant schedule does NOT specify mature heights or indicate which species are 'large trees' (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that large trees (mature height 40 feet or greater per ECM Appendix F) be positioned at least 25 feet from the outside conductor of overhead distribution facilities. The site has: (1) documented large native trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm) with diameters typically correlating to 40+ foot mature heights; (2) proposed plantings of the same large species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm); (3) trees visually positioned adjacent to or overlapping the overhead line on site boundary; and (4) NO clearance dimensions dimensioning the distance from tree trunk center to outside conductor to verify the 25-foot minimum. The failure to document mature heights on the plant schedule prevents verification of which species qualify as 'large trees,' and the absence of clearance dimensions on the landscape plan means the 25-foot setback cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Trees are proposed and existing trees are shown near underground electrical transformer pads and pull boxes. No root barrier specifications (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are documented on the landscape plan or landscape detail sheets for any trees within the 20-foot protection zone.
applicableAreas: Throughout site near electrical infrastructure, particularly transformer pads and pull boxes
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads and eight+ pull boxes (underground electric equipment) distributed throughout the site. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted 'significant overlap' between these underground electrical infrastructure locations and existing tree canopy zones shown on the electrical plan. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) is being coordinated to add 20 proposed trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) plus shrubs and groundcover. Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) provides standard tree planting specifications but contains no root barrier specifications or references. Examination of all landscape sheets (31, 35, 37) reveals NO documentation of required root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) for any trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers for trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment: 'minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment.' Sheet 21 shows multiple transformer pads and pull boxes with tree canopy overlaps. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) provides no callouts, detail references, or notes specifying root barrier requirements for any of the 20 proposed trees or existing trees. Without root barrier documentation on the landscape and detail sheets, compliance with this requirement cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Landscape plan and plant schedule do not document mature heights (per ECM Appendix F) for proposed and retained tree species, preventing identification of 'large trees' (40+ feet) requiring stricter 25-foot setbacks from distribution conductors.
applicableAreas: landscape plan and plant schedule for areas within clearance zones of overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 35 lists proposed shade trees (Live Oak 100 gal., Cedar Elm 100 gal.) and ornamental trees (Texas Mountain Laurel 45 gal., Mexican Redbud 45 gal.) with minimum specifications at planting (4 inch caliper for shade trees; 2.5 inch caliper for ornamental trees). Sheet 35 also provides a tree inventory showing existing large trees: Live Oak specimens ranging from 12 to 42 inches DBH, Cedar Elm 17 inches DBH. However, the plant schedule specifies planting-size caliper only (4-inch, 2.5-inch) and does not indicate MATURE HEIGHT for any species. Without documented mature heights in the plant schedule, it cannot be determined which trees qualify as 'large trees' (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) requiring stricter clearance distances (25 feet from distribution, 50 feet from transmission). The landscape plan does not differentiate or call out large tree locations.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention and UCM § 1.10.10.4, large trees (mature height 40 feet or greater) have different clearance requirements from smaller trees: 25 feet from distribution conductors vs. 15 feet for other trees; 50 feet from transmission vs. 50 feet for all trees. For inspectors and subsequent reviewers to verify that the proposed plantings and retained trees comply with these differential requirements, the landscape plan must explicitly identify which trees are 'large' (40+ feet mature height). The plant schedule must document mature heights per ECM Appendix F for each species proposed in clearance zones. Currently, the plans provide only planting-size specifications (caliper/container size) without mature height annotation, preventing differentiation of large vs. non-large trees.

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions, measurement lines, or distance callouts are shown on the landscape plan between trees and the overhead electric line or utility poles, preventing verification of compliance with minimum clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities throughout site, specifically southern OHE line
findings.observation: Comprehensive visual examination of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no dimension lines, measurement arrows, or numerical distance callouts between any proposed trees and the overhead electric (OHE) line or utility poles. A detailed scan of the entire sheet confirmed absence of: (1) dimension lines between tree symbols and utility infrastructure, (2) written notes specifying clearances, (3) references to utility clearance requirements, or (4) any measurements related to tree-utility separation. The plan shows the OHE line and tree locations but provides no quantitative clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires clearances measured as lateral distance from tree trunk center to the outside conductor. Measurement methodology must be documented on plans to verify compliance. The landscape plan shows trees at the OHE line but provides zero dimensional information. Without clearance dimensions, it is impossible to determine whether trees meet the required distances (15 feet for distribution clearance zones, 10 feet from poles). The absence of any measurement callouts is itself a deficiency.

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are provided from tree trunk centers (planting locations) to utility conductors. The large canopy circles shown for each tree could be misinterpreted as measurement origins if any dimensions were present.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities throughout site, specifically southern OHE line
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) displays trees as circular symbols with inner trunk-center points and larger outer circles representing canopy extent. No dimension lines originate from tree trunk centers (the inner circle points representing planting locations).
