Where tree-utility distances appear to be dimensioned at all (which they are not), any measurement endpoints would be at the canopy edge rather than the planting trunk location. Vision analysis confirmed no measurements of any kind are shown on the plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies that clearances must be measured from the tree trunk center (planting location), not from the projected canopy edge. The measurement methodology is critical because measuring from canopy edge significantly underestimates the distance available to utilities. The plan fails on two counts: (1) it provides no measurements at all, and (2) the tree symbols do not include dimension lines that would clarify measurement origin points (trunk vs. canopy).

findings.comment: Retaining walls are shown on the site plan around the perimeter (north, east, and south edges) and underground electric lines are routed near these locations, but no clearance dimensions or verification are documented showing that the required 5-foot minimum separation from duct banks is maintained. Provide clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan confirming that all retaining wall structures are positioned at least 5 feet from underground electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls shown along site perimeter (north, east, south boundaries)
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies multiple retaining wall segments throughout the site: a concrete retaining wall in the northeast corner along the biofiltration/detention pond, an existing retaining wall to be replaced along the entire eastern edge behind Buildings 5 and 6, and concrete retaining walls along the southern perimeter behind Buildings 7 and 8. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines forming a perimeter loop around the buildings, with the main lines running along the outer edges of the site where the retaining walls are located. However, no clearance dimensions are documented between the underground electric line routing and any of the retaining wall locations. No notes indicate that the required 5-foot separation has been verified. Sheet 38 (Wall Plan) would contain detailed wall dimensions and sections but was not reviewed in detail for this analysis.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that permanent structures (including retaining walls) maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric duct banks. The site plan shows both retaining walls and electric line routing in proximity to each other, but provides no documentation that this clearance requirement has been addressed. The absence of clearance dimensions or verification notes is a deficiency—required information is missing from the plans. While the general contractor verification notes reference utility coordination, they do not substitute for plan-based documentation showing that the clearance requirement has been satisfied.

findings.comment: Utility and storm drain plans show electric lines crossing storm drain lines at multiple locations (including a dense cluster between Buildings 4-7) but do not document the required minimum 12-inch (1 foot) clearance at any crossing. Provide utility profile sheets and crossing details for all electric-storm drain crossings documenting separation distance, or provide documentation confirming all crossings meet or exceed 12 inches horizontal clearance.
applicableAreas: Electric-storm drain crossing in central site area
findings.observation: Sheets 12 (Storm Sewer Plan), 19 (Utility Tap Plan), and 21 (Electrical Design Plan) collectively show proposed electric lines (yellow on Sheet 19) crossing storm drain lines (green on Sheet 19, shown as dashed lines on Sheet 12) at multiple locations. Vision analysis of Sheet 19 identified a tight cluster where electric, water, and storm drain lines all converge in the central crossing area between Buildings 4 and 7. Additionally, electric lines cross storm drain lines at other locations throughout the site. However, none of the utility plans contain explicit numerical separation dimensions, clearance specifications, or crossing detail drawings at any of these crossing points. The storm drain plan note (Block 13, Sheet 12) states only that 'Contractor shall field verify locations of utility crossings prior to beginning construction.'
findings.reasoning: Electric conduit routing must maintain minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal clearance from other private utilities (excluding gas, fuel, steam) when crossing perpendicularly per UCM § 1.10.5.A. The plans clearly show electric-storm drain crossings at multiple locations, including in a congested area where multiple utilities converge (Bldgs 4-7 area). The complete absence of numerical separation dimensions, clearance callouts, or crossing detail drawings at any crossing location represents a failure to document design compliance. Storm drain is specifically a utility that requires documented separation. The contractor directive to field-verify does not substitute for design documentation demonstrating adequate clearance before construction.

findings.comment: Utility plans show water, wastewater, electric, and storm drain utilities all routed through the same internal drive corridor rather than being separated by type to opposite sides of the roadway. Provide utility coordination documentation addressing the mixture of wet and dry utilities in the same corridor, or revise routing to separate wet utilities (water, wastewater) to one side of the roadway and dry utilities (electric, storm drain, communications) to the opposite side per standard utility separation practice.
applicableAreas: Internal roadway corridor containing multiple utility types
findings.observation: Sheets 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and 19 (Utility Tap Plan) show that water (W), wastewater (WW), electric (E), and storm drain (SD) utilities all run through the same internal roadway corridor(s) on the site. Specifically, vision analysis noted that utilities 'all converge in the central crossing area between Buildings 4 and 7.' The utility plans show wet utilities (water from Austin Water, wastewater) and dry utilities (electric) routed along the same internal drive loop rather than being separated to opposite sides of the roadway. No notes on the utility plans document that wet and dry utilities are properly grouped and alternated on opposite sides of the roadway for safety purposes, nor is there any documented coordination showing this mixing has been evaluated and is acceptable.
findings.reasoning: Wet and dry utilities should be properly grouped and alternated (wet utilities on one side of roadway, dry utilities on opposite side) for safety purposes per Reviewer Convention. The utility routing shown clearly places both wet and dry utilities in the same corridor running through the internal site loop. The absence of any note or coordination documentation indicating this arrangement has been evaluated or is acceptable for this site represents a failure to document compliance with the utility separation convention.

findings.comment: Three storm drain manholes are located directly in pedestrian sidewalk areas and vehicle driveway paths. Relocate manholes to utility easement areas outside of primary circulation routes, or modify site plan to accommodate manhole access without creating conflicts with pedestrian routes, ramps, or vehicle drives.
applicableAreas: Central area between Buildings 7-8, between Buildings 2-3, south of Building 7
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) identifies three storm drain manholes with locations that conflict with pedestrian and vehicular site features: (1) SD Manhole between Buildings 2 and 3 (Rim 684.71): Located in a landscaped/pedestrian area directly adjacent to a north-south sidewalk routing, creating a maintenance access conflict and potential trip hazard in a pedestrian circulation path; (2) SD Manhole between Buildings 7 and 8 (Rim 683.78): Located in a paved pedestrian sidewalk threshold connecting the southern parking area to the central courtyard, directly in a pedestrian travel path; (3) SD Manhole south of Building 7 (Rim 681.02): Located directly in the paved vehicle driveway path, a primary vehicle circulation area. These manhole locations overlap with primary site circulation routes rather than being positioned in dedicated utility access areas.
findings.reasoning: Manhole placement must not conflict with site features that require vertical transitions (stairs, ramps, accessible routes) and should not be located directly in high-traffic pedestrian or vehicular circulation paths. The three manholes are positioned in: one in a pedestrian sidewalk area, one directly in a pedestrian pathway serving multiple buildings, and one in a primary vehicle driveway. These locations create conflicts with site circulation, accessibility, maintenance access, and pose potential trip hazards. Manhole covers in circulation paths are a code compliance issue and accessibility/safety concern.

findings.comment: Communication conduit routing is not explicitly shown on the utility plans, and the electrical plans do not clearly identify which facilities constitute Austin Energy main line duct banks. If communications infrastructure is proposed for the site, provide documentation showing all communication conduit routing and confirming that no communications conduits are installed over or crossing main line duct banks (major electric feeders), or clearly identify main line duct bank locations on the electrical plan to enable coordination verification.
applicableAreas: Sites where communications infrastructure is proposed or exists
findings.observation: Sheets 19 (Utility Tap Plan) and 21 (Electrical Design Plan) do not explicitly show communications conduit routing on the site plans. The legend on Sheet 19 references a 'Legend' block that shows symbols for various utilities but does not specifically identify a communications line symbol on the visible portions of the plan. While telecommunications infrastructure may exist for the development (buildings require communication services), no explicit routing of communication conduit over or across main line duct banks was identified on the reviewed sheets. However, the electrical plan does not specify which of the shown electric facilities constitute 'main line duct banks' (which typically contain major feeders such as 1000 MCM in 5-inch conduit) versus smaller service conduits. Without clear identification of main line duct banks and without visible communications routing, this requirement cannot be definitively verified.
findings.reasoning: Communication conduits are prohibited from being installed over Austin Energy main line duct banks per UCM § 1.10.5.A. Main line duct banks typically contain major electrical feeders (1000 MCM cables in 5-inch conduit). The electrical plans do not clearly identify which electrical facilities constitute main line duct banks. Additionally, communications infrastructure routing is not explicitly shown on the utility plans. Without clear identification of main line duct banks and without documented routing of communications conduit relative to them, it cannot be verified whether this prohibition is being met. If communications infrastructure is proposed, its routing relative to main line duct banks must be documented.

findings.comment: Proposed underground electric line is shown crossing proposed water utility line on Sheet 20, but no concrete encasement detail or Austin Energy Design approval documentation is provided. Either provide a detail showing 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the electric/water crossing, or provide written confirmation from Austin Energy Design that encasement is not required for this crossing.
applicableAreas: Proposed electric utility crossing water facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows a proposed underground electric line (marked '- E -' in the legend, defined as 'Proposed Underground Electric') crossing the proposed water line in the plan view east of the meter vault area. The crossing is indicated by the intersection of the electric line graphic with the water line graphic on the plan portion of the sheet. However, no detail sheet, profile view, or note on Sheet 20 or any related sheet reviewed documents or specifies concrete encasement requirements at this crossing point. Specifically, there is no detail showing 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the crossing, nor is there any note referencing Austin Energy Design approval of the crossing configuration. The utility notes on Sheet 20 (Block 8) contain only general contractor verification directives and do not address the specific encasement requirement for electric conduit crossings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A specifies that when electric conduit crosses other utilities, it shall have 2-inch concrete encasement extending minimum 24 inches on either side of the crossing point, or encasement shall be verified as not required through Austin Energy Design approval. The site plan documents show an electric crossing occurring (Sheet 20 plan view), but no detail, note, or reference documentation is provided showing either: (1) the concrete encasement specification, or (2) written confirmation from Austin Energy Design that encasement is not required. Required information is missing from the plans. This is a deficiency because the applicant has not documented either the encasement detail or the design approval that would exempt this crossing from the encasement requirement.

findings.comment: Austin Water fire demand meter vault (8' x 12' structure shown on Sheet 20) is depicted on the utility tap plan, but no exclusive 5-foot space around and under the vault is documented on the plans. Provide dimension callouts or notes on the utility plan confirming that the vault maintains the required 5-foot exclusive space with no other utilities or structures encroaching within this zone.
applicableAreas: Fire demand meter vault area and surrounding utility infrastructure
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) identifies a structure labeled '8' Fire Demand Meter in 8' x 12' Vault' on the plan view west of the property entrance. The vault is shown with its footprint on the plan and appears to connect to the proposed water line at the tap location. Sheet 19 shows various utilities (water, wastewater, electrical) routed through the site in proximity to this vault area. However, no plan view or detail on either sheet documents or verifies that an exclusive 5-foot space exists around and under the vault structure, free of other underground utilities, appurtenances, or structures. UCM § 2.9.1.A.4 requires Austin Water vaults to maintain 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault; no plan notation, dimension callout, or specification confirms that this requirement has been addressed or verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.A.4 requires that Austin Water vaults maintain required 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault structure, with no other underground utilities, appurtenances, or structures allowed to encroach within this zone. The vault location is identified on the plan, and its general footprint is shown, but the plans provide no documentation that this exclusive space requirement has been verified or is being provided. Without dimension callouts or notes showing the 5-foot exclusion zone and confirming that no other utilities encroach within it, compliance cannot be confirmed from the available plan documentation. This is unclear because the plans lack sufficient information to verify the exclusive space requirement.

findings.comment: Building elevations or meter location detail sheets must be provided showing that electrical meters are NOT located on/under porches, stairways, overhangs exceeding 72 inches, carports, or other prohibited locations per UCM § 1.9.3.1. Provide building elevations with meter locations clearly identified relative to architectural features.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters are mounted directly on building foundation walls for all eight buildings. However, the plan does not provide sufficient detail regarding the specific mounting locations relative to building architectural features. Visual positioning suggests meters are mounted on exterior sidewalls, but the plans do not explicitly indicate: (1) Whether any meters are located under porches, covered entryways, or overhangs; (2) The exact relationship to stairways (some buildings have units with stairs); (3) Whether any meters are located under carports or covered parking areas; (4) The relationship to accessible routes or ramps. Sheet 21 notation indicates building FFEs and unit numbers but does not detail these specific meter location constraints.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 prohibits electric meters from being located on/under porches, stairways, under overhangs exceeding 72 inches, carports, or where moving objects might damage equipment. The site plan shows meters are wall-mounted but does not provide the architectural detail necessary to confirm they are not located under prohibited features. Meters appear to be on building sides, but without building elevation drawings or detail sections showing the relationship of meters to overhangs, carports, and architectural features, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Provide building electrical plans, riser diagrams, or service disconnect location drawings showing the distance between electrical meters and their serving main service disconnects, confirming distance does not exceed 20 feet and that meter and disconnect are within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meter locations but does not show or reference electrical service disconnect switch locations. The electrical design plan does not identify where main disconnect switches or service disconnects are located relative to meters. Without this information, the distance between meters and disconnects cannot be verified from the available site plan documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires that the distance between electric meter and disconnect does not exceed 20 feet, and meter and disconnect must be within line of sight. The site plan does not show disconnect switch locations, making it impossible to verify this requirement from the available evidence. Building electrical plans or riser diagrams that show disconnect switch locations would be necessary to make this determination.

findings.comment: Add barricade placement details to the Erosion Control Plan (Sheets 5-7) showing 10-foot barricades erected around all transmission structures (Pole 1 and Pole 3) and guy anchor locations before construction begins. Include this on the construction sequence diagram and reference it in construction notes.
applicableAreas: 10-foot zone around transmission poles (Pole 1 NW corner, Pole 3 SE corner) and guy anchor locations
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Electric Transmission Notes state: 'Barricades must be erected 10 feet from electric transmission structures during construction.' Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) shows temporary erosion control barriers and construction sequencing. However, the plan does not show barricades specifically placed 10 feet from the three utility poles (Pole 1 at NW corner where construction occurs, and Pole 3 at SE corner) or from the guy anchor location. The erosion control plan does not delineate a 10-foot protection zone around transmission structures with specific barricade placement as required.
findings.reasoning: The transmission structures (Pole 1 and Pole 3 with guy anchors) are located within or immediately adjacent to the construction limits (per Sheet 4 existing conditions and Sheet 9 site plan showing proposed buildings). Construction activities including grading, building construction, and utility work will occur near these structures. UCM § 1.14.9 requires barricades to be erected before construction commences. The specific placement of barricades at 10-foot distances from transmission structures is a safety and access requirement that must be shown on the construction/erosion control plans.

findings.comment: Show warning sign placement under all overhead electric transmission facilities on the construction plan or erosion control plan. Include sign specifications and exact locations where construction will occur under OHE lines. Add note: 'Danger - High Voltage Transmission Lines' signs to be installed before construction.'  References Sheet 3 requirement and existing OHE line locations shown on Sheets 4 and 31.
applicableAreas: under overhead electric transmission facilities along south boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes require: 'Warning signs must be placed under the overhead electric transmission facilities as notification of the electrical hazard.' Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows overhead electric lines (marked OHE) running along the south property boundary and across the north boundary. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows construction/grading occurring under these overhead lines. However, the construction plans (Sheets 5-7 for erosion control, Sheet 3 for general notes) do not show placement of warning signs under the overhead transmission facilities.
findings.reasoning: Overhead electric transmission lines are present on the site. Construction activities (grading, building construction, landscaping) will occur beneath these lines. OSHA and Austin Energy both require hazard notification to protect worker safety. The requirement is explicitly stated in the transmission notes but not documented on the construction plans.

findings.comment: Excavation exceeding 1 foot in depth (approximately 2-3 feet) within 25 feet of transmission structure lacks Austin Energy evaluation and approval documentation.
applicableAreas: NW corner of site near transmission pole and guy anchor on Valley View Road frontage
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms transmission pole and guy anchor at NW corner. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) documents excavation depths showing proposed cut of approximately 2-3 feet at the NW corner property line where the transmission structure is located. This exceeds the 1-foot depth threshold that triggers the UCM § 1.14.5.2 evaluation requirement. No documentation from Austin Energy indicating that this excavation greater than 1 foot in depth within 25 feet of the transmission foundation has been reviewed and approved is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.5.2 states that excavations greater than 1 foot in depth within 25 feet of transmission foundations require Austin Energy evaluation and approval. The grading plan clearly shows excavation at the NW corner of approximately 2-3 feet in depth, which exceeds the 1-foot threshold. Without documentation of Austin Energy review and approval in the site plan submittal, this deficiency cannot be resolved. The presence of excavation specifications on the plan without the corresponding approval documentation demonstrates non-compliance.

findings.comment: Irrigation system layout deferred to as-built plan; specific sprinkler clearances from transmission structures within 25 feet not documented despite plantings shown within easement areas requiring irrigation.
applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries where electric easements are located; landscape planting zones
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts numerous trees within and immediately adjacent to the 5-foot electric easements along north, east, and south property boundaries. Trees are coded as 'SY' (Street Yard), 'PL' (Parking Lot), 'P' (Buffer Point), and 'M' (Mitigation) within or overlapping the utility line corridors. Sheet 31 guidance note states: 'Specific irrigation layout is not shown. The drawing does not visually map out sprinkler heads, lateral lines, or valves. Therefore, it cannot be visually confirmed if heads are placed within 25 feet of structures or easements. However...Given that plantings (which require water) are shown in these areas, it is highly likely irrigation infrastructure will be present near the utilities.' Sheet 31 (Irrigation Notes) defers specific irrigation system design to an as-built plan: 'THE IRRIGATION INSTALLER SHALL DEVELOP AND PROVIDE AN AS-BUILT DESIGN PLAN TO THE CITY.' No specific irrigation layout showing sprinkler clearances from transmission structures is provided on the landscape plan.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 14) state: 'Sprinklers are prohibited within 25 feet of transmission poles and structures.' Sheet 31 shows that significant plantings requiring irrigation are located within and immediately adjacent to transmission easements. The specific irrigation system layout, including sprinkler head locations and distances from transmission structures, is deferred to an as-built plan not included in this submittal. While it may be possible that the final irrigation design will comply with clearance requirements, the current plans do not affirmatively demonstrate compliance with the 25-foot prohibition. Approval cannot be granted without documentation showing that irrigation infrastructure will maintain required clearances.

findings.comment: Biofiltration/detention pond with retaining wall proposed immediately adjacent to northeast corner transmission easement; no documentation that pond design preserves Austin Energy access and maintenance vehicle turnaround requirements.
applicableAreas: Northeast corner of site, biofiltration/detention pond area adjacent to transmission easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a 'Biofiltration/Detention Pond' located in the northeast corner of the site, immediately adjacent to the north property line where a 5-foot electric easement and a 15-foot drainage easement/electric easement are located. Sheet 15 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan) and Sheet 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles) detail the pond design and dimensions. The pond perimeter and retaining wall are shown immediately adjacent to the property boundary where the transmission easement is located. The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 16) explicitly prohibit: 'any structures, including but not limited to...drainage, filtration or detention ponds which would impair Austin Energy's access to the transmission easements or its lines, poles, structures, towers or appurtenant facilities in the easements.' The site plan does not provide documentation that the pond design has been reviewed for impact on transmission facility access or that the pond can be maintained while preserving Austin Energy's turnaround and maintenance vehicle access requirements.
findings.reasoning: While water quality features (detention ponds) may be allowable outside transmission easements with appropriate setbacks, the proposed pond's immediate adjacency to the transmission easement boundary raises questions about whether it impairs Austin Energy access as prohibited. The Electric Transmission Notes require that features not impair access, and the transmission facility access requirements (including 25-foot clearance from structure base for turnaround of 80,000-pound maintenance vehicles) must be verified. The site plan does not contain documentation that Austin Energy has reviewed and approved the pond location relative to access and maintenance requirements. The proximity of the pond with retaining wall immediately at the easement boundary creates uncertainty about whether the design preserves required access.

findings.comment: Shrubs and tree plantings with mature canopies proposed directly within and overlapping 5-foot electric easements along north, east, and south property boundaries; will obstruct required access to transmission structure base during maintenance.
applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries within and adjacent to electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts multiple trees and shrubs (coded as 'SY', 'PL', 'P', 'M') positioned directly on or overlapping the 5-foot electric easement boundaries along the north, east, and south property lines. Specific vision analysis identified: 'North Boundary: Numerous large tree canopies (indicated by circles) are drawn directly on or overlapping this line and the property boundary'; 'South Boundary: Large tree canopies are drawn overlapping this area'; 'East Boundary: Tree canopies overlap the property line in this area.' These planted trees and associated shrubs will mature and create dense vegetation directly within and immediately adjacent to the transmission easements. Sheet 31 does not provide density, spacing, or height specifications that would allow verification that plantings will not obstruct access to structure bases during maintenance.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 1) explicitly state: 'Vehicular access for Austin Energy trucks and equipment is always to be maintained within the easement' and 'Shrubbery must not obstruct access to structure base' (UCM § 1.14.6). Sheet 31 shows plantings directly on/within the easement boundaries. These plantings, as they mature, will create obstacles to the 'walking or vehicle access to transmission structure base' that must remain clear per the grouping's regulatory overview. Mature tree canopies and shrub plantings within the easement violate this requirement.

findings.comment: Retaining walls and permanent site features (concrete fence, pond perimeter wall) proposed immediately at/within transmission easement boundaries along north, east, and south property lines; prevents required 25-foot level access corridor for maintenance vehicle turnaround.
applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries; northwest and southwest corners where transmission structures located
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) show retaining walls proposed immediately along the north, east, and south property boundaries where the 5-foot electric easements are located. Specific observations: North boundary retaining wall immediately adjacent to north easement; East boundary: 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced' and new concrete fence at east property line within/adjacent to easement; South boundary: concrete retaining wall running 'tightly along the southern property line, parallel and immediately adjacent to the southern OHE line and 5' Electric & Tele Easement.' The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20) specify a '25-foot access corridor' that must remain 'level' and free for Austin Energy maintenance vehicles. The site plan shows retaining walls and permanent features immediately at or within the transmission easement boundaries, eliminating any clear 25-foot access corridor for turnaround of 80,000-pound maintenance vehicles (Condor trucks) with 75-foot turning radius.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4 requires a '25-foot access corridor' along the entire length of transmission ROW, with 'Level access...designed to support 46,000-48,000 lb tandem axle loads' for Condor truck turnaround. The site plan's placement of retaining walls and permanent structures immediately at or within the transmission easement boundaries prevents the maintenance of this required corridor. The transmission facility access requirement (Condor truck turnaround with 75-foot turning radius) cannot be satisfied if permanent walls and features occupy the easement at property boundaries.

findings.comment: Guy wire anchor locations from existing conditions survey not adequately depicted on grading and site plans; 25-foot clearance zones around guy anchors not established on working drawings despite proposed excavation at NW corner.
applicableAreas: NW and SW corners of property along Valley View Road where transmission structures and guy anchors located
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) clearly shows power poles ('P.P.') with guy wires ('GUY') and guy anchors at both the NW and SW corners of the property on Valley View Road. However, Sheets 9 (Site Plan) and 11 (Grading Plan) do not adequately depict these guy wire structures or establish 25-foot evaluation zones around them. The transmission notes require that guy anchors be treated as transmission structures for clearance purposes ('Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of the transmission structures, including down guy anchors'). While the poles themselves may be outside property boundaries, the guy anchors extend onto or very near the property, yet the grading plan shows excavation occurring at the NW corner with no indication of the guy anchor location or the required clearance envelope. The plans fail to show: (1) guy wire and anchor locations on grading and site plans, (2) 25-foot clearance zones around guy anchors, and (3) how proposed site improvements (excavation, retaining walls) maintain clearance from guy anchors.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that 'Existing guy wire foundations and anchors' be 'shown on plans' and that 'proposed construction does not maintain required clearances from these support structures.' The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows guy wires and anchors exist at NW and SW corners. The grading and site plans do not adequately depict these structures or the 25-foot clearance zones required around them. The lack of guy anchor depiction on the working plans (Sheets 9 and 11) combined with proposed excavation at the NW corner creates uncertainty about whether clearances are maintained. Adequate depiction of guy anchors and clearance zones on all relevant working plans is required.

findings.comment: Multiple proposed improvements (excavation, retaining walls, detention pond, landscaping) located within or immediately adjacent to existing electric easements without documented Austin Energy coordination, approval, or conflict resolution.
applicableAreas: Multiple locations: NW/SW corners (transmission poles), northeast corner (detention pond), north/east/south property lines (easements)
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing transmission poles and guy wires along Valley View Road (NW/SW corners) and multiple electric easements (5-foot and 15-foot) along property boundaries. Sheets 9, 11, and 15 show proposed improvements including: excavation at NW corner within/adjacent to transmission structure location; retaining walls along north, east, and south property lines within/adjacent to electric easements; biofiltration/detention pond in NE corner adjacent to transmission easement; landscape plantings within easement boundaries. The site plan indicates that electric easements exist but does not include documentation showing: (1) that Austin Energy has reviewed and approved proposed improvements relative to the easement; (2) how the site improvements will be modified/designed to avoid conflicts with transmission facility requirements; or (3) what tie-down arrangements or easement modifications (if any) have been agreed with Austin Energy. Site plan notes reference Austin Energy coordination requirements but do not document that the coordination has occurred or that conflicts have been resolved.
findings.reasoning: Proposed improvements (excavation, walls, pond, landscaping) occur within or immediately adjacent to existing transmission easements, but no documentation of Austin Energy review, approval, or conflict resolution is provided on the site plan. Documentation of easement coordination or relocation is needed.

findings.comment: Applicant must relocate all mitigation trees outside the transmission easement (minimum 25 feet from transmission structure base) and replace with utility-compatible species marked 'UC' in ECM Appendix F with mature height generally ≤20 feet. Live Oak cannot be planted within 50 feet of transmission facilities. Submit revised landscape plan showing compliance with transmission easement restrictions and species requirements per UCM § 1.14.6 and ECM Appendix F.
applicableAreas: south transmission easement area where mitigation trees are planted, within 50 feet of transmission overhead lines and Pole 3
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Electric Transmission Notes state: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows mitigation trees (marked with 'M' symbols) planted along the south property boundary, directly under the overhead electric line (OHE). These trees are located within 1-3 feet of the property line, meaning they are within the 5-foot transmission easement area or immediately adjacent to it. Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations) provides the plant list: 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia, 40-50 foot mature height) and 2 Live Oak (Quercus virginiana, 50-80+ foot mature height) are included in the mitigation planting. Live Oak is NOT listed as a utility-compatible species in ECM Appendix F. Cedar Elm, while sometimes acceptable near utilities, has a mature height exceeding the 20-foot guidance for utility-compatible species.
findings.reasoning: The transmission easement runs along the south boundary where trees are being planted. UCM § 1.14.6 prohibits trees in transmission easements and within 25 feet of transmission structures. The vision analysis confirms mitigation trees are placed within the easement area (1-3 feet from property line = within 5-foot easement) and directly under the overhead line. Additionally, non-utility-compatible species (Live Oak) are being planted in this location, violating the requirement for UC-marked species per ECM Appendix F. This represents a double violation: (1) trees placed in prohibited zone (transmission easement), and (2) non-compatible species used.

findings.comment: Applicant must provide one of the following: (1) Pavement Design Sheets certifying that all roads, driveways, and parking areas within transmission easements are designed to support 48,000 lb tandem axle loads with 5-foot spacing, including subgrade, base, and surface course calculations sealed by a registered engineer, OR (2) Revised site plan with a note explicitly stating that no roads, pavement, driveways, or parking areas are located within the transmission easement areas. Reference the 5-foot easement boundaries shown on Sheets 2 and 4.
applicableAreas: roads, driveways, pavement, parking areas, and any subsurface infrastructure within transmission easement (5-foot easement along north and south boundaries)
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Electric Transmission Notes require: 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5 foot spacing) to ensure safety.' UCM § 1.16.0 specifies 48,000 lbs as the most restrictive standard. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the site layout with proposed parking, driveways, and roadways. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows the grading throughout the site. Sheets 22-24 show construction details for driveways, curbs, and related infrastructure. However, NONE of these sheets provide pavement design calculations, load capacity certifications, or engineering documentation demonstrating that any surfaces within the transmission easement (5-foot easements along north and south boundaries) are designed and certified to support 48,000-pound tandem axle loads. There is no reference to pavement specifications, base courses, subgrade preparation, or structural design adequate for this load requirement.
findings.reasoning: The transmission easement requires that any pavement crossing or parallel to it must support 80,000-pound Condor trucks used by Austin Energy for maintenance. This is a structural design requirement, not merely a note. Per UCM § 1.14.4 and § 1.16.0, applicants must affirmatively demonstrate compliance through engineering calculations and design certification. The site plan does not provide this documentation. If any parking, driveway, or pavement is proposed within the 5-foot transmission easements, it must be designed accordingly. If no pavement is within the easements, this should be explicitly noted and shown on the plans.

findings.comment: No overhead distribution poles are shown on the electrical plans in the vicinity of the detention pond. If poles exist, their locations and clearances to the pond water's edge must be dimensioned and sealed by engineer.
applicableAreas: Biofiltration/detention pond area in northeastern portion of site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows no overhead distribution facility poles in proximity to the detention pond in the northeastern corner. The plan indicates underground transformers and pull boxes but does not show overhead distribution poles near the water quality feature. The overhead electric line ('-OHE-') is shown on the western boundary along Valley View Road. No dimension callouts show pole locations relative to the pond.
findings.reasoning: This checklist item is applicability-dependent: it applies 'Only when retention ponds are proposed on sites with overhead distribution facility poles.' Vision analysis of Sheet 21 shows no overhead poles indicated near the detention pond. If poles do exist in the area and are not depicted, this represents a documentation gap. However, based on available evidence, there does not appear to be overhead distribution poles in close proximity to the pond.

findings.comment: Provide utility plan with explicit confirmation and dimensions showing that all water meters, wastewater connection points, backflow preventers, and other utility equipment are located outside all electric easements and crossing utility lines cross only perpendicularly.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) vision analysis identified multiple utility easements: wastewater easement, drainage easements, public utility easement, and electric easements. Sheets 19-20 (Utility Tap Plans) show water meter and wastewater connection points on the western side of the property. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric transformers at locations: NW corner Bldg. 1, SW corner Bldg. 8, SE corner Bldg. 6, and between Bldgs. 4-5. The utility tap locations (water meter) do not appear to be within the 5' electric easement on the eastern boundary based on their western-side positioning. However, no explicit statement is provided on the plans confirming that all utility equipment (water meters, backflow preventers, wastewater connection points) are located outside the electric easements.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.13 requires: 'Water, wastewater, or gas utility facilities, meters, vaults, backflow preventers, valves, tanks, or equipment located within electric easements where only electric facilities are permitted.' The plans show utility infrastructure locations but do not explicitly confirm that all non-electric utility equipment is outside the electric easement boundaries. While visual inspection suggests water/wastewater connections are on the western side away from the eastern electric easement, explicit clearance confirmation with dimension callouts is absent. Marked 'unclear' because the issue cannot be definitively confirmed from available plan evidence.

findings.comment: The biofiltration/detention pond, including its retaining walls and required vegetation, is located within the 5' Electric Easement and must be relocated outside the easement boundary. Detention ponds cannot be located within electric easements as they obstruct required access and maintenance corridors.
applicableAreas: Biofiltration/detention pond in northeastern corner within 5' Electric Easement
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 explicitly confirmed: 'Yes, the Biofiltration/Detention Pond overlaps. The eastern edge of the "Concrete Retaining Wall" enclosing the pond is drawn completely within the 5-foot space between the dashed easement line and the eastern property line.' Sheet 2 (Plat) shows 5' Electric Easements along property boundaries. Sheets 15-16 detail the detention pond structure and vegetation requirements. The drainage easements shown on Sheet 9 are separate from the electric easements. The detention pond itself, with its retaining walls, biofiltration media, and required vegetation, is located within the 5' Electric Easement along the eastern boundary. This violates the principle that electric easements are reserved exclusively for electric facilities.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4 and § 1.14.7 specify that drainage structures, detention ponds, and other non-electric features are prohibited within electric easements where they would impair Austin Energy's access and maintenance of electric facilities. The submitted plans clearly show the detention pond retaining wall within the 5' electric easement. A detention pond with retaining walls, vegetation, and maintenance requirements is a drainage structure that obstructs the easement and prevents unobstructed access for electric facility maintenance.

findings.comment: Provide utility coordination plan documenting that all non-electric utilities (water, wastewater) cross electric easements at perpendicular or near-perpendicular angles. Confirm no utility lines run parallel or longitudinally within electric easements and no utility vaults or equipment are located within easement boundaries.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple easements including drainage, wastewater, utility, and electric. Sheets 19-20 (Utility Tap Plans) show water and wastewater service connections. Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing. The utility plans indicate water service connection on the western side and wastewater connection points, suggesting these utilities may cross the site. However, the plans do not show explicit routing alignments or crossing angles for utilities relative to the electric easements. No detail sheets or notes specify the crossing angles or confirm perpendicular crossings of non-electric utilities through electric easements.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.16 requires: 'Non-electric utility lines (water, wastewater, gas, private utilities) running parallel or longitudinally within electric easements rather than crossing perpendicularly.' The code allows perpendicular utility crossings but prohibits parallel runs or utility equipment/vaults within easements. The submitted plans do not explicitly document the routing angles and crossing methodologies for water and wastewater utilities relative to electric easements. Without these details, compliance with the perpendicular crossing requirement cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Provide dimensioned parking layout plan explicitly showing that all parking areas and paved surfaces are located outside the 5' Electric Easement boundaries. Confirm parking is setback minimum distance from easement lines.
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the site layout with buildings positioned primarily on the western and central portions. The 5' Electric Easements are located along the eastern and southern property boundaries. The parking areas and driveways appear to be located in the central and western areas, separated from the easement boundaries by the building clusters. However, no explicit dimension callouts confirm the exact distance of parking areas from the easement lines. The southern parking area location relative to the southern electric easement boundary is not dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.17 prohibits: 'Parking lots, parking areas, covered parking structures, or paved surfaces within electric distribution easements (voltage below 60kV, not transmission).' While visual inspection suggests parking is positioned away from the easements, specific dimension callouts confirming minimum clearances are absent. Marked 'unclear' because the evidence is not definitive enough to confirm the parking is entirely outside the distribution easement boundaries.

findings.comment: If any paving is proposed within the 5' Electric Easement, provide detail sheets with material specifications confirming use of flat concrete only and explicitly prohibiting pavers.
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) key notes identify: 'H.7 — SOD' shown in areas along the eastern boundary. Vision analysis of the landscape plan identified sod areas in the narrow strip between buildings and the eastern property line (within the electric easement area). However, the sheets do not provide detail specifications distinguishing between 'concrete' (allowed) and 'pavers' (prohibited) paving types. Construction detail sheets would be required to confirm paving material specifications.
findings.reasoning: The landscape plan shows sod/grass in the easement areas, not paving. If concrete or other hardscape is proposed in the easement areas, detail sheets must specify 'concrete' and explicitly exclude pavers. Marked 'unclear' because the specific paving detail specifications are not confirmed on available sheets.

findings.comment: Provide construction phasing plan and ESC plan demonstrating that no construction staging areas, materials, equipment, or spoils are placed within the 5' Electric Easement and that 24-hour emergency access is maintained during construction.
findings.observation: Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) and Sheet 6 (Erosion Control Notes) detail construction staging requirements. Vision analysis was not performed on these sheets specifically for staging area locations relative to electric easements. However, these sheets are included in the site plan submittal and would contain information about temporary construction staging, materials storage, and equipment placement.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.21 requires: 'Construction staging areas, construction materials, spoils areas, temporary structures, security fencing, concrete washout areas, or construction entrances located within electric easements obstructing required 24-hour access' are prohibited. The ESC plans and construction phasing documents would show whether any temporary construction features are placed within the electric easements. Without vision analysis of these specific sheets, the determination cannot be made with certainty. Marked 'unclear' pending review of ESC plan details.

findings.comment: Fire hydrant is located on or within the 5' Electric Easement boundary. While EL-5.23 is transmission-specific, fire hydrants should be located entirely outside distribution electric easements to prevent obstruction of access. Verify fire hydrant is completely outside all electric easement boundaries.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) identified fire hydrant 1 (FH) located 'directly intersecting the dashed line that marks the inner boundary of the 5' Electric Easement. This places the center of the fire hydrant exactly on the 5-foot mark from the eastern property boundary.' The fire hydrant appears to be partially within the distribution electric easement, not within a transmission easement. UCM § 1.14.7 cited in EL-5.23 specifically addresses transmission easements ('Easements for Transmission Facilities') with a 20-foot minimum clearance requirement from transmission structures.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.23 applicability is 'Only when transmission easements or transmission structures are present and fire hydrants are proposed.' This site has distribution easements and distribution-level infrastructure, not transmission. The cited code (UCM § 1.14.7) is transmission-specific. While fire hydrants should not be located in electric easements generally (per basic access principles), this specific checklist item is transmission-focused. The fire hydrant proximity to the distribution easement boundary is problematic for access but is not captured by EL-5.23's transmission-specific criteria. Marked 'unclear' because the fire hydrant location relative to distribution easements is a potential issue not specifically addressed by EL-5.23.

findings.comment: Public Utility Easements (PUE) may not be wide enough to accommodate all proposed utilities with required separation distances. The site plan shows 5-foot, 7.5-foot, and 10-foot PUEs but does not provide utility separation specifications or a utility coordination table. Provide a detailed utility coordination analysis showing the location and horizontal separation distances of all utilities (electric, water, wastewater, telecommunications, etc.) proposed within each PUE, verifying that PUE widths are adequate.
applicableAreas: Public Utility Easements along property boundaries (north, east, southeast boundaries)
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) confirms that PUEs are shown along property boundaries: '5' P.U.E. Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76' on the northern boundary, '10' P.U.E.' on the western boundary, and '10' P.U.E. Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76' on the southern boundary. The electrical plan indicates that proposed 'Underground Electric Line' crosses through at least one of these PUEs. However, the site plan does not show detailed utility separation specifications or a utility separation table documenting the distances between the proposed electric facilities and any other utilities potentially located within the PUEs (water, wastewater, telecommunications, etc.). Without this utility coordination detail, it is unclear whether the 5-foot and 10-foot PUE widths are sufficient to accommodate all utilities with required minimum separation distances.
findings.reasoning: Without detailed utility coordination and separation distances documented on the plans, the adequacy of PUE widths cannot be determined. The applicant must provide a utility coordination analysis showing all utilities within each PUE and the minimum separation distances between them, confirming that the 5-foot, 7.5-foot, and 10-foot PUE widths are adequate for all proposed utilities.

findings.comment: Laydown curb rated to withstand required vehicle loading not provided for Austin Energy truck access where parking areas or curbing are located along access routes to transmission easements. While COA 430S laydown curb specifications are available, the site plan does not explicitly specify where laydown curbs will be used in transmission easement areas. Clarify whether transmission easements exist on this site. If transmission easements are present along or near parking or curb areas, specify that all curbing within transmission easement access routes shall be laydown curb (over-roll curb) rated for 46,000 lb tandem axle loading with 5-foot spacing per SSM Item 430s and UCM § 1.14.4.
applicableAreas: Parking areas and curbing along access routes to transmission easements
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Construction Details Sheet 22 confirms that laydown curb specifications (COA 430S-1) are available and shown on the details sheet. The sheet explicitly depicts 'LAYDOWN CURB' in the curb type panel. However, vision analysis also confirms that 'There are NO transmission-specific or electrical easement-specific curb details shown on this document.' The site plan does not explicitly call out or specify which curb types will be used in areas where vehicles access transmission easements. The General Notes (Sheet 3) state that 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5 foot spacing)' and 'All curbing within the electric transmission easement must be over-roll curbing.' However, no site plan annotation indicates where transmission easements are located or whether laydown curbs are specified for those areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4.E and 1.14.4.F address transmission easement access and curb specifications. SSM Item 430s specifies laydown curb construction. The grouping's regulatory overview states 'Inadequate curb specification: Detail sheets show standard curb along transmission easement access route instead of laydown curb rated for required loading.' While the construction details sheet includes laydown curb specifications, the site plan itself does not specify whether transmission easement access routes will use laydown curbs. The applicability of this item hinges on whether transmission easements exist on this site and whether parking or curbing are located along their access routes. The extensive transmission notes on Sheet 3 suggest transmission facilities may be present, but the site plan layout is unclear about transmission easement locations and curb specifications. This creates ambiguity.

findings.comment: Minimum 25-foot wide all-weather access route for vehicles to transmission easements not provided or shown on plans. General Notes reference extensive transmission facility requirements (25-foot clearances, transmission structures, transmission wires), but no 25-foot transmission access corridors are shown or dimensioned on the Site Plan. Clarify the presence and location of transmission easements and facilities. If transmission easements exist, provide a clear delineation of the 25-foot minimum access corridor with 16-foot vertical clearance, all-weather paved surface (HMAC or PCC), and specifications for gates, grades, and curbs as required by UCM § 1.14.4.
applicableAreas: Entire site, if transmission easements are present
findings.observation: General Notes (Sheet 3) contain extensive transmission facility requirements, including: 'Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of transmission structures,' '25-foot clearance from energized transmission lines,' 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle,' and specific requirements for access corridors, gates (minimum 16 feet wide, 24-hour access), grades (no slopes greater than 8%), curbs (laydown curbs), and drainage restrictions. These transmission notes indicate that transmission facilities are either present on or immediately adjacent to the site. However, examination of the Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) reveals NO 25-foot-wide access corridors with 16-foot vertical clearance explicitly shown or dimensioned. The electric easements shown on the plans are only 5-foot, 7.5-foot, and 10-foot wide—far below the 25-foot transmission requirement. No transmission easement access routes are labeled or dimensioned with 25-foot widths.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4.A specifies 'Access (Transmission Facilities): A minimum 25-foot wide all-weather access route for vehicles to transmission easements with 16 feet minimum vertical clearance.' The regulatory overview defines transmission facilities as 'energized at 60kV or higher' and notes 'The 100-foot proximity threshold triggers specialized transmission review requirements.' The General Notes on Sheet 3 extensively reference transmission structures, transmission wires, and transmission easements with specific 25-foot requirements, strongly indicating that transmission infrastructure exists on or adjacent to the property. However, the site plan shows only 5-foot to 10-foot easement widths and provides no evidence of 25-foot access corridors. This creates a critical gap: either transmission facilities do not exist on the site (contradicting the extensive transmission notes), or the required 25-foot access corridors have not been shown on the plans. Without 25-foot access corridors clearly delineated and dimensioned on the plans, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with UCM § 1.14.4.A.

findings.comment: The presence of niche equipment cannot be determined from the plans. A 'Vault Easement' is shown adjacent to Building 8, but the plans do not explicitly designate this as niche equipment per UCM § 1.10.4 or provide required detail drawings showing entrance design, interior vertical clearances (minimum 35 feet), fire-rating (3-hour), and accessibility from outside the building. Please clarify whether this facility is: (1) routine transformer pad vault access (not niche equipment), or (2) niche equipment requiring full UCM § 1.10.4 compliance with supporting detail drawings.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 for niche equipment designation. Vision analysis identified: '"Vault Easement": Found on the lower left side, adjacent to Building 8 and encompassing an "Electrical Transformer Pad".** The plan does not appear to show designated, proposed internal electric easements...it only shows the lines themselves.' The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows this same 'Vault Easement' as a dashed rectangle near Building 8. Facts.md confirms the project site is in Zone X (outside floodplain) and the address is 3759 Valley View Road, South Lamar area. The Downtown Network Area is generally defined as the downtown core and close-in neighborhoods; South Lamar is typically outside this boundary. However, the term 'Vault Easement' and its location 'adjacent to Building 8 and encompassing an Electrical Transformer Pad' requires clarification. A 'vault' could indicate either: (1) a standard transformer access vault (which is merely an enclosure, not niche equipment), or (2) actual niche equipment as defined by UCM § 1.10.4 (an underground chamber accessible only from outside the building, with 35-foot minimum vertical clearance, 3-hour fire walls). The plans do not explicitly call it 'niche equipment' or reference UCM § 1.10.4 requirements.
findings.reasoning: EL-6.14 applicability states: 'Only where niche equipment is present or proposed.' A 'Vault Easement' shown on the plans adjacent to Building 8 could represent either: (1) routine transformer pad vault access (not niche equipment), or (2) actual niche equipment as defined in UCM § 1.10.4 (underground equipment accessible from outside only, with specific fire-rating and clearance requirements). The plans do NOT explicitly designate this as 'niche equipment' or provide the detailed drawings (entrance configuration, interior clearances, fire-rating, accessibility) required by UCM § 1.10.4. Without such designation and details, compliance with niche-specific requirements cannot be verified, and it is unclear whether this item applies.

findings.comment: Metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes not provided for new electric easement dedications required for interior electrical routing and transformer pad locations. Applicant must submit surveyor-executed field notes and metes and bounds descriptions for all proposed electric easement areas to Austin Energy for review and approval prior to recordation.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed underground electrical lines routing extensively through the interior of the site, with four transformer pads located outside the historic 5-foot perimeter electric easements shown on the 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat. The electrical system design requires new utility easement areas to cover interior line routing and transformer pad footprints. However, no easement exhibits, surveyor-sealed field notes, metes and bounds descriptions, or separate instrument dedication documents are evident in the site plan set or supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report references Austin Energy review completed, but no coordination correspondence regarding easement dedications is included in the submittal. Facts.md notes (line 10) state 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' indicating unresolved easement status. The existing 5-foot electric easements from the 1975 plat are insufficient for this project's proposed interior electrical infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: The project is filing a site plan (SP-2025-0126C) without a concurrent new subdivision plat, making EL-7.1 (plat dedication) inapplicable. Therefore, any new easements must be dedicated by separate instrument per Code § 14-1-21. The visual analysis of Sheet 21 confirms that proposed electrical facilities extend well beyond the historic 5-foot perimeter easements and require additional easement areas. Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) and UCM § 1.16.0(3) mandate that metes and bounds descriptions with field notes signed, dated, and sealed by a surveyor must be provided to Austin Energy for review. The absence of these documents constitutes a failure to meet the separate instrument dedication requirement. The fact that easements are merely noted as 'may be required at a later date' indicates the applicant has not yet submitted the required surveyor-sealed documentation.

findings.comment: Title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey with certification showing all easement encumbrances not submitted to Austin Energy for review. Applicant must obtain and submit to Austin Energy a formal title document (title commitment, title policy, ALTA/ACSM survey, or Ownership/Encumbrance Report) certified to show all existing easements and encumbrances affecting the property.
applicableAreas: All proposed and modified electric easement areas
findings.observation: No title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey certified to show all existing easement encumbrances is evident in the supplementary documents reviewed. The facts.md document identifies six existing easements of record (greenbelt access, drainage, wastewater, drainage, public utility, drainage) but does not indicate submission of a title document showing all encumbrances. The Project Review Form and Consolidated Site Plan Application do not reference submission of title documents to Austin Energy. Requirements per Land Development Engineering Review note that 'Current and proposed easements should be shown on all site plan sheets,' but no title commitment or ALTA survey is documented as submitted for Austin Energy review per UCM § 1.16.0(1).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) explicitly requires submission of 'a title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey' showing all easement encumbrances to Austin Energy for review to verify adequacy of existing easements and identify conflicts. This documentation is mandatory for projects with proposed or modified electric easements. The absence of this title document from the submittal package represents non-compliance with a foundational requirement for easement coordination. While facts.md documents existing easements, that internal research document does not substitute for the formal title document that must be submitted to and reviewed by Austin Energy.

findings.comment: Electric easements not shown on site plan sheets for all interior Austin Energy facilities. Electric easements for the underground lines routing through the site interior and for all transformer pad locations must be clearly depicted on Sheet 21 (and other applicable sheets) with dimensions and boundaries.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies easement boundaries on the perimeter (5' P.U.E. on north, 15' Drainage and Wastewater easements on east), but does not depict the extent or boundaries of the electric easement areas needed for the interior electrical infrastructure. The proposed electrical lines routing through the interior of the site between buildings and along driveways are shown, but the easement boundaries required for these interior lines and for the four transformer pad locations are not clearly delineated on the sheet. The design shows electric lines in the interior but fails to show corresponding easement areas. UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that easements be shown on site plan sheets for all Austin Energy facilities.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) mandates that electric easements must be depicted on site plan sheets for all Austin Energy facilities. Sheet 21 is the electrical design sheet and is the appropriate location to show these easements. While the perimeter easements are labeled, the interior routing of electrical infrastructure is not accompanied by corresponding easement delineations. The absence of easement boundaries for the interior electrical system leaves the extent and location of easement rights unclear. A complete site plan requires that all easement areas be clearly shown and labeled, allowing stakeholders and inspectors to understand the spatial scope of Austin Energy's rights and access requirements.

findings.comment: Moonlight tower proximity cannot be verified from submitted site plan documents. Requires verification using City of Austin geospatial moonlight tower location database to determine if a tower exists within 100 feet of the limits of construction.
applicableAreas: 100-foot radius around any existing moonlight tower or guy wires
findings.observation: The site plan documents, including the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) and all other sheets reviewed, do not identify or call out the location of any existing moonlight towers or associated guy wires on or within 100 feet of the property. The grouping instructions for this item explicitly note that moonlight tower locations 'requires geospatial data on moonlight tower locations not available from plans alone.' No geospatial analysis or moonlight tower proximity study is attached to or referenced in the site plan documents. The limits of construction are shown on the site plan, but without moonlight tower location data, the applicability of this requirement cannot be verified from the submitted site plan documents alone.
findings.reasoning: Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201 requires a moonlight tower construction permit when construction activities occur within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or associated guy wires. The requirement to include a plan note regarding removal and storage of moonlight towers during construction (EL-7.18) is triggered only when such a tower exists within 100 feet of the limits of construction. The submitted site plan documents do not contain sufficient information to determine whether a moonlight tower exists within the 100-foot proximity threshold. The City of Austin maintains geospatial data on moonlight tower locations that is not included in the site plan document set. This determination cannot be made from the plans alone and requires human verification using the City's moonlight tower inventory database.

findings.comment: Provide underground electric duct bank specifications and locations on Sheet 21 and obtain AE Design approval per UCM § 1.4.2. Include duct bank materials, sizing, installation details, and protection requirements.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing with blue lines indicating 'Underground Electric Line.' No specific duct bank specifications, materials, sizes, or design details are shown. No documentation found indicating duct bank design was discussed or approved by AE Design. The design is preliminary and unapproved.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Underground electric duct bank locations and design not meeting AE requirements or not approved.' While routing is shown on Sheet 21, no duct bank design specifications are provided, and no AE Design approval was found. Once AE Design approval is obtained, duct bank specifications must be verified to meet AE requirements.

findings.comment: Provide detailed specifications and locations for all electric service pull boxes and any required vaults per AE Design requirements. Include design details and obtain AE Design approval per UCM § 1.4.2.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing but does not specifically show electric service manholes or pull boxes with specifications. Vision analysis noted 'Electrical Pull Box' callouts on the drawing, but no detailed specifications, locations, or design documentation provided. No AE Design approval of manhole specifications located.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Electric service manhole locations and design not meeting AE requirements or not approved.' While pull boxes are referenced on Sheet 21, no specifications or AE Design approval documentation was found. Once AE approval is obtained, manhole/pull box design must be verified against AE requirements.

findings.comment: Provide detailed underground electric routing specifications including cable types, conduit requirements, depths, clearances from other utilities, and road crossings. Obtain AE Design approval of routing per UCM § 1.4.2.
applicableAreas: Underground electric routing shown on Sheet 21
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing with blue lines and callouts 'Underground Electric Line' connecting from the property boundary inward to transformer pads and service points. However, no detailed routing specifications, cable types, depths, clearances from other utilities, or design requirements are shown. No AE Design approval of routing was found. Design is preliminary.
findings.reasoning: This item requires verification that 'Underground electric cabling routing not meeting AE design requirements or not approved.' Sheet 21 shows general routing paths, but without detailed design specifications and AE approval, cannot confirm routing meets AE requirements for clearances, cable types, depths, and other specifications per UCM § 1.4.2.

findings.comment: Provide detailed transformer pad location and clearance drawings showing all dimensions, setbacks from buildings, property lines, utilities, and landscaping per UCM § 1.10.4 standards. If any clearance reductions are proposed, provide written approval from AE Design per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads but provides no clearance dimensions or specifications. Vision analysis indicated pads are positioned: (1) west of Bldg. 1, (2) west of Bldg. 8, (3) east of Bldg. 5, and (4) east of Bldg. 6. No measurements or setback distances shown. No documentation found indicating clearance reductions were discussed with or approved by AE Design. Standard AE requirements are 10-15 feet hot-stick area, 5 feet sides with operators, 3 feet other sides.
findings.reasoning: This item requires verification that non-standard clearances (if applicable) have written AE Design approval per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2. Without clearance dimensions shown on the plans and no AE approval of any non-standard configurations, cannot verify compliance. Need detailed transformer pad location drawings showing all clearances and dimensions relative to buildings, property lines, utilities, and landscaping.

findings.comment: Clearly identify and mark all existing Austin Energy underground infrastructure and duct banks on Sheet 21 and other relevant utility plans per UCM § 1.16.0. Include existing service locations and connection points.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows service entry from the west (Valley View Road right-of-way) with blue 'Underground Electric Line' entering the property, suggesting connection to existing AE infrastructure in/near the right-of-way. However, the plans do not clearly label or delineate existing AE duct banks, underground infrastructure, or service locations. Sheet 9 and Sheet 21 show some existing utilities but existing AE underground infrastructure is not clearly identified and marked.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Existing AE underground infrastructure and duct banks not clearly shown on plans' per UCM § 1.16.0. While Sheet 21 shows the service routing entry point, existing AE infrastructure upstream (in Valley View Road and adjacent right-of-way) is not clearly delineated. Need to verify whether existing AE underground facilities and duct banks in the area are clearly marked on the plans.

findings.comment: Add required callout to demolition/site plan notes: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' per UCM § 1.16.0.
findings.observation: Sheet 8 is titled 'Tree Removal & Demolition Plan.' The existing facility (demolished June 2022) had electric service that required removal. However, the current site plan sheets do not contain the required callout: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' per UCM § 1.16.0. While prior demolition is complete, any future excavation or construction activities affecting underground utilities must include this coordination note.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires a specific callout on demolition/relocation plans when existing AE facilities require removal or relocation. This callout must be clearly stated on the site plan. Although prior demolition occurred, the current site plan should document that this coordination was/is required. The callout is not present on the reviewed sheets.

findings.comment: Verify that proposed underground electric routing and all construction activities maintain required clearances from existing Austin Energy transmission structures and easement areas per UCM § 1.10.0. Provide documentation of clearance discussion with AE (contact Andrew Perez 512-505-7153 as noted on the plans).
applicableAreas: Entire site - proximity to existing AE transmission easement
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 20) lists 16 Austin Energy transmission easement requirements with strict clearances and access rules. Block 20 states: 'Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of transmission structures' (items 2, 15); 'Call Andrew Perez at 512-505-7153 to schedule a meeting' (item 2). Transmission poles/structures exist on or near the property based on these detailed requirements. The proposed electric service routing on Sheet 21 must avoid conflicts with transmission easement areas. No documentation found indicating clearance conflicts were discussed and resolved with AE Design prior to site plan approval.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Clearance conflicts with existing electric facilities not discussed and resolved with AE Design group prior to site plan approval' per UCM § 1.10.0. The site has existing AE transmission easement areas that require 25-foot clearances and specific access requirements. The new underground routing on Sheet 21 must be verified to avoid conflicts. Without evidence of AE coordination on clearances and transmission easement compatibility, this cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Provide documentation that Austin Energy removed the existing electric meter and service drop from the demolished facility before demolition. If not yet removed, submit work request to AE and document the removal per UCM § 1.10.13.
applicableAreas: Demolition of existing facility with electric service
findings.observation: Project involves demolition (facility demolished June 2022 per facts.md). Existing facility was an assisted living center that required electric service, meter, and service drop. No documentation found on current site plan or in supplementary documents confirming: (1) Austin Energy removed the electric meter and service drop before/during demolition, (2) whether site plan sheets include coordination notes for AE removal, or (3) evidence that work request was submitted to AE for removal. Sheet 8 (Demolition Plan) does not clearly document this coordination.
