findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.13 requires that 'Existing electric service, meter, and service drop not coordinated with AE for removal before demolition may proceed.' The regulation requires: (1) written verification that utilities are suitable/sufficient (if continuing), and (2) after demolition approval but before demolition, contact AE to arrange removal. While demolition is already complete (June 2022), the current site plan submittal should document that this coordination occurred. The absence of clear documentation is a deficiency.

findings.comment: Verify that storm drain routing on Sheet 12 does not conflict with underground electric routing and street light conduit on Sheet 21. If conflicts exist, provide documentation of AE Design coordination and approved resolution per UCM § 1.13.0.
findings.observation: Sheet 12 shows storm sewer plan; Sheet 21 shows electric design with underground routing. Both sheets would need to be examined together to identify potential conflicts between storm drain routing and electric conduit/transmission. Sheet 3 mentions street lighting and transmission easement requirements but no specific documentation found addressing storm drain vs. street light conduit conflicts.
findings.reasoning: This item requires verification that 'Proposed storm drain or utility conflicts with existing street light conduit not discussed with AE Design for resolution' per UCM § 1.13.0. This requires examining both the storm sewer and electric/lighting plans together. Without detailed visual analysis of both sheets and evidence of coordination, cannot confirm resolution of potential conflicts.

findings.comment: If this project is determined by Austin Energy to be a unified development, provide documentation that provisions are included for future separate electric service to individual properties in the event that unified development status is terminated per UCM § 1.3.8.
findings.observation: Project is a 39-unit multi-family townhome development under single ownership (WM 41 Austin RE LLC per facts.md and cover sheet). The grouping guidance for unified development states: 'This status cannot be determined from plans alone—requires Austin Energy determination based on ownership, development pattern, and operational characteristics.' No Austin Energy determination letter confirming unified development status was located. The issue of whether future cessation of unified status has been addressed with provisions for individual property service drops is not documented.
findings.reasoning: This item applies 'Only for unified developments (common ownership, integrated operation per AE interpretation).' While the project appears to be single-ownership multi-family development, AE must formally determine if this qualifies as a 'unified development' per their interpretation. If so, provisions for future separate service to individual properties in event of unified development dissolution must be in place. Without AE determination and provisions documentation, this item cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Point-of-service location not provided with ESPA form. Include point-of-service location in the completed ESPA submitted to Austin Energy.
findings.observation: No ESPA form located in submittal. Without the form, the point-of-service location cannot be verified. Sheet 21 shows electrical design with transformer locations and routing, but these appear to be preliminary applicant design rather than responsive to AE-determined service location. No documentation exists confirming AE Design has determined and approved the point-of-service location.
findings.reasoning: Point-of-service location is a critical AE Design determination that must be documented in the ESPA submission. The applicant cannot self-determine service location. Its absence from the ESPA (which is missing) prevents verification that AE has made this determination.

findings.comment: Projected electrical load not provided with ESPA form. Include electrical demand calculations and load projections in the ESPA submitted to Austin Energy, incorporating anticipated residential electrical demand for 39 units.
findings.observation: No load calculations or electrical demand projections found in supplementary documents or site plan. Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design layout with transformer and service configuration, but no supporting load analysis or demand calculation. No documentation submitted to AE Design specifying the projected electrical load for the 39-unit development.
findings.reasoning: Projected electrical load is a mandatory requirement in the ESPA submission per UCM § 1.4.2.6. This load determines transformer sizing, service capacity requirements, and eligibility for Service-Only vs. infrastructure construction designation. Absence of this calculation prevents AE Design from making proper service determinations.

findings.comment: Estimated service date not provided with ESPA form. Include estimated service date (month/year or season) in the ESPA submitted to Austin Energy.
findings.observation: No ESPA form located containing estimated service date. Cannot verify whether applicant provided month/year or season estimate for service availability/readiness.
findings.reasoning: The estimated service date is a required field in the ESPA submission per UCM § 1.4.2.6. This timeline helps Austin Energy coordinate construction staging and service activation.

findings.comment: Separate ESPA not submitted for each building in the 8-building project with building number included. Submit individual ESPA forms for each of the 8 buildings (Buildings 1 through 8) with building numbers clearly identified.
findings.observation: Site plan clearly shows 8 separate buildings (Buildings 1-8) on Sheet 9, containing a total of 39 townhome units. The Building Data Table identifies each building individually (4-plexes, 5-plexes, 6-plexes). However, no separate ESPA form submitted for each building. The absence of multiple ESPA submissions (one per building) prevents verification that AE Design has reviewed individual service requirements for each structure.
findings.reasoning: For multi-building projects, UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires a separate ESPA with building number included for each building to allow AE Design to evaluate individual transformer/service needs. One project-wide ESPA does not satisfy this requirement when multiple buildings with independent service needs exist.

findings.comment: Separate ESPA not submitted for each unit in the 39-unit multi-unit project with unit number included. Submit individual ESPA forms for each of the 39 units with unit numbers clearly identified.
findings.observation: Site plan Building Data Table (Sheet 9) shows 39 individual units distributed across 8 buildings. Individual unit addresses/identifiers are noted on Sheet 29 (Addressing Plan). However, no separate ESPA submitted for units. The applicant has submitted a single project-level approach rather than unit-level ESPA submissions for this multi-unit residential project.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, multi-unit projects require separate ESPA submissions for each unit with unit number included. This allows individual service coordination for each residential unit. The absence of unit-level ESPAs prevents verification that AE Design has reviewed individual unit service characteristics.

findings.comment: Full-scale copy of entire site plan submission to Austin Energy not verified. Provide documentation or correspondence confirming that a complete, full-scale copy of all 39 site plan sheets was submitted to Austin Energy Design for their review.
findings.observation: A Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) is part of the submitted site plan. However, no documentation confirms that a full-scale copy of the entire 39-sheet site plan was specifically provided to Austin Energy for their review and approval as required by UCM § 1.16.0. The Master Comment Report references AE site comments in an external Bluebeam link, but submission of a full-scale site plan copy to AE is not explicitly documented.
findings.reasoning: Applicants must provide a full-scale copy of the entire site plan to AE Design as part of the standard submission requirements. While the site plan exists and AE has reviewed it (per the Master Comment Report), the specific action of providing AE with a full-scale site plan copy is not documented in the submitted records. The external Bluebeam link suggests AE has reviewed the plans, but does not confirm that a full-scale copy meeting specification requirements was provided.

findings.comment: Total Gross Floor Area (GFA) not prominently displayed on site plan for Austin Energy system grid load monitoring. Add total project GFA (83,986 sq ft) to the site plan cover sheet or main site plan sheet in a prominent location visible to AE reviewers.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) provides a detailed Site Data Table (Block 16) that includes site area (94,192 sf / 2.162 acres), gross floor area by building type, building coverage, and impervious cover percentages. However, the total Gross Floor Area for the entire project is not explicitly stated as a single summary value on the site plan sheets or in the general notes. The Site Data Table on Sheet 9 shows individual building GFA values, and the guide indicates a total of 83,986 sf, but this is not clearly labeled as 'Total GFA' on the plan itself in a prominent location for AE system grid load monitoring purposes.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that total Gross Floor Area (GFA) in square feet be provided on the site plan for AE system grid load monitoring. This is a standard requirement for AE to assess system capacity and loading. While GFA data exists in the project documentation (83,986 sf total), if it is not prominently displayed on the site plan sheets themselves (as opposed to supplementary documents), this represents a documentation deficiency on the plans. AE reviewers expect to see total GFA clearly labeled on site plan cover sheets or plan sheets for easy reference.

findings.comment: Austin Energy approved detail for overhead to underground conversion not provided. If converting existing overhead electric service to underground, provide the Austin Energy approved conversion detail showing meter pedestal, service entry, and all related specifications.
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electrical routing and equipment placement, which may indicate conversion from overhead to underground service. However, no Austin Energy approved detail showing the specific design of overhead to underground conversion was located in the supplementary documents or site plan sheets. If conversion from overhead to underground is proposed, the specific conversion detail must be provided.
findings.reasoning: When converting existing overhead electric service to underground, an Austin Energy approved detail for the conversion must be provided per UCM § 1.3.13. This is an excess facilities item that requires AE design and approval. The detail specifies how the existing overhead service will be terminated and converted to underground service, including meter pedestal design, service entry, and related specifications. The absence of this specific detail, if overhead-to-underground conversion is part of the project scope, represents a deficiency.

findings.comment: Austin Energy approval for underground electric service trenching under detention pond not verified. Confirm the route of underground electric service trenching relative to the biofiltration-detention pond. If the trenching passes under the pond, provide approval from Austin Energy Design for this routing.
applicableAreas: drainage pond and electrical utility areas
findings.observation: The site plan includes a biofiltration-detention pond in the northeast corner of the site (Sheets 15, 16) and electrical routing shown on Sheet 21. Review of the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) blocks and guide does not clearly indicate whether electric service trenching crosses under the detention pond or whether such routing passes under retention features. If underground electric service trenching is routed to pass under the detention pond, Austin Energy approval would be required.
findings.reasoning: When electric service trenching is routed to pass under detention ponds, approval from Austin Energy Design must be obtained per UCM § 1.10.7. This is because utility routing under storage features requires specific design considerations and AE coordination. Without clear documentation of the underground service routing relative to the pond location, or without evidence of AE approval if such routing exists, this requirement cannot be verified as met.

findings.comment: Switchgear applicability to this project not verified. Provide load calculations confirming whether switchgear is required. If switchgear is needed, provide evidence of coordination with Austin Energy Design lead.
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformers and electrical equipment routing but does not specifically indicate whether switchgear is required or shown on the plans. No load calculations or correspondence indicating switchgear requirement was found in the documentation. Switchgear is typically required only for very high loads (generally >1000 kVA or complex multi-service installations), which may not apply to this 39-unit residential development.
findings.reasoning: Switchgear installation requires coordination with Austin Energy design lead only when high electrical loads require switchgear per UCM § 1.16.0(6). For a 39-unit townhome project, switchgear is likely not required (typical residential loads are served by standard service transformers and panels). However, without load calculations showing the total project demand, the applicability of this requirement cannot be definitively determined. If load calculations show switchgear is not needed, this item would be n/a.

findings.comment: Pad-mounted transformer coordination with Austin Energy Design lead not verified. Provide documentation or correspondence confirming that transformer locations and specifications have been coordinated with and approved by Austin Energy Design lead.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations on site plan
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pads located on the site plan (transformer symbols and locations are indicated). However, no documentation or correspondence confirming that pad-mounted transformer installation has been coordinated with Austin Energy Design lead was located. The block content for Sheet 21 does not mention transformer coordination or approval.
findings.reasoning: When new buildings increase load and require pad-mounted transformers, the installation must be coordinated with Austin Energy Design lead per UCM § 1.16.0(6). This is required to ensure proper siting, sizing, and connection to AE infrastructure. The presence of transformers on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan suggests they are part of the project design, but coordination with AE Design (beyond the general completeness check) is not documented. Evidence of this specific coordination should be provided.

findings.comment: Developer financial responsibility for electric facility relocation or removal not documented. If existing Austin Energy facilities must be relocated or removed for the development, provide cost responsibility acknowledgment per UCM § 1.3.13 and documentation from Austin Energy indicating relocation scope and costs.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission easement requirements and notes that existing electric transmission facilities are on or near the property. However, no documentation confirms whether existing AE facilities must be relocated or removed as part of the development. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed new infrastructure routing but does not document conflicts with existing AE facilities or required relocations. No cost responsibility acknowledgment for facility relocation was located.
findings.reasoning: When existing AE facilities must be relocated or removed, developer financial responsibility must be acknowledged prior to site plan approval per UCM § 1.3.13 (Excess Facilities/Excess Cost Policy). Without documentation of existing facility conflicts, relocation requirements, or cost responsibility, the applicability of this item cannot be fully determined. If facility relocation is required, the acknowledgment document is missing.

findings.comment: No correspondence from Austin Energy identifying required system upgrades found. If Austin Energy has determined that electric system upgrades are required for this development, provide documentation and acknowledge developer financial responsibility for these costs per UCM § 1.3.13.
findings.observation: No documentation from Austin Energy indicating that system upgrades are required due to area grid overload, capacity limitations, or infrastructure improvements was located in the submitted documents. The facts.md and project documents do not reference any correspondence about substation capacity concerns or required system improvements. Austin Energy's completeness check is marked complete, but no specific indication of required system upgrades was noted.
findings.reasoning: When AE indicates that system upgrades (beyond standard line extension) are required due to grid overload or capacity limitations, developer financial responsibility must be acknowledged prior to site plan approval per UCM § 1.3.13. This typically comes from Austin Energy as a formal determination during the ESPA or service request process. Without such correspondence from AE, it cannot be determined if upgrades are required or if developer financial responsibility acknowledgment is needed.

findings.comment: Pre-construction notification arrangement with Austin Energy for work near high-voltage lines to be documented prior to construction. Ensure that before any construction or grading activity begins within 10 feet of overhead transmission lines, Austin Energy is notified at least 48 hours in advance per Texas Health & Safety Code § 752.003 and arrangements are made to de-energize or relocate lines.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission facilities on the property and includes note 2 requiring pre-construction safety meeting 48 hours before construction commences, and note 3 referencing Texas OSHA 20-foot clearance requirements. However, no formal documentation from the grading plan (Sheet 11) or supplementary documents confirming that Austin Energy was notified at least 48 hours prior to work near high-voltage lines and that satisfactory arrangements were made to de-energize, move, or relocate lines was found. The general notes include transmission requirements but do not include specific notification documentation.
findings.reasoning: Texas Health & Safety Code § 752.003 and UCM § 1.10.2(B) require documentation that Austin Energy was notified at least 48 hours prior to work near high-voltage lines and that satisfactory arrangements were made for de-energization or relocation. This is an ongoing requirement during construction, not a pre-approval item. The notes on Sheet 3 show the requirement is acknowledged, but actual notification and arrangement documentation would come later during construction. At the site plan review stage, this may not be fully verifiable, but the general acknowledgment of the requirement on the plans is appropriate.

findings.comment: Multiple points of service or multiple voltages not verified. Confirm whether the project requires one or multiple points of service and one or multiple service voltages. If multiple points of service or voltages are proposed, provide AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval letter for the exception to the one-point-of-service rule.
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformers and equipment on the plan. From the available documentation, it appears there may be multiple transformer locations shown, but the specific number of service points (service drops from transformers) and whether multiple voltage levels are proposed cannot be definitively determined from the blocks.md review. No documentation of AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval for multiple points of service or multiple voltages was located.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 establishes a default rule of one point of service at one service voltage to a single building on a single lot. Exceptions require AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval. If the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows multiple points of service (multiple service drops to different buildings or multiple voltage levels), documentation of the exception approval is required. Without clarity on whether multiple service points are proposed, or without approval documentation if they are, this requirement cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Existing overhead electric facilities are partially shown but not completely. Please add detailed callouts to identify all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, transmission voltage designations, and poles with cross-arm details and heights to all sheets showing existing overhead facilities.
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 4, 9, 21 for existing overhead facilities. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing overhead electric lines (OHE) and power poles along the perimeter, and there is a transformer on pad shown outside the property near Valley View Road. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows existing OHE lines on site edges with dashed line notation. However, the vision analysis of Sheet 21 reveals these are labeled as 'OHE' but specifics are limited: no callouts identify all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, or transmission lines explicitly. Guy wires are noted on Sheet 4 legend but unclear if shown for existing poles on this specific site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires all existing electric facilities to be shown, including 'poles, all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, transmission lines, towers.' While existing overhead lines are depicted on Sheets 4 and 21, the plans do not provide explicit callouts or labels identifying: (1) all three phase conductors, (2) neutral conductor specifically, (3) transmission line voltage designation, or (4) detailed pole heights and cross-arm dimensions. The vision analysis found OHE lines but noted no detailed pole cross-sections or conductor specifications. This falls short of the 'completely shown' requirement in the deficiency title.

findings.comment: Section views showing existing electrical pole heights, all conductor elevations, and required clearance envelopes (minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance) are not provided. Please provide detailed electrical profile/section views showing all existing overhead facilities with heights and clearance demonstrations.
applicableAreas: All elevation/profile views with existing overhead facilities in proximity
findings.observation: Examined available section and elevation sheets. Sheet 21 references 'See Sheet 19 for Profile' but vision analysis of Sheet 19 found NO profile views present—only plan view with notes. No dedicated section views showing heights, conductor spacing, or clearance envelopes were located on Sheet 19. No profile sheets explicitly showing existing electrical pole heights and all conductors were found in the available plan set. While Sheet 3 contains transmission clearance notes, no graphical cross-sections or elevation views demonstrating pole heights and clearance envelopes are present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires section views to show 'height of existing electrical poles and all conductors with clearance envelopes.' Although section views exist in the plan set (e.g., storm sewer profiles on other sheets), the electrical profile information referenced on Sheet 21 is not provided. The absence of dedicated electrical section views with pole heights, conductor elevations, and clearance envelopes (typically 7.5 feet horizontal minimum clearance per UCM § 1.10.3) means the clearance compliance cannot be verified graphically.

findings.comment: Proposed conduit routing is not shown in profile/section view. Sheet 21 references Sheet 19 for profiles, but Sheet 19 contains no electrical profiles. Please provide detailed utility profile sections showing proposed electric conduit routing with: (1) depth of burial, (2) clearance from other utilities, (3) clearance from existing structures, and (4) elevation coordination with site grading.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 contains notation 'See Sheet 19 for Profile' directing readers to utility profile information. However, vision analysis of Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) revealed NO profile/section views of any utilities—only plan view drawing with tables. Sheet 19 shows water, wastewater, and storm drain linework and callouts but no vertical cross-sections or profiles. Examination of other sheets (Storm Sewer Plan, Biofiltration Pond Profiles) found drainage and pond profiles but no electric utility profiles.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires proposed conduit routing to be shown in profile view. The reference on Sheet 21 to Sheet 19 for profile information appears to be a cross-sheet coordination error—Sheet 19 lacks any electrical profiles. Conduit depth of burial, clearance from other utilities, and elevation coordination cannot be verified without profile views showing the underground electric routing in cross-section.

findings.comment: Existing electric easements are not shown on all required plan sheets. Please add electric easement depictions (with recording information and dimensions) to: (1) Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan); (2) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan); (3) verify depiction on all other applicable sheets (site, grading, irrigation, storm drain, wet utility sheets).
applicableAreas: All plan sheets: site, utility, landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, wet utility
findings.observation: Examined all required plan sheets for electric easement depiction. Sheet 21 shows 5' electric easements with recording info on southern boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows electric easements with citations on eastern and southern boundaries. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows electric easements on eastern and southern boundaries. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has legend entry for electric in legend but vision found NO easements drawn on the plan itself. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show electric easements—only shows utilities W, SD, and OHE line. Per facts.md, there are TWO 5' electric easements from Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol 73, Pg 76) plus additional easements from Cortez Heights plat (Vol 64, Pg 13).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires existing electric easements to be shown 'on all required plan sheets' (site, utility, landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, wet utility). Current status: Easements shown on Sheets 9, 11, 21 but MISSING on Sheet 19 and Sheet 31. The incomplete depiction across all sheets means coordination cannot be verified—particularly Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) where trees must not conflict with easement access and maintenance. The omission from Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) creates inconsistency in the utility coordination across sheets.

findings.comment: Equipment symbols are inconsistent across plan sheets. Please establish a consistent legend for all electrical equipment (transformer pads, meters, pull boxes, disconnects) and apply identical symbols and labels on all plan sheets. Include the legend on each sheet showing electric facilities.
findings.observation: Examined equipment symbols across sheets. Sheet 21 uses: large blue rectangles with zig-zag symbols for transformers labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad'; small blue circles with 'E' for pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box'; rectangles on building walls for meters labeled 'Electrical Meters.' Sheet 9 shows one 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' but the symbol and style may differ. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey legend) defines 'TRANSFORMER ON PAD' with a square 'T' symbol. The symbols are not consistent across sheets in terms of graphical representation and labeling style.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Equipment symbols consistent across plan sheets.' This is essential for plan reviewers and contractors to identify equipment reliably across all sheets. Inconsistent symbols create confusion and increase risk of misidentification (e.g., meter vs. disconnect, transformer vs. telecom box). All equipment of the same type must use identical symbols and labels across all sheets.

findings.comment: Electric facility locations do not consistently match across plan sheets. Please verify and ensure: (1) all transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 are also shown on Sheets 9, 11, 19, 31 at identical locations; (2) all meters shown on Sheet 21 are also shown on Sheets 9, 31 (landscape elevation); (3) pull boxes and conduit routing shown on Sheet 21 are shown on Sheets 9, 11, 19; (4) use consistent coordinate/dimension references to verify locations match across sheets.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations, meter locations, pull box locations
findings.observation: Compared facility locations across sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads at specific locations (NW, SW, central-south, central-east). Sheet 9 shows one transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the western side, which may correspond to one of the four on Sheet 21 but location does not clearly match. Sheet 31 (Landscape) shows OHE but NO transformer pads, meaning the transformers shown in detail on Sheet 21 are not depicted on the landscape plan. This prevents landscaping coordination with transformer locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Electric facility locations do not match across plan sheets' to be avoided. When the same facility (e.g., a transformer pad) is shown on multiple sheets, it must be in the same location relative to buildings, property lines, and other features. Discrepancies or omissions across sheets create confusion about the actual design and prevent verification of proper coordination (e.g., are trees within transformer access zones? is landscaping in staging areas?).

findings.comment: Landscape plans do not demonstrate that landscaping avoids required staging areas adjacent to transformer locations. Please: (1) show all transformer pad locations and their 20' × 35' staging areas (with 35' vertical clearance) on the landscape plan; (2) add note stating no landscaping (trees, shrubs, hardscape) is permitted within these clear zones; (3) provide detail showing how existing landscaping plan respects transformer access requirements.
applicableAreas: Areas adjacent to transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads at specific locations. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show these transformer pads. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Because the electric transformers and their associated required clearance/staging zones are not drawn on this sheet, it is impossible to determine from this document alone if landscaping elements conflict with those specific staging areas.' Cannot verify whether landscaping (trees, shrubs, hardscape, irrigation) is placed within the required 20' × 35' clear zone with 35' vertical clearance in front of transformer access doors.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 specifies that pad-mounted transformers require 'Minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal clear zone with 35 feet vertical clearance in front of pad-mounted transformers, vaults, and other AE equipment requiring crane/bucket truck access for installation and maintenance.' The landscape plan must show these clearance zones and must not include landscaping within them. Since Sheet 31 does not show the transformer pads, coordination cannot be verified. Without explicit depiction of staging areas and exclusion of landscaping, compliance cannot be determined.

findings.comment: Meter location compliance with prohibited locations and flood elevation requirements is not demonstrated. Please provide: (1) architectural elevations showing meter locations relative to building porch/stairway/overhang obstructions; (2) 3-foot separation verification from gas meters (show gas meter locations if present); (3) elevation certificates or grading plan showing meters are minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood level (or FEMA determination if in floodplain); (4) notes confirming meters are readily accessible and on first floor/ground level within sight of transformer.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows meters attached to building walls but does not provide documentation regarding: (1) flood elevation verification (meters must be minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood level per UCM § 1.9.3.1), (2) clearance to gas meters (3-foot minimum per UCM § 1.9.3.1(C)(3)), (3) clearance to porches/stairways/overhangs >72 inches, (4) meter accessibility and location on first floor/ground level. Sheet 9 does not show meters at all. Facts.md indicates site is in FEMA Zone X (outside 100-year floodplain), but architectural elevations showing meter locations relative to buildings are not provided in the available documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 specifies meter location requirements: (1) outdoors, readily accessible, on first floor/ground level, within sight of transformer; (2) not on/under porches or stairways; (3) not under overhangs >72 inches; (4) minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood elevation; (5) minimum 3-foot separation from gas meters/regulators/relief valves. The plans show meters but do not verify compliance with these location restrictions. Without architectural elevations or detailed meter location callouts showing compliance, UCM § 1.9.3.1 compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Cannot verify from available evidence whether required clearance zones from overhead electric facilities extend across property lines. This determination depends on the clearance verification exhibits referenced in deficiency EL-11.1. Please provide clearance verification exhibits that clearly show whether required clearance envelopes extend beyond the subject property boundary.
applicableAreas: Property boundaries where clearance zones extend across lines
findings.observation: Sheets 9 and 21 show property lines and existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along the southern property boundary near Valley View Road. The sheets show that the existing overhead line is located outside the subject property (on the street side). However, without clearance verification exhibits (as noted in deficiency EL-11.1), it is impossible to determine whether required clearance zones extend across the property line boundary. No clearance radius is drawn or calculated on the available sheets. The applicability of this item depends on whether clearances extend beyond property boundaries, which cannot be verified from the submitted evidence.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 specifies dual clearance zones (7'-6" horizontal and 15-foot radius) that may extend across property boundaries if structures are sufficiently close to the property line. However, without the clearance verification exhibits that should be provided in response to EL-11.1, this specific requirement cannot be evaluated. The determination of whether clearance lines should extend across property boundaries is dependent on the clearance exhibit analysis, which has not been provided.

findings.comment: Existing electric facilities to be removed or relocated are not clearly labeled on demolition plan, or the status of existing electric infrastructure from the prior use is unclear. Please clarify on the demolition plan whether any existing electric poles, lines, or transformers from the prior facility remain on site and if so, clearly label them with removal or relocation status.
applicableAreas: Demolition plan for areas with existing utilities
findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) guide.md mentions that Block 2 contains 'Notes instructing coordination with the City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.' However, in the detailed block content provided (Block 9 - Site Demolition Notes), the notes listed (items 1-10) do not include any specific instruction about removing or relocating electric facilities. The demolition notes address tree protection, private utility abandonment, materials removal, and gas/water meter removal, but no electric facility removal is explicitly noted. Block 2 description references power pole and line removal notes, but these are not clearly visible in the transcribed demolition notes content.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires that 'Existing electric facilities to be removed or relocated [be] clearly labeled on demolition plan'. The grouping guidance states this applies 'Only when existing electric facilities are being removed or relocated.' From facts.md and sheet reviews, the existing site was previously an assisted living facility that was demolished in 2022 (Building Permit 2022-096813 BP - Final). It is unclear from the current plans whether any existing electric infrastructure (poles, lines, transformers) from the prior structure require removal or relocation as part of the current townhome development. If they do, they must be clearly labeled on the demolition plan.

findings.comment: Electric notes are duplicated on the same sheet. Please remove the duplicate electric notes from Sheet 3 and retain only one complete set of consolidated electric notes on the general notes sheet.
applicableAreas: General notes sheet and other sheets
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains the 'Electric Notes' block showing 5 numbered notes addressing Austin Energy requirements (notes 1-5). Immediately below these 5 notes, the same 5 notes are repeated verbatim with no numbering or distinction. The content is identical word-for-word: (1) tree pruning rights, (2) easement provision, (3) tree removal responsibility, (4) clearance maintenance, (5) relocation costs. This exact duplication appears within the same single text block on the same sheet without any functional reason (no differentiation, no variation, no application-specific instances).
findings.reasoning: Reviewer Convention established in the grouping requires that 'Electric notes [should be] consolidated on cover sheet or general notes sheet' (singular instance), not duplicated. The applicant has consolidated the notes to the general notes sheet, which is correct, but then unnecessarily repeated them within the same block, which creates confusion and increases visual clutter without providing additional information. Best practice requires notes to appear once in a consolidated location.

findings.comment: Utility plan scale or layout may not be adequate for clear display of electric utilities. If electric utilities are shown on the utility plan, they must be at sufficient scale with adequate labeling and detail to distinguish from other utilities and allow clear review.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) titled 'Utility Tap Plan showing proposed water and wastewater connections.' Vision analysis showed: 'The entire drawing provided on this page is a top-down, "plan view" layout of the site' at 'Scale 1" = 20'.' The sheet shows water, wastewater, and storm drain utilities prominently with detailed labeling and DFU calculations. However, electric utility documentation is minimal—only a generic '-E-' (Proposed Underground Electric) line shown in legend and plan view routing, with no detail, specification, or emphasis. The electric routing shares plan space with water/wastewater systems without adequate separation or clarity. No profile view of electric utilities is shown (note: profiles shown are water-only). The utility plan does not 'fill the page' with adequate scale for electric facility detail—Sheet 19 appears to focus on water/wastewater with electric facilities shown secondarily.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Utility plan' be 'provided at adequate scale to fill page, resulting in excessive white space and insufficient detail.' The grouping's checklist item EL-11.20 specifies that the utility plan should not have 'excessive white space and insufficient detail.' While Sheet 19 at 1"=20' scale is technically correct, the electric utilities are shown with minimal detail and labeling compared to water/wastewater systems. The lack of electrical profile information and detailed routing specifications suggests the electric utility documentation may not fill adequate page space or provide sufficient detail. An electrically-focused utility plan sheet or enhanced electric documentation on Sheet 19 would be more adequate.

findings.comment: Building setbacks not clearly shown on electric facility plans. While property lines are delineated, explicit building setback lines and labels must be shown on the site plan and utility plan to clearly establish the required buffer zones for electric facility planning.
applicableAreas: Electric facility plans (Site Plan, Utility Plan)
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) for property lines. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Yes, property lines are clearly shown using a heavy dashed/dotted line type, accompanied by bearing and distance callouts (e.g., "N63° 32' 57"W 414.24'" along the bottom boundary).' Property lines ARE shown on Sheet 9. Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for property lines. Vision analysis noted property boundaries are shown on the electrical design plan with easement references. However, examined facts.md and found critical discrepancy regarding property delineation: Site area stated as 2.16 acres on site plan; 2019 deed states 2.158 ac; TCAD states 2.1970 ac; COA GIS parcel measures 2.111 ac. Additionally, legal description and boundaries may not fully account for two missing recorded easements (Greenbelt 0.31 ac, Drainage 0.130 ac). Building setbacks are shown via dimensions on Site Plan (e.g., 26.1' from western boundary to Bldg. 1, 21.3' from southern boundary to Bldg. 8) but are NOT labeled as explicit 'Building Setback' lines.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(v) requires 'Property lines and building setbacks' be shown on 'electric facility plans (site plan, utility plan).' While property lines are clearly shown with bearings and distances on Sheet 9, building setbacks are not explicitly labeled with 'Building Setback' or 'B.L.' designations. The setback distances exist as dimension calls but are not formally delineated as setback lines. Additionally, the property lines themselves may not accurately represent the controlled property given the missing easement areas documented in facts.md. Building setback lines should be explicitly drawn and labeled, not implied through scattered dimensional callouts.

findings.comment: Permanent structures not shown with both footprint and height on plans. Building elevation sheets must be provided showing building heights, roof lines, and all element dimensions (overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) for clearance verification.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for building heights. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Building heights are NOT shown on this plan view.' Buildings 1-8 show square footage and FFE (Finished Floor Elevation) but no height dimension. Examined Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) looking for building height information. The guide.md for Sheet 11 lists Building FFEs (e.g., Bldg. 1 FFE=687.50) but does not mention building heights or roof elevations. No building elevation sheets showing heights (facades with dimensions) appear to be included in the 39-sheet plan set. The README lists sheets 1-39; no dedicated building elevation sheet is identified. The grouping's Documents to Review lists 'Building Elevations - Building heights and element dimensions (overhangs, balconies, awnings) for clearance verification' as a required document. No such sheet was located.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(iii) requires 'Permanent structures' be shown 'with both footprint and height on plans.' While building footprints are shown on the electrical design plan and other sheets, building heights are NOT shown. Finished Floor Elevations provide vertical data but do NOT indicate roof heights or total building heights. No building elevation sheets showing heights and overhangs are provided. The absence of height documentation on permanent structures is a deficiency that prevents verification of clearances to electric facilities and other code compliance matters.

findings.comment: Plans do not explicitly demonstrate that proposed topology (grades, grade changes, floodplains, detention ponds) will not adversely impact electric facilities. Grading plan must coordinate with electrical infrastructure to confirm adequate clearances and access are maintained for all electric facilities.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) which shows 'existing and proposed topography, establish building finished floor elevations (FFEs), map storm drainage infrastructure, and indicate the location of retaining walls and utility easements.' Sheet 11 shows contour lines, building FFEs, and drainage infrastructure. Examined Sheet 15 which addresses 'Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan & Calculations' and references detention pond design. Sheet 21 (Electrical) shows final site layout with utilities. However, the grouping's requirement specifies 'final proposed topology including grades, grade changes, floodplains, and detention ponds for electric facility review.' While grading and detention ponds ARE shown, explicit coordination documenting how the final topology interacts with the electric facilities (especially underground lines and easements) is not provided. No plan explicitly states 'electric facilities are/are not located in floodplain areas' or confirms underground electric line routing accommodates proposed grading/slopes, or that detention pond construction will not impact easement access.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires plans 'show final proposed topology including grades, grade changes, floodplains, and detention ponds for electric facility review.' While the site plan shows grades, changes, and detention pond, explicit documentation coordinating these elements WITH the electric facilities (line depths relative to grades, easement access through detention areas, floodplain impacts) is not provided. The requirement specifically states this topography information must be shown 'for electric facility review'—meaning it must be reviewed in the context of electric infrastructure, not separately.

findings.comment: No setup areas (minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal) are shown in front of any of the four transformer pads. Design must designate and dimension the required crane/bucket truck access space for each piece of AE equipment per UCM § 1.3.16.
applicableAreas: Equipment setups in front of four transformer pads
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts four transformer pads (blue rectangles labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad') at four locations: west of Building 1/2, between Buildings 4 and 5, between Buildings 6 and 7, and west of Building 8. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the same equipment locations in context of buildings, parking, driveways, and sidewalks. However, neither sheet shows any delineated setup area in front of the transformers. No dashed lines, dimensions, or text labels indicating a 20-foot × 35-foot setup area (or any alternative dimensions) were found on either the electrical plan or site plan sheets. The transformer locations are shown graphically but the required horizontal space for truck/crane access is not designated.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal space in front of all AE equipment for crane and bucket truck access. The applicant has not designated or dimensioned this required space on the site plan or electrical plan. While the equipment locations are shown, the absence of a clearly marked and dimensioned setup area means compliance with this clearance requirement cannot be verified. The preliminary design stage does not exempt the applicant from showing how this mandatory clearance will be provided.

findings.comment: No vertical clearance (minimum 35 feet) is shown or verified above any transformer pad. Building elevations are required to demonstrate adequate clearance for crane/bucket truck access, or alternative equipment locations must be provided.
applicableAreas: Vertical clearance space above equipment setups
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations but does not indicate any vertical clearance envelope or dimension. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building heights ranging from 33'−4.75" to 36'−1". However, no indication is provided of the vertical clearance above each transformer, such as overhead obstructions (canopies, overhanging structures, tree branches, or overhead utility lines). The preliminary electrical design shows no analysis of vertical clearance above the equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 35 feet vertical clearance in front of AE equipment for crane/bucket truck access. Without building elevations or vertical clearance analysis, there is no evidence that 35 feet of vertical clearance is (or will be) available at each equipment location. The presence of buildings with 33−36 foot heights in proximity to the transformers raises questions about whether adequate clearance exists, but this cannot be verified without elevations.

findings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing relationship between proposed structures and overhead electric conductors. Provide building elevation sheets showing electric poles, cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide), and overhead conductors with dimensions confirming minimum 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities along western property boundary
Overhead electric facilities along southern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) marked with dashed lines along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also confirms the OHE line running along the southern boundary. Sheets 9 and 31 show the building footprints and layouts throughout the site. However, NO BUILDING ELEVATION SHEETS are included in the site plan submittal to verify the three-dimensional clearance between the proposed buildings and the overhead conductors. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that overhead electric facilities are shown along boundaries but no elevation views or clearance exhibits are provided. The buildings shown on the site plan and landscape plan would need elevation drawings to verify they maintain the required 7.5-foot horizontal clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from overhead primary and neutral conductors per UCM § 1.10.3.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes permanent clearance requirements from AE overhead distribution lines (7.5 feet horizontal, 15-foot radius). To verify compliance with these clearance requirements, building elevations must be provided showing the position of overhead conductors, poles, and cross arms relative to the proposed structures. The site plan shows the overhead facilities and building locations in plan view, but without elevation views and clearance exhibits, the three-dimensional clearance relationships cannot be determined. The 'Preliminary' designation of the electrical design may indicate coordination with Austin Energy is ongoing, but the site plan should include the necessary views to verify this critical clearance requirement. Without building elevation sheets showing these facilities, the deficiency status cannot be changed from 'unclear' to 'pass'.

findings.comment: Underground electric cable and conduit clearances from buildings, foundations, and permanent structures not shown or dimensioned on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned clearance details on utility plan showing minimum 60-inch horizontal clearance from all AE underground facilities to customer buildings, foundations, and permanent structures per UCM § 1.10.5.
applicableAreas: Underground electric conduit routing throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines (marked as blue solid lines with 'E' markers) routing throughout the site to connect buildings, pull boxes, transformer pads, and meters. The vision analysis confirmed that underground electric conduit is proposed throughout the site. However, there are no dimension lines or notes showing the clearances from the underground electric conduit to customer buildings, foundations, permanent structures, or other utilities. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations but provides no coordination dimensions between buildings and proposed underground electric facilities. The preliminary electrical plan shows the general routing of electric lines but provides no evidence that the minimum 60-inch clearance from buildings per UCM § 1.10.5 has been verified or documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires minimum 60-inch (5-foot) horizontal clearance from AE underground cable, conduit, and underground facilities to customer buildings, foundations, or permanent structures. The applicant must document this clearance through dimensioned drawings. The existence of underground electric lines on the preliminary electrical plan does not constitute compliance documentation; the clearances must be explicitly shown and dimensioned. The absence of clearance dimensions or notes demonstrating compliance with the 60-inch minimum clearance requirement means the deficiency cannot be marked as resolved. This is a documentation requirement that must be satisfied through additional detail.

findings.comment: Cross-section details not provided where storm drains and water lines cross underground electric conduit and facilities. Provide cross-section details at all utility crossing locations showing minimum 12-inch vertical clearance (24-36 inches for gas/fuel/steam lines) and horizontal separation per UCM § 1.10.5.
applicableAreas: Proposed storm drain and water line crossings with underground electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows a profile view of the proposed water line and a plan view indicating the location of proposed underground electric facilities (marked as 'Proposed Underground Electric' with transformer pad symbol). The vision analysis of Sheet 20 confirmed that the plan view shows both water utility and electric utility at the same general location, indicating a crossing or potential conflict. However, the profile view on Sheet 20 only depicts the water line elevations; there is NO cross-section detail showing the vertical relationship, clearance distance, or separation between the water line and the electric conduit at the crossing point. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) would show storm drain routing, and if it crosses the proposed underground electric lines shown on Sheet 21, a cross-section detail should be provided. No such detail has been located.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires cross-section details where utilities cross AE underground facilities to demonstrate required clearances. The grouping specifies that when storm drains and water lines cross underground electric lines, cross-section details must be provided showing vertical and horizontal clearance verification. The preliminary electrical plan and utility tap plan show the general locations and routing of utilities, but without cross-section details at crossing locations, the vertical and horizontal clearances cannot be verified. This is a documentation deficiency - the required cross-section views must be provided to demonstrate compliance with utility separation requirements.

findings.comment: Cross-section utility design drawings not provided showing vertical and horizontal clearances between underground electric lines and crossing utilities (water, wastewater, storm drainage). Provide cross-section details for each utility crossing showing minimum 12-inch vertical clearance for water/wastewater and minimum clearance distances per UCM § 1.10.5.
applicableAreas: Utility crossings between underground electric lines and water, wastewater, and storm drainage facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) shows the water utility tap plan and profile but does NOT provide cross-section details showing vertical and horizontal clearances at locations where the water line intersects with the proposed underground electric facilities shown on Sheet 21. Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing throughout the site, and Sheet 20 shows proposed water line routing. These utilities are indicated as crossing or in close proximity in the plan view, but no cross-section engineering drawings are provided demonstrating the specific clearance dimensions at crossing locations. The vision analysis of Sheet 20 confirmed that while utilities are shown in plan view, no cross-section details are provided showing utility separation and clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires that where utilities cross AE underground facilities, cross-section details must be provided that show both vertical and horizontal clearances. These clearances must be dimensioned and verified: minimum 12 inches for water/wastewater, 24-36 inches for gas/fuel/steam, and 12 inches for other utilities. The absence of cross-section views at utility crossing locations is a clear documentation deficiency. The applicant must provide cross-section drawings (not just plan views) showing the three-dimensional relationship of utilities at crossing points to verify clearance compliance. Without these details, the design cannot be verified as compliant.

findings.comment: Elevations not provided on utility crossing details where electric facilities cross storm drains and water lines. Provide cross-section details with vertical elevation dimensions showing how utilities cross and the separation distance maintained between them.
applicableAreas: Utility crossing locations throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) includes a profile view of the water line showing vertical elevations (labeled with flowline elevations such as 'FL 8": 674.33'), demonstrating that elevation information is available for water utilities. However, the profile view only depicts the water line and does not show the underground electric facility at crossing locations. No cross-section details with elevation dimensions are provided at locations where utilities cross. The vision analysis confirmed that while the water line profile includes elevation callouts, there are no elevation-detailed cross-sections showing the utility crossing locations or the relative elevations of the electric and water utilities at those points.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires that elevations be provided on utility crossings to demonstrate clearance compliance. The grouping specifies 'Elevations not provided on utility crossings' as a deficiency. While Sheet 20 provides a profile with elevations for the water line, it does not provide cross-sectional details with elevations at the actual crossing point with the electric utility. The absence of elevation dimensions at utility crossing locations prevents verification of the vertical clearance requirement. Cross-section details with labeled elevations for both utilities at crossing points must be provided.

findings.comment: No truck access path (minimum 12 feet width, 16 feet vertical clearance) is designated or dimensioned on site plan or electrical plan. Design must identify the truck access route(s) to all AE equipment and dimension them to verify compliance with UCM § 1.3.16 standards, including surface load rating specifications.
applicableAreas: Access paths to transformer pads and electrical equipment throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows internal driveways, parking areas, and pedestrian circulation. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad and pull box locations. However, neither sheet designates or dimensions a specific truck access path to the on-site electric facilities. No path is labeled with minimum 12 feet horizontal width or 16 feet vertical clearance specifications. While driveways exist on the site, there is no explicit confirmation that they will be maintained to support AE truck access to equipment, nor are the paths dimensioned to verify compliance with minimum width and clearance standards.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 12 feet horizontal width and 16 feet vertical clearance for truck access to AE facilities, with surfaces capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight). The applicant must explicitly designate, dimension, and label the truck access path(s) on the site plan and verify they meet these standards. Absence of documented access paths means the applicant has not demonstrated compliance with this mandatory requirement.

findings.comment: Sheet 3 includes detailed Transmission Notes (16 items), yet transmission structures are not clearly shown on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4), and no building elevations are provided. If transmission facilities exist, building elevations must be provided showing transmission lines and demonstrating compliance with transmission clearance requirements. If transmission facilities do not exist, the transmission notes should be removed from Sheet 3.
applicableAreas: Transmission facility locations (if present on or adjacent to site)
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) includes Block 20 titled 'Electric Transmission Notes' containing 16 detailed requirements for transmission easements, clearances, and access (e.g., 25-foot clearance zones, 48-hour pre-construction meetings, 46,000 lb tandem axle road support). These notes explicitly reference transmission structures, transmission easements, and transmission wire. However, Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not show visible transmission structures (only standard distribution poles). The preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) does not show transmission infrastructure. Despite the presence of transmission notes, no building elevations are provided that would demonstrate how proposed structures relate to transmission lines.
findings.reasoning: If transmission facilities are present on or adjacent to the site (as suggested by the inclusion of detailed transmission notes on Sheet 3), UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that building elevations be provided 'showing transmission lines where applicable.' The applicant cannot demonstrate whether this requirement is met or not, because: (1) transmission structures are not clearly documented on the existing conditions survey, and (2) no building elevations are provided in the site plan set. The inclusion of transmission notes without corresponding transmission detail on the existing survey creates ambiguity.

findings.comment: Retaining wall heights and footing details near electric easements not clearly documented on grading plan. Provide wall top and bottom elevations on grading plan for walls located near overhead electric easements, with detailed cross-sections showing toe and heel footing configuration to verify clearance compliance per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls along property boundaries near electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows retaining walls labeled along property boundaries: 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall', 'Tie into existing Retaining Wall Match existing Wall Elevations', 'Existing Retaining Wall', and 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced'. The grading plan also shows electric easements ('5' Electric Easement', '15' Electric Easement') in the same boundary areas where retaining walls are located. However, the retaining wall heights (top and bottom elevations) are not clearly labeled on the grading plan in the areas near the electric easements. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plan Details and Notes) would contain the detailed wall cross-sections and footing details. These details must be reviewed to determine if wall elevations and footing details near overhead electric facilities are adequately documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires that retaining wall heights and footing details be shown on grading plans when walls are proposed near overhead electric facilities to verify that the wall construction does not create clearance violations. The grouping specifies that 'Retaining wall heights (top and bottom elevations) not shown on grading plans or toe and heel footing details not provided for retaining walls near overhead electric facilities' is a deficiency. While walls are shown on Sheet 11 near electric easements, the specific top and bottom elevations are not clearly called out in those boundary areas. Whether detailed wall sections on Sheets 38-39 adequately document these clearances requires visual examination. The unclear status reflects uncertainty about whether the detail sheets (38-39) contain the required information.

findings.comment: No section and plan view exhibit is provided showing utility poles with cross arm dimensions and distances to proposed buildings/structures. Design must provide this exhibit with specific dimensions documenting compliance with UCM § 1.10.3 clearance requirements (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial).
applicableAreas: Clearance verification for proposed buildings near existing utility poles with cross arms
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing distribution poles and overhead utility lines. The poles are shown with cross arm symbols (approximately 8 feet wide for standard distribution poles). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations. However, no section or plan view exhibit is provided that shows the utility poles with cross arms (8 feet width) and dimensions from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a 'section and plan view exhibit showing utility poles with cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide) and dimensions from outer conductor to outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings.' This exhibit is a fundamental documentation requirement for verifying compliance with the 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearance requirements from overhead distribution lines. Without this exhibit, clearance compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: No clearance exhibits are provided showing AE, NESC, and OSHA clearance envelopes in relation to existing overhead facilities and proposed buildings. Exhibits must be provided documenting the clearance envelopes required by applicable standards (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial for distribution; larger for transmission).
applicableAreas: Clearance verification areas where proposed buildings are near overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Existing overhead distribution poles and lines are documented on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey). No clearance exhibits are provided in the site plan set. The preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed underground equipment but does not address existing overhead facilities or clearance envelopes.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 and UCM § 1.10.2 require that clearance exhibits document AE, NESC (National Electrical Safety Code), and OSHA clearance envelopes. These envelopes define the three-dimensional space that must be maintained clear of obstructions around energized conductors for safety. The applicant has not provided any exhibits showing these clearance envelopes in relation to proposed structures. This is a required exhibit that must accompany the site plan when overhead electric facilities are present.

findings.comment: No exhibit is provided with dimensions from proposed buildings to proposed electric routing. Design must provide dimensioned drawings showing the distance from each building footprint to the proposed underground electric conduit and lines, demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.5 (minimum 60 inches from customer buildings).
applicableAreas: Proposed underground electric routing between and near proposed buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed underground electric lines (blue lines) routing from the property boundary to four transformer pads and then daisy-chaining to building meter banks. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the building footprints. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that 'there are absolutely no dimensions shown on this sheet that quantify the relationship or distance between the proposed electrical facilities and the proposed buildings. The relationships shown are purely graphical.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that 'an exhibit be provided showing dimensions from proposed buildings to proposed electric routing.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement to verify that proposed underground electric facilities maintain adequate clearances from building foundations (minimum 60 inches per UCM § 1.10.5). Without dimensioned exhibits, the applicant has not demonstrated that the underground routing will comply with clearance standards.

findings.comment: Plan and profile views not submitted to verify required clearances between existing overhead electric lines and proposed buildings. Provide plan and profile cross-sections showing vertical separation between overhead conductors and building structures, with dimensions confirming 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances per UCM § 1.10.3 and UCM § 1.16.0(2).
applicableAreas: Proposed buildings 1-8 relative to existing overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheets 9, 21, and 31 show the locations of the proposed buildings relative to these overhead facilities in plan view. However, NO PLAN AND PROFILE VIEWS have been provided that show the vertical (profile) relationship between the existing overhead electric lines and the proposed buildings. UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires 'Plan and profile not submitted to verify required clearances between existing electric lines and proposed buildings.' The site plan includes plan views showing the buildings and OHE lines, but the profile views (cross-section views showing elevation differences) required to verify clearances are not present in the submittal.
findings.reasoning: Plan view alone is insufficient to verify clearance compliance between overhead conductors and building structures. Profile views (also called cross-sections in plan direction) are required to show the vertical separation between conductor height and building height/roofline. Without these profile views with dimensions, the clearance requirement of 7.5 feet horizontal and 15-foot radial separation cannot be verified. The code specifically requires 'plan and profile' views be submitted. The current submittal contains only plan views for this relationship.

findings.comment: Building construction types are not documented on plans. Specify the construction type for each building (e.g., 'brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating' or 'non-brick/masonry') on site plan or architectural notes to enable clearance verification from equipment per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4.
applicableAreas: All proposed buildings in proximity to AE equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) provides building type information (4-Plex, 5-Plex, 6-Plex), gross floor areas, and unit counts. However, there is no documentation of building construction type (e.g., 'brick or masonry with minimum 2-hour fire rating' vs. 'non-brick or masonry'). No architectural notes or specifications are provided indicating the exterior wall construction materials or fire ratings for any of the eight buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 distinguishes between brick/masonry structures with minimum 2-hour fire rating (allowing reduced clearances from equipment) and non-brick/masonry buildings (requiring standard clearances). The clearance requirements from pad-mounted equipment depend on building construction type. Without this information documented on the plans, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with the table, and the reviewer cannot determine which clearance standard applies. Per the grouping's regulatory overview, 'Default assumption is non-brick/masonry unless plans explicitly document brick/masonry construction with 2-hour fire rating.'

findings.comment: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking area or traffic lane to verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 requirement that pads be within 6 feet of parking/traffic for AE truck accessibility. If distances exceed 6 feet, provide written Austin Energy Design approval for alternative spacing.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations relative to parking and traffic areas
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 88 parking spaces (10 surface, 78 garage) and internal driveways. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads: one west of Buildings 1/2 adjacent to a driveway curve, one between Buildings 4 and 5 near parking/circulation, one between Buildings 6 and 7 near parking/circulation, and one west of Building 8 near the property line. Vision analysis indicates that transformers appear to be in close proximity to parking and traffic areas, but 'there are absolutely no dimensions shown on this sheet that quantify the relationship or distance between the proposed electrical facilities and the proposed buildings.' Distances from transformers to parking/traffic areas are not dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that 'Equipment pads be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for AE truck accessibility (unless otherwise specified by AE Design).' This requirement ensures that AE vehicles can position themselves close enough to equipment for safe and efficient maintenance. The applicant must either: (1) demonstrate that equipment pads are within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas (with dimensions), or (2) provide written AE Design approval if different spacing is used. Neither has been provided. The lack of dimensions prevents verification of compliance.

findings.comment: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the back (furthest from street/building) of adjacent sidewalks to verify minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4. If any pad is less than 2 feet from sidewalk, redesign pad location.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations near sidewalks and pedestrian paths
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows concrete sidewalks and decomposed granite walkways throughout the site near the buildings and around the detention pond. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations. However, there are no dimension lines or text specifying the clearance distances from any transformer pad to the adjacent sidewalks or pedestrian paths.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that 'Equipment pads be located minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' This requirement provides space for sidewalk maintenance and prevents equipment from interfering with pedestrian circulation. Without dimensioned drawings, the applicant has not demonstrated that this minimum 2-foot clearance is maintained at all transformer locations. Visual proximity does not constitute dimensional compliance verification.

findings.comment: Provide dimensioned underground utility plan showing minimum 60-inch horizontal clearance from proposed underground electric conduit to all building foundations and permanent structures per UCM § 1.10.5. If any location has less than 60 inches, provide alternative routing or written approval from Austin Energy Design.
applicableAreas: Underground electric lines routing to buildings and electrical equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines (depicted as solid blue lines) routing from the property boundary through the center of the site, connecting to the four transformer pads and daisy-chaining to building meter banks (located on building walls). Vision analysis found: 'There are no dimensions shown indicating the clearance or offset distance of the underground electrical routing from the building foundations or other structures.' The underground conduit is shown graphically but without dimensional clearances to buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires a minimum 60 inches (5 feet) horizontal clearance from AE underground cable, conduit, and underground facilities to customer building foundations and permanent structures (except other utilities, which require 12 inches minimum; gas/fuel/steam require 24-36 inches). Without dimensioned drawings showing the distance of the underground lines from building foundations, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with this requirement. This clearance is critical for future excavation safety and building maintenance.

findings.comment: Plat note regarding Austin Energy right to prune and remove trees and obstructions not shown on plat sheet. Add plat note: 'Austin Energy has the right to prune and to remove trees, shrubbery and other obstructions to the extent necessary to keep all electric facility easements clear' per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(i).
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) was examined and found to contain only historical plat notes from the original 1975 Mecey Subdivision dedication and does not include any notes regarding Austin Energy rights. The vision analysis of Sheet 2 confirmed: 'There are NO notes anywhere on this sheet regarding any of the specified Austin Energy (AE) requirements... there is no mention of: AE rights to prune trees and maintain easements.' Sheet 3 (Coversheet/General Notes) does contain an electric note (Block 8) that states: 'Austin Energy has the right to prune and/or remove trees, shrubbery and other obstructions to the extent necessary to keep the easements clear.' However, this note appears on the coversheet (Sheet 3), not on the plat sheet (Sheet 2). UCM § 1.16.0(8)(i) requires that this plat note appear on the plat itself or be incorporated by reference.
findings.reasoning: The code requirement is for a 'plat note' - which traditionally means a note that appears on the recorded plat document. While Sheet 3 (coversheet) contains the required language about Austin Energy pruning rights, the plat sheet (Sheet 2) itself does not contain this note. Having the note on the coversheet may provide general project notice, but it does not satisfy the specific requirement for a 'plat note.' To ensure the pruning right restriction is recorded with the property and binds future owners, the note should appear directly on the plat sheet. The current documentation does not meet the literal requirement for a plat note.

findings.comment: Plat note regarding owner responsibility for tree pruning within 10 feet of proposed overhead facilities not shown on plat.
