Add plat note: 'Owner shall be responsible for initial tree pruning and tree removal that is within ten feet of the centerline of the proposed overhead electric facilities' per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iii).
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) does not contain any note regarding owner responsibility for tree pruning or removal within 10 feet of overhead facilities. The vision analysis confirmed no such notes exist on the plat. Sheet 3 (Coversheet) contains electric notes (Block 8) that reference tree pruning responsibility: 'The owner shall be responsible for installation of temporary erosion control, revegetation and tree protection. In addition, the owner shall be responsible for any initial tree pruning and tree removal that is within ten feet of the center line of the proposed overhead electric facilities...' However, this appears on the coversheet, not as a plat note on Sheet 2.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iii) requires a plat note specifying owner responsibility for initial tree pruning and removal within 10 feet of the centerline of proposed overhead electric facilities. While similar language appears on the coversheet (Sheet 3), the specific requirement is for a plat note - which means the note should appear on the plat document itself to bind the property and provide notice to future owners. The plat sheet (Sheet 2) does not contain this note, representing a deficiency in the required plat documentation.

findings.comment: Plat note regarding owner responsibility for temporary erosion control, revegetation, and tree protection not shown on plat. Add plat note: 'Owner shall be responsible for installation of temporary erosion control, revegetation and tree protection during construction' per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iii).
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) was examined and contains no note regarding temporary erosion control, revegetation, or tree protection responsibility. The vision analysis confirmed: 'There are NO notes...regarding...Temporary erosion control and tree protection responsibility.' Sheet 3 (Coversheet/General Notes, Block 8) does contain relevant language: 'The owner shall be responsible for installation of temporary erosion control, revegetation and tree protection.' However, this language appears on the coversheet (Sheet 3), not on the plat document (Sheet 2) itself.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iii) requires that a plat note be added specifying owner responsibility for temporary erosion control, revegetation, and tree protection. While Sheet 3 (coversheet) contains general project notes with similar language, the specific code requirement is for a 'plat note' - meaning a note that should appear on the recorded plat to bind the property with this obligation. The absence of this note on Sheet 2 (Plat) constitutes a deficiency in the required plat documentation, even if similar language appears elsewhere in the project notes.

findings.comment: Plat note regarding owner responsibility to maintain NESC, NEC, OSHA, City, and Texas clearances not shown on plat. Add plat note: 'Owner is responsible for maintaining clearances required by the National Electric Safety Code, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations, City of Austin rules and regulations, and Texas state laws' per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iv).
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) does not contain a note regarding owner responsibility to maintain NESC, NEC, OSHA, City, and Texas clearances. The vision analysis confirmed the absence of such notes on the plat. Sheet 3 (Coversheet, Block 8) contains related language: 'The owner of the property is responsible for maintaining clearances required by the National Electric Safety Code, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations, City of Austin rules and regulations and Texas state laws...' However, this appears on the coversheet, not as a plat note on Sheet 2.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8)(iv) requires a plat note establishing that the owner is responsible for maintaining clearances per NESC, NEC, OSHA, City, and Texas requirements. This note should appear on the plat document itself to clearly bind the property and provide enduring notice to the owner and successors. While language addressing this requirement exists on Sheet 3 (coversheet), the plat document (Sheet 2) lacks this specific required note. A plat note is the appropriate vehicle for establishing a property-level obligation that runs with the land.

findings.comment: Transformer pads E of Building 4 and E of Building 7 are located immediately adjacent to a fire hydrant shown in the driveway curve on Sheet 10. Dimension callouts must verify minimum 5-foot clearance from hydrant to transformer pad edges.
findings.observation: Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) shows a 'Proposed Fire Hydrant' located in the curve between Buildings 4 and 7, at the intersection of the internal driveway loop. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the transformer pad locations relative to this hydrant. The transformer pads E of Bldg 4 and E of Bldg 7 are immediately adjacent to this fire hydrant location based on the site layout. Vision analysis confirms the fire hydrant is positioned directly in the curve where these two transformer pads are located. No dimension callout shows 5-foot minimum clearance between the pads and this hydrant.
findings.reasoning: Reviewer Convention establishes a minimum 5-foot clearance requirement between transformer pads and fire hydrants. Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) clearly identifies the hydrant location in the immediate vicinity of the two transformer pads on the east side of the site. The spatial layout on the plans indicates the pads and hydrant are in the same localized area without documented separation. Without specific dimensions verifying the 5-foot clearance, compliance cannot be confirmed. The immediate juxtaposition of these features on the plan suggests the requirement may not be met.

findings.comment: Tree species planted or retained within 10 lateral feet of transformer pads are not identified by scientific/common name on the landscape or tree list sheets. Provide a cross-referenced list showing each tree's species and confirmation of utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) designation for all trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment.
applicableAreas: Areas within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment or 15 lateral feet of overhead distribution
findings.observation: Sheet 32 (Tree List) provides tree inventory with functional categories (M=Mitigation, PL=Parking Lot, SY=Street Yard) but does NOT list specific tree species names. Without species identification, utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) column cannot be verified. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows tree symbols distributed across the site but does not cross-reference species against ECM Appendix F. Trees are present in the vicinity of transformer pads and electrical easements, but species-specific verification of utility compatibility is not documented on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 and ECM Appendix F require verification that trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment are utility-compatible species. The plans identify trees only by functional category (M, PL, SY), not by species name. The requirement cannot be verified without species identification. This is particularly important because the plans do not document whether trees identified as 'M' (mitigation trees) planted specifically for the development are utility-compatible, or whether existing trees within 10 feet of pads meet the requirement.

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows vegetation (shrubs, groundcover, sod) adjacent to all transformer pads but lacks dimension callouts verifying minimum 10-foot clearance from access door side and 5-foot clearance from other sides. Provide specific clearance dimensions on landscape plan.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations with adjacent vegetation
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows extensive vegetation throughout the site including landscape areas marked as H-3 (Street Yard Landscaping) and H-4 (Parking Lot Landscaping) adjacent to the buildings where transformer pads are located. Shrubs, groundcover, and sod (H-7) are shown in proximity to all five transformer pad locations. However, the Landscape Plan does not include specific dimension callouts or clearance annotations showing the distance from shrubs/low-lying vegetation to transformer pad edges. Without detailed cross-referencing to exact planting locations and dimensions, compliance with the 10-foot access door side and 5-foot other sides clearance requirements cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires shrubs or low-lying vegetation to maintain minimum 10 lateral feet clearance from transformer access door side and minimum 5 lateral feet clearance from other sides. The landscape plan shows vegetation distributed around all transformer pad locations but does not provide the detailed dimension callouts necessary to verify these clearances. Required clearance documentation is absent from the plans.

findings.comment: Root barriers for trees within 20 lateral feet of transformer pads are not documented on the landscape plan. The landscape plan and details must include dimensions and specifications for root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from pad-mounted equipment) for all trees within 20 lateral feet of transformers. Provide detail references and installation specifications on the landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment
findings.observation: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show any root barrier details or specifications. Tree list (Sheet 32) identifies mitigation trees ('M' designation) distributed throughout the site, including near electrical easements and transformer locations. At 1" = 20' scale, trees shown in vicinity of transformer pad areas (within estimated 20-foot radius) include marked 'M' trees. However, no root barrier dimensions (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from equipment) are documented on the landscape details or specifications.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, 5 feet from equipment) for trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. The landscape plan does not show root barriers anywhere. The absence of any root barrier callouts or detail references on sheets showing landscape elements near transformers and electrical easements suggests this requirement is not being addressed.

findings.comment: Transformer pads positioned adjacent to designated fire lanes lack documented 15-foot clearance dimensions. Provide dimension callouts on the electrical plan and fire protection plan showing the minimum 15-foot clearance from each transformer pad to the designated fire lane loop, or verify through AE Design approval that the configuration meets code requirements.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads adjacent to designated fire lanes
findings.observation: Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) identifies fire lanes as a continuous loop driveway marked with red curbing and white 'FIRE ZONE' stenciling throughout the property. Sheet 21 shows transformer pads positioned immediately adjacent to this main circulation loop: Pad 1 is at the primary entrance curve of the fire lane; Pads 2 and 3 are along the western edge adjacent to sidewalks that parallel the fire lane; Pad 5 is positioned north of the southern portion of the fire lane loop. The code requires minimum 15-foot clearance from fire lanes. Dimensional annotations are not provided to document compliance with this clearance requirement.
findings.reasoning: The fire lane is the primary circulation drive on the site, and visual analysis shows transformer pads are positioned immediately adjacent to (within 5-10 feet of) this marked fire lane at multiple locations. The code specifies a minimum 15-foot clearance from designated fire lanes. Without dimensional annotations verifying that each pad maintains 15-foot separation from the fire lane loop, compliance cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from transformer pads to overhead distribution conductors is not documented. Provide dimension callouts and/or cross-section drawings on the electrical plan showing the clearance from each transformer pad to the nearest overhead distribution line conductor, verifying the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to overhead distribution lines
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows an overhead electric line (-OHE-) designated on the southern property boundary. The general notes (Sheet 3) reference electric transmission clearance requirements, specifying '25 feet of transmission structures; 20-foot clearance for aerial equipment/staging.' However, no dimension callouts or cross-section drawings are provided on Sheet 21 to document the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from transformer pad locations to the overhead conductors. The plans do not indicate whether transformer pads are located within the clearance zone of the overhead lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead distribution primary, neutral, and secondary conductors extending from ground to sky. Without dimensional annotation or cross-section drawings showing that transformer pads are positioned beyond this clearance envelope, compliance cannot be verified. The presence of overhead lines on the property adjacent to transformer locations requires explicit clearance documentation.

findings.comment: Minimum 15-foot radius clearance from transformer pads to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors is not documented. Provide dimension callouts on the electrical plan showing the radial distance (measured from conductor centerline, not pole) from each transformer pad to the nearest primary and neutral conductor, verifying the minimum 15-foot radius clearance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows an overhead electric line (-OHE-) on the southern property boundary. The code requires minimum 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors, measured from the conductor centerline (not pole centerline). No dimension callouts are provided on the electrical plan to document the 15-foot radius clearance from transformers to the primary/neutral conductors. The distance from transformer pads to the overhead line location is not dimensionally verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes a 15-foot radius clearance requirement from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. This is a radial clearance measured from the conductor itself, not from the pole. Without specific dimension callouts showing that transformer pads are positioned beyond this 15-foot radius from the conductor location, compliance cannot be confirmed. The overhead line is present on the property adjacent to transformer locations, requiring explicit clearance documentation.

findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 is located adjacent to a Vault Easement callout, but the exact spatial relationship is not documented. Clarify whether the transformer pad is within, adjacent to, or separate from the Vault Easement. If the pad is located within any easement (drainage, water, sewer, or electrical), provide documentation of Austin Energy Design written approval for placement in that easement.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 (southwest location) relative to vault easement
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 identified a 'Vault Easement' callout immediately adjacent to Transformer Pad 3 in the southwest section of the site. The electrical plan does not document whether the transformer pad is located within the vault easement, adjacent to it, or what clearance is maintained. No notation indicates whether this pad has been approved by Austin Energy Design for placement in relation to the vault easement. The plans do not show the precise boundaries of the vault easement relative to the pad location.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 prohibits transformer pads from being placed in drainage easements, water easements, sewer easements, or electrical easements under overhead lines without AE Design written approval. While the plan shows a 'Vault Easement' near Pad 3, it is unclear whether the pad is within the easement boundary or what approvals have been obtained. If the pad is in a prohibited easement without documented approval, this is a deficiency.

findings.comment: Electrical service routing from transformer pads to meter locations is not documented as being 100% on private property. Provide annotations on the electrical plan confirming that all underground electric lines from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter remain entirely on private property and do not cross property lines or public right-of-way. Dimension the service routing paths to verify private property placement.
applicableAreas: Electrical service routing from transformers to meters
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads and electrical routing with meter locations labeled on building walls, but no notation documents whether 100% of the electrical service routing from transformers to meters is on private property. The plans show building locations and some meter positions but do not explicitly annotate or verify that underground electric lines routing from each transformer pad to corresponding meters do not cross into public right-of-way or property lines. The routing paths are not dimensionally verified as being fully on private property.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 requires that 'Electrical routing from transformer to meter must be 100% on private property.' The electrical plan shows general routing of underground electric lines but provides no annotation confirming that each service line from transformer to meter remains entirely on private property. Without explicit notation or dimension documentation showing that all routing is beyond property lines and not crossing into right-of-way or adjacent properties, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Horizontal width of truck access paths to transformer pads not dimensionally verified. Provide dimensioned site plan showing minimum 12-foot width access route from drivable surface to each transformer pad, measured at the narrowest point of the access path.
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads are shown adjacent to paved internal driveways. The 1" = 20' scale plan shows the pads in proximity to driveways, but no specific width dimensions are labeled for the access routes to the transformer pads. Sheet 9 shows driveway details referencing "Construct Type III Driveway See Detail 433S-2", but transformer-specific access route width requirements are not explicitly dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 12-foot horizontal width for truck access paths to transformer pads. While the plans show transformer pads adjacent to driveways, the width of the access path from the drivable surface to the transformer pad is not dimensionally verified. Typical internal site driveways may be 12-20 feet wide overall, but the specific access route to each transformer pad must meet the 12-foot minimum. Without dimensional verification at the transformer pad locations, compliance is unclear.

findings.comment: Vertical clearance of truck access paths to transformer pads not verified. Provide grading plan or building section details showing transformer pad locations with spot elevations, and verify that minimum 16-foot vertical clearance is maintained along all access routes to transformer pads, including clearances from building eaves, overhangs, and any other overhead structures.
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows extensive contour lines and spot elevations across the site, indicating significant grade changes (9+ feet total elevation change across site). However, transformer pad locations are NOT shown on the grading plan. Building Finished Floor Elevations (FFE) are provided but transformer pad elevations are not. Without transformer pad elevations and spot elevations along the access routes, the vertical clearances and access route slopes cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance for truck access paths to transformer pads. This clearance must be verified by checking building heights, overhead structures, and any other obstructions above the access route. The grading plan does not show transformer pad locations or their associated vertical clearance zones. Without this information, it is impossible to verify that 16-foot vertical clearance is maintained along all access paths. Any overhead structures, eaves, awnings, or other features crossing above the access routes would need to be checked against this requirement.

findings.comment: Transformer pad access surfaces not specified as hot mix asphaltic concrete (HMAC) or Portland cement concrete (PCC) pavement. Provide detailed construction specifications and engineering calculations confirming that all transformer pad access surfaces meet all-weather pavement requirements and load capacity standards.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations on electrical plan
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) which show four transformer pad locations adjacent to driveways. Transformer pads are drawn as rectangular symbols within landscaped islands adjacent to paved access routes. No specifications or annotations are provided on any sheet indicating the surface material of the transformer pad access areas. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad in a landscaped/unpaved island area between a sidewalk and drive aisle. No notes or details specify that access surfaces are HMAC or PCC pavement, nor are any structural specifications or load capacity information provided.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformer pad access surfaces to be all-weather prepared surfaces (HMAC or PCC pavement). UCM § 1.3.16 and LDC § 25-12-173 establish that access surfaces must be hot mix asphaltic concrete or Portland cement concrete pavement capable of supporting required vehicle weight. The site plan shows transformer pads in landscaped areas adjacent to driveways but does not confirm the pad access surfaces themselves are prepared pavement. Gravel, grass, or unpaved surfaces do not meet this requirement. Without explicit specification and detail of the transformer pad access surface material as HMAC or PCC with adequate structural design, compliance cannot be verified. The preliminary electrical plan does not include construction details or material specifications for transformer pad surfaces.

findings.comment: Structural capacity of transformer pad access surfaces not documented. Provide pavement design calculations and structural engineering certification confirming that all transformer pad access surfaces can support 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight) without damage.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations on electrical plan
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21 for access surface design and load capacity documentation. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows spot elevations and contour lines across the site but does NOT show transformer pad locations or elevations. Sheets 9 and 21 show four transformer pads adjacent to paved driveways but provide no pavement design calculations, structural details, or load capacity specifications. No engineering calculations or structural design documentation is visible on any sheet confirming the access surfaces can support the required 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight with maximum 32,530 lbs rear axle weight.
findings.reasoning: Code requires access surfaces to be capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight with 32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight without damage. This requires structural design calculations appropriate to soil conditions and pavement type. The site plan and grading plan do not show transformer pad locations with associated structural details or pavement design calculations. Without structural calculations specific to each transformer pad location, it cannot be verified that the access surfaces meet load capacity requirements. The burden is on the applicant to demonstrate compliance through engineering design.

findings.comment: Distances from transformer pads to drivable surfaces not dimensionally verified on plans, and laydown curb specifications not shown. Provide dimensioned measurements confirming distances from each transformer pad to nearest drivable surface, and if distances exceed 6 feet, provide laydown curb details with minimum 12-foot width and adequate load capacity specifications.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads adjacent to driveways where distances exceed 6 feet
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads are shown adjacent to paved driveways within approximately 6 feet based on visual scale (1" = 20'). However, specific measurement dimensions are not labeled on the plans. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" in a landscaped island between a sidewalk and drive aisle curb. No laydown curb specifications, dimensions, or details are shown on any sheet. No notes or details indicate whether laydown curbs are provided or what their specifications are (width, height, load capacity).
findings.reasoning: Code requires laydown curbs when transformer pads are not within 6 feet of drivable surface, with minimum 12-foot width and load capacity for transformer truck loads. The site plan shows transformers adjacent to driveways but does not explicitly measure the distances or confirm they are within 6 feet. More importantly, no laydown curb specifications are shown if any are required. Without clear dimensional verification of distances and explicit design details for any laydown curbs (including 12-foot minimum width and load capacity specifications), compliance cannot be determined. The exact location relationship of pads to curbs and drivable surfaces is ambiguous without precise measurements.

findings.comment: Site plan shows entrance and exit gates controlling access to the property. Transformers 2 and 3 are located inside the gated perimeter, preventing 24/7 Austin Energy truck access for emergency response and maintenance. Provide: (1) evidence that all transformers are relocated outside the gated perimeter with direct unrestricted access from Valley View Road, OR (2) a recorded easement document providing Austin Energy unlimited 24/7 property access regardless of gate status, OR (3) documented written approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing gated access with emergency procedures.
applicableAreas: Entire site - all transformer pads (T2 and T3 inside gated property perimeter)
Main entrance driveway and property gates
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 site plan which shows an 'Entrance Gate' and 'Exit Gate' at the western property boundary on Valley View Road. Vision analysis identified that Transformer 1 and Transformer 4 are located at or near the entrance gate line, while Transformer 2 (eastern side, between Bldg. 4 and 5) and Transformer 3 (southeastern corner, south of Bldg. 6) are located deep within the gated property perimeter. The site plan shows a residential condominium development (39 units, 8 buildings per facts.md) with controlled entry access via gates. Austin Energy personnel would require gate access codes or keys to reach T2 and T3, preventing 24/7 unrestricted emergency access.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 and § 1.11.1 explicitly require that all Austin Energy electrical equipment (including transformer pads) be accessible 24 hours per day, 7 days per week for emergency response and maintenance operations. The controlling provision states 'Transformers must be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations' and requires 'Access to AE Facilities' without restriction. Gated residential communities with restricted access prevent Austin Energy trucks from having immediate, unrestricted 24/7 entry to reach transformer equipment during emergencies or for routine maintenance. When transformers are located within a gated property perimeter, Austin Energy requires either: (1) external placement of the transformer outside the gate line with direct truck access, (2) a permanent easement document providing Austin Energy unlimited 24/7 access regardless of gate status, or (3) a documented AE Design exception authorizing the gated configuration with specific operational procedures. None of these alternatives are documented on the submitted plans.

findings.comment: Relationship between transformer pad locations and subsurface structures not verified. Provide building sections and parking structure plans showing the subsurface conditions below each transformer pad location, confirming no transformers are located over basement levels, subgrade parking garages, or other subsurface structures.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations at Buildings 1, 2, 4, and 7
findings.observation: Examined Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Grading Plan (Sheet 11). The buildings are shown as slab-on-grade construction on the site plan. However, Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does NOT show transformer pad locations, so it is impossible to verify whether transformers are located over basement levels, subgrade parking garages, or other subsurface structures. The site plan shows buildings are slab-on-grade but building sections showing subsurface conditions are not provided in the available sheets. Site plan notes indicate parking exists (88 spaces: 10 surface + 78 garage), but the relationship between individual transformer locations and the subsurface parking structure locations cannot be verified from the available plans.
findings.reasoning: Code requires verification that transformer pads are not located over basement levels, subgrade parking garages, or other subsurface structures. The site has underground parking (78 garage spaces) but transformer pad locations are not shown on the grading plan or any section views. Without building sections or subsurface structural plans showing the locations of underground parking areas and vaults in relation to each transformer pad location, it is impossible to verify compliance. The preliminary electrical plan shows only the top-level transformer pad symbols without subsurface coordination.

findings.comment: Transformer to meter line of sight distance may be excessive. Routing from western transformer pad to Building 3 appears to exceed 150 feet, potentially exceeding operational practice standards for 'within sight' requirement.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to distant meters
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan, scale 1" = 20') vision analysis measured distances along electrical routing paths: 'Based on the 1" = 20\' scale, distances vary significantly. For example, the distance from the western transformer pad to the Bldg 8 meters is roughly 30-40 feet, while the routing from that same pad to the Bldg 3 meters appears to be over 150 feet along the designated path.' The routing from the west pad to Bldg 3 meters is stated as 'over 150 feet along the designated path.' The vision analysis flagged that some routing distances exceed 150 feet, which is the operational practice standard for 'within sight' per the grouping regulatory overview.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires transformers to be 'within sight' of meters. The code does not specify a maximum distance. Operational practice, as noted in the grouping regulatory overview, suggests 150 feet as the maximum reasonable sight distance. The electrical routing from the western transformer pad to Building 3 meters is estimated at 'over 150 feet' along the path. This suggests potential non-compliance with operational practice standards for line-of-sight interpretation, though the code technically does not specify a maximum distance.

findings.comment: Electrical routing from public utility connection point to transformer and meters not verified as 100% on private property. Provide routing diagram or plan notes clearly indicating property line boundaries and confirming that all electrical routing from the initial public utility connection point through transformers to all meters is located entirely on private property and does not route through public ROW or public easements.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from public ROW entry point through transformer and meter locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) which shows blue electrical routing lines entering from Valley View Road (public right-of-way) on the left side of the plan. The routing line is labeled "Underground Electric Line" where it enters from the public ROW. The majority of the electrical routing network shown on the site appears to be within private property boundaries, but the entry point and initial routing segment from Valley View Road into the site are clearly shown originating in public ROW. The plan does not explicitly denote property line boundaries along the entire routing path to verify that the routing is 100% on private property after connection to the system.
findings.reasoning: Code requires electrical routing from riser to transformer and meter to be 100% on private property. Sheet 21 shows the electrical routing line entering from Valley View Road (public ROW). While most of the internal site routing appears to be on private property, the plans do not clearly verify that all electrical routing from the initial connection point is on private property and does not route through any public easement areas. The entry point in the ROW raises questions about whether initial segments comply with the 100% private property requirement.

findings.comment: No electrical engineering load calculations, transformer specifications, or ESPA form reference are provided on Sheet 21 or in supplementary documents. Provide: (1) Complete electrical engineering calculations including transformer count, kVA ratings, voltage classes, and amperage specifications for all proposed transformers, (2) ESPA (Electrical System Project Application) form completed and submitted to Austin Energy Network Design, (3) Final voltage and load documentation confirming the proposed equipment meets the development's power requirements and complies with Austin Energy standards.
applicableAreas: Transformer equipment specifications and vault design (if applicable)
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and the Engineer's Summary Letter supplementary document. Block 3 of Sheet 21 drawing shows 'electrical elements such as transformers, pull boxes, underground electric lines, and electrical meters' but provides no equipment specifications. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 explicitly states: 'None are provided on this sheet. The items are generically labeled Electrical Transformer Pad.' No electrical engineering report, load calculations, transformer kVA ratings, voltage specifications, phase information, or ESPA (Electrical System Project Application) form references are provided in any of the submitted documents. The Engineer's Summary Letter (supplementary doc) addresses only water and wastewater utilities, with no mention of electrical load calculations or transformer specifications. No transformer count is documented anywhere on the submitted plans.
findings.reasoning: Without load calculations and transformer specifications, Austin Energy Design and Network Design cannot verify that the proposed electrical infrastructure is adequate for the development's power requirements. The design is incomplete per UCM § 1.11.1 and cannot proceed to construction without this essential information.

findings.comment: Transformer pad 2 is positioned less than 2 feet from a surface parking space, triggering the bollard requirement per UCM § 1.10.4. No bollards are shown on the electrical or site plans. Provide: (1) Detail drawing for 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards (per UCM § 1.10.4 standard specification) positioned around Transformer 2, with spacing adequate to allow equipment door openings and access (minimum 3-foot clear width for door swing), OR (2) Reposition Transformer 2 to a location more than 4 feet from all parking spaces and traffic areas.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 2 (eastern location, between Bldg. 4 and 5, adjacent to parking)
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21 and 9 to identify transformer pad locations and proximity to parking areas. Transformer 2 (eastern side, between Bldg. 4 and 5) is positioned immediately adjacent to a surface parking space with less than 2 feet of separation per vision analysis: 'T2 is located directly adjacent to a perpendicular surface parking space. It appears to share a boundary or sit mere inches from the northernmost parking space in the cluster west of Bldg. 5. It is absolutely within 6 feet of this parking space.' No bollard symbols or notations are shown on Sheet 21 or Sheet 9 at this transformer location. Sheet 22 (Construction Details 1) was not reviewed but would be the expected location for bollard specifications if they were required and shown elsewhere on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Bollard requirement when transformer pad is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas... 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards are required and must be spaced to allow equipment door opening.' When transformer equipment is installed less than or equal to 4 feet from a parking space or traffic area, bollards must be provided to prevent vehicles from striking and damaging the transformer. Transformer 2 is less than 2 feet from a parking space, well within the 4-foot trigger distance. This proximity to parking makes the transformer vulnerable to vehicle impact and also creates a safety hazard for parked vehicles in an adjacent space that is separated only by the thin equipment pad. Bollards serve a dual purpose: (1) protecting the transformer from vehicle damage, and (2) preventing vehicles from parking or maneuvering too close to the electrical equipment. The absence of bollards at T2 violates this requirement.

findings.comment: Transformer vault is referenced by 'Vault Easement' label on electrical plan, but no vault design specifications or evidence of AE Network Design approval is provided. If transformer vault service is proposed, provide complete vault design including interior dimensions, access specifications, fire ratings, ventilation details, load calculations, and documented AE Network Design approval. If vault is not proposed, clarify the purpose of the vault easement notation.
applicableAreas: Transformer locations near Building 2 with nearby 'Vault Easement' label
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan). Near Building 2, one of the four transformer pad locations is accompanied by a text label reading "Vault Easement" pointing to a dashed rectangular boundary area that also contains an "Electrical Pull Box" label. This label indicates the presence of a vault easement in that location. However, no vault design details are shown on this sheet or any other electrical, grading, or site plan sheet in the available documentation. There are no vault door specifications, vault interior dimensions, access details, fire rating notes, ventilation provisions, or any other vault-specific design information visible.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformer vaults to be submitted to AE Network Design for approval, and vault location, access, and elevation must be coordinated with AE Network Design (allow 3-6 months for vault design review per UCM § 1.11.1.D). The presence of a "Vault Easement" label suggests a subsurface vault may be planned, but the preliminary electrical plan provides no vault design documentation or AE Network Design coordination evidence. If a transformer vault is being planned (indicated by the easement), it should be accompanied by detailed vault design, load calculations, fire rating specifications, and documented AE Network Design approval. The lack of vault design details alongside the easement label creates ambiguity about whether a vault is actually planned or if this is merely an easement designation.

findings.comment: Many meter locations shown on Sheet 21 are not within sight of transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path (see EL-14.38 findings). Provide: (1) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design AND Distribution Metering business units authorizing meter locations without direct line of sight to transformers, OR (2) Reposition all meters to locations that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer on first floor/ground level per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
applicableAreas: Multiple meter locations throughout the site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 to identify meter locations and access. Vision analysis identified: 'Locations: Meters are explicitly labeled as Electrical Meters using text boxes with leader lines. The leader lines point directly to the exterior walls of the buildings. Locations include: West side of Bldg. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8; East side of Bldg. 1, 2, 4, 6, 8; South side of Bldg. 7.' All meters appear to be exterior wall-mounted locations with no indication on Sheet 21 that any meters are behind doors, in enclosed rooms, or elevated above ground level. Standard notation on electrical plans would explicitly indicate 'Meter Room' or location callouts if meters were not directly accessible. The notations appear to place meters on first-floor/ground-level building faces.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 addresses 'Meters shown not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer, without written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units documented.' Two alternative compliance paths exist: (1) Meters are on first floor/ground level AND within sight of transformer (standard requirement), OR (2) Meters are not on first floor/ground level OR not within sight of transformer (exception scenario that requires written approval). The deficiency statement in EL-14.70 specifically addresses the exception case: 'when meters are shown not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer.' This triggers if either condition is not met. Vision analysis from EL-14.38 documented that 'many meters do NOT have a direct line of sight to a transformer' because they are on opposite sides of buildings. This represents a failure of the 'within sight' requirement. The Regulatory Overview clarifies the requirement: 'Meter locations not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer require written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units.' The submitted plans show many meters without line of sight but provide no documented approval from AE Design or Distribution Metering. Therefore, EL-14.70 is a fail.

findings.comment: Adequate set-up area and clearances at transformer equipment not documented, and AE Design approval of any deviations not shown. Provide either (1) dimensioned plans confirming 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance at all transformers, or (2) documented AE Design written approval of specific project deviations with approval conditions clearly noted on plans.
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. Neither sheet provides dimensioned set-up areas, vertical clearance measurements, or AE Design approval documentation for the transformer equipment. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad in a landscaped island adjacent to a driveway and sidewalk area. The constrained site layout with retaining walls and limited maneuvering space suggests that the standard 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance may be difficult to achieve without deviations. No AE Design approval documentation is visible on the plans authorizing any reduced clearances or alternative configurations.
findings.reasoning: Code allows for AE Design-approved deviations from standard set-up area and clearance requirements. However, any such deviations require documented AE Design approval with specific conditions. The preliminary plans show no evidence of such approval. Without either confirmation of standard set-up areas and clearances, or documented AE Design approval of deviations, compliance cannot be verified. The site's constrained layout strongly suggests that deviations from standard requirements may be necessary, but these must be explicitly approved and documented.

findings.comment: If transformer locations are within 20 feet of building features (windows, doors, stairs, fire escapes) per UCM § 1.10.4, transformer locations and clearances must be shown on building elevation sheets to verify compliance. Provide elevations if transformers are located adjacent to buildings.
findings.observation: The primary site plan set (39 sheets) does not include dedicated elevation sheets showing transformer, meter, or electrical equipment details. Sheet index in README.md lists sheets 1-39, which include site plan, utilities, grading, drainage, landscape, and construction details, but no architectural elevation sheets specific to building facades or electrical equipment elevations. Building heights are shown on Sheet 9 site plan data table, but no vertical cross-sections showing transformer locations relative to building features are provided.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer locations and clearances must be shown on elevation sheets to verify compliance with clearance requirements from windows, doors, stairs, fire escapes, and building overhangs. If the site plan set does not include elevation sheets that show transformers, this deficiency cannot be fully evaluated. It is possible that elevation sheets exist in a separate architectural drawing set not included in the primary site plan submission.

findings.comment: Existing transformer pad shown on survey (Sheet 4) must be depicted and labeled as 'Existing' or 'EX' on all applicable plan sheets, with notation indicating whether it will be retained, removed, or replaced.
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an existing transformer pad in the southeast corner of the property with a clear label 'TRANSFORMER PAD' visible in the bottom right area, along with existing overhead electric lines (OHE) and utility poles (marked TYP.). However, this existing transformer pad is NOT shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), or Sheet 11 (Grading Plan). The demolition plan (Sheet 8) notes 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines' but makes no specific reference to the existing transformer pad, and it is not marked for removal or abandonment.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when existing electrical facilities are present on a site, their locations must be shown on all applicable plan sheets. This informs Austin Energy and other stakeholders whether the existing transformer is being retained, abandoned, replaced, or relocated. The absence of the existing transformer from the new development plans creates ambiguity about its disposition and prevents clear visual coordination of existing vs. proposed infrastructure. The grouping guidance states: 'Transformer locations must be shown consistently across multiple plan sheets' and specifies this applies 'when existing transformers present on site.'

findings.comment: Transformer clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 must be clearly shown on the electrical plan with dimension lines indicating minimum clearance distances from buildings, structures, obstacles, and access areas.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations as simple rectangular symbols with no clearance dimensions, clearance zones, or buffer areas indicated around them. Vision analysis confirms: 'No clearance zones marked, No indication of dedicated electrical clearance zones, specific electrical maintenance access routes, or bollard locations protecting the electrical equipment.' Transformers are shown but with no notation of required clearance distances in any direction.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies detailed clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers including 10-ft clearance for hot-stick use areas adjacent to open areas or buildings, 15-ft clearance when facing confined spaces, 3-5 ft clearances from ventilated obstructions, 20-ft clearance from fire escapes, 5-12 ft clearance from building walls depending on material, and no covering above. These clearances must be shown on plans with dimensions and notations to document compliance. Without clearance zones depicted, review agencies cannot verify that the site design accommodates these requirements.

findings.comment: Provide plan and profile exhibits showing transformer locations, elevations, and proximity to existing electrical facilities and other buried utilities to verify clearances and identify conflicts.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric routing (blue lines) connecting service stubs to transformers and meters in plan view only. Sheet 21 references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains only water and wastewater utility profiles; no electrical profiles are provided. Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) similarly shows only water utility profiles in the 'Wtr-Ln-A' section. No profile view showing transformer locations, elevations, or proximity to existing electrical facilities (such as overhead transmission lines, underground utilities at depth, or utility conflicts) is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires 'georeferenced AutoCAD drawings that clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations, demonstrate sufficient clearances, and show access routes.' Plan and profile exhibits showing vertical relationships (elevations, depths, clearances) are necessary to demonstrate compliance with separation distances and to identify conflicts with other utilities. Vertical profiles showing how electrical routing crosses or interfaces with storm drain, water, wastewater, and other buried infrastructure are essential for construction sequencing and conflict resolution.

findings.comment: Indicate the horizontal and vertical distance between each transformer pad and the nearest existing overhead electric line to verify compliance with required clearance distances.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing overhead electric lines (OHE) running along the southern and eastern property boundaries. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) also depicts existing overhead electric lines but does not indicate distances or clearance relationships between the transformer pads and these overhead lines. No dimension lines, callouts, or notes specify the horizontal or vertical distance between any transformer pad and the nearest existing overhead line.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad placement must account for clearances to existing overhead electrical lines per National Electrical Safety Code (NESC) standards and Austin Energy design requirements. Showing the transformer pad location without indicating its distance from existing overhead lines creates ambiguity about whether clearances are adequate. This information is essential for Austin Energy design review and for construction coordination.

findings.comment: Identify all curbing that falls within transmission easements or along transformer equipment pad access routes, and label as 'Laydown Curb' per UCM § 1.14.4.E and Austin Energy requirements. Show curb profiles and clearance dimensions for access.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 20 states: 'All curbing within the electric transmission easement must be laydown curbing' and 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5 foot spacing).' The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows transmission easement boundaries and various curb details but does not explicitly show or label curbing as 'laydown curb' in the transmission easement areas. No drivable access routes to the transformer pads are shown, and therefore no corresponding laydown curb specifications are visible. Vision analysis of Sheet 11 confirms: 'Because there are no transformers depicted or located on this specific sheet, there is no visual indication or specific spot elevations demonstrating how grading directs drainage around them.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.14.4.E, laydown curbs (which provide lower profile and allow equipment access) are required when curbing is installed within transmission easements or along Austin Energy truck access routes to transformer pads located more than 6 feet from drivable surfaces. Standard curbs impede equipment access. Sheet 3 Block 16 notes specify that grading near transmission structures must be coordinated with Austin Energy. Without showing the transformer access routes and identifying required laydown curb locations, it cannot be verified that the design accommodates Austin Energy truck access for equipment installation and maintenance.

findings.comment: Show drivable access routes from the nearest parking/traffic area to each transformer pad, with dimensions indicating the distance. If distance exceeds 6 feet, show the dedicated access route design.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) do not show drivable access routes to the transformer pad locations. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows transformers but does not indicate how Austin Energy trucks would access them for installation and maintenance. The grouping guidance specifies: 'Equipment pads must be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for Austin Energy truck accessibility unless otherwise approved by AE Design.' Without showing access routes, it cannot be verified that the transformer pads are accessible.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad-mounted transformers require drivable access routes for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. If a transformer is located more than 6 feet from an existing parking or traffic area, a dedicated access route must be provided and documented on the plans. Showing transformer locations without indicating access routes creates ambiguity about whether Austin Energy can reach the equipment for installation, operation, and maintenance.

findings.comment: Provide profile view(s) showing how underground electrical routing crosses storm drain piping, including crossing location, elevation differences, separation distance, and any special protection required at crossing points.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) contains a note: 'See Sht. 19 for Profile.' However, Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) is a water/wastewater utility sheet and contains no electrical profiles. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows storm drain piping routing and details but does not overlay or cross-reference electrical routing. No profile view is provided that shows electrical conduit or cables crossing or running parallel to storm drain piping, including identification of crossing points, separation distances, or special construction details required at crossings.
findings.reasoning: When underground electrical routing crosses stormwater piping, special design considerations are required including clearance distances, use of conduit sleeves or casings at crossing points, and coordination of excavation depths. Per UCM § 1.16.0, 'georeferenced drawings' must clearly show these interactions. Without profiles showing electrical-storm drain crossings, the design cannot be reviewed for compliance with electrical and drainage standards, and the contractor cannot identify required construction sequences or protection measures.

findings.comment: Show transformer pad door locations and control positions on the electrical plan, and indicate clearance zones appropriate to each side per UCM § 1.10.4 based on equipment orientation and adjacent features.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads as simple rectangular symbols with no indication of door locations, swing arcs, clearance zones, or operational access areas. Vision analysis confirms: 'There is no indication of door locations or designated clearance zones around the transformer pads.' The transformer pad symbols do not differentiate between different sides of the pad or indicate which side has the operating door and controls.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, the clearance requirements for pad-mounted transformers vary depending on the equipment side. Sides with operating controls/doors ('hot-stick use areas') require 10-15 ft clearance depending on whether they face open space or confined space. Sides without controls require 3-5 ft clearance. Showing the door location and control side is essential for proper site design to ensure the specified clearances are available on the correct sides of the equipment. Without this detail, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: If transformer screening is proposed, show on site plan, landscape plan, and grading plan: screening wall/fence extent and dimensions, door swing clearances relative to screening, and landscape plantings around screening. If no screening is proposed, note 'No Screening' on electrical plan.
findings.observation: Vision analysis of all plan sheets confirms no transformer screening is shown. Sheet 21 electrical plan shows transformer pads as basic symbols with no screening details. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) makes no reference to transformer screening or landscape treatment around electrical equipment. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not indicate screening. No notes, elevations, or details show whether screening walls, fencing, berms, or landscaping are planned around the transformers.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when transformer screening is proposed to mitigate visual impact, site plans must clearly show 'Transformer screening extent, dimensions, and door swings on all plan sheets (site, grading, landscape).' This ensures that screening design does not interfere with required clearance zones or door operations, and allows Austin Energy to verify access compatibility. Screening details are also necessary for architectural and landscape integration review.

findings.comment: Transformer labels missing on required sheets or inconsistent. Establish consistent labeling (e.g., "Electrical Transformer Pad - Type [X], Size [Y] kVA") and show transformers on all required sheets: site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan (where applicable). Use a standard notation on all sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels transformers as "Electrical Transformer Pad" on the electrical plan. Sheet 9 labels one transformer as "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" on the site plan. Sheets 19, 31, 11, and 12 contain no transformer labels whatsoever because transformers are not depicted on these sheets. The irregular labeling, combined with the absence of transformers from required sheets, means that the reviewer cannot verify consistent identification of electrical infrastructure across the document set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that electrical infrastructure be clearly labeled on all required plan sheets. Consistent, informative labeling enables Austin Energy and the City to verify that all proposed equipment is accounted for and properly identified across all disciplines. The current labeling is inconsistent ("Electrical Transformer Pad" vs. "Transformer Pad (Typ.)") and incomplete (missing from landscape, wet utilities, grading, and storm plans). This prevents confident cross-reference of electrical equipment across the plan set.

findings.comment: Provide transformer pad dimensions (length × width × height where applicable) on all plans where transformers are shown, ensuring dimensions are consistent across sheets and adequate for the specified transformer kVA rating.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformers as rectangular symbols with no dimension callouts indicating pad width, length, or height. Sheet 9 shows one transformer symbol as a simple rectangle with no dimensions. Pad dimensions are not provided on either sheet, making it impossible to verify consistency or to confirm that the dimensions are adequate for the specified transformer size and clearance requirements.
findings.reasoning: Transformer pad dimensions must be consistent across all plan sheets and must be adequate for the specified transformer size. Different transformer kVA ratings require different pad sizes. Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad clearance requirements depend partly on equipment size. Without documented pad dimensions, reviewing agencies cannot verify design adequacy or construction completeness.

findings.comment: Provide electrical load calculations showing total connected load and demand for all buildings, and confirm that the proposed four transformers with specified kVA ratings are adequate to serve this load per Austin Energy requirements.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers serving 39 units across 8 buildings. The plan does not include a load calculation or documentation showing that four transformers are adequate to serve all buildings and units. No calculations, Austin Energy requirements letter, or specifications document is provided that confirms transformer capacity (kVA) is sufficient for the project's electrical load.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must be adequate to support Austin Energy coordination. Without documented electrical load calculations and transformer capacity specifications, it cannot be verified that the proposed transformers are adequate to serve the project. The grouping guidance states: 'Transformer quantity not adequate to serve all buildings in development' as a potential deficiency. While four transformers appear reasonable for 39 units, this must be documented with engineering calculations or Austin Energy requirements confirmation.

findings.comment: Transformers not delineated in legend as proposed utilities. Add a Utility Legend to the site plan, wet utilities plan, and electrical plan defining the symbols for: (1) Transformer Pad, (2) Proposed Underground Electric Line, (3) Electrical Meter, (4) Electrical Easement, and (5) Pull Box. Use consistent symbols across all sheets. Ensure symbols are actually applied on the plans.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) contains no utility legend. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) contains no utility legend defining transformer or meter symbols. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains a Legend in the top-right corner that defines two electrical symbols: "- E - Proposed Underground Electric" and "[Square symbol] Transformer Pad". However, on Sheet 19, neither of these symbols are actually drawn on the plan—the legend defines symbols that are not used. Sheets 11, 12, and 31 contain no transformer symbols or legends.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires plans to delineate proposed utilities clearly. A utility legend is the standard method for communicating utility symbols and line types. The absence of a consistent legend across the site plan set, combined with the fact that the legend on Sheet 19 defines symbols that are not actually used, violates the clarity requirement. Austin Energy and City reviewers expect a unified legend identifying all proposed electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines, easements) with symbols consistently applied across all relevant sheets.

findings.comment: Confirm with Austin Energy Design whether switchgear is required for the four-transformer configuration. If switchgear is required, show its location and integrate it into the electrical plan with proper labeling and coordination notes.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers but does not show a switchgear, load centers, or transmission interconnects linking the transformers. The grouping guidance states: 'Switchgear location not shown when required based on electrical service configuration' and 'Requires AE Design coordination to determine applicability.' With multiple transformers (four) proposed, it is unclear whether they are configured as independent service points or as a coordinated system requiring switchgear.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, when two or more transformers are proposed, Austin Energy may require switchgear for coordination and switching capability. The necessity of switchgear is determined during Austin Energy Design coordination. Without evidence of this coordination or a documented Austin Energy requirements letter, it cannot be determined whether switchgear is required and whether its location must be shown on plans.

findings.comment: Show and label the existing meter (with 'EX' or 'Existing' notation) on the electrical plan, site plan, and landscape plan. Include notation indicating whether it will be abandoned, removed, or retained and integrated into the new service design.
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) clearly shows an existing electrical meter labeled 'ELEC. METER' attached to the exterior wall of the main building structure. However, this existing meter is NOT shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), NOT shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and NOT shown on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). The demolition plan (Sheet 8) does not specifically reference the existing electrical meter, nor is it marked for removal or abandonment.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when existing electrical facilities are present on a site, their locations must be shown on all applicable plan sheets. Similar to the existing transformer, the existing meter disposition must be clear: is it being retained, removed, or replaced? Without showing the existing meter on the development plans, there is ambiguity about its status and how it relates to the new electrical service design.

findings.comment: Clearly identify the service configuration: if meters are served from a single point of service, show the service distribution enclosure and disconnect locations grouped with the meters. If each building has an independent service point, note that on the plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters (one per building) on building exteriors but does not show any disconnects or service distribution enclosures. The grouping guidance states: 'When two or more meters are installed at one location and served from one set of service conductors, meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location with a service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway.' With 8 buildings and 8 individual meters, the grouping/point-of-service configuration is unclear. No legend or notes explain the service configuration.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B, when multiple meters serve a single development, they must be coordinated as a grouped metering system if they share a point of service. If each building has its own individual service point, that must be clearly documented. Without showing disconnects and grouping configuration, it cannot be determined whether the design complies with grouped metering requirements.

findings.comment: On the site plan (Sheet 9), clearly show existing power poles and electric lines, indicate which will be removed/relocated/retained, and show any new poles or overhead electric routing required for the development. Include Austin Energy coordination notes referencing removal approvals.
findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) contains two callout boxes stating 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.' This indicates that existing utility poles and overhead electric lines are present on the site and must be coordinated for removal or relocation. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show these poles with specific location callouts, nor does it provide a utility coordination drawing showing which poles are to be removed vs. retained or relocated.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, plans must show any required utility relocation. The demolition plan notes indicate pole/electric line removal is necessary but provides no visual coordination drawing. The development site plan should show existing poles, indicate which are to be removed or relocated, and show any new poles or routing required for the development. Without this coordination visible on the final site plan, contractors may not clearly understand the scope of electrical work required.

findings.comment: Verify with City of Austin GIS or Austin Energy records whether a moonlight tower exists within 100 feet of the property. If yes, show guy wire locations and labels on plans, and provide documentation of required Moonlight Tower Construction Permit.
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not indicate the presence of a moonlight tower on or within 100 feet of the property. The grouping guidance notes: 'Moonlight tower locations are not defined in code and require verification with City GIS or Austin Energy records—this cannot be determined from plans alone unless the survey shows a moonlight tower.' The property location (3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704) would need to be cross-referenced with the City of Austin moonlight tower inventory.
findings.reasoning: Per Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201, construction within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or its guy wires requires special permits, protective barriers, and enhanced insurance. However, this information is not derivable from the submitted plans and requires external verification with City GIS or Austin Energy records. The grouping guidance explicitly states this 'cannot be determined from plans alone.'

findings.comment: Measure and show the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area. If any pad is within 4 feet, show bollard locations and spacing (minimum 4-inch galvanized rigid metal posts) designed to allow equipment door opening.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations but does not indicate distances to adjacent parking or driveway areas, nor are any bollards shown. No dimensions are provided that would allow verification of whether transformer pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas or outside this distance. Vision analysis confirms: 'There is no indication of dedicated electrical clearance zones, specific electrical maintenance access routes, or bollard locations protecting the electrical equipment.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, when pad-mounted transformers are located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas, 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards are required, spaced to allow equipment door opening. Bollards protect the equipment from vehicle damage. Without measuring distances from transformer pads to parking areas and showing required bollards, it cannot be verified that the site design protects equipment or meets code requirements.

findings.comment: Show transformer pad locations on the grading plan with spot elevations on all four sides of each pad, demonstrating that ground slopes direct drainage flow away from buildings and towards site drainage areas.
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows site contours, retaining walls, and drainage features but does not indicate transformer pad locations or spot elevations around them. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Because there are no transformers depicted or located on this specific sheet, there is no visual indication or specific spot elevations demonstrating how grading directs drainage around them.' Without transformers shown on the grading plan, it is impossible to verify that drainage slopes direct liquid flow away from buildings.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 1, grading around oil-filled pad-mounted transformer equipment must direct liquid flow away from buildings. This is a critical safety and environmental requirement. The grading plan must show transformer locations with spot elevations on all sides of the pad demonstrating that slopes direct flow away from building foundations and towards site drainage. Without this detail, code compliance cannot be verified and environmental risks cannot be assessed.

findings.comment: Show on the electrical plan the locations of all proposed electrical meters and reference existing/proposed gas meters, gas regulators, and other utilities to verify minimum 3-foot separation per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exterior walls but does not indicate proximity to gas meters, regulators, or other equipment within 3-foot separation distance. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows an existing 'GAS METER' attached to the left exterior wall of the main building structure. New site plans do not show gas meter locations or infrastructure, making it impossible to verify the 3-foot separation requirement between electrical and gas facilities.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C, meter locations must be at least 3 feet away from gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus. Without showing both electrical meter locations and gas utility locations on the same plan, this separation requirement cannot be verified. The absence of gas utility information from the electrical plan creates ambiguity about compliance.

findings.comment: Show disconnect locations on the electrical plan and indicate the distance from each meter. Verify that meter-to-disconnect distance does not exceed 20 feet and that they are within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exteriors and four transformers at various locations, but no disconnects are shown. The code requirement per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J states: 'Maximum distance between meter and disconnect is 20 feet; they must be within line of sight of each other and readily accessible.' Without showing disconnect locations, distances between meters and disconnects cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J, the meter-to-disconnect distance is limited to a maximum of 20 feet, and they must be within line of sight of each other. This ensures that the disconnect can be located quickly in an emergency and that the electrical service can be readily shut off. Without showing disconnects on the electrical plan, this code requirement cannot be reviewed or verified during plan check or construction.

findings.comment: Root barrier details are not shown on any landscape plan sheet. Trees proposed within 5-20 feet of underground electric equipment require root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) per UCM § 1.10.10.4, but no such details are provided. Add root barrier construction details specifying depth (minimum 4 feet) and placement (5 feet from equipment edge) for all affected trees.
applicableAreas: Areas within 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric infrastructure
findings.observation: Examined landscape sheets 31, 35, and 37 to identify root barrier details for trees proposed within 5-20 feet of underground electric equipment. The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows multiple underground electric lines and pull boxes distributed throughout the site, with some located between 5-20 feet of proposed tree planting areas based on visual proximity on the electrical plan. However, the landscape plans contain NO root barrier details, cross-sections, or notes specifying root barrier construction (depth and placement). Sheet 37 shows standard tree planting and protection details, but these address only tree protection fencing and general planting requirements—not root barriers required for underground utility clearances. No reference to root barrier specifications meeting UCM § 1.10.10.4 requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment edge) appears anywhere in the landscape documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that trees planted within 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment must have root barriers. The applicant's responsibility is to demonstrate this requirement is met by showing root barrier specifications on the plans. The complete absence of root barrier details is a failure to comply. While the grouping guidance notes that 'missing elements are deficiencies,' the presence of trees at these distances without the required accompanying root barrier specifications constitutes a failure to meet the code requirement. No assumption can be made that root barriers will be installed if not shown and specified on the plans.

findings.comment: Root barrier construction details are completely absent from the landscape plans. Provide a detail sheet showing root barrier construction with minimum 4-foot depth and positioning exactly 5 feet from underground equipment edge, per UCM § 1.10.10.4 requirements.
applicableAreas: Areas with trees proposed within 5-20 lateral feet of underground equipment
findings.observation: Reviewed all landscape detail sheets (Sheets 31, 35, 37) and supporting documentation for root barrier specifications. Sheet 37 contains standard City of Austin tree planting and protection details (tree protection fencing per 610S-4, shrub planting detail, tree planting detail with rootball specifications). No root barrier detail is present. The landscape plans reference standard details but none pertain to root barriers for utility clearances. Without a detail sheet showing depth and placement specifications, there is no means to verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.10.4 root barrier requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned exactly 5 feet from equipment edge).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies precise requirements for root barriers: minimum 4 feet deep and positioned 5 feet from the equipment edge. The applicant must demonstrate this through detail drawings and/or plan notes. The complete absence of any root barrier detail or specification means the requirement cannot be verified. This is not a case where details might be incorrect—no details exist at all. The deficiency is the missing specification itself.

findings.comment: Trees proposed near overhead electric line (southern boundary) have not been verified as utility-compatible species against ECM Appendix F. Verify all species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) in ECM Appendix F UC column and provide documentation. For any non-UC species within 15 feet of OHE, provide written Austin Energy approval.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric line runs and trees are proposed within 15 lateral feet
