findings.observation: Vision analysis of landscape plan Sheet 31 identified multiple trees (marked 'M' for mitigation trees) positioned along the southern property boundary. The sheet clearly shows the OHE (Overhead Electric) line labeled running the entire length of the southern boundary. Several proposed tree canopy circles visually overlap or are immediately tangent to the OHE line, with at least three 'M' trees having canopy circles crossing directly over the OHE line and utility pole symbols. From Sheet 32 (Tree List) and Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations), the proposed trees include Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, and Mexican Redbud. However, ECM Appendix F (the definitive reference for Utility-Compatible species identification) is not provided in the site plan documentation. Without access to the UC column of ECM Appendix F, the utility-compatible status of these species cannot be verified. The grouping guidance explicitly states that UC designation must be verified by cross-reference with the UC column of Appendix F, not by assumption based on species name or size. No Austin Energy approval letter, coordination note, or design stamp indicating approval for non-UC species placement is visible on the landscape plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that only utility-compatible (UC) trees be planted within 15 lateral feet of overhead electric distribution conductor or equipment. The critical point is that UC status is definitive—only species with 'x' in the UC column of ECM Appendix F qualify. The grouping guidance warns against common review errors: assuming all small trees are UC without Appendix F verification. Because Appendix F is not provided in the site plan, UC status cannot be determined from available evidence. Furthermore, the trees are positioned directly under the OHE line (southern boundary), which is within the 15-foot zone. Even if some species might be UC (Live Oak and Cedar Elm are typically UC), this cannot be confirmed without Appendix F. The fact that non-UC species may be among the proposed trees, combined with their proximity to the OHE line and lack of documented Austin Energy approval, constitutes a failure. The burden is on the applicant to demonstrate compliance through documentation.

findings.comment: Large trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak both with mature heights ≥40 feet) are proposed along the southern property boundary within the overhead electric line corridor. These species must be maintained at least 25 lateral feet from the OHE line per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Revise landscape plan to show either: (1) relocation of large trees to maintain 25-foot clearance from OHE line, or (2) substitution with smaller species (mature height <40 feet).
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric distribution line runs
findings.observation: Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations) specifies proposed shade trees: 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia) and 2 Live Oak (Quercus virginiana), both specified as 100 GAL. container grown with 4' caliper and 16' height minimum. Standard references (landscape industry data, ECM Appendix F) list Cedar Elm and Live Oak with mature heights in the range of 40-50 feet or greater, placing both species in the 'large tree' category (≥40 feet mature height per grouping definition). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows mitigation trees (M) positioned along the southern boundary where the OHE line is located. Vision analysis confirms at least three trees with canopy circles overlapping or directly tangent to the OHE line. No ECM Appendix F reference is provided in the site plan to definitively confirm mature height specifications, but based on standard horticultural data, both Cedar Elm and Live Oak commonly achieve or exceed 40 feet mature height. No verification that these large trees are positioned more than 25 feet from the overhead electric distribution line is evident on the landscape plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states: 'Large trees (mature height ≥40 feet) may not be planted within 25 lateral feet of overhead electric distribution conductor or equipment.' The proposed large trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak) are positioned directly along the OHE line at the southern boundary, well within 25 feet. The landscape plan does not show distance annotations or clearance verification. The applicant must demonstrate either (a) that the proposed trees are NOT large trees by providing mature height specifications from a qualified source (ECM Appendix F), or (b) that they are positioned more than 25 feet from the OHE line. Neither has been demonstrated. The conservative interpretation, given that both species are known to reach 40+ feet, is that large trees are proposed in violation of the 25-foot clearance requirement.

findings.comment: No License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is evident for trees/landscaping proposed within electric easements. Before installation of any landscaping, irrigation, or trees within electric easement areas, obtain License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement and provide copy to City. Add plan note: 'License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement obtained prior to installation of landscaping within electric easement areas' [date/agreement number to be inserted].
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas (5' Electric Easements per Mecey Subdivision plat)
findings.observation: Reviewed all landscape and supplementary documents for evidence of a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement for trees proposed within electric easements. Facts.md identifies two electric easements on the Mecey Subdivision plat: '5' Electric Easements (×2)' (Document Ref: Travis County Doc 73/76, Case C8S-75-160). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees (M for mitigation) distributed around the site perimeter, some of which visually appear to fall within or adjacent to easement areas based on the site layout. However, Sheet 31 does not display easement boundaries overlaid with the landscape plan, making it difficult to determine precisely which trees fall within easement areas from the landscape plan alone. More critically, the landscape plans, site plans, and supplementary documents contain NO reference to a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement, NO plan notes stating 'License Agreement obtained from Austin Energy Public Involvement,' and NO attached license agreement documentation. Per grouping guidance: 'License agreements are administrative documents that may not be attached at early review stages. Flag requirement for verification before certificate of occupancy.' However, per UCM § 1.10.10.3, the agreement must be 'obtained and filed before the activity occurs,' and missing license agreements result in certificate of occupancy holds.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that before landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings are installed within electric easement areas, a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement must be obtained and filed. The applicant's responsibility at site plan stage is to demonstrate awareness of this requirement through either (a) a reference to an obtained license agreement (date and agreement number), or (b) a plan note committing to obtain the agreement before construction. Without such documentation, the reviewer cannot confirm the requirement will be met. The presence of proposed trees within or likely within electric easement areas, combined with the complete absence of license agreement documentation, constitutes a deficiency. The grouping guidance acknowledges license agreements may not be attached at early review but flags for verification—this is that flag. The applicant must either provide evidence of a license agreement or add a plan note committing to obtain one before construction/installation of any landscaping within the electric easements.

findings.comment: Proposed trees are positioned within 10 lateral feet of overhead electric utility poles (southern boundary). Relocate trees to maintain minimum 10-foot lateral clearance from all utility poles, or provide distance callouts on landscape plan demonstrating compliance. Do not plant trees within 10 feet of poles per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: Utility pole locations along western and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) labels and identifies utility poles with 'x' symbols positioned along the overhead electric (OHE) line. Vision analysis confirms utility poles are located along the western and southern property boundaries, with at least two poles clearly marked along the southern OHE line. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows mitigation trees (M) and other proposed trees with canopy circles positioned directly along the southern boundary where the OHE line (and thus utility poles) is located. At least three 'M' trees have canopy circles visually overlapping or immediately tangent to utility pole symbols on the OHE line. No distance annotations are provided on the landscape plan to demonstrate the required 10-foot clearance from poles. The proximity of tree canopy circles to the pole symbols suggests distances are measured in single-digit feet, not 10 feet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that no trees be planted within 10 lateral feet of electric utility poles. The landscape plan shows trees with canopy circles overlapping utility pole locations. The burden of compliance is on the applicant to demonstrate the 10-foot clearance through either plan annotations (distance callouts) or relocation of trees. The visual evidence from the landscape plan suggests canopy overlap, which indicates non-compliance. Standard interpretation: if trees are not clearly shown to be at or beyond the 10-foot clearance distance, they are assumed to be in violation.

findings.comment: Underground electric facilities (conduits, duct banks, pull boxes, transformer pads, vaults) shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21) are not depicted on landscape plan (Sheet 31). To verify tree clearances from underground utilities per UCM § 1.10.10.4, add underground electric infrastructure to the landscape plan, showing all pulls boxes, transformers, duct banks, and service routes. This allows verification that trees do not violate 0-5 foot prohibition or 5-20 foot root barrier requirements.
applicableAreas: Entire site for underground electric infrastructure
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) contains a comprehensive site plan showing underground electric lines (blue lines), electrical pull boxes (circles), electrical transformer pads (squares), electrical meters on all buildings, overhead electric lines (OHE), and associated easements. The plan is detailed and clearly labeled. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) at the same scale (1" = 20') shows building footprints, parking areas, trees, shrubs, contours, water lines (W), storm drain lines (SD), and overhead electric (OHE) line. HOWEVER, Sheet 31 does NOT show the underground electric facilities visible on Sheet 21: no underground electric lines, no pull boxes, no transformer pads are depicted on the landscape plan. The notation on Sheet 31 lists 'Utility lines such as water (W), storm drain (SD), and overhead electric (OHE)' per the vision analysis, confirming that while OHE is shown, underground electric infrastructure is not. This is a coordination gap: the landscape plan cannot show proper tree clearance verification for underground utilities if those utilities are not depicted.
findings.reasoning: The grouping guidance emphasizes: 'A requirement met on the grading plan may still be missing from pond plan sheets, profile sheets, or detail sheets. If a requirement applies to multiple sheets, finding it on one sheet does not constitute a pass—verify each relevant sheet independently.' This is a coordination requirement: for landscape planners and reviewers to verify clearances between trees and Austin Energy facilities, those facilities must be shown on the landscape plan. The grouping requires 'Landscape Plans - Tree and shrub locations, species, mature sizes, mature canopy spread, root barrier details' and 'Utility Plans - Underground electric facilities routing, duct banks, vaults, manholes, transformer pads.' When electric utilities are shown on utility/electrical plans but NOT on landscape plans, the reviewer cannot verify compliance with clearance requirements. This is a classic coordination deficiency: missing information on a required plan that prevents compliance verification.

findings.comment: Trees proposed within restricted zones relative to overhead electric facilities (under OHE line, near utility poles) lack documented Austin Energy written approval. Any variation from UCM § 1.10.10.4 clearance or species requirements requires explicit Austin Energy approval. Provide one of the following: (1) Austin Energy approval letter/email with date, (2) plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative, or (3) Austin Energy Design approval stamp on plans. Alternatively, relocate trees to comply with required clearances without variation.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within clearance-restricted zones (under/near OHE line, near poles)
findings.observation: Vision analysis of landscape plan Sheet 31 shows mitigation trees (M) positioned directly along the southern property boundary where the OHE line runs, with canopy circles overlapping the OHE line and utility pole symbols. Sheet 35 identifies the proposed species: Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud. Based on standard horticultural data, Live Oak and Cedar Elm are large trees (≥40 feet mature height). Texas Mountain Laurel and Mexican Redbud are smaller species (20-25 feet typically). The landscape plan shows trees positioned under/near the OHE line without (a) distance annotations demonstrating >15 feet (for non-UC species) or >25 feet (for large trees) clearance, or (b) explicit notation of Austin Energy approval, Austin Energy Design stamp, or attached approval letter/email. The grouping guidance lists 'Missing Austin Energy written approval for variations' as a common violation pattern: 'Landscape plans show trees within restricted zones (e.g., within 15 feet of overhead distribution, within 5 feet of underground equipment) without documented Austin Energy approval letter, email, or plan note.' This situation matches that pattern. The trees are within restricted zones relative to the OHE line, and no Austin Energy approval is documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states that any variation from the planting distances or species requirements requires explicit written approval from Austin Energy. The grouping identifies acceptable documentation forms: (1) Austin Energy approval letter/email attached to plan set or referenced by date, (2) plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative, or (3) Austin Energy Design plan stamp with specific approval notation. None of these appear on the landscape plans. The trees shown under/near the OHE line represent a variation from standard clearance requirements (they are within 15 feet of overhead distribution, and some appear to be within or adjacent to utility pole locations). Without documented Austin Energy approval for this variation, the requirement is not met. Per the grouping: 'Acceptable documentation includes: Austin Energy approval letter/email attached to plan set or referenced by date in plan notes; Plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative; Austin Energy Design plan stamp with specific approval notation.' The complete absence of such documentation, combined with trees positioned in restricted zones, constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: Proposed tree species cannot be verified as utility-compatible without ECM Appendix F. Provide either: (1) a copy of ECM Appendix F with UC column marked for all proposed species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud), or (2) a letter from City forester confirming UC status of each species. Species shown near overhead electric facilities (southern boundary) must be verified as having 'x' in the UC column of ECM Appendix F per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: All areas where proposed trees are within 15 feet of overhead electric distribution or 50 feet of overhead transmission
findings.observation: Sheet 35 lists proposed tree species: Live Oak (Quercus virginiana), Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia), Texas Mountain Laurel (Sophora secundiflora), and Mexican Redbud (Cercis canadensis var. mexicana). Both common names and scientific names are provided, which allows cross-reference against ECM Appendix F. However, the site plan documentation does NOT include ECM Appendix F itself. The grouping guidance emphasizes: 'Cross-reference proposed tree species (common or scientific name from landscape plan) against ECM Appendix F table. Only species with x in the UC column qualify as utility-compatible.' And: 'Common review errors to avoid: Assuming all small trees (<20 feet) are UC without verifying UC column.' Without access to the actual ECM Appendix F document, the UC status of these species cannot be definitively determined from the site plan alone. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows some trees positioned near the overhead electric line (southern boundary) where utility-compatible species are required (within 15 feet of OHE). While Live Oak and Cedar Elm are commonly known to be utility-compatible species in Austin practice, this should be verified against the actual Appendix F table, not assumed. Texas Mountain Laurel is noted in the grouping regulatory overview as a possible UC species (25-foot example), but again, definitive verification requires Appendix F.
findings.reasoning: The issue is evidentiary: the applicant must provide proof that species used near electric facilities comply with the UC requirement. Proof consists of either (a) ECM Appendix F included in the site plan documentation with UC column marked for each species, or (b) a reference letter from the City's urban forester or landscape code reviewer confirming UC status. The site plan provides species names but not the definitive Appendix F verification. While it is likely that Live Oak and Cedar Elm are UC (they are well-known compatible species), the grouping guidance explicitly warns against assumption. Without the Appendix F document in the site plan set, the UC status is 'unclear'—which under the review protocol means it cannot be confirmed. This becomes a 'fail' if any trees shown near electric facilities are later found (via Appendix F review) to be non-UC. For now, it is 'unclear' because the species names alone, without Appendix F, are insufficient proof of compliance.

findings.comment: Clarify whether a separate Master Electrical Plan from the MEP consultant is required for this multi-building residential development. If required, provide the master electrical plan showing loads for all buildings and service routing strategy per Reviewer Convention.
findings.observation: This is a master planned development with 39 townhome units across 8 buildings in a unified site plan, but it is not a multi-lot subdivision with separate lot development phases. The single site plan shows all proposed buildings and infrastructure in one development. No separate master electrical plan from the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) consultant is provided in the supplementary documents or referenced in the plan set. The applicability note states "Only for master planned developments with multiple lots" - the interpretation of whether this unified multi-building development triggers the master plan requirement is ambiguous.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item's applicability language states "Only for master planned developments with multiple lots." This site is a single unified development of 39 units in 8 buildings, not a platted subdivision with separate lots held by different owners. However, the phrase "master planned development" could potentially include any large multi-building development. The grouping does not define this term precisely. Without a clear definition distinguishing single-site multi-building developments from true master planned multi-lot subdivisions, the applicability cannot be definitively determined. If this project type is intended to require a separate master plan from an MEP consultant, that requirement should be clarified.

findings.comment: Service type (overhead or underground) is not clearly designated on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Add a clear note or legend entry on each required plan sheet stating the service type (e.g., 'Proposed Service: Underground Electric Distribution' or similar) to eliminate ambiguity and ensure all required sheets clearly identify whether the development uses overhead, underground, or mixed service type.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly designates the service type as UNDERGROUND through explicit labels 'Underground Electric Line' pointing to the routing, blue line styling, and underground pull box locations. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows both existing overhead electric (OHE) on the western boundary AND proposed transformer pad, but the relationship between these and the service type is ambiguous - is the service overhead from the OHE source into an underground distribution on site? Or is there both overhead and underground proposed? The sheet does not explicitly state 'Service Type: Underground' or similar designation. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows OHE (Overhead Electric) lines on the southern boundary but provides no clarity on the overall service type for the development. A reviewer examining Sheets 9 and 31 cannot definitively determine whether the development is served by overhead service, underground service, or a combination without cross-referencing Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires service type (overhead or underground) to be 'clearly designated' on plans. While Sheet 21 makes this clear through labeling and line styling, the requirement is for the designation to appear on all required plan sheets (site plan, landscape plan, and electrical plans). Sheets 9 and 31 do not clearly designate the overall service type. The grouping's 'Common Violation Patterns' specifically lists 'Service type ambiguity: Plans show both overhead and underground elements without clearly designating which service type applies.' A plan reviewer examining the site plan and landscape plan should be able to immediately determine the service type without referencing other sheets.

findings.comment: Cannot verify vault requirements from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy Design documentation (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes) confirming the approved service type (pad-mounted transformer, vault, or specialized niche). If pad-mounted transformers are approved, verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements per UCM § 1.5.1.6.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads (5 total) but no indication of vault structures. The facts.md indicates the site is located in Austin, TX but does NOT place it within the Downtown Network Area per facts.md statement "Regulating Plan: None". UCM § 1.11.5 defines the Network Area boundaries where vaults are permitted. The applicability note in the checklist states vaults are required only "Inside Network Area: vaults required for services above 800 amps. Outside Network Area: vaults generally not permitted - only pad-mounted transformers or specialized niches." The site appears to be outside the Network Area, suggesting pad-mounted transformers (which are shown) would be the appropriate service type. However, without formal Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the service type decision and demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 (Clearances from AE Padmount Equipment) if pedestals/niches are used, the determination cannot be conclusively verified.
findings.reasoning: The determination of whether vaults are required cannot be made from site plan features alone - it requires (1) confirmation of location relative to Network Area boundaries, and (2) Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the approved service type. While the site appears to be outside the Network Area (suggesting pad-mounted transformers are appropriate), formal AE Design documentation is required to verify this determination. The absence of such documentation means the applicant's choice of pad-mounted transformers cannot be verified as AE-approved.

findings.comment: Existing electric facilities (Austin Energy transmission/distribution structures, poles, guys, anchors, transformers) are not clearly shown and identified on the site plan. While an existing overhead electric line runs along the southern property boundary per the site plan, the specific utility pole locations and pole numbers supporting that line are not clearly marked. All existing Austin Energy facilities on or adjacent to the site must be shown with accurate locations per UCM § 1.16.0(1)(ii).
findings.observation: The vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identified 'existing electric facilities and easements along the boundaries' including 'An Overhead Electric line, marked by the linetype "- OHE -", runs along the entire southern property boundary' and 'An easement labeled "5' Elec. & Tele. Easement" is noted near the bottom right (southeast) corner' and 'An easement labeled "Electric Easement" is noted along the eastern property line boundary.' However, the site plan does not show specific identification of existing Austin Energy infrastructure such as utility pole numbers, transformer identification, guy wire locations, anchor points, or the locations and identifications of existing distribution structures. Facts.md does not list any existing AE facilities recorded in the property description, suggesting existing AE infrastructure is limited to the boundary easements and overhead line.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires showing 'existing AE infrastructure' and the grouping definition specifies 'Verify all existing AE transmission/distribution structures, poles, guys, anchors, and transformers are shown with accurate locations.' While the overhead electric line and easements along the southern and eastern boundaries are referenced on Sheet 9, the specific existing AE facilities (such as utility pole locations, pole numbers, or transformer identification) are not clearly marked with locations and identifications. For the existing overhead electric line along the southern boundary, the specific utility poles supporting that line should be identified and located on the site plan.

findings.comment: Clarification needed regarding the two transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 and whether they represent separate services with different voltages. Provide Austin Energy documentation (ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement) confirming whether the two transformers are part of a single point of service at one voltage, or whether exceptions to UCM § 1.16.0(5) have been approved for multiple service points or voltages. If the transformers are step-down stages of a single service, add labeling to Sheet 21 clarifying the service configuration and voltage(s).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows two electrical transformer pads, which may indicate two service points, but the vision analysis and detailed examination do not reveal explicit documentation of service voltage or whether exceptions to the one-POS/one-voltage rule have been approved. The plan shows: 'Two proposed transformers shown, and both are explicitly designated as pad-mounted. One is located on the western side of the property...The second is located on the eastern side of the property.' The question is whether these two transformers serve different buildings with different voltages (which would violate the one-voltage rule) or whether they are both serving the same development at the same voltage (which would be acceptable step-down transformers). The blocks.md for Sheet 21 does not specify the voltage(s) for each transformer. No documentation from Austin Energy (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement) was provided that would confirm whether exceptions to the one-POS/one-voltage rule have been approved.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) allows 'only one point of service and one service voltage' unless exceptions are 'approved by Austin Energy Design.' The presence of two transformers on the plan is not inherently a violation if they are both part of a single service point and serve the same voltage. However, without explicit documentation of the service voltage and Austin Energy approval for the transformer configuration, it cannot be verified whether the requirement is met. The grouping's regulatory overview states: 'Several infrastructure requirements cannot be determined from site plan review alone and require formal determination by Austin Energy during the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) review process' and specifically lists 'Vaults and pedestals: Service type selection is made during AE Design coordination and documented in Letter of Agreement or ESPA approval.' Similarly, the one-POS/one-voltage requirement requires Austin Energy confirmation. This item cannot be marked pass without evidence of AE approval, nor can it be marked fail without evidence of AE non-compliance.

findings.comment: Current Austin Energy contact information (phone number and department name) is not provided on the cover sheet or plan sheets. Add a contact block with Austin Energy department phone number and current contact information for coordination purposes.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 1 (Cover) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) and all other plan sheets for Austin Energy contact information. Sheet 1 (Cover) contains contact information for City of Austin - Water and Wastewater Utility, Austin Water, and Austin Fire Department, but no Austin Energy contact block with phone numbers, addresses, or department names. Sheet 3 contains utility-related notes but no standalone contact information block for Austin Energy.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.16.0 requires current Austin Energy contact information to be shown on plan sheets to enable coordination. The absence of contact information (phone number, department name, address) means developers and contractors cannot readily reach Austin Energy for required coordination. The presence of contact information for other city departments (Water, Fire) but not Austin Energy constitutes a deficiency in providing this required information.

findings.comment: Electric Transmission Notes are included on Sheet 3 (Block 20), but no transmission infrastructure, transmission structures, or transmission easements are shown on the site plan. Remove the 16 Electric Transmission Notes, or provide evidence of transmission infrastructure presence. If transmission facilities are located adjacent to the property, obtain and reference a specific Austin Energy coordination letter confirming transmission proximity and the applicability of these notes.
applicableAreas: Austin Energy Transmission Notes on Sheet 3
findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains 'Electric Transmission Notes' (Block 20) with 16 detailed notes addressing transmission easement requirements, clearances, pre-construction meetings, barricades, and construction coordination. Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) using vision analysis specifically searching for transmission infrastructure. Result: No transmission towers, transmission structures, transmission poles, or transmission easement labels are shown on the site plan. The site shows only 5-foot distribution electric easements and standard overhead distribution lines (OHE notation). Facts.md confirms plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements (distribution voltage) but lists no transmission easements or transmission structures on the property.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.14.0 defines transmission facilities as operating at 60kV phase-to-phase or higher and establishes that transmission-specific requirements apply only 'when transmission infrastructure is involved' or when development is within 100 feet of transmission line wires. The site plan shows no transmission infrastructure, transmission structures, or transmission easements. Including detailed transmission notes (addressing 48-hour pre-construction meetings, transmission easement road requirements, 25-foot clearance zones, and OSHA transmission safety) when no transmission infrastructure is shown or present on the plans constitutes inclusion of inapplicable notes.

findings.comment: The four Electric Notes on Sheet 3 contain non-standard wording with additions and modifications to the required text. Replace all four notes with the exact text from the current General Site Plan Notes document. The General Site Plan Notes document preface states that changing the required text will result in application rejection.
applicableAreas: Austin Energy Notes section on Sheet 3
findings.observation: Transcribed the complete text of the four Electric Notes on Sheet 3 (Blocks 8 and 14) and compared each against the standard four notes specified in the grouping's Regulatory Overview section. All four required notes are present, but each contains material modifications and additions beyond the standard text: Note 1 adds 'Austin Energy will perform all tree work in compliance with Chapter 25-8, Subchapter B...'; Note 2 changes 'shall' to 'of this subdivision/lot shall' and adds a full sentence about Chapter 25-8 compliance and easement location; Note 3 replaces 'proposed overhead electrical facilities' with 'proposed overhead electric facilities designed to provide electric service to this project' and adds 'The owner shall include Austin Energy's work within the limits of construction for this project'; Note 4 changes 'owner' to 'owner of the property' and adds two sentences about rendering electric service and cost responsibility.
findings.reasoning: The General Site Plan Notes document preface states: 'Changing the required text in your plan set will result in rejection of the application.' The grouping reinforces this requirement, stating 'Notes must use the exact wording provided in the current General Site Plan Notes document.' The four notes on Sheet 3, while addressing the correct topics, have been substantively modified with additional clauses, different word order, and supplementary text. These modifications constitute non-standard wording that deviates from the required standard text.

findings.comment: Network Area status must be verified by cross-reference to the official Network Area Map per UCM § 1.11.5. If site is within Network Area, duct bank design coordination with Austin Energy Network Design (512-505-7682) must be documented on the electrical sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric service routing to four transformer pads and buildings. However, no documentation is provided confirming whether the site is within the Downtown Network Area boundaries per UCM § 1.11.5 Network Area Map. The grouping explicitly states 'Network Area determination requires cross-referencing the project address against the official Network Area Map... as this cannot be determined from site plans alone.' No duct bank design for a Network distribution system loop is visible on any sheets. The Master Comment Report references a Bluebeam review from Austin Energy but those comments are not provided in the submitted documentation.
findings.reasoning: Applicability of EL-19.1 depends entirely on confirming that the site is within Network Area boundaries AND will tie into Network distribution system. The project address (3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704, South Lamar area) location relative to the downtown Network Area cannot be verified from the site plan documents alone. No Network Area determination letter or ESPA documentation is provided. Without this external verification, the applicability cannot be confirmed, and therefore the deficiency cannot be definitively assessed.

findings.comment: Obtain Austin Energy ESPA approval documentation to determine if loop system is required for this site. If required, show loop system design on all applicable plan sheets per UCM § 1.10.4.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed underground electric lines with routing from transformers to pull boxes and building meters. However, no loop system design is depicted, labeled, or referenced on this or any other sheet. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when loop system is required for the site per Austin Energy service requirements.' No Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval letter or Austin Energy correspondence confirming loop system requirement is present in the submitted documentation. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references Bluebeam comments (not provided) which may contain details about loop system requirements.
findings.reasoning: Loop system is a specialized service configuration required only in certain Austin Energy network conditions. The preliminary site plan documents do not include ESPA approval documentation that would clarify whether a loop system is required for this project. Without the ESPA determination, the applicability cannot be confirmed. The grouping explicitly requires 'Austin Energy ESPA approval letters and correspondence confirming loop system requirement' to establish applicability.

findings.comment: If dual feed electricity service is being requested, provide electrical load calculations, service configuration details on the electrical site plan, and Austin Energy approval letter specifically addressing dual feed service per UCM § 1.5.2.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows what appears to be a single electrical service configuration with four transformer pads serving the 39 townhome units. No dual feed electrical service is mentioned in the electrical design, electrical load calculations, or on any plan sheets. No Austin Energy approval letter specifically addressing dual feed is present in the submitted documentation. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when dual feed service is requested,' which appears not to be the case based on the preliminary design shown.
findings.reasoning: Dual feed service is a specialized configuration where a site receives power from two separate Austin Energy service points. This is typically requested for large commercial or critical facilities requiring redundancy. The preliminary electrical design shown on Sheet 21 does not indicate a dual feed configuration. Without evidence of a dual feed request, this item appears not applicable. However, the final determination cannot be confirmed without Austin Energy ESPA documentation.

findings.comment: Obtain and provide Austin Energy's Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval letter which contains the determination of whether line extension is required to serve the site, and if required, documentation of Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC) or line extension fees per UCM § 1.3.12.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformer pads and underground service routing to the buildings. No plan notes reference line extension, Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC), line extension fees, or any line extension requirements. The grouping states that line extension determination 'cannot be determined from site plans alone' and 'is made exclusively by Austin Energy during the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) review process.' No ESPA approval documentation is provided in the submitted plans or supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report confirms 'AE completeness check complete' but the actual ESPA letter with line extension determination is not provided.
findings.reasoning: Whether a line extension is required to serve the site is a technical determination made exclusively by Austin Energy during ESPA review based on existing infrastructure capacity and location. This determination is not visible in the site plan documents. Without the ESPA documentation that contains Austin Energy's line extension determination, the applicability cannot be confirmed. The preliminary electrical design assumes service is available, but whether extension of existing infrastructure is required remains undetermined.

findings.comment: Confirm in writing that the site at 3759 Valley View Road is within Austin Energy's service territory. If confirmed, ensure all Austin Energy standards and references remain on plans. If outside service territory, remove all Austin Energy references and notes from plans.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) includes Site Plan Release Note item (e) stating 'Water and wastewater service will be provided by the City of Austin (or identify the service provider if other than the City of Austin).' This phrasing indicates the service provider for water/wastewater may not be confirmed as City of Austin. However, the equivalent note for electrical service is not explicit on the plans. The site location is in Austin city limits (jurisdiction confirmed as 'City of Austin — Full Purpose'), but specific verification that the site is within Austin Energy's electrical service territory is not documented on the plans or in supplementary documents. Without explicit confirmation of Austin Energy service territory inclusion, compliance with Code of Ordinances § 15-9-1 cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: Code of Ordinances § 15-9-1 establishes service territory boundaries. Sites outside Austin Energy's service territory must have all Austin Energy references and notes removed from plans. Conversely, sites within the territory must maintain appropriate Austin Energy references. The grouping requires 'site location relative to Austin Energy service boundaries' and states 'if outside AE territory, plans should not reference AE standards.' The submission contains multiple Austin Energy design criteria references (Sheet 3 transmission clearances, Master Comment Report electric review), which implies territory inclusion, but explicit confirmation is not provided.

findings.comment: Determine whether the site is in a dual service area between Austin Energy and another utility provider. If so, and if non-territorial service is requested, complete and submit the Public Utility Commission Service Area Exception Application per Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act.
codeCitations: Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act (state law)
applicableAreas: Service provider selection in dual territory areas
findings.observation: No documentation is provided indicating whether the site is located in a dual service area where both Austin Energy and another utility provider operate. No Public Utility Commission Service Area Exception Application or service provider selection documentation is present in the submitted materials. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when development is in dual service area between Austin Energy and another provider AND requests service from non-territorial provider.' No evidence of this scenario is apparent from the site plan documents or supplementary files.
findings.reasoning: PUC Service Area Exception Applications are required only when a customer in a dual service area (where both Austin Energy and another provider operate) requests service from the non-territorial provider. This is a state-level regulatory requirement under the Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act. The site location relative to dual service areas cannot be determined from site plan documents alone, and no service provider selection documentation is provided that would indicate this is applicable. The grouping explicitly requires 'Service territory maps, provider selection documentation, PUC application submittal' to assess this item.

findings.comment: Building electrical plans must clearly show the meter location and electrical service configuration, with explicit labeling of the boundary between Austin Energy-owned facilities (up to and including meter) and customer-owned facilities (load side of meter). Customer-owned conduit and cable are under City Electrical Inspector jurisdiction and should not be submitted for Austin Energy approval. This determination cannot be made from site plan review alone; verification is required during building plan stage.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) at the site plan stage shows only a high-level service routing diagram with transformer locations, underground line routing, pull boxes, and meters. The distinction between Austin Energy-owned infrastructure (up to meter) and customer-owned infrastructure (from meter/load side) is not explicitly shown or labeled on the site plan. The specific identification of customer-owned conduit and cable on the load side of the meter typically requires building electrical plans with detailed electrical room design and service panel locations. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when customer-owned conduit and cable on load side of meter is proposed' and requires 'Electrical service design, meter location, ownership boundaries; customer-owned facilities beyond meter point are under City Electrical Inspector jurisdiction, not Austin Energy.'
findings.reasoning: This deficiency addresses a jurisdictional issue: customer-owned facilities beyond the meter point fall under City of Austin Building/Electrical Inspector jurisdiction, not Austin Energy jurisdiction. The site plan documents do not show the interior building electrical design or meter room configuration that would clarify where the meter is located and what facilities are customer-owned. This determination requires building electrical plans rather than site plan review. However, to avoid future confusion, the site plan should either clarify this boundary or the building plans must show the proper jurisdictional delineation.

findings.comment: Electrical room design and exterior door access requirements will be verified during building plan review per Austin Energy requirements under UCM Section 1. Building electrical plans must show each electrical room with an exterior-accessible door for Austin Energy service access, proper clearances, ventilation, and fire-rated walls as required.
findings.observation: The Site Plan (Sheet 9) provides overall site layout and building footprints for eight multi-unit townhome buildings. Visual analysis of the site plan found 'no rooms within the building footprints labeled as electrical rooms' and 'no doors explicitly labeled or marked as electrical room doors on any of the buildings.' The interior building electrical room design and door configuration are architectural/building plan elements not typically depicted on site plans. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when electrical room is provided in building' and requires 'Building plans, electrical room design, exterior access per Austin Energy requirements.' These details are documented on building electrical plans, not site plans.
findings.reasoning: Electrical room exterior door requirements are specified in Austin Energy design standards (UCM Section 1) to ensure that Austin Energy service personnel can access metering and service equipment without entering tenant-occupied spaces. This is a building-level design requirement verified during building plan review, not a site plan-level requirement. The site plan review stage does not typically include verification of interior building room configurations or door placements. This deficiency should be assessed during building electrical plan review with the City Electrical Inspector and Austin Energy reviewers.

findings.comment: Coordinate with Austin Energy to determine the voltage class of existing overhead electric (OHE) lines shown on the property perimeter. If lines are transmission-class (69kV or higher), implement the tailgate safety meeting requirement with Austin Energy Transmission C&M per UCM § 1.14.0 and add the requirement to construction documents. If distribution-class (<60kV), standard distribution clearance and safety requirements apply.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains a section titled 'Electric Transmission Notes' referencing transmission clearances and UCM transmission requirements. Sheet 21 shows dashed lines labeled 'OHE' (Overhead Electric) running along the property perimeter. However, the voltage class of these overhead electric lines is not specified on either sheet. The grouping defines 'Transmission vs. Distribution Facilities' as transmission being ≥60kV phase-to-phase (Austin Energy operates at 69kV, 138kV, or 345kV) and distribution being <60kV (typically 12.5kV). The sheet notes and visual depiction do not identify whether the existing OHE lines are transmission-class (69kV+) or distribution-class (12.5kV), making it impossible to determine if the transmission safety meeting requirement applies.
findings.reasoning: The tailgate safety meeting requirement per UCM § 1.14.0 applies only when site work is 'adjacent to or affects transmission facilities' defined as ≥60kV. Distribution facilities (12.5kV) have different, less stringent requirements. The site plan documents show existing overhead electric lines but do not specify their voltage class. Transmission structures are 'substantially larger—taller poles, wider spacing, conductors spread further apart' than distribution, but without explicit voltage information or structural descriptions confirming transmission-class infrastructure, the voltage level cannot be determined from the plans alone. This determination would require coordination with Austin Energy to identify the existing line voltage.

findings.comment: If cranes or other mechanical equipment will be used during construction near existing Austin Energy facilities (existing OHE lines shown on property perimeter), crane operating plans must include Austin Energy facility clearance analysis. Implement the crane safety personnel pre-construction safety meeting requirement per UCM § 1.14.3.2 and specify minimum clearances: 20 feet for transmission facilities or 10 feet for distribution facilities per OSHA 1926.1400.
findings.observation: No construction methodology plan, equipment plan, or crane use documentation is included in the submitted site plan documents. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when cranes will be used during construction near Austin Energy facilities.' The site plan depicts eight multi-story townhome buildings (up to 6-plex units) on a 2.16-acre site in a residential area. Construction of these buildings will likely require crane use for heavy material handling and roof assembly, and the site is adjacent to existing overhead electric lines. However, specific crane operation plans and proximity analysis are construction document-level details, not site plan-level details.
findings.reasoning: Crane safety requirements per UCM § 1.14.3.2 address operational safety during construction when cranes are in proximity to electric facilities. Detailed crane operating plans, equipment specifications, and crew safety briefing requirements are documented during the construction document and permitting phases, not the site plan phase. While the site plan provides sufficient information to infer that cranes may be needed and electric facilities exist, the specific crane safety documentation cannot be assessed at the site plan review stage. This should be addressed during building permit and construction document review.

findings.comment: Notice of Electrical Hazard meeting with AE Transmission Construction & Maintenance not documented. Schedule and conduct pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy Transmission (Contact: Andrew Perez 512-505-7153; Chuck Hendry 505-7151 if cranes used) at least 48 hours before construction begins. Submit meeting confirmation documentation with grading and demolition permit applications.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains Austin Energy transmission notes requiring: 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction. Call Andrew Perez at 512 505 7153 to schedule a tailgate safety meeting.' This requirement is clearly documented on the plans. However, no documentation, meeting minutes, confirmation letter, or other evidence is provided in the submitted site plan materials indicating that this required pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy Transmission has been scheduled or completed.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires a Notice of Electrical Hazard meeting with Austin Energy Transmission Construction & Maintenance before demolition begins (when demolition or grading near transmission structures is proposed). While this site plan document shows the requirement for a pre-construction safety meeting on Sheet 3, the site plan application materials do not include evidence that the meeting has been scheduled or held. Without documentation of compliance with this pre-construction coordination requirement, it cannot be verified that the project is proceeding safely with proper AE Transmission awareness.

findings.comment: Provide CAD file showing plan view of all building footprints overlaid on transmission line easement boundary with dimensions showing distances from transmission structures. Coordinate with Austin Energy to verify clearance compliance.
findings.observation: No transmission easement is shown on the site plans (Sheets 9 and 21), therefore no CAD overlay showing building footprints relative to transmission line easement can be verified. Multiple electric easements are labeled (5', 15' widths) on the property perimeter, but the transmission easement boundary is not depicted. Without the transmission easement depicted and building footprints overlaid, accurate clearance measurement cannot be performed.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires CAD files showing building footprint overlaid on transmission easement for accurate clearance verification when buildings encroach into easements. The absence of the transmission easement on the plans prevents verification of clearances. While this site shows electric easements, the transmission easement referenced in Sheet 3 coordination notes is not depicted, making it impossible to verify that buildings maintain required clearances from transmission structures.

findings.comment: Landscaping in transmission areas not approved by AE transmission reviewer. Revise landscape plan to remove trees from transmission easement and 25-foot clearance zones around transmission structures. Obtain Austin Energy transmission reviewer approval of final landscape plan demonstrating compliance with 25-foot clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees planted along the southern boundary of the property in proximity to an overhead electric (OHE) line. The landscaping plan includes multiple tree planting symbols (large circles) positioned near this overhead electric facility. However, there are no clearance zone notations, no warnings, and no indication that Austin Energy transmission reviewer approval was obtained for this landscaping plan. No documentation of AE transmission review or approval is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires landscaping in transmission areas to be approved by Austin Energy transmission reviewer. Sheet 3 transmission notes explicitly state: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' The landscape plan shows tree plantings without documented compliance with these clearances or AE approval. Trees planted within clearance zones pose safety hazards and violate transmission protection requirements.

findings.comment: Inter-departmental agreement or MOU not obtained between AE and other city departments regarding overlapping easement requirements. Submit inter-departmental agreement or MOU between Austin Energy, Austin Water, and City Watershed Protection Department addressing transmission easement and drainage easement overlaps. Agreement must clarify access rights, maintenance responsibilities, and emergency protocols.
findings.observation: The site plan and facts show multiple overlapping utility easements: (1) Austin Energy electric easements (5', 15' widths) shown on Sheets 9 and 11; (2) City of Austin drainage easement (0.130 acres, NE corner of site per facts.md); (3) Austin Water wastewater and water easements. Sheet 3 contains extensive Austin Energy transmission easement coordination requirements. However, no inter-departmental agreement or MOU between Austin Energy and other city departments (such as Austin Water Watershed Protection or Public Works) is evident in the submitted materials documenting how overlapping easement requirements will be managed.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires inter-departmental agreement or MOU when transmission easements or facilities overlap with other department jurisdictions. While the facts show multiple city departments have interests (Austin Energy, Austin Water, City Watershed Protection), no documentation is provided showing coordination agreements, MOUs, or formal communication between departments. Overlapping easements create complex access and maintenance scenarios that require formal inter-agency coordination.

findings.comment: Austin Water approval not explicitly documented for overlapping easement coordination with Austin Energy easements. Submit confirmation from Austin Water that water/wastewater service plans have been coordinated with Austin Energy regarding overlapping or adjacent easement requirements and construction impacts.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 includes approval letters from Austin Water confirming adequate capacity for water and wastewater service. The facts show a City of Austin drainage easement (0.130 acres) on the site. However, the Austin Water approval documentation on Sheet 3 does not explicitly address coordination of water/wastewater easements with overlapping Austin Energy electric easements. The coordination between Austin Water and Austin Energy utilities is not documented beyond the general approvals.
findings.reasoning: When Austin Water and Austin Energy easements overlap, explicit coordination is necessary to address access, maintenance, and potential conflicts. The facts show both utilities have interests on this site, but the submitted materials do not demonstrate that Austin Water and Austin Energy have coordinated their respective requirements. While Austin Water has provided service capacity approval, coordination regarding overlapping easement impacts is not evident.

findings.comment: Proposed construction entrance location not clearly shown on site plan. If a temporary stabilized construction entrance is required for construction access, clearly label its location on the site plan and confirm it does not encroach on Austin Energy property. If located on AE property, relocate within limits of construction. Provide documentation of construction entrance location relative to AE easement boundaries.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows two permanent driveways on the western property line labeled 'Construct Type II Driveway' and 'Construct Type III Driveway.' These are the only vehicle access points shown to the site. However, a temporary stabilized construction entrance is not specifically labeled or depicted as a distinct feature on the site plan. The permanent driveways pass through multiple easements (Sidewalk Easement, Wastewater Easement, 12' Water Line Vault Easement) but do not explicitly cross Austin Energy property or electric easements at these points. The construction entrance location and whether it's on AE property is unclear from the available plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that if a proposed construction entrance is located on AE property, it must be relocated within the limits of construction of the site plan. The site plan does not show a distinct temporary construction entrance feature, and the relationship of the permanent driveways to Austin Energy property is not clearly documented. Without clear labeling and location confirmation, it cannot be verified whether the construction entrance complies with this requirement.

findings.comment: Proposed fire lane routing relative to AE transmission easement not clearly documented. Depict transmission easement boundary on site plan and verify that fire lane routing does not cross the easement or, if it must cross, confirm it is relocated within construction limits and maintains all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.0 and Sheet 3 transmission easement requirements (25-foot clearance from structures, 46,000 lb pavement design in easement).
findings.observation: Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) shows internal drive aisles serving the eight buildings with fire lanes, but does not explicitly label any routes as passing through an Austin Energy transmission easement. Sheet 9 shows internal driveways but the transmission easement is not depicted, making it unclear whether fire lanes/driveways technically pass through the transmission easement area or merely adjacent to it. The site plan lacks clear visualization of the transmission easement boundary relative to fire lane routing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.0 requires that if a fire lane routing crosses AE property, it must be relocated within limits of construction and necessary clearances must be met. Without the transmission easement boundary depicted on the site plan, it cannot be verified whether fire lanes pass through the easement or maintain required clearances. Sheet 3 transmission notes indicate 25-foot clearances are required from transmission structures, but the actual easement boundaries are not shown for comparison against fire lane locations.

findings.comment: Site plan not following UCM § 1.14.0 Transmission and Substation Requirements - transmission easement not depicted on working plans. Add transmission easement boundary to all relevant site plan sheets (Site Plan, Grading Plan, Electrical Design Plan) with dimensions and coordinates. Show 25-foot clearance zones from transmission structures. Demonstrate compliance with all transmission easement requirements on the plans, not just in general notes.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains comprehensive transmission and substation requirements per UCM § 1.14.0 with detailed notes on easement clearances, access provisions, grading restrictions, fencing coordination, and construction protocols. However, examination of Sheets 9, 11, and 21 (Site Plan, Grading Plan, and Electrical Design Plan) reveals that the transmission easement is NOT depicted on these working sheets. The transmission easement boundary is not shown on the site or grading plans where it is essential for design coordination. Transformer pads are shown but are not correlated with transmission easement requirements. The site plan layout does not explicitly demonstrate compliance with transmission easement requirements through visual representation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 Transmission and Substation Requirements mandate that sites with transmission facilities must follow specific design and coordination protocols. While the general notes on Sheet 3 reference these requirements, the actual site plan sheets do not demonstrate compliance through proper depiction of the transmission easement, clearance zones, and design accommodations. The transmission easement must be depicted on the working plans with dimensions and coordinates so that all designers (landscape, grading, electrical, site) can coordinate their work to maintain required clearances and access provisions.

findings.comment: AE vehicle turnaround or exit capability not provided. Revise site plan to provide a turnaround area (hammerhead, T-turn, or cul-de-sac) at the eastern drive aisle terminus with minimum dimensions per UCM § 1.3.16 (minimum 20 feet × 35 feet set-up area with 35 feet vertical clearance for AE vehicles). Show AE truck access routing and confirm turn-around capability.
applicableAreas: Dead-end access for emergency and utility vehicles
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows internal drive aisles with two permanent driveway entrances on the western property line. The eastern drive aisle extends into the site to service Buildings 3-6 but terminates in a dead-end configuration at a curb and gutter line with a retaining wall beyond. No labeled or graphically defined turnaround area (hammerhead, T-turn, cul-de-sac, or other turning radius) is shown for vehicles to turn around or exit. The sheet provides no information about AE truck access requirements or vehicle turnaround capability.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires that all AE facilities have truck access with the ability to turn around or exit the property. The site has four transformer pads (shown on Sheet 21) that require periodic maintenance and service access by Austin Energy vehicles. The dead-end eastern drive aisle does not provide the AE vehicles with ability to turn around or exit efficiently. This violates the truck access turnaround requirement.

findings.comment: Biofiltration/detention pond in the northeast corner is adjacent to overhead distribution electric line on eastern property boundary. No engineer-sealed profile or section exhibits demonstrate the required minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from conductors to pond edge. Provide profile sheets showing measured horizontal clearance from outermost conductor to nearest pond edge, with professional engineer seal confirming minimum 7.5-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Detention pond in northeast corner adjacent to overhead electric line on eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeast corner of the site adjacent to the eastern property boundary. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) confirms an overhead electric line labeled '-OE-' running north-south along the eastern property boundary, positioned directly adjacent to the pond wall. Sheet 15 shows the pond plan details with rim elevation 681.00' and water surface elevations ranging from 676.25' to 676.75' for various storm events. Sheet 16 shows pond section profiles with detailed elevations but does NOT include elevation views or cross-sections showing the horizontal distance or clearance from the overhead conductors to the pond edge. No engineer-sealed profile exhibits demonstrating the 7-foot-6-inch minimum sky-to-ground clearance were found.
findings.reasoning: The detention pond is a man-made water quality feature (defined as a water quality feature under the checklist). The overhead electric line running along the eastern boundary serves distribution facilities (indicated by '-OE-' notation and transformer pads shown on Sheet 21, confirming distribution voltage, not transmission). UCM § 1.10.3 requires a minimum 7-foot-6-inch horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the pond edge to the nearest overhead distribution conductor. The site plan documents do not provide evidence of this clearance: Sheet 16's pond profiles show only the pond's internal cross-sections and elevation changes, not the clearance to the adjacent overhead line. No dimension lines, callouts, or professional engineer certification showing the measured distance between the pond boundary and the overhead conductors are present in the submitted plans. The absence of this clearance verification documentation, combined with the pond's adjacency to the overhead line, indicates non-compliance with the requirement.

findings.comment: Detention pond does not demonstrate required minimum 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Provide engineer-sealed radial clearance exhibits showing distances from conductor locations to pond edge measured in all directions, with professional engineer certification confirming minimum 15-foot radial clearance per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Detention pond in northeast corner relative to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows the detention pond in the northeast corner adjacent to the eastern property boundary. Sheet 12 shows the overhead electric line (-OE-) running along that boundary in close proximity to the pond wall. Sheet 15 and 16 provide pond details and profiles but do NOT include radial clearance exhibits showing distances from the overhead primary and neutral conductors to the pond edge measured in all directions (north, south, east, west from the conductors). No engineer certification or dimension callouts showing the 15-foot radial clearance are present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires water quality features to maintain a minimum 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors, measured as a radius in all directions from the conductor locations. The detention pond's proximity to the overhead line on the eastern boundary suggests potential non-compliance. The submitted plans do not provide professional engineer-sealed exhibits demonstrating that the pond maintains this 15-foot radial clearance. Without such documentation, the application cannot demonstrate compliance. The presence of the pond adjacent to the overhead line, without radial clearance verification, indicates a deficiency.

findings.comment: Missing engineer-sealed profile plans or section exhibits showing clearance verification and dimensions between detention pond and overhead electric conductors. Submit professional engineer-prepared profiles showing conductor locations (all phases), pond boundary location, and horizontal/vertical clearances with dimension callouts demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.3 minimum clearances (7.5 feet horizontal, 15 feet radial).
applicableAreas: Detention pond near overhead electric facilities in northeast corner
findings.observation: The detention pond is positioned within 15 feet of overhead electric conductors on the eastern property boundary (confirmed by Sheet 9 showing pond position and Sheet 12 showing overhead line location). Sheets 15 and 16 contain pond design cross-sections and profiles showing internal pond elevations and sedimentation/filtration details. However, these sheets do not include professional engineer-sealed profile sections or elevation views that show: (1) the location of the overhead conductors (all phases), (2) the exact location of the pond boundary, and (3) the horizontal and vertical clearances between the pond edge and the nearest conductor with dimension callouts. No detail sections referenced in the drainage plan sheets (Sheets 15-16) are cross-referenced to sheets showing this clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires that where water quality features are proposed near electric facilities (within 15 feet of overhead conductors), plans must include profile plans, engineer-scaled section exhibits, or elevation views showing clearance verification with dimensions between water quality features and electric facilities. The requirement is explicit: applicants must demonstrate compliance through professional engineer-certified exhibits showing measured clearances. The pond profiles provided (Sheets 16 Sections A-A and B-B) show pond geometry and internal elevations but do not extend to show the overhead conductors or clearance dimensions. This deficiency requires submission of additional exhibit sheets showing the clearance verification.

findings.comment: Tree plantings and landscaping are shown within 5-foot electric easements on north, south, and east boundaries without documented evidence of executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Provide executed license agreement letter from Austin Energy Public Involvement confirming that landscaping/irrigation within the easement has been 'obtained from and filed with' the City (not 'to be obtained'). Agreement must be attached to site plan submittal prior to approval.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings within 5-foot electric easements on northern, eastern, and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows tree plantings (marked with symbols including 'M' for mitigation trees, 'SY' for street yard trees, 'PL' for parking lot trees) positioned directly adjacent to and overlapping the property boundary lines on the north, south, and east sides of the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts 5-foot electric easements running along these same property boundaries: '5' Electric Easement' on the south, '5' Electric Easement' on the east (lower portion), and '5' P.U.E.' on the north. The tree plantings shown on the landscape plan, being placed at or within the property boundary, fall within the 5-foot easement widths. No notes, callouts, or attached documentation on either the landscape plan or site plan reference an executed license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement. The landscape plan's 'IRRIGATION NOTES' section discusses TCEQ Chapter 344 compliance but makes no reference to an easement license agreement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping and irrigation are permissible within electric easements only with a license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement. The checklist specifically requires that plans demonstrate the license agreement has been 'obtained from and filed with' Austin Energy—not to be obtained. The site plan notes in Sheet 9 do not confirm that this agreement exists; instead, note d mentions 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' which acknowledges potential future easement constraints but does not address current compliance. Without documented evidence of the executed license agreement, the landscaping plantings shown within the easements cannot be approved. This is a certificate of occupancy hold item per the grouping guidance.

findings.comment: Tree plantings shown within electric easements would obstruct 24/7 vehicular access required for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the 5-foot electric easement boundaries to maintain unobstructed access corridor, or provide engineer certification that design maintains minimum 12-foot clear width for maintenance vehicle access along entire easement length. Additionally, obtain and file executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement per UCM § 1.10.10.3.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings and landscaping within 5-foot electric easements on property perimeters
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts tree plantings positioned within the 5-foot electric easements running along the north, south, and east property boundaries. Trees are shown with canopy symbols (circles) that extend several feet from the trunk location. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows that these easements run the full length of these property lines. The placement of trees with mature canopies within these easement corridors would create physical obstructions that would prevent unrestricted vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance personnel and equipment. Easement widths (5 feet) are minimal; tree canopies, trunks, and root systems would occupy much of this width, leaving insufficient space for a maintenance vehicle to traverse the easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that landscaping within electric easements be positioned such that it does not restrict 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. The fundamental purpose of an electric easement is to provide Austin Energy with unrestricted access for construction, operation, maintenance, and repair of electric facilities. Tree plantings shown within the 5-foot easement corridors, with typical canopy spreads of 20-40+ feet (varying by species), would substantially obstruct this required access. Even if a license agreement were in place (which it is not, per EL-5.11), landscaping must be designed to maintain unobstructed access. The current landscape plan does not demonstrate this; trees are shown directly within the easement boundaries.

findings.comment: Permanent wood fencing is shown within 5-foot electric easements on eastern and southern property boundaries. UCM § 1.10.10.2 permits only removable wooden fences under license agreement. Either: (1) remove fencing from easement boundaries and relocate outside easement areas, (2) replace with removable fence type with notation indicating removable design allowing Austin Energy access, or (3) obtain executed license agreement from Austin Energy permitting the fence type proposed. Provide details showing fence construction and removability certification if fences will remain within easements.
applicableAreas: Wood fencing along eastern and southern property boundaries within 5-foot electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows fencing lines drawn directly along the eastern and southern property boundaries. These same property boundaries have 5-foot electric easements dedicated to utility use (labeled on Sheet 9 as '5' Electric Easement Vol. 60...' on the east and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885...' on the south). The fence lines follow the property boundary, placing them within the 5-foot easement width. The site plan notes describe these as 'Wood Fence' (eastern boundary), consistent with a typical residential privacy fence constructed of wood. Site plan details and notes do not identify these fences as removable, temporary, or specially designed to allow Austin Energy access. Standard residential wood fencing would constitute a permanent, non-removable obstruction within the easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 explicitly allows removable wooden fences within electric easements under a license agreement if they permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. However, it prohibits permanent or non-removable fencing. The distinction is critical: 'removable wooden fences' implies temporary structures that can be taken down during maintenance, whereas standard residential wood fences (which appear to be shown on Sheet 9) are permanent structures. The submitted plans do not specify that these fences are removable or designed for Austin Energy access. Additionally, there is no documented license agreement for easement use (per EL-5.11), which would be a prerequisite even for removable fencing. The presence of permanent-appearing wood fences within the easements violates the prohibition on non-removable fencing.
